body.text: Parātriṃśikāvivaraṇa
body.translated_text: <s>Parātriṃśikāvivaraṇa</s> (Commentary on the Supreme Thirty [Verses])

body.text: oṃ namaḥ śivāya
body.translated_text: Oṃ, salutation to <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: vimalakalāśrayābhinavasṛṣṭimahā jananī bharitatanuś ca pañcamukhaguptarucir janakaḥ /
children.translated_text: The great Mother who rests upon the pure <s>kalā</s> (creative phase) and whose creation is ever-fresh, and the Father whose body is full and whose splendor is concealed within the five faces —

children.text: tad ubhayayāmalasphuritabhāvavisargamayaṃ hṛdayam anuttarāmṛtakulaṃ mama saṃsphuratāt //
children.translated_text: May that Heart, which is the <s>visarga</s> (creative emission) consisting of the flashing forth of both in union (<s>yāmala</s>), the family of the nectar of <s>anuttara</s> (the unsurpassable), throb vibrantly within me. //

children.text: yasyām antar viśvam etad vibhāti bāhyābhāsaṃ bhāsamānaṃ visṛṣṭau /
children.translated_text: She within whom this entire universe shines, appearing as external manifestation in <s>sṛṣṭi</s> (creation),

children.text: kṣobhe kṣīṇe 'nuttarāyāṃ sthitau tāṃ vande devīṃ svātmasaṃvittim ekām //
children.translated_text: And when agitation subsides, [it shines] in the state of <s>anuttara</s> (the unsurpassable) — I bow to that one <s>Devī</s> (Goddess) who is one's own self-awareness. //

children.text: naraśaktiśivātmakaṃ trikaṃ hṛdaye yā vinidhāya bhāsayet /
children.translated_text: She who, having placed within the heart the <s>trika</s> (triad) consisting of <s>nara</s> (individual), <s>śakti</s> (power), and <s>Śiva</s>, causes it to shine forth —
I bow to that supreme, unsurpassable <s>Parā</s> (Supreme), the wonder of <s>pratibhā</s> (creative flash) that is her own radiance. //
Victorious is the one of priceless majesty, who has liberated the multitude of bound souls (<s>paśu</s>),
The glorious <s>Śambhu</s>, <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s>, <s>Parameśvara</s> (Supreme Lord), the primordial <s>Guru</s>. //
For the awakening of his own disciples, and for the remembrance of one who is [already] awakened,
This small effort is undertaken by me, <s>Abhinavagupta</s>. //

body.text: ParTri 1:

children.translated_text: O <s>Deva</s> (God), how [is] the <s>anuttara</s> (unsurpassable)
that immediately bestows <s>kaulika-siddhi</s> (the attainment of the Kaula tradition),
by the mere knowledge of which
one attains equality with the <s>Khecarī</s> (the power that moves in the void of consciousness)?

body.text: parameśvaraḥ pañcavidhakṛtyamayaḥ satatam anugrahamayyā parārūpayā śaktyā ākrānto vastuto 'nugrahaikātmaiva na hi śaktiḥ śivād bhedam āmarśayet /
body.translated_text: <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord), who consists of the fivefold act, is perpetually pervaded by <s>Parā</s> (the Supreme) <s>Śakti</s> (Power) whose nature is <s>anugraha</s> (grace); in reality He is nothing but grace alone, for <s>Śakti</s> does not apprehend any difference from <s>Śiva</s>. And that <s>Śakti</s>, whose nature is the reflective awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>) of grace toward the world, is first — inseparable from the hundreds of infinite powers that are about to be threaded forth in <s>Paśyantī</s> (visionary speech) through the act of supreme reflection — primarily established in the consciousness (<s>saṃvid</s>) that constitutes the supreme great <s>mantra</s>, which is not delimited by space or time; to that extent she abides in <s>Paśyantī</s> with no separation between the utterance and the response that are about to arise. And she, whose nature is the non-duality of the consciousness of all cognizing subjects, is ever-present in her abiding form. Then, <s>Paśyantī</s> reflects upon whatever is desired, awakened by the appropriate causal conditions, through the mere threading of awareness — just as memory, from among the impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) of a dark cognition shaped by the dispositions of knowledge and non-knowledge of manifold entities, reflects upon only a particular thing due to the fitness of the seed of memory to awaken. For at the time of the initial cognition, no differentiation had flashed forth there, where there is non-difference between the signified and the signifier. <s>Madhyamā</s> (middle speech), however, by making manifest the distinction between those very signified and signifier, operates through reflection (<s>vimarśa</s>) in their co-referentiality. And <s>Vaikharī</s> (corporeal speech) consists precisely in the full manifestation of the distinction between both — thus, in this arrangement which is established through one's own self-awareness, that very ground of <s>Parā Vāk</s> (Supreme Speech), whose essence is the supreme conventional disposition — being the ultimate true nature of the <s>Māyīya</s> (Māyā-born) word-power, neither artificial nor merely conventional — impelled by the <s>mantra-vīrya</s> (potency of mantra) which will be explained, is in reality established also in the stages of <s>Paśyantī</s> and beyond. For without her, there would be the consequence of inertness in <s>Paśyantī</s> and the rest, due to the impossibility of manifestation. And in that [state of <s>Parā</s>], there is no differentiation whatsoever such as 'this,' 'thus,' 'here,' or 'now.' And therefore, from the form of the emission of the supreme great <s>mantra-vīrya</s> (mantra-potency) up to the manifestation of differentiated entities that stream forth in <s>Vaikharī</s>, this [awareness], consisting of its own wonder (<s>camatkṛti</s>), resting in its own self which is nothing but luminosity (<s>prakāśa</s>), flashes forth — and this flashing forth, whose ultimate reality is uninterrupted continuity, is 'I' (<s>aham</s>). This will become clearer further on. But within that middle [range], in <s>Paśyantī</s> where there is the threading of the aspect of differentiation, and in <s>Madhyamā</s> where differentiation appears — in both of these, in the form consisting of the powers of knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) and action (<s>kriyā</s>), whose essence is <s>Sadāśiva</s> and <s>Īśvara</s>, that very wonder of 'I' (<s>aham</s>), whose activity is full with the wonder that has internalized the entire infinite universe, being of the nature of <s>Paśyantī</s> and <s>Madhyamā</s>, reflects upon its own self as in reality being the Supreme Consciousness (<s>parasaṃvid</s>).

body.text:
sā ca śaktiḥ lokānugrahavimarśamayī prathamataḥ parāmarśamayapaśyantyāsūtrayiṣyamāṇānantaśaktiśatāvibhinnā prathamataraṃ paramahāmantramayyām adeśakālakalitāyāṃ saṃvidi nirūḍhā tāvatpaśyantyudbhaviṣyaduktipratyuktyavibhāgenaiva vartate / saiva ca sakalapramātṛsaṃvidadvayamayī satatam eva vartamānarūpā / tatas tu paśyantī yad yat abhīpsitaṃ tat tad eva samucitakāraṇaniyamaprabodhitaṃ bodhasūtraṇamātreṇa vimṛśati, yathā anekabhāvābhāvajñānasaṃskārasaṃskṛtāyā mecakadhiyaḥ smṛtibījaprabodhakaucityāt kiṃcid eva smṛtir vimṛśati / na hi prathamajñānakāle bhedo 'trāsphurat yatra vācyavācakaviśeṣayor abhedaḥ / madhyamā punas tayor eva vācyavācakayor bhedam ādarśya sāmānādhikaraṇyena vimarśavyāpārā / vaikharī tu
tadubhayabhedasphuṭatāmayy eva -- iti tāvadvyavasthāyāṃ svasaṃvitsiddhāyāṃ yaiva parāvāgbhūmiḥ saiva māyīyaśabdaśaktiparamārthasvabhāvāsāṃketikākṛtakapāramārthikasaṃskārasārā vakṣyamāṇanayena mantravīryabhūtāṃśacoditā taduttaraṃ paśyantyādidaśāsv api vastuto vyavasthitā / tayā vinā paśyantyādiṣu aprakāśatāpattyā jaḍatāprasaṅgāt / tatra ca idam evam atra idānīm ityādibhedakalanā na kācit / tata eva ca paramahāmantravīryavisṛṣṭirūpāyā ārabhya vaikharīprasṛtabhāvabhedaprakāśaparyantaṃ yad iyaṃ svacamatkṛtimayī svātmany eva prakāśanamaye viśramya sphurati tad evaṃ sphuritam avicchinnatāparamārtham aham iti / tad etat agre sphuṭībhaviṣyati / tanmadhya eva tu paśyantyāṃ yatra bhedāṃśasyāsūtraṇaṃ yatra ca madhyamāyāṃ
bhedāvabhāsas tatrobhayatra jñānakriyāśaktimaye rūpe sadāśiveśvarasāre saiva aham iti camatkṛtir antaḥkṛtānantaviśvedantācamatkṛtipūrṇavṛttis tatpaśyantīmadhyamātmikā svātmānam eva vastutaḥ parasaṃvidātmakaṃ vimṛśati /
body.translated_text: And the Supreme Consciousness herself is called <s>Bhagavatī Devī</s> (the Blessed Goddess). By this much — through the sequence of creation beginning with <s>Paśyantī</s> extending to external [objects] such as blue and so forth — through her play (<s>krīḍā</s>) whose nature is the bliss of her own reflective awareness; through the will of <s>Bhagavān Bhairava</s> to remain thus in the state of supreme excellence, being transcendent over all, in the form of the desire to conquer; through engaging in the countless activities of knowledge, memory, doubt, certainty, and so forth; through illumination (<s>dyotana</s>) in the form of manifesting the nature of blue and so forth in everything that appears; through being praised by all those who are immersed in and devoted to His light; and through assuming the nature of all things by delimiting [herself in] space and time as she wishes. Therefore, divinity (<s>devatva</s>) is primarily ascribed to <s>Bhairava-nātha</s> alone. The status of <s>Bhagavatī Devī</s> belongs to His <s>Śakti</s> alone. As it has been said: [the verbal root] <s>divu</s> [is used] in the senses of play, desire to conquer, transaction, shining, praise, and motion. And thus, from a fractional share of grace from that principal supreme divine sovereignty, there is the conventional usage of the term 'deity' for <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Viriñci</s> (Brahmā), and others. Thus, when <s>Bhagavatī</s> <s>Paśyantī</s> and <s>Madhyamā</s> reflect upon their own self — 'I, who am of the nature of the <s>Parā Vāk Devī</s> (Goddess of Supreme Speech), have thus spoken' — then, by virtue of the commencement of <s>Māyā</s> flashing forth in that form, from their own standpoint, following the differentiation belonging to that <s>Māyā</s>, they reflect upon that very ground of <s>Parā</s>, which is of their own nature, as something past, in the third person, because it transcends the path of the inner and outer faculties that vivify the appearance of differentiation, and because the division of days such as 'today' — dependent on the movement of the sun and so forth — is indeterminate: a day of <s>Brahmā</s> equals many <s>kalpas</s>, and still more for <s>Viṣṇu</s> and others, while internally even a hundred-thousandth part of the vital breath's movement is called a 'day' — thus 'today' is unstable and imagined; how can it apply to the unconditioned body of consciousness? By this reasoning, since it fulfills the meaning of past, non-present, and indirect [reference], she would reflect in the third-person past tense. The purport is: 'I myself, being of the nature of <s>Parā Vāk Devī</s>, in the non-division of all signified and signifier, have thus spoken.' The justification is exactly like [the expression] 'While asleep, I apparently spoke.' For one does not remember that past state, since it was previously unknown [as an object]; now, through the greatness reported by another person, or through bodily transformations such as choking of the voice produced by actions like excessive lamentation and singing, one recognizes that state through wonder. For this is not mere non-recognition. 'While drunk or asleep, I apparently spoke' — for in states of intoxication, sleep, or swoon, there is indirectness due to the non-apprehension of any particular object of knowledge; but in the state of <s>Parā</s>, there is the complete absence of any particular object of knowledge,

body.text:
paraiva ca saṃvid bhagavatī devī ity ucyate / iyatā paśyantyādisṛṣṭikrameṇa bāhyanīlādiparyantena svavimarśānandātmanā krīḍanena, sarvottīrṇatvena sarvotkarṣāvasthiter bhagavato bhairavasya tathā sthātum icchayā vijigīṣātmanā, iyadanantajñānasmṛtisaṃśayaniścayādivyavahārakaraṇena, sarvatra ca bhāsamāne nīlādau tannīlādyātmabhāsanarūpeṇa dyotanena, sarvair eva tadīyaprakāśāveśais tatpravaṇaiḥ stūyamānatayā, yathecchaṃ ca deśakālāvacchedena sarvātmatāgamanena / ata eva mukhyato bhairavanāthasyaiva devatvam iṣyate / tacchakter eva bhagavatyā devīrūpatā / yad uktaṃ divu kriḍāvijigīṣāvyavahāradyutistutigatiṣv iti / tathā ca evaṃvidhamukhyapāramaiśvaryamayadevatvāṃśāṃśikānugrahād viṣṇuviriñcyādiṣu devatāvyavahāraḥ / evaṃ
bhagavatī paśyantī madhyamā ca svātmānam eva yadā vimṛśati aham eva parāvāgdevatāmayī evam avocam iti, tadā tena rūpeṇollasanmāyārambhatayā svātmāpekṣatayā tanmāyīyabhedānusārāt tām eva parābhuvaṃ svātmamayīṃ bhūtatvena abhimanvānā, bhedāvabhāsaprāṇanāntarbahiṣkaraṇapathavyativartinītvāt parokṣatayā sūryādisaṃcārāyattadinavibhāgakṛtādyatanānavacchedāt / brahmaṇo 'nekakalpasaṃmitam ahaḥ, tato 'pi viṣṇuprabhṛteḥ, antaś ca prāṇacārādau prāṇīyaśatasahasrāṃśe 'pi aharvyavahāra ity anavasthitaṃ kālpanikaṃ cādyatanatvam akālpanike saṃvidvapuṣi katham iti nyāyāt bhūtānadyatanaparokṣārthaparipūraṇāt parokṣottamapuruṣakrameṇa vimṛśet / aham eva sā parāvāgdevīrūpaiva sarvavācyavācakāvibhaktatayaivam
uvāceti tātparyam / supto' haṃ kila vilalāpa iti hy evam evopapattiḥ / tathāhi tām atītām avasthāṃ na smarati prāgavedyatvāt, idānīṃ puruṣāntarakathitamāhātmyāt ativilāpagānādikriyājanitagadgadikādidehavikriyāveśena vā tadavasthāṃ camatkārāt pratipadyate / na hy apratipattimātram evaitat / mattaḥ supto vāhaṃ kila vilalāpa iti madasvapnamūrchādiṣu hi vedyaviśeṣānavagamāt parokṣatvam, parāvasthāyāṃ tu vedyaviśeṣasyābhāva eva,
body.translated_text: only here, because it is of the nature of <s>Turya</s> (the fourth state) through the identity with the knowing subject, whereas in intoxication and the like, the predominance of the seizure of delusion [prevails] — this is the distinction; but the indirectness is the same. Thus, every cognizing subject, whether established in the role of <s>guru</s> or disciple or in any other activity, at all times, whatever one may be doing, enters into this very consciousness and thereby becomes the vessel of all activity. Therefore, in reality one reflects upon that very [consciousness] — '<s>Devī</s> spoke' — meaning: 'I myself constantly reflect upon everything without difference in the ground of <s>Parā</s>; otherwise this manifest expression belonging to the planes of <s>Paśyantī</s> and <s>Madhyamā</s> would not be possible' — to that extent it is said '<s>Devī</s> spoke.' In exactly the same way, the preceding '<s>Bhairava</s> spoke' should be understood. For there too, it is <s>Bhairava</s> himself, whose nature is the non-separation of his own <s>Śakti</s>, who is the meaning of 'I spoke.' Only, in the reflective awareness whose nature is <s>sṛṣṭi</s> (creation), where <s>Śakti</s> predominates, the reflection as '<s>Devī</s>' in the form of 'I' (<s>aham</s>) is appropriate; whereas in the reflective awareness of <s>saṃhāra</s> (withdrawal), where the possessor of <s>Śakti</s> predominates, the wonder of the <s>Bhairava</s>-form is [expressed as] 'ma-ha' (the reverse of <s>aham</s>). This will be elucidated further.

body.text:
kevalam atra vedakatādātmyapratipattyā turyarūpatvāt, madādiṣu tu mohāveśaprādhānyāt - itīyānviśeṣaḥ, parokṣatā tu samānaiva / evaṃ sarva eva pramātā guruśiṣyādipade anyatra vā vyavahāre sthitaḥ sarvakālam eva yat kiṃcit kurvāṇa enām eva saṃvidam anupraviśya sarvavyavahārabhājanaṃ bhavati / atas tām eva vastuto vimṛśati devī uvāca iti / yāvad uktaṃ syād aham eva satataṃ sarvam abhedena vimṛśāmi parābhūmau, anyathā paśyantīmadhyamābhūmigaṃ sphuṭam idaṃ prathanaṃ na syāt, tāvad evoktaṃ bhavati devī uvāca iti / evam eva purastād bhairava uvāca iti mantavyam / tatrāpi hi svaparaśaktyavibhāgamayo bhairavātmaiva aham uvāca ity arthaḥ / kevalaṃ śaktipradhānatayā sṛṣṭisvabhāvākhyāmarśe aham ity ucito devīparāmarśaḥ, śaktimatpradhānatayā
saṃhārāveśavimarśe maha iti bhairavarūpacamatkāraḥ / sphuṭayiṣyate caitat /
body.translated_text: And this reflection of the Supreme Consciousness, whose nature is <s>icchā-śakti</s> (the power of will), [occurs] in the ground of <s>Paśyantī</s> and <s>Madhyamā</s> which consists of <s>jñāna-śakti</s> (the power of knowledge); and that itself is the purpose of all scripture (<s>śāstra</s>) from beginning to end. Therefore, in <s>jñāna-śakti</s> alone, which is of the nature of <s>Sadāśiva</s>, through the sequential unfolding of prior and subsequent words and sentences, the reflection of the true supreme great <s>mantra-vīrya</s> (mantra-potency) is itself the arrangement of words and sentences beginning with the syllables da-e-va-ya-u-va-ā-ca, bha-ai-ra-a-va-a, and so forth. And it has been said in the <s>Svacchandatantra</s>:

body.text: etac ca paśyantīmadhyamābhuvi jñānaśaktimayyām eva parasyā icchāśaktimayyāḥ saṃvido vimarśanaṃ, tad eva ca sarvārambhaparyantaśāstraprayojanam / ata eva jñanaśaktāv eva sadāśivamayyāṃ pūrvottarapadavākyakramollāsād vāstavaparamahāmantravīryavimarśa eva dakāra-ekāra-vakāra-yakāra-ukāra-vakāra-ākāra-cakāra, bhakāra-aikāra-repha-akāra-vakāra-akārādipadavākyayojanā / uktaṃ ca svacchandatantre
body.translated_text: Q: Having assumed the positions of <s>Guru</s> and disciple, the god <s>Sadāśiva</s> himself, Q: through prior and subsequent words and sentences, brought down the <s>tantra</s>. //

body.text:
Q: guruśiṣyapade sthitvā svayaṃ devaḥ sadāśivaḥ /
Q: purvottarapadair vākyais tantraṃ samavatārayat //
body.translated_text: Thus, the power of grace (<s>anugraha-śakti</s>) is never setting in all cognizing subjects — and this is the supreme <s>sambandha</s> (connection), which is the very life-breath of the scripture whose essence is the six half-[verses]. And in this <s>anuttara</s> (unsurpassable [reality]), since all other connections — the great intervening divine and non-divine ones — are of the nature of the Supreme alone, as taught above. As stated in the <s>Trikahṛdaya</s>:

body.text: iti / evaṃ cānugrahaśaktiḥ satataṃ sarvapramātṛṣv anastamitaiveti saiṣa ṣaḍardhasāraśāstraikaprāṇaḥ para eva saṃbandhaḥ / atrānuttare saṃbandhāntarāṇāṃ mahadantarāladivyādivyādīnām uktopadeśena paraikamayatvāt / tad uktaṃ trikahṛdaye
body.translated_text: Q: <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord), whose supreme [nature] is <s>visarga</s> (emission), eternally [acts] upon his own <s>Śakti</s>, Q: being of the nature of grace, both creator and destroyer, unrestricted. //

body.text:
Q: nityaṃ visargaparamaḥ svaśaktau parameśvaraḥ /
Q: anugrahātmā sraṣṭā ca saṃhartā cāniyantritaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus, by this sequence, the state of being eternally arisen (<s>sadodita</s>) [is established].

body.text: iti / evam amunā krameṇa sadoditatā /
body.translated_text: Because <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord), who is the reality of consciousness (<s>citta-tattva</s>), is of this ultimate nature, whatever flashed forth internally without differentiation is then reflected upon in the ground of <s>Paśyantī</s> with the desire to differentiate into <s>varṇa</s> (phoneme), <s>pada</s> (word), and <s>vākya</s> (sentence), and in the stage of <s>Madhyamā</s> it stands as differentiated, grounded in reality, extending through to <s>Vaikharī</s> where it culminates in the composition of differentiated <s>Māyīya</s> (Māyā-born) phonemes, words, and sentences such as '<s>anuttaraṃ katham</s>' and so forth. This itself is that imperceptible mouth of <s>Bhairava</s> (<s>Bhairava-vaktra</s>), whose nature is the reflective awareness of creation — being of the nature of the conjunction (<s>saṃghaṭṭa</s>) of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s> in the form of A and Ā, whose essence is the 'I'-consciousness (<s>aham-bhāva</s>) of <s>anuttara</s>, the seed of the outpouring of <s>Trika</s> scripture, the fixed abode, the fundamental [reality], which is the sole life of all living beings. Therefore, because there is no delimitation, and because the designation of place and the like is inapplicable, the precedence of place and so forth is not tenable. And the reality, in the form of the question and its answer, is eternally arisen, primordially undifferentiated. Thus, the purport here is just this — the Self, whose nature is the essence of all entities, manifesting itself, reflects upon its own Self through question and answer that are undifferentiated from the Self, consisting of the questioner and respondent who are of the nature of the Self, wondering at itself as 'I.' 'I myself, desiring such variegated wonder, knowing thus, become just so' — to that extent is '<s>Devī</s> spoke,' from '<s>anuttaraṃ katham</s>' through the middle up to '<s>Bhairava</s> spoke, listen O <s>Devī</s>,' and this is the <s>Rudrayāmala</s>. Or rather, all scriptures beginning with the <s>Pañcasrotas</s> up to this worldly activity [are included]. This is what has been called the supreme <s>sambandha</s> (connection).

body.text:
evaṃparamārthamayatvāt parameśvarasya cittattvasya yad evāvibhāgenāntarvastu sphuritaṃ tad eva paśyantībhuvi varṇapadavākyavibibhājayiṣayā parāmṛṣṭaṃ madhyamāpade ca bhedena sthitaṃ vastupūrvakaṃ saṃpannaṃ yāvad vaikharyantam anuttaraṃ katham ityādi bhinnamāyīyavarṇapadavākyaracanāntam / etad eva tad anupalakṣyaṃ bhairavavaktraṃ sṛṣṭiparāmarśātmakam, anuttarāhaṃbhāvasārākārākārarūpaśivaśaktisaṃghaṭṭasamāpattikṣobhātmakaṃ trikaśāstraprasarabījaṃ dhruvapadaṃ maulikaṃ sarvajīvatāṃ jīvanaikarūpam / ata eva vyavacchedābhāvāt sthānanirdeśādyayogāt sthānādipūrvakatvaṃ nopapannam / vastu ca praśnataduttararūpaṃ satatoditam eva prathamam avibhāgamayam / tena etāvad evātra tātparyam -- svātmā sarvabhāvasvabhāvaḥ svayaṃ
prathamānaḥ svātmānam eva svātmāvibhinnena praśnaprativacanena praṣṭṛprativaktṛsvātmamayenāhantayā camatkurvan vimṛśatīti / aham evaivaṃvicitracamatkārecchus tathā jānann eva tathaiva bhavāmīti yāvat tāvad eva devī uvāca, anuttaraṃ katham ity ārabhya bhairava uvāca śṛṇu devi iti madhyato yāvad ity etad rudrayāmalam iti / yad vā sarvāṇi pañcasrotaḥprabhṛtīni śāstrāṇi yāvat laukiko 'yaṃ vyavahāraḥ / sa eṣa uktaḥ paraḥ saṃbandhaḥ /
body.translated_text: The secret essence of instruction, which constantly bestows the state of immediate <s>Bhairava</s>-hood — the entirety of the question has been commented upon by me, <s>Abhinavagupta</s>. //

body.text:
gopyam upadeśasāraṃ sadyobhairavapadāvahaṃ satatam /
abhinavaguptena mayā vyākhyātaṃ praśnasarvasvam //
body.translated_text: But out of devotion to the welfare of disciples, we state this much in summary:

body.text: śiṣyahitaparatayā tu idam eva saṃgṛhyābhidadhmaḥ /
body.translated_text: Whatever is to be known and whatever is to be done in all activities, all that, having transcended differentiation, unfolds in the <s>Turya</s> (fourth) ground of <s>Parā</s> (the Supreme). //

body.text:
sarveṣu vyavahāreṣu jñeyaṃ kāryaṃ ca yad bhavet /
tatparasyāṃ turyabhuvi gatabhedaṃ vijṛmbhate //
body.translated_text: In <s>Paśyantī</s>, whose nature is the threading of differentiation, [operating] on the plane of sequence, and in <s>Madhyamā</s>, where sequence is internally manifest [but] not [yet externally] conjoined, that [reality] becomes possessed of differentiation. //

body.text:
bhedāsūtraṇarūpāyāṃ paśyantyāṃ kramabhūjuṣi /
antaḥsphuṭakramāyogaṃ madhyāyāṃ tad vibhedabhāk //
body.translated_text: <s>Madhyamā</s> and <s>Paśyantī</s>, having deeply entered <s>Parā</s> in non-difference, would reflect upon that [state] as if indirectly, like one intoxicated or asleep, at that time. //

body.text:
madhyā paśyanty atha parām adhyāsyābhedato bhṛśam /
parokṣam iva tatkālaṃ vimṛśen mattasuptavat //
body.translated_text: In exactly this way will the <s>anuttaratva</s> (unsurpassable nature) be explained. As stated by the venerable <s>Somānanda-pāda</s>:

body.text: evam eva etad anuttaratvaṃ nirvakṣyatīti / tad uktaṃ śrīsomānandapādaiḥ
body.translated_text: Q: Simultaneously with the first <s>Śākta</s> vibration (<s>spanda</s>) of <s>Bhagavān Bhairava Bhaṭṭāraka</s>, who is devoted to the fivefold act,

body.text: Q: pañcavidhakṛtyatatparabhagavadbhairavabhaṭṭārakasya prathamaśāktaspandasamantaram
body.translated_text: and so forth, in his own <s>Vivṛti</s> (sub-commentary).

body.text: ityādi nijavivṛtau /
body.translated_text: This effort of ours, who have been purified by His teaching, is for the purpose of cutting open the knot of that [text]. The <s>sambandha</s> (connection) has been stated. The <s>abhidheya</s> (subject matter) is <s>Trīśikā</s> — the sovereign (<s>Īśikā</s>) of the three <s>śaktis</s> (powers): <s>Icchā</s> (will), <s>Jñāna</s> (knowledge), and <s>Kriyā</s> (action), which are internally inexpressible, [also known as] <s>Sṛṣṭi</s> (creation) and so forth, impulse (<s>udyoga</s>) and so forth. And sovereignty (<s>Īśanā</s>) exists only as inseparable from what is to be governed — therefore, the <s>abhidheya</s> is <s>Bhagavatī Bhaṭṭārikā Parā</s> (the Supreme Blessed Sovereign Goddess), the Consciousness that transcends this triad of powers and is of the nature of non-separation from those powers; and by virtue of connection with that, this is the <s>abhidhāna</s> (designation/text). The <s>Gurus</s> also read '<s>Triṃśakā</s>,' and on account of the equivalence of syllables, they give the etymology: 'she who embodies (<s>kāyati</s>) the three <s>śaktis</s> is <s>Triṃśakā</s>' — not '<s>Triṃśikā</s>' from the connection with thirty verses, since the meaning of <s>Triṃśakā</s> extends beyond just that number. As stated in the venerable <s>Tantrasāra</s>:

body.text: tadgranthinirdalanārtha eva ayam asmākaṃ tacchāsanapavitritānāṃ yatnaḥ / uktaḥ saṃbandhaḥ / abhidheyaṃ trīśikā iti / tisṛṇāṃ śaktīnām icchājñānakriyāṇāṃ sṛṣṭyādyudyogādināmāntaranirvācyānām īśikā īśvarī / īśanā ca īśitavyāvyatirekeṇaiva bhāvinīti etacchaktibhedatrayottīrṇā tacchaktyavibhāgamayī saṃvidbhagavatī bhaṭṭārikā parā abhidheyam, tadyogād eva ca idam abhidhānam / triṃśakā ity api guravaḥ paṭhanti, akṣaravarṇasāmyāt ca niruktam āhuḥ tisraḥ śaktīḥ kāyatīti triṃśakā, na tu triṃśacchlokayogāt triṃśikā / atāvato 'pi triṃśakārthatvāt / tathāhi śrītantrasāre
body.translated_text: Q: The meaning of <s>Triṃśakā</s> has been expounded by you in an elaboration of one and a half <s>koṭi</s> (fifteen million [verses]).

body.text: Q: triṃśakārthas tvayā proktaḥ sārdhakoṭipravistaraḥ /
body.translated_text: Q: The meaning of <s>Triṃśakā</s> has been expounded by you in an elaboration of one and a half <s>koṭi</s> (fifteen million [verses]).

body.text: iti / abhidhānābhidheyayoś ca para eva saṃbandhas tādātmyād ity uktaprāyaṃ prayojanaṃ ca sarvapramātḥṇāṃ vibhoḥ paraśaktipātānugrahavaśotpannaitāvadanuttarajñānabhājanabhāvānām itthaṃnijasvarūpahṛdayaṅgamībhāvena nijāmodabharakrīḍābhāsitabhedasya nikhilabandhābhimatatattvavrātasya svātmacamatkārapūrṇāhantātādātmyabhairavasvarūpābhedasamāveśātmikā jīvata eva muktiḥ / prāṇadehādibhūmāv eva hy antarbahiṣkaraṇaviṣayāyāṃ preraṇākhyāyām udyogabalajīvanādirūpāyāṃ rūḍhasya bandhābhimatebhyo muktir iti gīyate / truṭite 'pi hi māyīye saṃskāramātre keyaṃ muktivācoyuktiḥ, kimapekṣayā veti / tad uktaṃ śrīspande
body.translated_text: Thus. And the relationship between word and referent is indeed the supreme one, being of the nature of identity — this has been virtually stated already. And the purpose is: for all <s>pramātṛs</s> (knowing subjects) of the all-pervading Lord, who have become vessels for this much <s>anuttara</s>-knowledge through the grace born of the descent of supreme <s>śakti</s> (<s>paraśaktipāta</s>), liberation is alive — that is, liberation while living (<s>jīvanmukti</s>) — consisting in the absorption into identity with the <s>Bhairava</s>-nature that is the fullness of one's own <s>camatkāra</s> (aesthetic rapture) as complete <s>āhantā</s> (I-consciousness), wherein the entire mass of principles considered to be bondage, whose differentiation has been illuminated as the play of the fullness of one's own delight, has been made to enter one's own heart-essence in this manner. For indeed it is proclaimed that liberation from what is considered bondage occurs for one who is established in the very ground of <s>prāṇa</s>, body, and so forth — that is, in the domain of inner and outer faculties and their objects, called impulsion, whose nature is the force of arising, vitality, and the like. For even if the <s>māyīya</s> (pertaining to <s>Māyā</s>) is severed as a mere <s>saṃskāra</s> (impression), what is this talk of liberation, and with reference to what? This has been stated in the sacred <s>Spandakārikā</s>:

body.text:
Q: iti vā yasya saṃvittiḥ krīḍātvenākhilaṃ jagat /
Q: sa paśyan satataṃ yukto jīvanmukto na saṃśayaḥ //
body.translated_text: "Or he whose <s>saṃvitti</s> (awareness) regards the entire world as play, he, constantly united, seeing thus, is liberated while living — there is no doubt."

body.text: iti / sphuṭībhaviṣyati ca etat avidūra eva /
body.translated_text: Thus. And this will become clear very shortly.

body.text: tadanena svasaṃvedanena prayojanam eva atra sakalapumarthaparyavasānam iti prayojanaprayojanānavakāśaḥ / uktāny eva saṃbandhābhidheyaprayojanāni /
body.translated_text: Therefore, by this self-experience, the purpose here is indeed the culmination of all human aims (<s>puruṣārtha</s>), and so there is no occasion for a further purpose-of-the-purpose. The relation, referent, and purpose have already been stated.

body.text: atha granthārtho vyākhyāyate / anuttaram iti /

children.text: na vidyate uttaram adhikaṃ yataḥ / yathā hi tattvāntarāṇī ṣaṭtriṃśad anāśritaśivaparyan tāni parabhairavabodhānupraveśāsāditatathābhāvasiddhīni saṃvidam adhikayanti naivaṃ parā paripūrṇā parabhairavasaṃvit, tasyāḥ sadā svayam anargalānapekṣaprathācamatkārasāratvāt /
children.translated_text: That than which there is nothing <s>uttara</s> (higher or greater). Just as the other thirty-six <s>tattvas</s> (principles), culminating in <s>Anāśritaśiva</s>, which achieve their status through entering into the awareness of supreme <s>Bhairava</s>, do augment <s>saṃvid</s> (consciousness) — not so the supreme, perfectly full awareness of <s>Parabhairava</s>, for it is eternally of the essence of unobstructed, independent, spontaneous manifestation and <s>camatkāra</s> (aesthetic rapture).

children.text: tathā na vidyaty uttaraṃ praśnaprativacorūpaṃ yatra / yata eva hi mahāsaṃvitsindhor ullasadanantapratibhāparyantadhāmna ullāsya praśnapratibhānādipātraṃ bhavati śiṣyaḥ, tad eva vastutas tattvaṃ satatoditam iti kimiva ācāryīyam uttaram anyat syāt /
children.translated_text: Likewise, there is no <s>uttara</s> (answer) in the form of question and reply there. For the very principle from which the disciple becomes a vessel for the arising of question and insight — out of the radiance of the great ocean of <s>saṃvit</s> (consciousness), whose extent reaches to infinite <s>pratibhā</s> (creative intuition) — that very principle is in reality eternally arisen (<s>satatodita</s>); so what other answer from the teacher could there be?

children.text:
uttaraṇam uttaro bhedavādābhimato 'pavargaḥ / sa hi vastuto niyatiprāṇatāṃ nātikrāmati / tathā hi prathamaṃ śarīrāt prāṇabhūmāv anupraviśya, tato 'pi buddhibhuvam adhiśayya, tato 'pi spandanākhyāṃ
jīvanarūpatām adhyāsya, tato 'pi sarvavedyaprakṣayātmaśūnyapadam adhiṣṭhāya, tato 'pi sakalamalatānavatāratamyātiśayadhārāprāptau śivatvavyaktyā aṇur apavṛjyate āropavyarthatvāt iti /
children.translated_text: <s>Uttaraṇa</s> (crossing over) — <s>uttara</s> means <s>apavarga</s> (final liberation) as conceived by the dualist doctrines. That, in reality, does not transcend the level of <s>niyati</s> (limitation) and <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath). For first, entering from the body into the domain of <s>prāṇa</s>, then surpassing even that to the level of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), then surpassing even that to assume the nature called <s>spandana</s> (vibration), which is vitality itself, then surpassing even that to abide in the void-state that is the dissolution of all objectivity, then surpassing even that, upon attaining the stream of graduated degrees of descent of all impurities, the <s>aṇu</s> (individual soul) is liberated through the manifestation of <s>Śivatva</s> (Śiva-nature), since the superimposition becomes purposeless — thus they say.

Just so, the ascending sequence (<s>uttara</s>) attained progressively through the stations of <s>nābhi</s> (navel), <s>hṛd</s> (heart), <s>kaṇṭha</s> (throat), <s>tālu</s> (palate), <s>brahmarandhra</s>, the aperture of <s>Bhairava</s>, and so forth, is also of this same kind.

children.text: tathā uttaranti ata iti uttaro bandhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Likewise, that by which they cross over (<s>uttaranti</s>) is <s>uttara</s>, meaning bondage.

children.text: uttaraṇam uttaro mokṣaḥ / tad evaṃvidhā uttarā yatra na santi /
children.translated_text: <s>Uttaraṇa</s> (crossing over) is <s>uttara</s>, meaning <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation). Thus, <s>anuttara</s> is that in which such kinds of <s>uttara</s> do not exist.

children.text: uttaraṃ ca śabdanam / tat sarvathā īdṛśaṃ tādṛśam iti vyavacchedaṃ kuryāt / tad yatra na bhavaty avyavacchinnam idam anuttaram /
children.translated_text: And <s>uttara</s> also means verbal expression (<s>śabdana</s>). That would make a delimitation — 'it is of this kind' or 'of that kind.' That in which this does not occur is the undelimited — this is <s>anuttara</s>.

children.text:
idam ity api hi vyavacchinnottaravyavacchedaprāṇam eveti vyavacchedakatvāt vikalpātmaiva / ata eva yāvad anuttare rūpe pravivikṣur māyīyaḥ pramātā tāvat kalpita eva viśeṣātmani / tatratv avikalpitaṃ yad avinābhāvi, tadvinā kalpitarūpāsphuraṇāt,
tad eva vastuto 'nuttaram / tatra hi bhāvanāder anupapattir eva vastuta iti bhāvanākaraṇojjhitatvam uktam, na tu anupayuktita eva /
children.translated_text: For even the word 'this' (<s>idam</s>) is of the nature of <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual construction) alone, since it functions as a delimiter, its life-breath being the exclusion of the delimited <s>uttara</s>. Therefore, so long as the <s>māyīya</s> (conditioned) knower wishes to enter the <s>anuttara</s> form, he is constructed only in the particularized. But therein, that which is unconstructed and invariably concomitant — without which the constructed form does not even flash forth — that alone is in reality <s>anuttara</s>. For there, <s>bhāvanā</s> (contemplative meditation) and the like are in reality simply inapplicable — thus it is said that it is free from the action of <s>bhāvanā</s>, not that it is merely useless.

children.text: tad īdṛśam anuttaraṃ vyavahāravṛttiṣv apy evam eva / tad uktaṃ mayaiva stotre
children.translated_text: Such is <s>anuttara</s> even in the operations of ordinary experience. As I myself have said in a hymn:

body.translated_text: Now the meaning of the text is explained. <s>Anuttara</s> (the unsurpassed) —

body.text:
Q: vitata iva nabhasy avicchidaiva pratanu patan na vibhāvyate jalaughaḥ /
Q: upavanataruveśmanīdhrabhāgādhyupadhivaśena tu lakṣyate sphuṭaṃ saḥ //
body.translated_text: "Just as a stream of rain falling spread out across the sky, unbroken and fine, is not perceived, but is clearly seen through the adventitious conditions of garden trees, houses, peaks, and mountain ridges —"

body.text: tadvat
body.translated_text: In the same way,

body.text: Q: ... parabhairavo 'tisaukṣmyād anubhavagocaram eti naiva jātu //
body.translated_text: "...Supreme <s>Bhairava</s>, due to extreme subtlety, never comes within the range of experience."

body.text: Q: atha deśākṛtikālasanniveśasthitisaṃspanditakārakatvayogāḥ //
body.translated_text: "But the conjunctions of place, form, time, arrangement, condition, vibration, and agency —"

body.text: Q: janayanto hy anubhāvinīṃ citiṃ te jhaṭiti nyakkṛtabhairavīyabodhāḥ //
body.translated_text: "Generating cognition that apprehends, they instantly suppress the <s>Bhairava</s>-awareness."

body.text: itiyādi / tathā ca vakṣyate uttarasyāpy anuttaram iti / vyākhyāyate caitat /

children.text: evam eva narātmanaḥ śāktam uttaraṃ tato 'pi śāmbhavam / tathā teṣv api bhūtatattvātmamantreśvaraśaktyādibhedena svātmany eva uttarottaratvam, bhūtādiṣv api pṛthivyādirūpatayā, jāgrata uttaraṃ svapnaḥ, tataḥ suptam, tatas turyam, tato 'pi tadatītam, jāgradādiṣv api svātmany eva caturādibhedatayā uttarottaratvam / tad etat śrīpūrvapañcikāyāṃ mayaiva vistarato nirṇītam iha anupayogād granthagauravāc ca na vitatyoktam /
children.translated_text: In just this way, beyond the human self (<s>nara</s>) is the <s>śākta</s> (pertaining to <s>Śakti</s>) <s>uttara</s>, and beyond even that is the <s>śāmbhava</s> (pertaining to <s>Śiva</s>). Likewise within those, through the differentiation of element-principles, self, <s>mantreśvara</s>, <s>śakti</s>, and so forth, there is successive superiority within one's own self; and within the elements too, in the form of earth and the rest; waking has its <s>uttara</s> in dream, beyond that is deep sleep, beyond that is <s>turya</s> (the fourth state), and beyond even that is <s>turyātīta</s> (beyond the fourth); and within waking and the rest too there is successive superiority within one's own self through the fourfold and other divisions. All this has been determined in detail by me in the sacred <s>Pūrvapañcikā</s> (Īśvarapratyabhijñāvivṛtivimarśinī); here it is not elaborated, being inapplicable and to avoid excessive length of the treatise.

children.text: tad īdṛśam auttarādharyadvaitasaṃmohādhāyi uttaratvam / tathā viprarājanyaviṭsūdrāntyajātivibhāgamayam ūnādhikatvaṃ yatra na syāt / bhāvaprādhānyam uttaraśabdasya
children.translated_text: Such is the <s>uttaratva</s> (state of being higher) that engenders the delusion of duality between higher and lower. Likewise, <s>anuttara</s> is that in which there is no inferiority or superiority constituted by the divisions of <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>kṣatriya</s>, <s>vaiśya</s>, <s>śūdra</s>, and outcaste. The word <s>uttara</s> has a predominance of the sense of being —

children.text: uttarāḥ paśyantyādyāḥ śaktayaḥ, aghorādyāḥ, parādyāḥ, tā yatra na syuḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>uttarā</s> <s>śaktis</s> (powers) are <s>Paśyantī</s> and the rest, <s>Aghorā</s> and the rest, <s>Parā</s> and the rest — <s>anuttara</s> is that in which these do not exist separately.

children.text:
nuda
preraṇe iti nodanaṃ nut / tayā taraṇaṃ dīkṣākrameṇa taraḥ / śiṣyacaitanye gurucaitanyaṃ preryate / tena haṃsaprāṇādiśūnyaviṣuvatprabhṛtisthānabhedaparipāṭyā sakale niṣkale 'pi vā pūrṇāhutiyojanikādisthityā mokṣadāṃ dīkṣāṃ vidhatte / tad atra caitanyasya svaprakāśasya vyāpino de śakālākāraviśeṣāviśeṣitasya kathaṃkāram imā viḍambanāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Nud</s> means 'to impel' (<s>preraṇa</s>), hence impulsion is <s>nut</s>. By that, <s>tara</s> is the crossing over through the sequence of <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation). The consciousness of the <s>guru</s> is impelled into the consciousness of the disciple. By that, through the progressive series of stations — <s>haṃsa</s>, <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>śūnya</s> (void), <s>viṣuvat</s> (equinox/equilibrium), and so forth — whether in <s>sakala</s> (with parts) or <s>niṣkala</s> (without parts) initiation, through the procedure of <s>pūrṇāhuti</s> (final oblation) and the like, one bestows <s>dīkṣā</s> that grants liberation. But here, for consciousness that is self-luminous, all-pervading, undifferentiated by any particular form of space, time, or shape — how can these mockeries apply?

body.translated_text: And so forth. And it will be stated: 'the <s>anuttara</s> even of <s>uttara</s>' — and this will be explained.

body.text: tad evaṃvidho nudā preraṇena taras taraṇaṃ yatra na bhavati tad anuttaram / yad vakṣyate
body.translated_text: Thus <s>anuttara</s> is that in which there is no <s>tara</s> (crossing) through <s>nud</s> (impulsion) — that is, no crossing over through impulsion. As will be stated:

body.text:
Q: evaṃ yo vetti tattvena tasya nirvāṇagāminī /
Q: dīkṣābhavati ...
body.translated_text: "For one who knows thus in truth, there arises the <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) leading to <s>nirvāṇa</s> (final liberation)..."

body.text: iti /

children.text: aniti svasitīti kvipi an aṇur ātmā dehapuryaṣṭakādiḥ / tathā ananaṃ jīvanam / an dehādyantargataiva bhinnabhinnaśaktyādyahantāśūnyaprāyā jīvanākhyā vṛttiḥ, yaḥ śūnyapramātā ity abhihitaḥ, tasyaivottaratvaṃ sarvataḥ paramārthatayā ādhikyaṃ yatra, bhairavaikamayatvāt / jaḍājaḍabharite jagati jaḍair jīvadekamagnaiḥ sthīyate, jīvatāṃ ca jīvanaṃ nāma prāguktam, jñānakriyārūpam ekaṃ pārameśvaryaṃ sarveṣāṃ, paratrāpi hi svavad dehādir eva pṛthaktayā bhāti / yat punaḥ prāṇanaṃ tad abhedenaiva svaprakāśam / etad eva ca paramārtho yad uktaṃ śrīmadutpaladevapādaiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>An</s> — 'he breathes' — by the <s>kvip</s> suffix, <s>an</s> means the <s>aṇu</s> (individual self), comprising body, <s>puryaṣṭaka</s> (subtle body), and so forth. Likewise, <s>anana</s> means living, vitality. <s>An</s> is the activity called 'living' (<s>jīvana</s>), situated within the body and the rest, mostly void of the I-consciousness of differentiated and undifferentiated <s>śakti</s> and the like — that which has been designated as the 'void-knower' (<s>śūnyapramātṛ</s>). <s>Anuttara</s> is that in which there is supreme superiority (<s>ādhikya</s>) in the truest sense over that very <s>an</s> from all sides, because it is entirely of the nature of <s>Bhairava</s> alone. In the world filled with the sentient and the insentient, one abides through the insentient, sunk in the mere fact of being alive; and what is called living (<s>jīvana</s>), as stated before, is one sovereign <s>pārameśvarya</s> (supreme lordship) in the form of knowledge and action belonging to all; for even in the other world, body and the rest appear separately just as in one's own experience. But the vital animation (<s>prāṇana</s>) is self-luminous through non-difference alone. And this indeed is the ultimate truth, as stated by the revered <s>Utpaladeva</s>:

body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: Q: jñānaṃ kriyā ca bhūtānāṃ jīvatāṃ jīvanaṃ matam /
body.translated_text: "Knowledge and action of beings — this is considered the life, the living, of those who are alive."

body.text: iti / tathā jīvanaṃ jñānakriye eva iti /

children.text: a iti ca yeyam amāyīyāśrautanaisargikamahāprakāśaviśrāntanistaraṅgacidudadhisvātmacamatkārarūpā śāktollāsamayaviśvāmarśanarūpaparipūrṇāhaṃbhāvaprathamaparyavasānobhayabhūmigā kalā tasyā eva vakṣyamāṇanayena yeyaṃ nud visargāntatā tasyā eva taraḥ plavanaṃ sarvoparivṛttitvaṃ yatra /
children.translated_text: <s>A</s> — this <s>kalā</s> (creative power) that is non-<s>māyīya</s>, not Vedic, spontaneous, the great radiance, reposing in the waveless ocean of consciousness that is the <s>camatkāra</s> (rapture) of one's own Self, whose nature is the complete I-consciousness (<s>pūrṇāhaṃbhāva</s>) that is the reflective awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>) of the universe pervaded by the upsurge of <s>Śakti</s>, reaching both grounds whose first culmination is that — of that very <s>kalā</s>, by the method to be explained, that which is <s>nud</s> (the state of ending in <s>visarga</s>), and of that very <s>kalā</s>, <s>tara</s> is the floating, the revolving above all — <s>anuttara</s> is that in which this obtains.

children.text:
avidyamānā deśakālagamanāgamanādidvaitasāpekṣā nut preraṇā kramātmakakriyāmayī yatra tat anud ākāśādi lokaprasiddhyā / tato 'pi sātiśayam anuttaram / tasyāpi hy ākāśādeḥ saṃyogighaṭādicitropādhivaśāt samavāyiśabdādiyogāc ca syād api īdṛśī sakramā kriyā / saṃvittattve tu sarvato 'navacchinnapūrṇasvātantryaiśvaryasāre 'vicchinnacamatkāramayaviśrāntyā svīkṛtaśaṅkyamānopādhibhāve
sakaledantāspadabhāvapūgaparipūritāhamātmani nirābhāse sadābhāsamāne svīkārābhāsīkṛtānābhāse idantābhāsatadanābhāsasāradeśakālāpekṣakramābhāvād akramaiva svātmavimarśasaṃrambhamayī matsyodarīmatādiprasiddhā vimarśābhidhā kriyā iti tad eva anuttaram /
children.translated_text: Where there is no <s>nut</s> — impulsion dependent on the duality of space, time, coming, going, and so forth — that is, no sequential action-based activity — that is <s>anud</s>, like <s>ākāśa</s> (space) and the rest, by common worldly understanding. But <s>anuttara</s> surpasses even that. For even <s>ākāśa</s> and the rest might have such sequential activity due to adventitious conditions such as a pot in contact with them and other variegated limiting adjuncts, and due to the conjunction with inherent properties like sound. But in the reality of <s>saṃvit</s> (consciousness), whose essence is the sovereignty of complete, unrestricted <s>svātantrya</s> (absolute freedom) in every respect, through the repose that is unbroken <s>camatkāra</s> (rapture), wherein the suspected limiting adjuncts have been absorbed; in the Self that is <s>aham</s> (I), filled with the entire mass of entities that serve as the locus of all <s>idantā</s> (this-ness), objectless yet eternally shining, having made the non-appearing appear through absorption, having made the appearance and non-appearance of <s>idantā</s> (this-ness) its very essence — because of the absence of sequence dependent on space, time, and the appearance and non-appearance of objectivity, the action called <s>vimarśa</s> (reflective awareness), which is indeed without sequence, consisting of the impetus of self-reflective awareness, well-known in the tradition of <s>Matsyodarī</s> and others — that alone is <s>anuttara</s>.

body.translated_text: Thus. And likewise: 'living is knowledge and action alone.'

body.text:
atiśayamātre tamapo vidhiḥ, dvivacanavibhajyopapade atra tarap / tatrāyaṃ śuklo 'yaṃ śuklaḥ, ayam anayor atiśayena śukla iti vākye 'yam arthaḥ - anayoḥ śuklayoḥ madhyāt atiśayenāyaṃ śuklaḥ śuklataraḥ leṣāṃ tu śuklānām ayam atiśayena śukla iti ko 'yam adhiko 'rthaḥ / tathā hy ayaṃ prāsādaḥ śuklaḥ, ayaṃ paṭaḥ śuklaḥ, ayaṃ haṃsaś ca śuklaḥ, eṣāṃ sātiśayaḥ śuklatama iti / tatra prāsādo 'pi śuklaḥ paṭo 'pi śukla iti kim iva adhikam uktaṃ syāt / tamapi pratyaye evaṃvidhavākyakaraṇam ayuktam eva / na ca tarapaḥ tamap adhikam atiśayam abhidadhyāt, evaṃ tāvat tu syāt, avivakṣite pratiyogiviśeṣe tamapprayogaḥ, pratiyogiviśeṣāpekṣāyāṃ tu tarap / pratiyogyapekṣaiva dvivacanavibhajyopapadārthaḥ / eka eva hi pratiyogī bhavet / anayor ayaṃ
śuklo 'tiśayena iti na tṛtīyaḥ pratīyate, nirdhāraṇārthena prathamasyaiva pratiyogitvāvagateḥ / na ca dviprabhṛtyapekṣā bhavati ekasya yugapat, ekaikāpekṣā matā iti tasya krameṇa nādhiko 'rthaḥ kaścit / tāratamyam iti tu prayogaḥ kramātiśaye 'vyutpanna eva / na tu taraptamappratyayārthānugamāt tāryaṃ tāmyam ityādy api hi syāt / tad alam akāṇḍe śrutalavakauśalaprathanena / iha tūttarakramikapratiyogyapekṣāyām anuttamam ity api prayoge ayam evārthaḥ / tathāhy āgamāntare
body.translated_text: The <s>tamap</s> suffix is prescribed for the sense of mere surpassing; the <s>tarap</s> suffix applies when the basis of comparison is expressed with a dual number distributively. Here the meaning in the sentence 'this one is white, this one is white, this one is white by surpassing these two' is: among these two white things, this one is white by surpassing, hence 'whiter' (<s>śuklatara</s>). But in 'among these white things, this one is white by surpassing,' what additional meaning is there? For this palace is white, this cloth is white, this swan is white — the most surpassing among these is 'whitest' (<s>śuklatama</s>). But since the palace too is white and the cloth too is white, what additional meaning could be stated? The construction of such sentences even with the <s>tamap</s> suffix is indeed inappropriate. Nor could <s>tamap</s> express a greater degree of surpassing than <s>tarap</s>. Rather, it would be thus: <s>tamap</s> is used when no specific counterpart is intended, while <s>tarap</s> is used when a specific counterpart is intended. The meaning of the dual-distributive basis is precisely the expectation of a counterpart. For there can be only one counterpart: 'of these two, this one is white by surpassing' — no third is apprehended, since by the partitive sense, the first itself is understood as the counterpart. And since one thing cannot have expectation of two or more simultaneously — it is held that expectation is of one at a time — there is no additional meaning through sequence. The usage '<s>tāratamya</s>' (gradation) is simply unetymological for 'sequential surpassing.' It does not follow from the meanings of the <s>tarap</s> and <s>tamap</s> suffixes, for then forms like '<s>tārya</s>' and '<s>tāmya</s>' would also have to occur. Enough of this untimely display of superficial grammatical cleverness. Here, however, when the expectation of a sequential counterpart that is <s>uttara</s> is intended, even in the usage <s>anuttama</s> (unsurpassed), the meaning is the same. As in another <s>āgama</s> (scripture):

body.text:
Q: adyāpi yan na viditaṃ siddhānāṃ bodhaśālinām /
Q: na cāpy aviditaṃ kasya kim apy etad anuttamam //
body.translated_text: "That which even to this day is not known to the <s>Siddhas</s> (perfected ones) who possess awakening, nor is it unknown to anyone — this indefinable something is <s>anuttama</s> (the unsurpassed)."

body.text: iti / evaṃ svātantryasārākalitakriyāśaktiśarīram anuttaram / tad uktam utpaladevapādaiḥ
body.translated_text: Thus. In this way, <s>anuttara</s> has as its body the power of action (<s>kriyāśakti</s>) whose essence is <s>svātantrya</s> (absolute freedom) that is beyond construction. As stated by <s>Utpaladeva</s>:

body.text:
Q: sakramatvaṃ ca laukikyāḥ kriyāyāḥ kālaśaktitaḥ /
Q: ghaṭate na tu śāsvatyāḥ prābhavyāḥ syāt prabhor iva //
body.translated_text: "The sequentiality of worldly action is possible through the power of time (<s>kālaśakti</s>), but not of the eternal sovereign power — it would be as the Lord's own."

body.text: iti / tat vyākhyātam idam anuttaraṃ ṣoḍaśadhā / yad uktaṃ sāraśāstre
body.translated_text: Thus. This <s>anuttara</s> has been explained in sixteen ways. As stated in the <s>Sāraśāstra</s>:

body.text:
Q: anuttaraṃ tad dhṛdayaṃ hṛdaye granthirūpatā /
Q: granthiṃ ṣoḍaśadhā jñātvā kuryāt karma yathāsukham //
body.translated_text: "<s>Anuttara</s> is the heart (<s>hṛdaya</s>); in the heart there is the form of a knot (<s>granthi</s>). Having known the knot in sixteen ways, one should act as one pleases."

body.text: iti / tathā
body.translated_text: Thus. And likewise:

body.text: Q: hṛdaye yaḥ sthito granthiḥ

children.text: adha ūrdhvaniyāmakaḥ, \cit \IPVV 3 p. 293 attrib. to Mālinīsāra

body.translated_text: "The knot that abides in the heart —"

body.text: ityādi /
body.translated_text: And so forth.

body.text: tad īdṛg anuttaraṃ kena prakāreṇa kim uttararūpaparityāgena utasvid anyatheti / kaś cāyaṃ prakāraḥ, yad anuttaraṃ sarvam idaṃ hi jñānajñeyajātaṃ sarvata evānyonyaṃ bhedamayaṃ virodham upalabhate, tataś cedam auttarādharyaṃ bhaved eveti / kasmiṃś ca prakāre mokṣa eva kiṃ vā bandhābhimate 'pīti / thamupratyayasya vibhaktiviśeṣārthāniyamena prakāramātre vidhānāt prakāramātraviṣaya evāyaṃ praśnaḥ / deva iti vyākhyātam /
body.translated_text: Now, in what manner is such <s>anuttara</s> to be understood — by abandoning the form of <s>uttara</s>, or otherwise? And what is this 'manner'? For all this — the entire collection of knowledge and the knowable — is <s>anuttara</s>, yet it encounters mutual differentiation and opposition from all sides, and thus this hierarchy of higher and lower would inevitably arise. And in what manner — in liberation alone, or even in what is considered bondage? Since the <s>tham</s>-suffix (instrumental/locative), without restriction to a specific case-meaning, denotes manner in general, this question pertains to manner alone. <s>Deva</s> — this has been explained.

body.text: kulaṃ sthūlasūkṣmaparaprāṇendriyabhūtādi samūhātmatayā kāryakāraṇabhāvāc ca / yathoktaṃ saṃhatyakāritvād iti / tathā kulaṃ bodhasyaiva āśyānarūpatayā yathāvasthānād bodhasvātantryād eva cāsya bandhābhimānāt / uktaṃ hi kula saṃstyāne bandhuṣu ca iti / na hi prakāśaikātmakabodhaikarūpatvād ṛte kim apy eṣām aprakāśamānaṃ vapur upapadyate / tatra kule bhavā kaulikī siddhis tathātvadārḍhyaṃ parinirvṛtyānandarūpaṃ hṛdayasvabhāvaparasaṃvidātmakaśivavimarśatādātmayam / tāṃ siddhiṃ dadāti / anuttarasvarūpatādātmye hi kulaṃ tathā bhavati / yathoktam
body.translated_text: <s>Kula</s> (the group/totality) — because of the nature of a collectivity of gross, subtle, supreme, <s>prāṇa</s>, sense-faculties, elements, and so forth, and because of the relation of cause and effect. As stated: 'because of acting in concert.' Likewise, <s>kula</s> is because consciousness itself abides as it is in the form of condensation (<s>āśyāna</s>), and because the conceit of bondage arises from the <s>svātantrya</s> (freedom) of consciousness alone. As it is said: '<s>kula</s> means staying together and kinship.' For apart from the singular nature of consciousness, whose sole essence is luminosity (<s>prakāśa</s>), no non-luminous form of these is possible. In that <s>kula</s>, the <s>kaulikī siddhi</s> (realization pertaining to <s>kula</s>) is the firmness of that state, of the nature of the bliss of complete fulfillment (<s>parinirvṛti</s>), identity with the <s>Śiva</s>-awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>) whose nature is the supreme <s>saṃvid</s> (consciousness) that is the heart-essence. He bestows that <s>siddhi</s> (realization). For when there is identity with the nature of <s>anuttara</s>, <s>kula</s> becomes thus. As stated:

body.text:
Q: vyatireketarābhyāṃ hi niścayo 'nyanijātmanoḥ /
Q: vyavasthitiḥ pratiṣṭhātha siddhir nirvṛtir ucyate // Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi_12
body.translated_text: "For through mutual exclusion and inclusion, the ascertainment of what is other and what is one's own self — the establishment, the abiding — this is called <s>siddhi</s> (realization), <s>nirvṛti</s> (fulfillment)." — <s>Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi</s>, verse 12.

body.text: iti / sadya iti śabdaḥ samāne ahani ity arthavṛttir uktanayena ahno 'navasthitatvāt samāne kṣaṇe ity atrārthe vartate / samānatvaṃ ca kṣaṇasya na sādṛśyam, api tu tattvaparyavasāyy eva / evam eva sadyaḥśabdāt pratītiḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Sadyas</s> (instantly) — this word, whose conventional meaning is 'on the same day,' by the principle already stated, since the 'day' has no fixed standing, applies in the sense of 'at the same instant.' And the sameness of the instant is not similarity, but rather culminates in identity of reality (<s>tattva</s>) itself. Such indeed is the understanding conveyed by the word <s>sadyas</s>.

body.text: atas tasminn eva kṣaṇa iti vartamānakṣaṇasya sāvadhāraṇatvena bhūtabhaviṣyatkṣaṇāntaranirāse tadubhayāpekṣakalanāprāṇāṃ vartamānasyāpi kālatāṃ nirasyeta yato yāvad idaṃ parameśvarasya bhairavabhānoḥ raśmicakrātmakaṃ nijabhāsāsphāramayaṃ kulam uktam / tac ced antarmukhaparabhairavasaṃvittādātmyalakṣaṇaṃ nirodham eti, tadā tad eva paramānandāmṛtāsvādamayam adeśakālakalitam anuttaraṃ dhruvaṃ visargarūpaṃ satatoditaṃ / tad uktaṃ śrīvādyatantre
body.translated_text: Therefore, "at that very moment" — by the emphatic determination of the present moment, when past and future moments are negated, the temporality of the present itself, which depends on the calculation relative to both of those, would also be negated. For insofar as this <s>kula</s> (totality) of the radiant Lord <s>Parameśvara</s>, the sun that is <s>Bhairava</s>, consisting of the mass of rays, pervaded by the expansion of His own luminosity, has been described — if that enters into absorption (<s>nirodha</s>), whose nature is identity with the inner-directed supreme <s>Bhairava</s>-consciousness, then that itself, consisting of the savoring of the nectar of supreme bliss, unconditioned by place or time, is the unsurpassed (<s>anuttara</s>), the eternal, having the form of <s>visarga</s> (emission), perpetually arisen. As stated in the revered <s>Vādyatantra</s>:

body.text:
Q: saṃrudhya raśmicakraṃ svaṃ pītvāmṛtam anuttamam /
Q: kālobhayāparicchinnaṃ vartamāne sukhī bhavet //
body.translated_text:
Q: Having withdrawn one's own mass of rays, having drunk the supreme nectar,
Q: Unconditioned by both aspects of time, one becomes blissful in the present moment.

body.text: iti / vistāritaś ca vistarato 'nyatra mayaiva kālobhayāparicchedaḥ / tathā kulāt prāṇadehāder āgatā siddhir bhedaprāṇānāṃ nīlasukhādīnāṃ niścayarūpā tāṃ dadātīti / śarīrādayo hi jhagiti anuttaradhruvavisargavīryāveśena akālakalitena prāṇādimadhyamasopānāroheṇaiva bhāvānāṃ tathātvaniścayarupāṃ siddhiṃ vidadhate / yathoktam
body.translated_text: iti / And the meaning of "unconditioned by both aspects of time" has been elaborated in detail by me elsewhere. Likewise, from <s>kula</s> — from the body, <s>prāṇa</s>, and so forth — comes <s>siddhi</s> (attainment), which is the ascertainment of differentiated <s>prāṇas</s> such as blue, pleasure, and so on — it bestows that. For the body and so forth, through the sudden immersion in the potency (<s>vīrya</s>) of the eternal <s>visarga</s> of <s>anuttara</s>, unconditioned by time, through the ascent via the central ladder of <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest, bring about the <s>siddhi</s> that is the ascertainment of the true nature of things. As stated:

body.text: Q: api tv ātmabalasparśāt puruṣas tatsamo bhavet
body.translated_text: Q: But by the touch of the Self's own power, a person becomes equal to That.

body.text: iti / tathā
body.translated_text: iti / Likewise:

body.text: Q: ... karaṇānīva dehinām /
body.translated_text: Q: ... like the sense organs for embodied beings.

body.text: iti / tathā kule śivaśaktyātmani saṃnihite 'pi siddhir uktanayena jīvanmuktatāmayī samabhilaṣitāṇimādiprasavapadaṃ / tāṃ sadyaḥ anākalitam eva bhāvanākaraṇādirahitatvenaiva dadāti / yad uktaṃ śrīsomānandapādaiḥ /
body.translated_text: iti / Likewise, even when <s>kula</s>, whose nature is <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s>, is present, <s>siddhi</s> in the manner described is the state of <s>jīvanmukti</s> (liberation while living), the ground for the production of desired powers such as <s>aṇimā</s> and the rest. That it bestows immediately, without any process of cultivation or practice whatsoever. As stated by the revered <s>Somānanda</s>:

body.text: Q: bhāvanākaranābhyāṃ kiṃ śivasya satatoditeḥ /
body.translated_text: Q: What need is there of meditation or practice for <s>Śiva</s>, who is perpetually arisen?

body.text: iti / tathā
body.translated_text: iti / Likewise:

body.text:
Q: ekavāraṃ pramāṇena śāstrād vā guruvākyataḥ /
Q: jñāte śivatve sarvasthe pratipattyā dṛḍhātmanā //
body.translated_text:
Q: Once, through a means of valid knowledge — whether from scripture or the guru's word —
Q: The <s>Śiva</s>-nature, which abides in all, is known with firm conviction,

body.text: Q: karaṇena nāsti kṛtyaṃ kvāpi bhāvanayāpi vā /
body.translated_text: Q: There is nothing to be accomplished anywhere through practice or through meditation.

body.text: iti / kule jātā siddhiḥ śāktahādirūpaprasaraṇād ārabhya bahirbhāvapaṭalavikāsaparyantaṃ bhedāvabhāsanā / tāṃ dadāti /
body.translated_text: iti / The <s>siddhi</s> born in <s>kula</s>, beginning from the outpouring in the form of <s>śākta</s> and other levels, extending up to the full blossoming of the external plane of manifested objects — that is the manifestation of differentiation. That it bestows.

body.text:
tad eva hy anuttaraṃ mahāprakāśātma antaḥkṛtabodhamayaviśvabhāvaprasaram anuttaratvād eva niratiśayasvātantryaiśvaryacamatkārabharād bhedaṃ vikāsayati / na hy aprakāśarūpaṃ bhāvavikāsaprakāśe kāraṇaṃ bhavet / prakāśātmakaṃ cen nūnaṃ tat parameśvarabhairavabhaṭṭārakarūpam eveti kim apareṇa vāgjālena / tathā yena anuttareṇa viśeṣeṇa jñātā mātrā mānena pramātmanā trāṇaṃ pālanaṃ patitvaṃ yāsāṃ pramātṛpramāṇaprameyapramitirūpāṇāṃ tā mātrā vijñātā yena tat vijñātamātraṃ / tathā viśeṣeṇa pratipattidārḍhyabandhena yaj jñātaṃ tad vibhātam eva, na punaḥ bhāvanīyaṃ sakṛdvibhātātmatvāt / tathā jñātamātraṃ jñātam eva jñeyaikarūpatvāt, na tu kadācit jñātṛrūpaṃ ghaṭādi / tathā jñātā jñeyarūpā
bhedamayī iyaṃ māyā / tadubhayaṃ vigataṃ yatra tat vijñātamātram / ghaṭādayo yatra jñātrekarūpatvena svaprakāśātmānaḥ, yatra ca māyā na prabhavati, tena vijñātamātreṇa /
body.translated_text:
For that very <s>anuttara</s>, whose nature is the great Light, having internalized the expansion of the universe pervaded by consciousness, precisely because it is <s>anuttara</s>, from the sheer force of the <s>camatkāra</s> (wonder) of unsurpassed sovereign freedom, causes differentiation to blossom forth. For surely nothing whose nature is non-luminous could be the cause of the manifestation and illumination of entities. And if it is of the nature of Light, then it is certainly nothing other than the form of the Lord <s>Parameśvara</s>, the venerable <s>Bhairava</s> — so what need is there of further nets of words? Likewise, "by which" — by that <s>anuttara</s> specifically — "the <s>mātrās</s> are known": <s>mātrā</s> means measure, the knower (<s>pramātṛ</s>), and <s>trāṇa</s> means protection, lordship — those whose nature is knower, means of knowledge, object of knowledge, and cognition — those <s>mātrās</s> are known by which: that is <s>vijñātamātra</s> (known-only). Likewise, what is known through the specific firmness of realization is already manifest — it need not be further contemplated, since it is of the nature of what is manifest at once. Likewise, <s>jñātamātra</s> (the mere known) is just the known, being identical with the knowable — never does a pot and the like become the nature of the knower. Likewise, the known, having the form of the knowable,
is this <s>māyā</s> full of differentiation. Where both of those are gone, that is <s>vijñātamātra</s>. Where pots and the like, being of one nature with the knower, are self-luminous, and where <s>māyā</s> has no power — by that <s>vijñātamātra</s>,

body.text: khe brahmaṇy abhedarūpe sthitvā carati viṣayam avagamayati / tathā hānādānādiceṣṭāṃ vidhatte svarūpe cāste iti khecary antarbahiṣkaraṇatadarthasukhādinīlādirūpā / tathāhi vedyavedakabhāvānullāsipade śūnye saṃvinmātradṛgullāse saṃvedyagatāntaraikyarūpadiśyamānabhedollāse sphuṭabhedodreke ca krameṇa vyomacarīgocarīdikcarībhūcarībhūtā yāḥ śaktayas tā vastuta uktanayena svabhāvacarakhecarīrūpaśaktyavibhaktā evety ekaiva sā pārameśvarī śaktiḥ / yad uktam
body.translated_text: abiding in the space (<s>kha</s>) that is <s>Brahman</s>, whose nature is non-differentiation, one moves — that is, one illuminates objects. Likewise, one performs activities such as grasping, releasing, and so on, while resting in one's own nature — this is <s>khecarī</s>, whose form encompasses the inner and outer organs, their objects, pleasure and the like, blue and other sense-data. For indeed, the <s>śaktis</s> (powers) that become progressively <s>vyomacarī</s>, <s>gocarī</s>, <s>dikcarī</s>, and <s>bhūcarī</s> — in the void where the distinction of known and knower does not arise, in the pure flash of awareness as mere seeing, in the indication of unity within the objects of experience where differentiation is being pointed at, and in the full emergence of manifest differentiation — these powers, in truth, according to the principle stated, are undivided from the <s>khecarī</s> power whose nature moves in its own being. Thus she is one alone, the supreme <s>Śakti</s> of the Lord. As stated:

body.text: Q: śaktayo 'sya jagat kṛtsnaṃ śaktimāṃs tu maheśvaraḥ /
body.translated_text: Q: His powers are the entire universe; the possessor of powers is <s>Maheśvara</s>.

body.text: iti / tataḥ strīliṅgena nirdeṣaḥ / na hy ātmano manasa indriyāṇāṃ bāhyānāṃ ca bhedaviṣayasya vyavasthāpanaṃ vyavasthā ca yujyate, abhisaṃdhānādyayogād aprakāśatvāc ca / saiva khecarī kāmakrodhādirūpatayā vaiṣamyena lakṣyate / tasyāḥ samatā sarvatraiva paripūrṇabhairavasvabhāvāt / aṇumātram apy avikalānuttarasvarūpāparijñānam eva cittavṛttīnāṃ vaiṣamyam, sa eva ca saṃsāraḥ, apūrṇābhimānena svātmany aṇutvāpādanāt āṇavamalasya, tadapūrṇarūpaparipūrṇākāṅkṣāyāṃ bhedadarśanāt māyākhyasya malasya, tacchubhāsubhavāsanāgraheṇa kārmamalasya collāsāt /
body.translated_text: iti / Hence the designation in the feminine gender. For the establishment and ordering of the differentiated domain of the self, mind, sense organs, and external objects is not possible, due to the impossibility of intentional coordination and due to the non-luminous nature [of those]. That very <s>khecarī</s> is perceived unevenly as having the form of desire, anger, and so forth. Her equilibrium (<s>samatā</s>) exists everywhere, due to the all-pervading <s>Bhairava</s>-nature. Even the slightest non-recognition of one's own unfragmented <s>anuttara</s> nature is itself the disequilibrium of mental states, and that alone is <s>saṃsāra</s> — because of <s>āṇavamala</s> (impurity of finitude), which imposes finitude upon one's own Self through a sense of incompleteness; because of <s>māyīyamala</s> (impurity of <s>māyā</s>), which is the seeing of differentiation in the desire for fullness born of that incompleteness; and because of <s>kārmamala</s> (impurity of action), which arises through the grasping of auspicious and inauspicious impressions thereof.

body.text: svarūpāparijñānamayatadvaiṣamyanivṛttau malābhāvāt / krodhamohādivṛttayo hi paripūrṇabhagavadbhairavabhaṭṭārakasaṃvidātmikā eva / yad uktaṃ śrīsomānandapādaiḥ
body.translated_text: When the disequilibrium consisting of non-recognition of one's own nature ceases, the <s>malas</s> (impurities) are absent. For the mental states of anger, delusion, and the like are nothing but the consciousness of the fully perfect Lord, the venerable <s>Bhairava</s>. As stated by the revered <s>Somānanda</s>:

body.text: Q: ... tat saratprakṛtiḥ śivaḥ /

children.translated_text: iti / Likewise:

body.translated_text: Q: ... that, whose essential nature flows forth, is <s>Śiva</s>.

body.text: Q: sukhe duḥkhe vimohe ca sthito 'haṃ paramaḥ śivaḥ /
body.translated_text: Q: In pleasure, in pain, and in delusion, I abide as the supreme <s>Śiva</s>.

body.text: iti /
body.translated_text: iti /

body.text: Q: duḥkhe 'pi pravikāsena sthairyārthe dhṛtisaṃgamāt /
body.translated_text: Q: Even in suffering, through expansion, for the purpose of stability, through the conjunction with fortitude,

body.text: ityādi / krodhādivṛttayo hi ciccamatkāratādātmyād anyathā tatsvarūpalābhasyaivāyogāc ca parameśvaryaḥ karaṇadevatā eva bhagavatyas tās tāḥ krīḍā vitanvatyaḥ śivārkasya dīdhitirūpāḥ / tathā tā eva tattatparasparasāṃkaryalabdhāsaṃkhyeyarūpās tattaduccāṭanamāraṇaśāntyādirūpeṣu karmasu parikalpitatattatsamucitasaumyaraudraprakārāḥ kṛtyādibhedād devatātvenopāsyā uktā matādiśāstreṣu bhagavadbhairavabhaṭṭārakaparivārabhūtāś ca / yathoktam
body.translated_text: ityādi / For the mental states of anger and the like, by virtue of their identity with the <s>camatkāra</s> (wonder) of consciousness — and because otherwise the attainment of their very nature would be impossible — are the supreme goddesses, the deities of the sense organs, performing their various divine plays (<s>krīḍā</s>), being the rays of <s>Śiva</s>, the sun. Likewise, those very powers, having obtained innumerable forms through the mutual intermixture of each with each, are prescribed as deities to be worshipped in various rites such as <s>uccāṭana</s> (eradication), <s>māraṇa</s> (destruction), <s>śānti</s> (pacification), and so on, fashioned in appropriate gentle and fierce modes according to the differentiation of functions — and they are the retinue of the Lord, the venerable <s>Bhairava</s>. As stated:

body.text: Q: uccāṭane kākavaktrā ... /
body.translated_text: Q: In <s>uccāṭana</s> (eradication), the crow-faced one ...

body.text: ityādy upakramya
body.translated_text: ityādi — and beginning thus:

body.text: Q: tā eva devadevasya raśmayaḥ kādidhārikāḥ /
body.translated_text: Q: They are the very rays of the God of gods, bearing the phonemes beginning with <s>ka</s>.

body.text: ityādi / tathātvena tv aparijñātasvarūpāś ciccamatkāraṃ vikalpe 'pi nirvikalpaikasāraṃ tena tena vicitravarṇākṣarapuñjātmanā ghoratarātmanā vikalparūpeṇa devatātmanā śaṅkātaṅkānupraveśena tirodadhatyaḥ sāṃsārikapāśyapaśubhāvadāyinyaḥ / yathoktam
body.translated_text: ityādi / But when their true nature is not recognized, they conceal the <s>camatkāra</s> (wonder) of consciousness — which is, even in <s>vikalpa</s> (discursive thought), essentially non-discursive — through various forms of the deity that are masses of diverse letters and phonemes, of a most terrible nature, in the form of <s>vikalpa</s>, by introducing doubt and anxiety, thus bestowing the condition of a bound soul (<s>paśu</s>) enmeshed in the bonds (<s>pāśa</s>) of <s>saṃsāra</s>. As stated:

body.text: Q: pīṭheśvaryo mahāghorā mohayanti muhur muhuḥ /

children.text: Timirodghāṭa acc. to Kṣemarāja ad Śivasūtra 1.4

body.translated_text: Q: The goddesses of the sacred seats, most terrible, delude again and again.

body.text: iti / tathā
body.translated_text: iti / Likewise:

body.text: Q: viṣayeṣv eva saṃlīnān adho 'dhaḥ pātayanty aṇūn /
body.translated_text: Q: They cause the individual souls (<s>aṇus</s>), absorbed in sense objects, to fall ever lower and lower.

body.text: ityādi / tathā
body.translated_text: ityādi / Likewise:

body.text:
Q: śabdarāśisamutthasya śaktivargasya bhogyatām /
Q: kalāviluptavibhavo gataḥ san sa paśuḥ smṛtaḥ //
body.translated_text:
Q: He who has come under the enjoyment of the host of <s>śaktis</s> arising from the aggregate of sounds,
Q: Whose splendor has been devoured by the <s>kalās</s> (limited powers), is called a <s>paśu</s> (bound soul).

body.text: iti / jñātasvarūpās tā evoktayuktyā jīvanmuktatāpradāyinyaḥ / tathā uktam
body.translated_text: iti / When their true nature is recognized, those very same powers, by the reasoning stated, become the bestowers of <s>jīvanmukti</s> (liberation while living). As stated:

body.text:
Q: yadā tv ekatra saṃrūḍhas tadā tasya layodbhavau /
Q: niyacchan bhoktṛtām eti tataś cakreśvaro bhavet //
body.translated_text:
Q: But when one is established in the One, then controlling the dissolution and arising of that,
Q: One attains the state of enjoyer, and thereby becomes the lord of the circle (<s>cakreśvara</s>).

body.text:
iti / svarūpaparijñānaṃ ca etāvad eva yad etāsu vṛttiṣūdayasamayanirvikalpaikarūpāsu vikalpo 'py udayamāno varṇarāśisamārabdhatattadvicitraśabdārūṣitatve 'pi na tādṛśena varṇapuñjātmanā śakticakreṇa yujyate, yat tasya prāktananirvikalpaikavyavahāramayasya vikalpātmano mātuḥ svarūpaṃ khaṇḍayet / na ca vikalpā anubhavād vikalpāntarād vā bhinnāḥ, api tu sa evaikaḥ svātantryabheditabhāvoparāgalabdhabhedabhūtādyabhidhavijñānacakraprabhuḥ / tad evaṃ khecarīsāmyam eva mokṣaḥ / tac cānuttarasvarūpaparijñānam eva satatoditaṃ parameśvaryāḥ śivātmani saṃghaṭṭasamāpattyā ubhayavimarśānandarūḍhi / śivo hi paravāṅmayamahāmantravīryavisṛṣṭimayaḥ parameśvarīvisṛṣṭyā tadvīryaghanatātmakaprasūnanirbharayā sṛṣṭyā yujyate
/ tathā hi sarveṣām antarbahiṣkaraṇānāṃ yad yad anupraviśati tat tan madhyamanāḍībhuvi sarvāñgānuprāṇanasārāyāṃ prāṇātmanā cetanarūpeṇāste yad oja iti kathyate / tad eva sarvāṅgeṣv anuprāṇakatayā tadavibhaktavīryarūpatvena /
body.translated_text:
iti / And the recognition of one's own nature amounts to just this: that in these mental states, which at the moment of their arising are of a single non-discursive nature, even the <s>vikalpa</s> (discursive thought) that arises, though it may be clothed in diverse words composed of the aggregate of phonemes, is not identified with that circle of <s>śaktis</s> in the form of that mass of phonemes, such that it would fragment the essential nature of the knower who, in his prior non-discursive unified activity, has the nature of <s>vikalpa</s>. Nor are <s>vikalpas</s> different from experience or from other <s>vikalpas</s>; rather, it is that one alone, who, through the diversity of appearance colored by entities differentiated by His own sovereign freedom, is the lord of the wheel of cognitions designated as "earth" and so forth. Thus indeed, the equilibrium of <s>khecarī</s> is itself <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation). And that is nothing other than the perpetually arisen recognition of one's own <s>anuttara</s> nature — the firm establishment of the bliss of the mutual awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>) of both, through the union (<s>saṃghaṭṭa</s>) of the supreme Goddess (<s>Parameśvarī</s>) with <s>Śiva</s>. For <s>Śiva</s>, who consists of the emission of the great <s>mantra</s>-potency (<s>vīrya</s>) that is the supreme <s>Vāk</s> (Speech), is united with the emission of <s>Parameśvarī</s> — with a creation overflowing with the flower that is the condensed form of that <s>vīrya</s>.
For indeed, whatever enters into all the inner and outer organs abides in the ground of the central channel (<s>madhyamā nāḍī</s>), whose essence is the vivification of all the limbs, as <s>prāṇa</s>, as the conscious principle — that which is called <s>ojas</s> (vital force). That very thing, by virtue of its vivifying all the limbs, has the form of <s>vīrya</s> (potency) undivided from them.

body.text: tato 'pi punar api nayanaśravaṇādīndriyadvāreṇa bṛṃhakarūpaṃ rūpaśabdādy anupraviśad bṛṃhakatvād eva tadvīryakṣobharūpakāmānalaprabodhakaṃ bhavati / yathoktam
body.translated_text: And then again, entering through the gateways of the sense organs such as the eyes, ears, and so on, in the form of nourishment — entering as form, sound, and so forth — precisely because of its nourishing nature, it becomes the awakener of the fire of desire (<s>kāma</s>), whose nature is the agitation (<s>kṣobha</s>) of that <s>vīrya</s>. As stated:

body.text: Q: ālāpād gātrasaṃsparśāt
body.translated_text: Q: From conversation, from the touch of limbs,

body.text:
ityādi / ekenaiva ca rūpādyanyatamenodriktaprāktanabalopabṛṃhitasya sarvaviṣayakaraṇīyoktakṣobhakaraṇasamarthatvaṃ sarvasya sarvasya sarvasarvātmakatvāt / smaraṇavikalpanādināpi sarvamayamanogatānantaśabdādibṛṃhaṇavaśāj jāyata eva kṣobhaḥ / paripuṣṭasarvamayamahāvīryam eva puṣṭikāri na tv apūrṇaṃ nāpi kṣīnam samucitaṃ śaiśavavārddhakayor / vīryavikṣobhe ca vīryasya svamayatvenābhinnasyāpy adeśakālakalitaspandamayamahāvisargarūpam eva paripūrṇabhairavasaṃvidātmakaṃ svātantryam ānandaśaktimayaṃ sukhaprasavabhūḥ / nayanayor api hi rūpaṃ tadvīryakṣobhātmakamahāvisargaviśleṣaṇayuktyā eva sukhadāyi bhavati / śravaṇayoś ca madhuragītādi / anyatrāpīndriye anyat kevalaṃ paripūrṇasṛṣṭitām nāśnute svātmany evocchalanāt
/ tathā ca tadvīryānupabṛṃhitānām avidyamānatathāvidhavīryavikṣobhātmakamadanānandānāṃ pāṣāṇānām iva ramaṇīyatarataruṇīrūpam api nitambinīvadanaghūrṇamānakākalīkalagītam api na pūrṇānandaparyavasāyi / yathā yathā ca na bṛṃhakaṃ bhavati tathā tathā parimitacamatkāraparyavasānam / sarvato hy acamatkāre jaḍataiva / adhikacamatkārāveśa eva vīryakṣobhātmā sahṛdayatā ucyate / yasyaiva etadbhogāsaṅgābhyāsaniveśitānantabṛṃhakavīryabṛṃhitaṃ hṛdayaṃ tasyaiva sātiśayacamatkriyā / duḥkhe 'py eṣa eva camatākraḥ / antarvyavasthitaṃ hi yat tad dayitasutasukhādi vīryātmakaṃ tad eva bhāvanāsadṛśadṛgākrandādibodhena kṣobhātmakam vikāsam āpannaṃ punar na bhaviṣyatīti nairapekṣyavaśasaviśeṣacamatkriyātma
duḥkhasattvam / tad uktam
body.translated_text:
ityādi / And through even a single one among form and other sense-data, when augmented by the previously accumulated force in its heightened state, one becomes capable of producing the agitation described in all sense-domains and their functions, because everything is the nature of everything. Even through remembering, imagining, and so forth, the agitation inevitably arises due to the nourishment of infinite sounds and the like coursing through the mind, which pervades everything. Only that which is fully nourished and pervaded by the great <s>vīrya</s> (potency) of all things has the power to nourish — not what is incomplete, nor what is depleted, as is appropriate in childhood and old age. And in the agitation of <s>vīrya</s>, although <s>vīrya</s> is undivided since it pervades its own nature, the sovereign freedom that is of the nature of <s>Ānandaśakti</s> (the power of bliss), having the form of the great <s>visarga</s> (emission) — a vibration (<s>spanda</s>) unconditioned by place or time — identical with the fully perfect <s>Bhairava</s>-consciousness, is the ground for the generation of bliss. For even in the case of the eyes, form becomes the bestower of pleasure precisely through the method of the outpouring of the great <s>visarga</s> that is the agitation of that <s>vīrya</s>. And for the ears, sweet song and the like. In other sense organs too, other things — only they do not attain complete creative fullness, since they surge forth within the self alone.
And thus, for those whose <s>vīrya</s> has not been nourished, who lack the bliss of <s>Madana</s> (the god of love) characterized by the agitation of <s>vīrya</s> of that kind — like stones — even the most beautiful form of a young woman, even a warbling melodious song issuing from the face of a woman with full hips, does not culminate in complete bliss. And to the degree that the nourishing does not occur, to that degree the result is limited <s>camatkāra</s> (aesthetic rapture). For where there is no <s>camatkāra</s> at all, there is nothing but insentience. The heightened immersion in <s>camatkāra</s>, which has the nature of the agitation of <s>vīrya</s>, is called <s>sahṛdayatā</s> (aesthetic sensitivity, lit. "having a heart"). Only for one whose heart has been nourished by the infinite nourishing <s>vīrya</s> established through the practice of immersion in this enjoyment — for that one alone there is surpassing aesthetic rapture (<s>camatkriyā</s>). Even in suffering, this very same <s>camatkāra</s> operates. For that which is inwardly established — the <s>vīrya</s> that is the beloved, the son, happiness, and so on — that very thing, through the agitation that is the awakening by lamentation, weeping, and the like, which are similar to contemplation, having attained expansion and then the realization that it will not come again — through the dispassion born of that,
its nature is the distinctive <s>camatkāra</s> that constitutes the reality of suffering. As stated:

body.text: Q: dukhe 'pi pravikāsena
body.translated_text: Q: Even in suffering, through expansion,

body.text:
iti / yadā sakalendriyanāḍībhūtamarudādiparipūraṇe tu mahāmadhyamasauṣumnapadānupraveśe nijaśaktikṣobhatādātmyaṃ pratipadyate tadā sarvato dvaitagalane paripūrṇasvaśaktibharavimarśāhantāmayacamatkārānupraveśe paripūrṇasṛṣṭyānandarūparudrayāmalayogānupraveśena tanmahāmantravīryavisargaviśleṣaṇātmanā dhruvapadātmakanistaraṅgākulabhairavabhāvābhivyaktiḥ / tathā hi tanmadhyanāḍīrūpasyobhayaliṅgātmano 'pi tadvīryotsāhabalalabdhāvaṣṭambhasya kampakāle sakalavīryakṣobhojjigamiṣātmakam antaḥsparśasukhaṃ svasaṃvitsākṣikam eva / na caitat kalpitaśarīraniṣṭhatayaiva kevalam / tadabhijñānopadeśadvāreṇeyati mahāmantravisargaviśleṣaṇāvāptadhruvapade parabrahmamayaśivaśaktisaṃghaṭṭānandasvātantryasṛṣṭiparābhaṭṭārikārūpe
'nupraveśaḥ / tad vakṣyate
body.translated_text:
iti / But when, through the filling of all the channels (<s>nāḍīs</s>), which are the seats of all the sense organs, with the vital breath (<s>marut</s>) and the rest, one enters the great central <s>suṣumnā</s> path and attains identity with the agitation of one's own <s>śakti</s> — then, with the complete dissolution of all duality, through entering into the <s>camatkāra</s> of the "I"-awareness (<s>ahantā</s>) that is the reflective awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>) of the fullness of one's own <s>śakti</s>, through entering into the bliss of creation that is the complete <s>Rudrayāmala</s>-yoga (the union of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s>), by means of the outpouring of the great <s>mantra</s>-potency (<s>vīrya</s>) of that <s>visarga</s>, there is the manifestation of the waveless, undisturbed <s>Bhairava</s>-state that is the eternal ground (<s>dhruva-pada</s>).
