For indeed, at the time of trembling, when that which has the form of the central channel (<s>madhya-nāḍī</s>), though possessing the nature of both <s>liṅgas</s> (marks), has gained its support through the power and force of that <s>vīrya</s> — the inner tactile bliss, whose nature is the total agitation of all <s>vīrya</s> seeking to surge forth, is witnessed by one's own consciousness (<s>saṃvit</s>) alone. And this is not merely confined to the imagined body. Through the gateway of instruction regarding the recognition of that, one enters into the eternal ground (<s>dhruva-pada</s>) obtained through the outpouring of the great <s>mantra</s>-<s>visarga</s> — into the form of the supreme Goddess <s>Parābhaṭṭārikā</s>,
which is the bliss of the union (<s>saṃghaṭṭa</s>) of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s> pervaded by the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the sovereign freedom of creation. That will be stated:

body.text: Q: tatra sṛṣṭiṃ yajed
body.translated_text: Q: There one should worship creation,

body.text: ityādi / tathā
body.translated_text: ityādi / Likewise:

body.text: Q: yathā nyagrodhabījasthaḥ
body.translated_text: Q: Just as within the seed of the banyan tree,

body.text: ityādi / tathā
body.translated_text: ityādi / Likewise:

body.text: Q: ity etad rudrayāmalam
body.translated_text: Q: This is the <s>Rudrayāmala</s> (the union of <s>Rudra</s> and his <s>Śakti</s>),

body.text: ityādi / anyatrāpy uktam
body.translated_text: ityādi / Elsewhere too it is stated:

body.text:
Q: lehanāmanthanākoṭaiḥ strīsukhasya bharāt smṛteḥ /
Q: śaktyabhāve 'pi deveśi bhaved ānandasaṃplavaḥ //
body.translated_text:
Q: Through the intensity of the memory of the bliss of woman, through the strokes of licking and churning,
Q: Even in the absence of <s>Śakti</s> (the female partner), O Goddess of gods, there arises a flood of bliss.

body.text: iti / bharāt smaryamāṇo hi sa sparśas tatsparśakṣetre ca madhyamākṛtrimaparātmakaśaktinālikāpratibimbitas tanmukhyaśāktasparśābhāve 'pi tadantarvṛttiśāktasparśātmakavīryakṣobhakārī bhavatīty abhiprāyeṇa / tathā
body.translated_text: iti / For when that touch is remembered with intensity, even in the field of that touch — reflected in the channel (<s>nālikā</s>) of the <s>Śakti</s> that is the uncontrived supreme Self-nature of the <s>madhyamā</s> (central channel) — even in the absence of the primary physical <s>śākta</s> touch, it produces the agitation of <s>vīrya</s> whose nature is the inner <s>śākta</s> touch operating within: this is the intended meaning. Likewise:

body.text:
Q: śaktisaṃgamasaṃkṣobhaśaktyāveśāvasānakam /
Q: yat sukhaṃ brahmatattvasya tat sukhaṃ svākyam ucyate //
body.translated_text:
Q: The bliss that arises from the agitation born of the union with <s>Śakti</s>, culminating in the immersion in <s>Śakti</s> —
Q: That bliss of the <s>Brahman</s>-principle is said to be one's very own bliss.

body.text: iti /
body.translated_text: iti /

body.text: Q: ... snehāt kaulikam ādiśet /
body.translated_text: Q: ... out of affection, one should teach the <s>kaulika</s> (pertaining to <s>kula</s>).

body.text: iti ca / mahāvīreṇa bhagavatā vyāsenāpi
body.translated_text: iti / And by the great hero, the Lord <s>Vyāsa</s> as well:

body.text:
Q: mama yonir mahad brahma tasmin garbhaṃ dadhāmy aham /
Q: saṃbhavaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ tato bhavati bhārata //
body.translated_text:
Q: My womb is the great <s>Brahman</s>; in that I place the seed.
Q: The birth of all beings comes from that, O <s>Bhārata</s>.

body.text: ity {api} gītam / somānandapādair api nijavivṛtau
body.translated_text: — this too was sung {also}. And by <s>Somānanda</s> as well, in his own commentary (<s>vivṛti</s>),

body.text: Q: bhagavatyā ratasthāyā praśna iti paraikamayatve 'pi tanmayamahadantarālābhiprāyeṇa/
body.translated_text: Quote: 'The question by the Goddess while in the state of union' — even in the state of complete identity with the other, with the intent of the great interval of being absorbed in that —

body.text: iti / tad alam amunā trikaśāstrarahasyopadeśakathātiprastāvena / tad idam anuttaraṃ kaulikasiddhidaṃ yena jñātamātreṇa khecarīsāmyam uktanayena
body.translated_text: Thus. Enough of this extended discourse expounding the secrets of the <s>Trika</s> scriptures. Now this supreme [teaching], bestowing <s>kaulika</s> (pertaining to <s>kula</s>) accomplishment, by the mere knowledge of which equality with <s>Khecarī</s> is attained in the manner stated:

body.text: ParTri 2ab:

children.translated_text: "This secret, the great secret,
tell me, O Lord!"

body.text: guhyam aprakaṭatvāt / yato guhāyāṃ svarūpāparijñānamayyāṃ satyāṃ sthitam apy aprakaṭam / atha ca mahad aguhyaṃ sarvasya evaṃvidhacamatkāramayatvāt / mātṛmānameyamayabhedāvibhāgaśālinī bhagavatī śuddhavidyaiva trikoṇā māyāyām atiśayapratiphalitabhedāvagrahā bhavatīti māyāpi jagajjananabhūr vidyaiva vastutaḥ / tad uktena nayena saivaṃbhūtatvena parijñāyamānatvād abhedamāhātmyatirohitatatpramātrādikoṇatrayatvān mahāguhety ucyate / saiva ca vastutaḥ pūjādhāma triśūlaṃ trikārthe / tad uktam
body.translated_text: Secret, because it is unmanifest; since even though it abides in the cave of non-recognition of one's own nature, it remains unmanifest. And yet it is the great non-secret, because everything is of the nature of such wonder. The blessed <s>Śuddhavidyā</s> (Pure Knowledge) itself, which is the triangle, endowed with the non-differentiation of knower, knowledge, and known, when its exceedingly reflected apprehension of difference appears in <s>Māyā</s>, even <s>Māyā</s>, the ground of the universe's birth, is in reality <s>Vidyā</s> itself. Therefore, since it is recognized in the stated manner as being of such a nature, because the triad of corners — the knower and the rest — is concealed by the greatness of non-difference, it is called 'the great secret.' And that very thing is in reality the abode of worship, the trident, in the sense of <s>Trika</s>. As it is said:

body.text:
Q: sa trikoṇā mahāvidyā trikā sarvarasāspadam /
Q: visargapadam evaiṣa tasmāt saṃpūjayet trikam /
body.translated_text:
Quote: 'She is the triangle, the great <s>vidyā</s>, the <s>Trikā</s>, the abode of all essences;
she is the state of emission itself; therefore one should worship the <s>Trika</s>.'

body.text: iti / tathā
body.translated_text: And likewise:

body.text: Q: udety ekaḥ samālokaḥ pramāṇārthapramātṛgaḥ /

children.translated_text: (<s>Kramastotra</s> of <s>Erakanātha</s>)

body.translated_text: Quote: 'There arises one radiance, consisting of the means of knowledge, the object, and the knower.'

body.text: iti / tataś ca īdṛśyāṃ mahāguhāyāṃ śuddhavidyāhṛdayamayyāṃ mahāsṛṣṭirūpāyāṃ jagajjanmabhūmau svacamatkārarūpeṇa bhavati yan maha iti yad etad guhyam / etena hi yad idam avicchinnabhairavabhāsāvimarśarūpaṃ svātantryaṃ bhāvebhyaḥ svarūpapratyupasaṃhārakrameṇa ātmavimarśaviśrāntirūpatvam / prakāśasya hi svābhāvikākṛtrimaparavāṅmantravīryacamatkārātma aham iti / yathoktam
body.translated_text: And therefore, in such a great cave, consisting of the heart of <s>Śuddhavidyā</s>, being of the nature of the great creation, in the ground of the universe's birth, that which exists in the form of one's own wonder — that is what is called 'the great' in 'this secret.' For this autonomy, which is of the nature of the unbroken <s>Bhairava</s>-manifestation and reflective awareness, through the process of withdrawing from objects into one's own essential nature, becomes of the nature of resting in Self-awareness. For the inherent, unartificial wonder of <s>Parā Vāk</s> (Supreme Speech) and <s>mantra</s>-power of <s>Prakāśa</s> (luminosity) is 'I.' As stated:

body.text: Q: prakāśasyātmaviśrāntir ahaṃbhāvo hi kīrtitaḥ /
body.translated_text: Quote: 'The Self-repose of <s>Prakāśa</s> (luminosity) is declared to be the 'I'-consciousness.'

body.text:
iti / tad eva guhyam atirahasyam / tathā hi sṛṣṭikrameṇa yathāvikṛtānuttaradhruvarūpaviśrānto bhairavabhaṭṭārakaḥ sakalakalājālajīvanabhūtaḥ sarvasyādisiddho 'kalātmakaḥ sa eva prasarātmanā rūpeṇa visargarūpatām aśnuvāno visargasyaiva kuṇḍalinyātmakahaśaktimayatvāt punar api tacchāktaprasarābhedavedakarūpabindvātmanā nararūpeṇa prasarati / tathā punar api tanmūlatriśūlaprāṇaparaśaktitrayopasaṃhāre tadvisargaviśleṣaṇayā mūladhruvapadānuttarapraveśaḥ sarvadā / sphuṭayiṣyate caitad avidūra eva / mahe paramānandarūpe pūrvokte yad idam uktanayena a iti rūpaṃ tad eva guhyam / etad eva ca mahāguhyaṃ jagajjananadhāma / tathobhayasamāpattyānandenāguhyaṃ sarvacamatkāramayam / sva ātman eva he prabho evaṃvidhavaicitryakāritayā prabhavanaśīla / āmantraṇam
etat / tac cāmantryasyāmantrakaṃ prati tādātmyam ābhimukhyaṃ prātipadikārthād adhikārthadāyi / yathoktam /
body.translated_text:
That very thing is the secret, the supreme mystery. For thus, in the order of creation, <s>Bhairava</s> the Lord, resting in the unwavering form of the unchanging supreme (<s>anuttara</s>), being the life of the entire network of <s>kalās</s>, primordially established, of the nature beyond <s>kalā</s> — He himself, in the form of emanation, attaining the nature of <s>visarga</s> (emission), and because <s>visarga</s> itself is of the nature of the <s>ha</s>-power which is <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s>, again through the <s>bindu</s>-nature, which is of the form of cognizing the non-difference of that <s>Śākta</s> emanation, He proceeds in human form. And again, in the withdrawal of the trident-root <s>prāṇa</s> and the triad of supreme powers, through the separation of that emission, there is entry into the original unwavering supreme (<s>anuttara</s>) state always. And this will be elucidated very shortly. In 'the great' — of the nature of supreme bliss as stated before — that which in the stated manner has the form 'a' — that very thing is secret. And that very thing is the great secret, the abode of the universe's birth. And through the bliss of the union of both, it is the non-secret, consisting entirely of wonder. In one's own Self, O Lord — one whose nature is to be the origin of such variety — this is a vocative address.
And the vocative, expressing the identity and directness of the addressed toward the addresser, gives more meaning than the stem-meaning. As stated:

body.text: Q: saṃbodhanādhikaḥ prātipadikārtha /
body.translated_text: Quote: 'The vocative adds more than the stem-meaning.'

body.text: iti / nirṇītaṃ caitan mayaiva śrīpūrvapañcikāyām / etat kathaya parāvāgrūpatayāvibhaktaṃ sthitam api paśyantībhuvi vākyaprabandhakramāsūtraṇena yojaya / yathoktaṃ prāk
body.translated_text: And this has been determined by me in the <s>Śrīpūrvapañcikā</s>. 'Tell this' — though it abides undivided in the form of <s>Parā Vāk</s> (Supreme Speech), at the level of <s>Paśyantī</s> (the 'seeing' level of speech), connect it through the sequential arrangement of sentences. As stated before:

body.text: Q: guruśiṣyapade sthitvā ...
body.translated_text: Quote: 'Having established in the positions of teacher and disciple...'

body.text: ityādi / parābhaṭṭārikāyāś ca paśyantyāditādātmyaṃ nirṇītaṃ prāg eva /
body.translated_text: And so on. And the identity of <s>Parā Bhaṭṭārikā</s> (the Supreme Goddess) with <s>Paśyantī</s> and the rest has been determined previously.

body.text: tathā mama ity asya pratyagātmasaṃbandhitvasya idaṃbhāvasya yad guhyaṃ maha ity uktam aham iti / tathā hi mamedaṃ bhāsata iti yad bhāsanaṃ tasya vimarśaḥ punar apy ahaṃbhāvaikasāraḥ / sa punar ahaṃbhāvo bhāvapratyupasaṃharaṇamukheneti maha ity etadrūpa eva yathoktaṃ prāk / yad uktam
body.translated_text: Likewise, 'my' — of the relatedness to the inner Self, of the 'this'-nature — what is secret in 'the great' has been stated as 'I.' For indeed, the reflective awareness of the manifestation 'this appears as mine' is again of the sole essence of the 'I'-consciousness. And that 'I'-consciousness is through the process of withdrawing objects — thus it is of the form of 'the great' as stated before. As said:

body.text:
Q: idam ity asya vicchinnavimarśasya kṛtārthatā /
Q: yā svasvarūpe viśrāntir vimarśaḥ so 'ham ity ayam //
body.translated_text:
Quote: 'The fulfillment of this severed reflective awareness called "this"
is the repose in one's own nature — that reflective awareness is this "I".'

body.text: iti / anyatrāpi
body.translated_text: And elsewhere:

body.text:
Q: ghaṭo 'yam ity adhyavasā nāmarūpātirekiṇī /
Q: pareśaśaktir ātmeva bhāsate na tv idantayā //
body.translated_text:
Quote: '"This is a pot" — the determination that transcends name and form
is the power of the Supreme Lord, appearing as if the Self, not as "this"-ness.'

body.text: iti / tad uktaṃ śrīsomānandapādair nijavivṛtau /
body.translated_text: This has been stated by <s>Śrī Somānandapāda</s> in his own commentary:

body.text: Q: abījaṃ śuddhaśivarūpam
body.translated_text: Quote: 'The seedless, of the nature of pure <s>Śiva</s>...'

body.text:
ityādi / tad evāsmābhir vipañcitam iti / tathā svamama suṣṭhv avidyamānaṃ mama iti yasya / ahantābharaikarūḍhatvāt viśvaṃ na kiṃcid yasya vyatiriktanirdeśaprāṇaṣaṣṭyarthayogi bhavati / śāstrāntaradīkṣitānāṃ vijñānākalānāṃ pralayakevalināṃ ca yady api mameti vyatiriktaṃ nāsti tathāpi yad bhedayogyatāvāsanā syād eva prabodhasamaye tadvikāsāt ahaṃbhāvārūḍhiḥ / tadapākṛtyai suṣṭhuśabdārthe suḥ / yad uktaṃ mayaiva stotre
Q: yan na kiṃcana mameti dīnatāṃ prāpnuvanti jaḍajantavo 'niśam /
Q: tan na kiṃcana mamāsmi sarvam ity uddhurāṃ dhuram upeyivān aham //

iti / śobhanena dvaitakalaṅkāṅkanākāluṣyaleṣaśūnyenāmena paramārthopadeśadvayātmanā jñānena mā mānam avabodho yasya svaprakāśaikarūpatvāt / amatīti amā, a iti mā yatra, avidyamānaṃ mā mānaṃ niṣedhaś ca yatra, nityoditatvāt saṃhāraś ca yatra nāsti, sā bhagavatī amā iti ucyate / amā śobhanā satatoditā yatra māyāyāṃ pramāṇaprameyavyavahṛtau sā tādṛśī mā yasyeti bahuvrīhyantaṃ bahuvrīhiḥ /
body.translated_text: By the auspicious name, free from the slightest taint of the stain of duality — by knowledge that is of the nature of the twofold supreme teaching — 'mā' means understanding whose measure (<s>māna</s>) is self-luminous in nature. 'Amā' — where 'a' means 'mā' (measure/understanding), where measure is absent, where negation is absent, and where, because of being eternally risen, destruction too is absent — she, the blessed one, is called <s>Amā</s>. <s>Amā</s>, the auspicious, perpetually risen — where in <s>Māyā</s>, in the activity of means of knowledge and knowable, she is such a 'mā' — this is a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound ending in a <s>bahuvrīhi</s>.

body.text: parameśvaro hi pramāṇādivyavahāre 'pi paraśaktimaya eva sarvathādvaitarūpatvāt tasya / āmantraṇam ātmana eva /
body.translated_text: <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord), even in the activity of means of knowledge and the rest, is of the nature of the Supreme Power alone, because He is in all ways of non-dual nature. The vocative is of the Self itself.

body.text: idam eva sārdhaślokanirūpitānantapraśnatātparyam / saṃgraheṇaitad uktaṃ bhavatīti nirṇetuṃ nirūpyate /
body.translated_text: This alone is the purport of the boundless question formulated in the one and a half verses. To determine that this is said in summary, it is now being examined:

body.text: ParTri 2cd-3ab:

children.translated_text: "The power that abides in the heart,
the <s>Kaulinī</s>, the mistress of <s>Kula</s>,"
"Tell me of her, O Lord of gods,
by which I may obtain satisfaction."

body.text: sarvasya nīlasukhāder dehaprāṇabuddhyādeś ca paraṃ pratiṣṭhāsthānaṃ saṃvidātma hṛt / tasyaiva nijasvātantryakalpitabhedā ayā vicitrāni ghaṭādijñānāni / tatsthā iyaṃ sphuraṇamayī śaktiḥ kulasya nāyikā śarīraprāṇasukhādeḥ sphurattādāyinī brāhmyādevatācakrasya vīryabhūtā nikhilākṣanāḍicakrasya madhyamadhyamarupā jananasthānakarṇikā liṅgātmā asti / tatraiva ca kule bhavā kularūpā kaulikī / yad vā kule bhavam akulātma kaulam / tad yasyām antas tādātmyenāsti sā kaulikī / kulaṃ hy akulaprakāśarūḍham eva tathā bhavati / yad uktam
body.translated_text: The heart (<s>hṛt</s>), whose nature is consciousness, is the supreme ground of establishment for everything — blue, pleasure, and so on — and for the body, vital breath, intellect, and so on. Its cognitions of various objects such as pots are the differences fashioned by its own autonomy. This power, consisting of vibrant manifestation, abiding therein, is the mistress of <s>kula</s> — the bestower of the nature of vibrant manifestation to the body, vital breath, pleasure, and so on — the essential power of the circle of deities beginning with <s>Brāhmī</s>, the central core of the entire network of sense-channels, the womb-ground of generation, of the nature of the <s>liṅga</s>. And being born in <s>kula</s>, she is of the nature of <s>kula</s>, hence <s>kaulikī</s>. Or: that which is born in <s>kula</s>, being of the <s>akula</s> nature, is <s>kaula</s>; that which is within her in identity is <s>kaulikī</s>. For <s>kula</s> ascends to the <s>akula</s>-light and thus becomes so. As stated:

body.text: Q: api tv ātmabalasparśāt /
body.translated_text: Quote: 'But by the touch of the Self's own power...'

body.text: iti / tathā
body.translated_text: And likewise:

body.text:
Q: tad ākramya balaṃ mantrāḥ sarvajñabalaśālinaḥ /
Q: pravartante 'dhikārāya karaṇānīva dehinām //
body.translated_text:
Quote: 'Having resorted to that power, the <s>mantras</s>, endowed with the strength of omniscience,
proceed to their function, like the senses for embodied beings.'

body.text: iti / devānāṃ brahmaviṣṇurudrādīnām īśasyāmantraṇaṃ / tan me kathaya ity api paṭhanti śrīsomānandapādā vyācakṣate ca tat tasmād iti / yad vā tat kathaya yena tṛptiṃ paramānandamayīṃ labhe paramādvayanirvṛtisvātantryarasībhavāmīti samanvayaḥ / vrajāmi ity api pāṭhaḥ / aham ity anena sarvapramātṛjīvanarūpam eva satataṃ parāmṛśyate / tac caivam abhihitasvarūpopadeśena pratyabhijñāya nijam īśvararūpaṃ paripūrṇabhāvātmikāṃ tṛptiṃ vindatīti prāk prakaṭitam eva /
body.translated_text: Of the gods — <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, and the rest — this is the vocative of the Lord. <s>Śrī Somānandapāda</s> also reads 'tan me kathaya' ('tell me that') and explains 'tat' as 'therefore.' Or: 'tell that, by which I may obtain satisfaction' — full of supreme bliss, I may become one with the flavor of freedom in supreme non-dual repose — this is the syntactic connection. 'Vrajāmi' ('I attain') is also a reading. By 'I' (<s>aham</s>), what is constantly reflected upon is the very nature of the life of all knowers. And that very thing, by recognizing one's own <s>Īśvara</s>-nature through the instruction of the essential nature thus described, one obtains satisfaction of the nature of complete fullness — this has been made clear before.

body.text: tad uktaṃ somānandapādaiḥ svavivṛtau
body.translated_text: This has been stated by <s>Somānandapāda</s> in his own commentary:

body.text: Q: hṛdy ayo gamanaṃ jñānam
body.translated_text: Quote: 'Knowledge is the going to the heart...'

body.text: ityādi /
body.translated_text: And so on.

body.text:
iti śivarasaṃ pātuṃ yeṣāṃ pipāsati mānasaṃ satatam aśivadhvaṃse sattāṃ śivena niveśitām /
hṛdayagaganagranthiṃ teṣāṃ vidārāyituṃ haṭhād abhinava imāṃ praśnavyākhyāṃ vyadhāt trikatattvagām //
body.translated_text:
Thus, for those whose minds perpetually thirst to drink the essence of <s>Śiva</s>, who have been established in existence by <s>Śiva</s> for the destruction of the un-<s>Śiva</s>,
<s>Abhinava</s> has forcefully composed this exposition of the question to tear open the knot in the sky of their hearts, reaching the reality of <s>Trika</s>.

body.text: tad atra praśnasarvasve
body.translated_text: Now, regarding the totality of this question:

body.text: ParTri :

vyākhyātaṃ prāg evaitat / kiṃ punaruktatāpādanena / bhairavo bharaṇātmako mahāmantraravātmakaś ca / kevalam atra śaktimatprādhānyaṃ saṃhārarūpeṇa maha ity evaṃrūpam ity uktaṃ prāk sphuṭībhaviṣyati cāgrata eva / tad iyān atra tātparyārthaḥ /
body.translated_text: This has been explained previously. What is the point of repetition? <s>Bhairava</s> is of the nature of 'bearing' (<s>bharaṇa</s>) and of the essence of the great <s>mantra</s>-sound. Only here the emphasis is on the possessor of power, in the form of withdrawal, as 'the great' — this form has been stated before and will become clear just ahead. Such then is the purport here:

body.text:
parā bhagavatī saṃvit prasarantī svarūpataḥ /
parecchāśaktir ity uktā bhairavasyāvibhedinī //
body.translated_text:
"<s>Parā</s> (the Supreme), the blessed consciousness,
emanating from her own nature,
is called the Supreme Will-power of <s>Bhairava</s>, non-different from Him."

body.text:
tasyāḥ prasaradharmatvāj jñānaśaktyādirūpatā /
parāparāparārūpapaśyantyādivapurbhṛtiḥ //
body.translated_text:
"Because she has the nature of emanation,
she takes the form of the power of knowledge and so on;
bearing the forms of <s>Parā</s>, <s>Parāparā</s>, and <s>Aparā</s>,
<s>Paśyantī</s> and the rest."

body.text:
tad eva prasarākārasvarūpaparimarśanam /
praśna ity ucyate devī tanmayapraśnakāriṇī //
body.translated_text:
"That very reflective awareness of the essential nature
of the form of emanation
is called 'the question' — the Goddess
is the questioner, being of the nature of that."

body.text:
tasya prasararūpasyā parāmarśanam eva yat /
tad eva paramaṃ proktaṃ tatpraśnottararūpakam //
body.translated_text:
"That very reflective awareness
of that which has the form of emanation —
that alone is declared to be supreme,
having the form of both question and answer."

body.text:
tad evāparasaṃvitter ārabhyāntastarāṃ punaḥ /
parasaṃvidghanānandasaṃhārakaraṇaṃ muhuḥ //
body.translated_text:
"That very thing, beginning from the lower consciousness,
again toward the innermost,
repeatedly effecting the withdrawal
into the dense bliss of supreme consciousness,"

body.text:
antarbhāvitaniḥśeṣaprasaraṃ bhairavaṃ vapuḥ /
prativaktṛsvarūpeṇa sarvadaiva vijṛmbhate //
body.translated_text:
"having internalized the entirety of emanation — the <s>Bhairava</s> form —
always expands
in the nature of the respondent."

body.text:
etau prasarasaṃhārāv akālakalitau yataḥ /
tad ekarūpam evedaṃ tattvaṃ praśnottarātmakam //
body.translated_text:
"Since these two — emanation and withdrawal —
are not divided by time,
this reality, having the form of both question and answer,
is of one single nature."

body.text:
tad evaṃ parasaṃbandham anuttaratayānvitam /
ṣaḍardhasārasarvasvaṃ guravaḥ prāṅ nyarūpayan //
body.translated_text:
"Thus, this supreme connection, endowed with the <s>anuttara</s> (supreme),
the totality and essence of the six half-[verses] —
the teachers have previously elucidated."

body.text: ParTri 3cd-4cd:

children.translated_text: "Listen, O Goddess, O greatly fortunate one,"
"to that which is the supreme beyond even the answer,"
"that which is this <s>Kaulika</s> teaching,"
"established in the sky of my heart."
"I shall tell it — there is no doubt —"
"it immediately bestows <s>Kaulika</s> accomplishment."

body.text: devi iti prāgvat / mahān bhāgo yasyā yā bhajyamānā uktavakṣyamāṇopadeśānuśīlanena sevyamānā pārameśvaryākhyamahābaladā bhavatīti / mahat paramamahadrūpatayā prasiddho 'nāśritaśivarūpaḥ sa yasyā bhāga aṃśaḥ / pārameśvarī hi śaktiḥ anantaṣaṭtriṃśadāditattvagarbhiṇī / mahān buddhyādis tattvaviśeṣo bhāgo vibhāgaḥ kalāpekṣi rūpaṃ yasyāḥ / pārameśvarī hi saṃvidekaghanaśaktiḥ svasvātantryopakalpitabhinnajñeyakāryapratiṣṭhāpadatve buddhir ity ucyate / yad uktaṃ śrīsomānandapādaiḥ
body.translated_text: 'Goddess' — as before. 'Of great fortune' (<s>mahābhāga</s>) — she whose portion is great, who being resorted to, being served through the practice of the teachings stated and to be stated, becomes the bestower of the great power called supreme lordship. Or: great, renowned as being of the supreme, great form, the uneclipsed <s>Śiva</s>-nature — that is her portion. For the Supreme Power (<s>Pārameśvarī Śakti</s>) is pregnant with the infinity of thirty-six and other <s>tattvas</s>. Or: the great specific <s>tattva</s> beginning with <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) is a portion, a division, a form dependent on <s>kalā</s>. For the Supreme Consciousness-power (<s>Pārameśvarī Saṃvid Śakti</s>), being of one dense consciousness, when established in the ground of differentiated knowable effects by her own freedom, is called 'intellect' (<s>buddhi</s>). As stated by <s>Śrī Somānandapāda</s>:

body.text: Q: ... aparasthitau //
body.translated_text: Quote: '...in the state of the other.'

body.text:
Q: sā buddhir yat punaḥ sūkṣmaṃ sarvadikkam avasthitam /
Q: jñānaṃ bodhamayaṃ tasya śivasya sahajaṃ sadā //
body.translated_text:
Quote: 'That <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) — the subtle knowledge that pervades all directions,
the knowledge consisting of awareness, is always innate to that <s>Śiva</s>.'

body.text: iti / bhāgo bhedaḥ sa yatrāstīti matvarthīyākārapratyayāntena bhāgaśabdena vibhaktaṃ rūpam ucyate / vibhakte ca vapuṣi paricchedo 'nyonyavyavacchedenaiva bhavatīti prasādātmakaviṣayaniścayo buddhāv upajāyamāno 'pararamyāramyādiviśvavartino bhāvān aspṛśann eva pratyuta tān vyavacchindan upajāyata iti / sukhavṛttibuddher dharmaiśvaryādirūpatvāt sattvātmako guṇaniḥṣyanda iti gīyate / yadi tu tatrāpi antastamām anupraviśyate tat taddvāreṇaiva tanmūlavartini paramānandadhāmni bhaved eva satatam udayaḥ / ata eva mahasya sarvato 'khaṇḍitaparipūrṇanirargalanirapekṣasvātantryajagadānandamayasya ā īṣad bhāgāḥ sukhalakṣaṇā aṃśāḥ / yato yat yat kila sukhaṃ tanmahānandanirvṛtiparamadhāmni visargaśaktāv anupraveśāt tathā 'cetyamānatayā kiyadrūpatāṃ prāptam /
body.translated_text: The word 'bhāga' with the suffix expressing 'possessing that' denotes a differentiated form. And in a differentiated body, delimitation occurs through mutual exclusion alone. Thus the ascertainment of an object of the nature of clarity, arising in the intellect, not touching the objects existing in the other-beautiful-and-ugly universe, but rather cutting them off, arises. Because the intellect functioning in a pleasant mode is of the nature of <s>dharma</s>, lordship, and so on, the effluence of the <s>sattva guṇa</s> is celebrated. But if one penetrates inward even there, through that very gateway, in the supreme abode of bliss rooted therein, there would indeed be perpetual arising. Therefore, of 'the great' — which is in every way unbroken, perfectly full, unrestricted, independent, and consisting of universal bliss — the portions, characterized by happiness, are 'ā' (slightly). For whatever happiness there may be, because of entry into the <s>visarga</s>-power, the supreme abode of the great bliss-repose, it has attained a limited form due to being not fully perceived.

body.text: tad uktaṃ bhaṭṭanārāyaṇena
body.translated_text: This has been stated by <s>Bhaṭṭa Nārāyaṇa</s>:

body.text:
Q: trailokye 'py atra yo yāvān ānandaḥ kaścid īkṣyate /
Q: sa bindur yasya taṃ vande devam ānandasāgaram //
body.translated_text:
Quote: 'Whatever bliss is seen anywhere in the three worlds,
that is but a drop of His — I bow to that God, the ocean of bliss.'

body.text:
iti prāṅnayena yad uktaṃ maha iti rūpaṃ tad eva bhajanīyaṃ yasyāḥ / parameśvarasya hi svacamatkārabṛṃhitaṃ yad aham iti tad eva śāktaṃ vapuḥ, tad eva ca parābhaṭṭārikārūpam ity ucyate / ata eva saiva ca parameśvarī sarvaṃ śṛṇoti / śravaṇākhyayā sattayā tiṣṭhantī śravaṇasaṃpuṭasphuṭakramikasvaspandamayavarṇarāśiniṣṭham aikātmyāpād anarūpasaṃkalanānusaṃdhānākhyaṃ svātantryam / tena hi vinā kalakalalīnaśabdaviśeṣaṃ śṛṇvann api na śṛṇomīti vyavaharati pramātā / kalakalamātraviṣayam eva tu saṃkalanam iti tatraiva śrutam iti vyavahāraḥ / vastutas tu sa kalakaladhvaniḥ śrotrākāśa anupraviśan varṇān anupraveśayan tathā bhavet tadvarṇātiriktasya kalakalasyaivābhāvāt / tadvarṇaviśeṣavivakṣāyāṃ ca kalakalasya ca
kāraṇābhāvād evānutpattiḥ syāt, tadvivakṣotpannasphuṭavarṇamayaśabdakāryatve 'pi sajātīyaśabdotpattyupapatteḥ / sarvathā ta eva varṇās tena sphuṭarūpeṇa saṃkalanām agacchantaḥ kalakalaśabdavācyāḥ / tatsaṃkalanāvadhānodyuktasya bhaved eva kiyanmātrasphuṭopalambha iti saṃkalanam evātropayogi / saṃkalanaṃ ca bhagavatī saiva parā parameśvarī karoti / yad uktam
body.translated_text: Thus, by the method stated previously, the form expressed as 'maha' is indeed what is to be worshipped by her. For the self-delight-nourished 'I' (<s>aham</s>) of <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord) is itself the body of <s>Śakti</s>, and that very thing is said to be the form of <s>Parā Bhaṭṭārikā</s> (the Supreme Goddess). Therefore, it is she, the Supreme Goddess (<s>Parameśvarī</s>), who hears everything. Abiding in the state called hearing (<s>śravaṇa</s>), [she exercises] the sovereignty called sequential awareness-synthesis (<s>anusaṃdhāna</s>) — which consists of the unification of the mass of <s>varṇas</s> (phonemes) that manifest as sequential self-vibrations becoming distinct within the cavity of the ear, bringing them into a single identity with their non-separate form. For without that [synthesis], even while hearing a particular sound immersed in cacophony, the cognizing subject declares 'I do not hear.' When there is mere synthesis of the cacophony alone, then indeed the conventional usage 'I have heard' applies precisely there. But in reality, that cacophonous sound, entering the space of the ear and causing the <s>varṇas</s> (phonemes) to enter, would become such [i.e., articulate sound], since there is no cacophony apart from those very <s>varṇas</s>. And when there is no intention to express those particular <s>varṇas</s>, the cacophony would simply not arise due to the absence of its cause; even though it would have the nature of a sound-effect composed of distinct <s>varṇas</s> produced by the intention to express, this is because the production of homogeneous sounds is logically established. In all cases, those very <s>varṇas</s>, not attaining synthesis in their distinct form, are called cacophonous sound. For one who is attentive to their synthesis, there would indeed be some degree of distinct apprehension — thus synthesis alone is useful here. And it is the blessed <s>Parā Parameśvarī</s> (Supreme Goddess) herself who performs that synthesis. As has been said —

body.text: Q: tad ākramya balaṃ mantrāḥ
body.translated_text: Q: By resorting to that, the <s>mantras</s> [gain their] power —

body.text: ityādi / vastuto hi śṛṇoti paśyati vakti gṛhṇātītyādi bhagavatyā eva rūpam / yathoktam
body.translated_text: and so on. In reality, hearing, seeing, speaking, grasping, and so forth are the very form of the Blessed Goddess (<s>Bhagavatī</s>). As has been stated —

body.text:
Q: yena rūpaṃ rasaṃ gandhaṃ sparśaśabdau ca maithunam /
Q: etenaiva vijānāti kim atra pariśiṣyate //
body.translated_text: Q: By which one knows form, taste, smell, touch, sound, and sexual union — what remains beyond that? //

body.text: iti vedānte parameśvareṇa /
body.translated_text: Thus [it is said] by <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord) in the <s>Vedānta</s>.

body.text: na tu śravaṇaṃ nāma sphuṭakalakalātmakatāragadgadādirūpavarṇākarṇanam eva / tathā hi śrīparameśvara eva śrīsvacchandaśāstre japavibhāganirṇayāvasara evam eva nirūpitavān
body.translated_text: But hearing (<s>śravaṇa</s>) does not mean merely the perceiving of <s>varṇas</s> (phonemes) in the form of distinct or indistinct, loud or stammering sounds. For thus indeed <s>Śrī Parameśvara</s> (the Glorious Supreme Lord) himself, in the sacred <s>Svacchanda Śāstra</s>, in the context of determining the classification of <s>japa</s> (recitation), has explained in exactly this way —

body.text: Q: ātmanā śrūyate yas tu sa upāṃśur iti smṛtaḥ /
body.translated_text: Q: That which is heard by oneself alone is known as <s>upāṃśu</s> (whispered recitation).

body.text: atra hi madhyamāpade ātmaiva saṃśṛṇute nāpara ity uktam / sthānādiprayatnasphuṭatāyāṃ dantauṣṭhapuṭādisaṃyogavibhāgenātinibhṛtam api śabdoccāre nikaṭataravartiparaśravaṇam api syād iti saśabdatāpāttir eva /
body.translated_text: Here, in the stage of <s>madhyamā</s> (intermediate speech), it is said that the self alone hears, not another. When there is distinctness of articulatory effort involving place of articulation and so forth, even in extremely quiet utterance of sound, due to the conjunction and separation of teeth, lips, palate, and so forth, hearing by another person standing very close would also occur — thus the condition of being 'with sound' (<s>saśabda</s>) would inevitably arise.

body.text: Q: paraiḥ saṃśrūyate yas tu saśabdo'sau prakīrtitaḥ /
body.translated_text: Q: That which is heard by others is declared to be 'with sound' (<s>saśabda</s>).

body.text:
ity uktaṃ / yataḥ na cātra nikaṭādiviśeṣaḥ kaścid iti / parapramātṛdarśanamātragocarajihvoṣṭhapuṭādisaṃyoge tu yady apy ātmana eva śravaṇaṃ syān na parasya tathāpi madhyamāpadam evaitat saṃpadyate varṇasya bahirātmalābhābhāvāt / vāyvabhighātād dhi sphuṭavarṇaniṣpanna eva / na ca tatra vāyvabhighāto bāhyatāpattiparyantaḥ syāt / oṣṭhādicalanam api na tatra varṇāṃśe 'nupraviśed api tu svātmaniṣṭham eva tātkālikaṃ tat syāt / tātkālikeṅgitanimiṣitakaravyāpārādisthānīye sphuṭasthānakaraṇaprayatnayoge tu varṇaniṣpattāv api yadi nāma dhvanīnāṃ tāratamyena tāramandrādivibhāge dūrādūrādiśravaṇaṃ syāt, sarvathā paraiḥ śrūyata iti vaikharīpadam evaitad ity alaṃ prasaktānuprasaktyā / saiva parameśvarī āmantraṇayogena sphuṭaṃ
śaktirūpatayoktā / naraśaktiśivātmakaṃ hīdaṃ sarvaṃ trikarūpam eva / tatra yat kevalaṃ svātmany avasthitaṃ tat kevalaṃ jaḍarūpayogi mukhyatayā narātmakaṃ ghaṭas tiṣṭhatītivat / eṣa eva prathamapuruṣaviṣayaḥ śeṣaḥ / yat punar idam ity api bhāsamānaṃ yadāmantryamāṇatayā āmantrakāhaṃbhāvasamacchāditatadbhinnedaṃbhāvaṃ yuṣmacchabdavyapadeśyaṃ tac chāktaṃ rūpaṃ tvaṃ tiṣṭhasīti / atra hy eṣa eva yuṣmacchabdārtho āmantraṇatattvaṃ ca /
body.translated_text: Thus it is said. Because here there is no distinction of proximity and so on. But when there is conjunction of tongue, lips, palate, and so forth that falls only within the visual perception of another cognizing subject, even though hearing would belong to oneself alone and not to another, still this amounts only to the stage of <s>madhyamā</s>, since the <s>varṇa</s> (phoneme) has not attained external existence. For only through the impact of breath (<s>vāyu</s>) is a distinct <s>varṇa</s> actually produced. And in that case, the impact of breath does not reach the point of externality. Even the movement of lips and so forth would not enter into the phonemic aspect there, but would remain established in one's own self at that very moment. That momentary [movement] would be analogous to contemporary gestures, winks, hand movements, and so on. But when there is a conjunction of distinct place of articulation, organ, and effort — even though <s>varṇas</s> are produced — if, due to the gradation of sounds, there is hearing from far or near according to the high-low pitch division and so on, in all cases this is heard by others, and thus this is the stage of <s>vaikharī</s> (corporeal speech) alone — but enough of this pursuit of tangential topics. That very <s>Parameśvarī</s> (Supreme Goddess), through the act of invocation (<s>āmantraṇa</s>), is explicitly declared to be of the nature of <s>Śakti</s>. For all this is of the nature of the <s>Trika</s> — consisting of <s>nara</s> (individual), <s>śakti</s> (power), and <s>śiva</s> (absolute). Therein, that which abides solely in its own self, being associated merely with inert form, is primarily of the nature of <s>nara</s> — as in 'the pot stands,' and the like. This is the domain of the third person, the remainder. But that which, even while appearing as 'this,' when being addressed, has its separate 'this-ness' concealed by the I-consciousness of the one who addresses — that which is designated by the word 'you' (<s>yuṣmad</s>) — that is the form of <s>Śakti</s>, as in 'you stand.' Here indeed, this alone is the meaning of the word 'you' and the principle of address (<s>āmantraṇa</s>).

body.text: tathā hi yathāhaṃ tiṣṭhāmi tathaiva ayam apīti tasyāpy asmadrūpāvacchinnāhaṃbhāvacamatkārasvātantryam avicchinnāhaṃcamatkāreṇaivābhimanvāna āmantrayate yuṣmadarthena madhyamapuruṣeṇa vyapadiśati / seyaṃ hi bhagavatī parāparā / sarvathā punar avicchinnacamatkāranirapekṣasvātantryāhaṃvimarśe ahaṃ tiṣṭhāmīti parābhaṭṭārikodayo yatrottamatvaṃ puruṣasya / yad uktam
body.translated_text: Thus indeed: 'Just as I stand, so does this one also' — in this way, acknowledging that the other too possesses the sovereignty of I-consciousness delimited by our own nature, [the speaker,] through uninterrupted I-consciousness itself, addresses [the other] and designates [them] with the second person, which is the meaning of 'you' (<s>yuṣmad</s>). This indeed is the Blessed <s>Parāparā</s> (the Supreme-and-non-Supreme Goddess). But in every case, in the self-referential awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>) of 'I' — which is the sovereignty of uninterrupted delight independent [of anything else] — 'I stand' is the arising of <s>Parā Bhaṭṭārikā</s> (the Supreme Goddess), wherein lies the supreme nature (<s>uttamatva</s>) of the <s>Puruṣa</s> (Self). As has been said —

body.text:
Q: yasmāt kṣaram atīto 'ham akṣarād api cottamaḥ /
Q: ato 'smi loke vede ca prathitaḥ puruṣottamaḥ //
body.translated_text: Q: Since I transcend the perishable and am supreme even beyond the imperishable, therefore I am celebrated in the world and in the <s>Veda</s> as <s>Puruṣottama</s> (the Supreme Person). //

body.text:
iti / atra kṣarākṣararūpād ubhayato 'pi hy uttamatvam asmīty asmadarthenoktam / na hy atra sarvatra aham iti parimitaṃ śarīrady apadiśyate tasya pratyakṣeṇaiva tādrūpyavirodhāt / tad evam īdṛśaṃ svayaṃprathātmakaṃ śivātmakaṃ rūpam / ata eva bodhasyāsya svasaṃvitprathātmakasya kiṃcin nonaṃ nāpy adhikaṃ tasyāprakāśarūpasya cinmaye ananupraveśāt, tadapekṣayā ca mādhyasthyam api na kiṃcid ity upacayāpacayamadhyasthānīyedantānirdeśyabhāvalabdhapratiṣṭhāne na prabhavanti tadbodhāvicchedarūpā asmadarthāḥ / vicchedito 'pi yuṣmadartha evam eveti / ata eva aliṅge yuṣmadasmadī gīte / dehagatasaṃkhyādhyupacāreṇa parāparādiśaktigarbhīkārāt saṃkhyāyogas tūpapadyate / tathā hi svasvātantryopakalpitabhedāvabhāsy anantaśarīrādy ekatayaiva vimṛśed āvāṃ
yuvāṃ vayaṃ yūyam iti ca / upacayādyās tu dehagatā upacaritum api na śakyāḥ, cidrūpasyonādhikatānupapatteḥ / sarvaṃ hi sarvātmakam iti narātmāno jaḍā api tyaktatatpūrvarūpāḥ śāktaśaivarūpabhājo bhavanti, śṛṇuta grāvāṇaḥ

children.translated_text: , 'Among peaks, I am <s>Meru</s>' —

children.text: , ahaṃ caitro bravīmīty api pratīteḥ / śāktam api yuṣmadartharūpam api narātmakatāṃ bhajata eva śaktarūpam ujjhitvā tvaṃ gatabhayadhairyaśaktir ity anāmantraṇayogenāpi pratipatteḥ / bhavān ity anena pādā gurava ityādipratyayaviśeṣaiś cāparāvasthocitanarātmakaprathamapuruṣaviṣayatayāpi pratītisadbhāvāt /
children.translated_text: , and also because of the cognition 'I, <s>Caitra</s>, speak.' Even the form of <s>Śakti</s>, which is of the nature of the second-person meaning, assumes the nature of <s>nara</s> when it abandons the form of power — as in the apprehension 'you who have attained fearless fortitude-power' even without the mode of address. And because of the existence of cognition through expressions like 'your honor' (<s>bhavān</s>), through specific conventional usages like 'feet' [meaning 'your lordship'], 'venerable ones,' and the like — even in the domain of the third person appropriate to the lower state of <s>nara</s>.

body.translated_text: Here, supremacy over both — the perishable and the imperishable forms — is stated using the first person 'I am.' For here the limited body and so forth are not indicated everywhere by 'I,' since that would contradict what is directly perceived. Thus, such is the self-luminous form that is of the nature of <s>Śiva</s>. Therefore, of this consciousness (<s>bodha</s>), whose nature is the self-manifestation of one's own awareness (<s>svasaṃvit</s>), nothing is less and nothing is more — for that which has the nature of non-manifestation cannot enter into what is of the nature of consciousness (<s>cinmaya</s>); and with respect to that, there is not even any neutrality. Thus, in that which has gained its ground in a state where 'this-ness' — which is the locus of increase, decrease, and middle ground — cannot be indicated, the first-person meanings (<s>asmadartha</s>), which are of the nature of non-interruption of that consciousness, do not prevail. Even when there is interruption, the second-person meaning (<s>yuṣmadartha</s>) is just the same. Therefore [it is said in the grammar]: 'In the absence of gender, the second and first persons' are proclaimed. Through the conventional attribution of number based on the body, the application of number is justified because it incorporates the powers of <s>parā</s> (supreme), <s>aparā</s> (non-supreme), and so forth. For thus, [the Supreme Lord,] manifesting distinctions fashioned by his own sovereignty, may cognize infinite bodies and the like as a single unity — 'we two,' 'you two,' 'we,' 'you all,' and so on. But increase and so forth, which pertain to the body, cannot even be figuratively attributed [to consciousness], since increase or decrease is impossible for that which is of the nature of consciousness. For everything is of the nature of everything — therefore even inert things of the nature of <s>nara</s>, abandoning their previous form, become partakers of the forms of <s>Śakti</s> and <s>Śiva</s> — 'Listen, O stones!' (<s>śṛṇuta grāvāṇaḥ</s>) —

body.text: tyaktaśāktarūpasyāpi cāhaṃrūpaśivātmakatvam api syāt, vayasye dayite śarīracittattvam evāhaṃ bhavāmīti pratyayāt / śivasvarūpam api cojjhitacidrūpam iva naraśaktyātmakaṃ vapur āviśaty eva / ko 'ham, eṣo 'ham, aho ahaṃ, dhik mām, aho mahyam ityādau hy aham iti guṇīkṛtam avicchinnaṃ svātantryam / mukhyatayā tu vicchinnaivedantā pratīyate yatra bhagavatyā aparāyā udayaḥ / he 'ham ityādau parāparaśāktaspandasparśa eva śivasya / kiṃ tu pūrvaṃ pūrvam avyabhicaritam uttaratra / tena nararūpaṃ sphuṭayaiva pratipattyā śāktaśāṃbhavadhuram āroḍhuṃ śaknuyād eva / na punar vaiparītyenārohaṇaṃ sphuṭapratītimayam / atyaktanijanijarūpatayā tryātmakatvād ekadvibahurūpabhāgitvam eti pratyekam etat trikam / uktaṃ hi
body.translated_text: And even when the form of <s>Śakti</s> has been abandoned, there can be the <s>Śiva</s>-nature of the I-form, because of the cognition 'To my dear friend, I am the very truth of body and mind.' Even the essential nature of <s>Śiva</s>, as though having abandoned its consciousness-nature, enters the form that is of the nature of <s>nara</s> and <s>śakti</s>. In expressions like 'Who am I?', 'This I am!', 'Ah, I!', 'Woe to me!', 'Oh, for me!' — here 'I' has its uninterrupted sovereignty subordinated. But primarily, it is the interrupted 'this-ness' that is cognized — wherein is the arising of the Blessed <s>Aparā</s> (the lower Goddess). In expressions like 'Hey, I!' and so on, there is the touch of the vibration of the <s>Parāparā Śakti</s> (Supreme-non-Supreme Power) upon <s>Śiva</s>. However, each earlier [level] is invariably present in the subsequent ones. Therefore, from the form of <s>nara</s>, through clear cognition itself, one is indeed capable of ascending to the burden of <s>Śakti</s> and <s>Śambhava</s> (the Śiva state). But the reverse ascent is not [characterized by] clear cognition. Because each [level] does not abandon its own essential nature, [and] because of having three selves, each member of this triad partakes of one, two, and many forms. For it has been said —

body.text: Q: ekaṃ vastu dvidhā bhūtaṃ dvidhā bhūtam anekadhā /
body.translated_text: Q: One reality becomes twofold, and the twofold becomes manifold.

body.text: iti / ekātmakatve hy apratiyogitvāc chivatā pratiyogisaṃbhave śāktatvam anekatāyāṃ bheda eva narātmabhāva ekasyaiva / ghaṭaḥ ghaṭapaṭau ghaṭāḥ ghaṭapaṭapāṣāṇā ity api hi tiṣṭhati tiṣṭhataḥ tiṣṭhantīti caikyenaiva kriyāśaktisphuritam evaitat / yathoktaṃ
body.translated_text: In the state of oneness, since there is no counterpart, there is <s>Śiva</s>-nature; when a counterpart is possible, there is <s>Śakti</s>-nature; in multiplicity, differentiation alone is the <s>nara</s>-state — of the one [reality] itself. [In expressions like] 'the pot,' 'the pot and the cloth,' 'the pots,' 'the pot, the cloth, and the stone' — also 'it stands,' 'they two stand,' 'they stand' — this is indeed the vibration of the power of action (<s>kriyāśakti</s>) through unity itself. As has been stated —

body.text: Q: anekam ekadhā kṛtvā ko na mucyeta bandhanāt /
body.translated_text: Q: Having made the many into one, who would not be liberated from bondage?

body.text: iti / ata eva naraśaktiśivātmanāṃ yugapad ekatra parāmarśe uttarottarasvarūpānupraveśa eva tasyaiva vastutas tatparamārtharūpatvāt / sa ca tvaṃ ca tiṣṭhathaḥ, sa ca tvaṃ cāhaṃ ca tiṣṭhāma iti pratītikrama evākṛtakasaṃskārasāraḥ śābdikair lakṣaṇair anugamyate / tathā ca nijabhāṣāpadeṣv api saṃskārasya yatra nāmāpi na avaśiṣyate bauddhāndradraviḍādiṣu tatrāpy ayam eva vācanikaḥ kramaḥ /
body.translated_text: Therefore, in the simultaneous apprehension of <s>nara</s>, <s>śakti</s>, and <s>śiva</s> in one [awareness], there is invariably the entry of each successive higher nature into [the lower], since that alone is in reality their ultimate nature. 'He and you stand,' 'he and you and I stand' — this very order of cognition, which is the essence of uncreated disposition (<s>saṃskāra</s>), is traced by the grammarians through [their] grammatical rules. And even in the conventions of one's own language, where not even a trace of [grammatical] disposition remains — among the <s>Bauddha</s> (Buddhist), <s>Āndhra</s>, <s>Drāviḍa</s> (Dravidian), and other [languages] — even there, this same linguistic order prevails.

body.text: vacanakramaś ca hārdīm eva pratītiṃ mūlato 'nusaran tatpratītirasarūpatayā pratīter apy evaṃrūpatvam avagamayet / yathoktaṃ mayaiva
body.translated_text: And the order of speech, following from its very root the cognition of the heart, being of the nature of the essence of that cognition, would make one understand that cognition too is of this very form. As I myself have stated —

body.text: Q: ... na hṛdayaṃgamagāminī gīḥ /
body.translated_text: Q: ... speech that penetrates to the heart.

body.text: iti / tat sarvathākṛtakaiveyaṃ pratītiḥ / yathoktam
body.translated_text: Thus this cognition is in every way uncreated. As has been stated —

body.text: Q: na tair vinā bhavec chabdo nārtho nāpi citer gatiḥ /
body.translated_text: Q: Without them there would be no sound, no meaning, nor any movement of consciousness.

body.text:
iti / śrīmālinītantre 'pi /
Q: evaṃ sarvāṇusaṃghātam adhiṣṭhāya yathā sthitā /
Q: tathā te kathitā śambhoḥ śaktir ekaiva śāṃkarī //
body.translated_text: And in the sacred <s>Mālinī Tantra</s> also: Q: Thus, presiding over the aggregate of all atoms, just as she abides, so has been described to you, O <s>Śambhu</s>, the one and only power of <s>Śaṃkara</s>. //

body.text: iti / śrītantrasamuccaye 'pi
body.translated_text: And in the sacred <s>Tantrasamuccaya</s> also —

body.text:
Q: naraśaktiśivāveśi viśvam etat sadā sthitam /
Q: vyavahāre krimīṇāṃ ca sarvajñānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ //
body.translated_text: Q: This universe, pervaded by <s>nara</s>, <s>śakti</s>, and <s>śiva</s>, always abides thus — in the transactions of worms as well as of the omniscient ones, in every way. //

body.text: iti / tad eva naraśaktiśivātmakaṃ sphuṭapratipattisaṃpradāyopadeśena darśitam / naraḥ śaktiḥ śiva iti tu sarvaṃsahaḥ pratipattikramaḥ parameśvarecchāsvātantryasṛṣṭa ity alaṃ paraśaktipātapavitritabahuśrutasahṛdayasopadeśakatipayajanahṛdayahāriṇyā prasaktānuprasaktyā /
body.translated_text: Thus that very [reality] of the nature of <s>nara</s>, <s>śakti</s>, and <s>śiva</s> has been shown through the teaching tradition of clear understanding. But the order of cognition — <s>nara</s>, <s>śakti</s>, <s>śiva</s> — which bears everything, is created by the sovereign will of <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord). Enough of this tangential discussion, which captivates the hearts of only those few persons who are well-instructed, learned in many [scriptures], sympathetic, and purified by the descent of supreme grace (<s>paraśaktipāta</s>).

body.text:
tad vyākhyātaṃ \pratika{śṛṇu devi} iti / \pratika{uttarasyāpi} iti yad uktaṃ katham anuttaram iti tatra prativacanam / uttarasyāpi saṃnihitasya yad anuttaram / prāguktakrameṇa
hy uttaram apy anuttaratādātmyenaiva bhavet nānyathā / ata eva uttaram apy anādṛtya
body.translated_text: Thus 'listen, O Goddess' (<s>śṛṇu devi</s>) has been explained. As for what was said — 'of the answer (<s>uttara</s>) too' — [the question is:] how can it be the <s>anuttara</s> (the unsurpassed, that which has no answer beyond it)? To that, the reply: of the answer that is present, that which is <s>anuttara</s>. For by the method stated previously, the answer too would exist only in identity with the <s>anuttara</s>, not otherwise. Therefore, disregarding even the answer —

body.text: Q: anādare ṣaṣṭhī /
body.translated_text: Q: The sixth case [genitive] is used in the sense of disregard.

body.text: uttaraṃ rūpaṃ hy anādṛtatadbhāvam anuttararūpam eva / bhedo hy ayam uttararūpo nitarām evābhedabhuvam adhiśayya tathā bhavet / yathoktam
body.translated_text: For the form of the answer, having its own nature disregarded, is itself of the nature of <s>anuttara</s> (the unsurpassed). For this differentiation, which is of the form of the answer, would become so only by thoroughly surpassing the ground of non-differentiation. As has been stated —

body.text:
Q: paravyavasthāpi pare yāvan nātmīkṛtaḥ paraḥ /
Q: tāvan na śakyate kartuṃ yato buddhaḥ paraḥ paraḥ //
body.translated_text: Q: Even the establishment of the other [as other] — as long as the other has not been made one's own, until then it cannot be accomplished, because the other is known [only] as other. //

body.text: iti /

tathottarasyāpi granthabhāgasyānuttaraṃ tenāpi uttarītuṃ na śakyate / paśyantyā api parābhaṭṭārikāyāḥ prathamaprasaratvād uttarasyāpi ca madīyasyaitad evānuttaraṃ paramārthaḥ / uttarasya triśūlapreraṇādimayasya yad anuttaraṃ viśrāntisthānam / kiṃ tad ity āha yataḥ syād ayaṃ kauliko vidhiḥ / kaulikaḥ kulākulātmā prāg vyākhyātaḥ vidhīyamānatvād vidhir mahāsṛṣṭirūpo garbhīkṛtānantasṛṣṭyādikoṭiśato yasmāt prasṛta etad eva tad anuttaram / yad uktam
body.translated_text: Likewise, the <s>anuttara</s> (the unsurpassed) of the subsequent portion of the text too — even by that [subsequent portion], it cannot be surpassed. Because <s>Parā Bhaṭṭārikā</s> (the Supreme Goddess), even in her <s>paśyantī</s> (visionary) [level], has primacy of first emanation, and because this very <s>anuttara</s> is the ultimate meaning of even my own subsequent [commentary]. The <s>anuttara</s> — the resting place — of the answer, which consists of the impelling of the trident and so forth. What is that? He says: 'from which would arise this <s>kaulika</s> (pertaining to <s>kula</s>) procedure.' <s>Kaulika</s> means 'of the nature of <s>kula</s> and <s>akula</s>' — as explained previously. The procedure (<s>vidhi</s>), because it is that which is being enjoined, is of the nature of the great emanation (<s>mahāsṛṣṭi</s>), containing within it hundreds of millions of cycles of emanation and so on, from which [everything] has issued forth — that itself is the <s>anuttara</s>. As has been stated —

body.text: Q: yataḥ sarvam
body.translated_text: Q: From which [comes] everything —

body.text:
iti / tathā hīdaṃ viśvaṃ ciccittaprāṇadehasukhaduḥkhendriyabhūtaghaṭādimayam ekasyāṃ parasyāṃ parameśvaryāṃ bhairavasaṃvidy avibhāgenaiva bodhātmakena rūpeṇāste / yady api bodhātmakaṃ rūpaṃ nāstameti jātucid api tadastamaye aprakāśamānatāpatteḥ, tathāpi parasparābhāvātmako 'vacchedaḥ tatra nāsti / viśvātmāna eva bhāvāḥ, tatra ca yady eṣām avasthitir na syāt tat prathamānusaṃdhānādikam evākṣapreraṇopayogy api na bhaved iti samucitānuditedantākam ahaṃparāmarśamātrābhinnam eva bhāvajātaṃ vigatabhedakalanaṃ tiṣṭhati / na tatra kaścid avacchedaḥ / tathā yad yatra spaṣṭaḥ sann ayaṃ vidhiḥ kaulikaḥ sthito viśrāntiṃ prāptaḥ / sarvam idaṃ hi ṣaṭtriṃśadātma tataḥ sāmānyaspandasaṃvidātmanaḥ śaktimataḥ paraśaktipradhānāc
chivāt svaśaktyā sṛṣṭam api sat tatraiva bhairavaviśeṣaspandātmani śaktipradhāne svasvarūpe viśrāmyet / tad eva svasvabhāvaniṣṭhitatvaṃ bhāvānām / yad uktaṃ
body.translated_text: Thus indeed, this universe — consisting of consciousness (<s>cit</s>), mind (<s>citta</s>), vital breath (<s>prāṇa</s>), body (<s>deha</s>), pleasure (<s>sukha</s>), pain (<s>duḥkha</s>), senses (<s>indriya</s>), elements (<s>bhūta</s>), pots, and so forth — rests in the one Supreme Goddess (<s>Parā Parameśvarī</s>), in the awareness of <s>Bhairava</s> (<s>Bhairava-saṃvid</s>), in an undifferentiated form that is of the nature of consciousness. Although the form that is of the nature of consciousness never sets — for if it were to set, the condition of non-manifestation would ensue — nevertheless, there is no mutual negation-based limitation there. All things are of the nature of the universe; and if their abiding were not there, then even the first synthesis and so on, which are useful for impelling the senses, would not occur. Thus the totality of entities, with its appropriate arisen and unarisen 'this-ness,' remains identical with the mere awareness of 'I' (<s>ahaṃparāmarśa</s>) alone, free from the operation of differentiation. There is no limitation whatsoever there. Likewise, where this <s>kaulika</s> procedure, being manifest, abides — has come to rest. For all this, which is of thirty-six [principles] in nature, though emanated by his own power from <s>Śiva</s> — who is the possessor of power, whose essence is the general vibration of awareness, and in whom the Supreme Power (<s>Paraśakti</s>) predominates — rests in that very <s>Bhairava</s>, whose essence is the particular vibration, in whom <s>Śakti</s> predominates, in its own essential nature. That alone is the abiding of entities in their own nature. As has been stated —

body.text: Q: yasmin sarvam
body.translated_text: Q: In which everything [rests] —

body.text: iti / tad etad śivaśaktyātmaiva sāmānyaviśeṣarūpam ekātmakam api parameśvareṇaivopadeśopāyapraveśāya pṛthakkṛtya nirūpyamāṇaṃ vastutaḥ punar ekam eva svatantracinmayam aham ity aiśvaryaśaktisāram anuttaram / yatra kīdṛśe svasvarūpe 'vasthitaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus. This [reality], which is of the nature of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s>, which is of the form of both the universal and the particular, and which is one in essence, has been analyzed by the Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>) as if separated for the purpose of introducing the means of instruction — yet in reality it is nothing but the one, autonomous, consciousness-consisting 'I' (<s>aham</s>), the unsurpassed (<s>anuttara</s>), whose essence is the power of sovereignty (<s>aiśvaryaśakti</s>). 'Where' — in what kind of own nature — [does He] abide?

body.text: Q: mama hṛdvyomni /
body.translated_text: "In the space of my heart" (<s>mama hṛdvyomni</s>).

body.text: mameti yad etad dhṛdayaṃ sarvabhāvānāṃ sthānaṃ pratiṣṭhādhāma / nīlādīnāṃ hy antataḥ krimiparyantaṃ cidaṃśāniviṣṭānāṃ na kiṃcit nīlādirūpam iti pramātur eva yat
body.translated_text: By 'my' (<s>mama</s>) — this 'heart' (<s>hṛdaya</s>) is the locus, the abode of foundation (<s>pratiṣṭhādhāma</s>) of all entities. For blue and other [objects], down to the lowest worm, which are pervaded by the aspect of consciousness (<s>cid-aṃśa</s>) — nothing has any form such as blue, etc., in itself; rather, it belongs only to the knowing subject (<s>pramātṛ</s>),

body.text: Q: mameti
body.translated_text: as expressed by 'my' (<s>mama</s>) —

body.text: avicchinnacamatkārāṃśopārohitvaṃ
body.translated_text: the state of being elevated upon the uninterrupted aspect of wonder (<s>camatkāra</s>).

body.text: Q: mama nīlaṃ bhātam
body.translated_text: "Blue has appeared as mine" (<s>mama nīlaṃ bhātam</s>).

body.text: iti tadeva nīlādirūpatvam iti /
body.translated_text: That alone is the nature of being blue, etc.

body.text: tasya mamety asya nīlādyanantasarvabhāvahṛdayasya yad vyoma yatra tat mamakārātmakaṃ viśvaṃ samyag dhṛtam / ata eva tyaktabhinnanijarūpatayā śūnyarūpaṃ vyoma yatra / tathā mamety asya bhinnābhinnarūpaparāparasaṃvidātmano yad dhṛdayaṃ paryantapratiṣṭhādhāma aham iti tasyāpi vyoma saṃhārarūpakalanena maha iti narātmakaṃ līnaṃ bindvātmaśaktau ma iti, kuṇḍalinīhakalārūpāyāṃ praviśya paripūrṇanirargalacamatkāre sarvāvicchinne a ity anupraviṣṭaṃ tathā bhavati / etad eva mama hṛdvyoma / evaṃ yata idaṃ praṣṛtaṃ yatra ca viśrāntaṃ tad eva nityam anāvṛtasvabhāvaṃ svayaṃ prathamānam anapahnavanīyam anuttaram / yathoktam
body.translated_text: Of this 'my' (<s>mama</s>) — the heart of all entities beginning with blue and extending infinitely — that which is the 'space' (<s>vyoma</s>), wherein the universe consisting of the sense of 'mine' (<s>mamakāra</s>) is perfectly held; and therefore, having abandoned its separate form, it is a space that is void in nature. Likewise, the 'heart' (<s>hṛdaya</s>) of this 'my' (<s>mama</s>), which is of the nature of the supreme and non-supreme consciousness (<s>parāpara-saṃvid</s>) in both differentiated and undifferentiated form — the abode of ultimate foundation — of even that, the 'space' (<s>vyoma</s>), through the operation of withdrawal (<s>saṃhāra</s>), becomes 'ma-ha' — the self of 'nara' dissolved into the <s>Śakti</s> whose nature is <s>bindu</s> as 'ma'; entering into <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s> whose form is the <s>hakala</s>, it merges into the fully perfect, unobstructed <s>camatkāra</s>, the all-undivided 'a'. Thus it becomes so. This alone is 'the space of my heart' (<s>mama hṛdvyoma</s>). Thus, that from which this [universe] has issued forth and in which it rests — that alone is eternal, of unrestricted nature, self-luminous, undeniable, unsurpassed (<s>anuttara</s>). As stated:

body.text:
Q: yatra sthitam idaṃ sarvaṃ kāryaṃ yasmāc ca nirgatam /
Q: tasyānāvṛtarūpatvān na nirodho 'sti kutracit /
body.translated_text: "That in which all this effect abides, and from which it has emerged — because its nature is unrestricted (<s>anāvṛta</s>), there is no obstruction of it anywhere."

body.text: iti / āvarakatvena nirodhakābhimato 'pi hi tadāvaraṇādisvātantryeṇa prakāśamāno dṛkkriyātmaka eva parameśvaraḥ / yad ity ayaṃ nipātaḥ sarvavibhaktyarthavṛttir aparavākyīyasaṃbandhaucityād viśeṣe sthāsnur atra pañcamyarthe saptamyarthe ca vartate / ayaṃ hy āñjasyena artho yad ayaṃ kaulikaḥ sṛṣṭiprasaraḥ, yac ca mama hṛdvyomny avasthitas tad evānuttaram /
body.translated_text: Thus. Even that which is considered an obstructor by way of covering — even it, shining forth through the autonomy (<s>svātantrya</s>) of that very covering, etc., is nothing but the Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>), who is of the nature of perception and action (<s>dṛk-kriyā</s>). The particle 'yad' functions in the sense of all case-endings; here, by the fitness of connection with the other sentence, it stands in the sense of the ablative and the locative in a particular usage. For this is the straightforward meaning: that this <s>kaulika</s> emanation (<s>sṛṣṭi-prasara</s>), and that which abides in the space of my heart — that alone is the unsurpassed (<s>anuttara</s>).

body.text: evaṃ tasyaiva prasaraviśrāntyubhayasthānatvaṃ nirūpya prasarakramasvarūpaṃ kriyāśaktispandavisargaṃ nirūpayati
body.translated_text: Having thus established that it [the <s>anuttara</s>] is the locus of both emanation and repose, he now sets forth the nature of the process of emanation — the vibration-emission (<s>spanda-visarga</s>) of the power of action (<s>kriyāśakti</s>):

body.text: Q: kathayāmi
body.translated_text: "I declare" (<s>kathayāmi</s>),

body.text: ityādi / tad eva hi rūpam ahaṃ parānuttarātma parāparādimayapaśyantyādiprasaraparipāṭyā 'vicchinnaikatāparamārthaḥ kathayāmīti samucitavyapadeśaṃ parābhaṭṭārikodayabhāgi vaikharyantaṃ vākyaprabandhaṃ śāstrīyalaukikādibahubhedaṃ vyaktayāmīti / taduktam
body.translated_text: and so forth. That very form — I, whose essence is the supreme unsurpassed (<s>parānuttara</s>), through the sequence of emanation of <s>Paśyantī</s> and the rest which are of the nature of the supreme-and-non-supreme (<s>parāpara</s>), etc., whose ultimate reality is unbroken unity — 'I declare', that is, through appropriate designation, partaking of the arising of the supreme Goddess (<s>Parā Bhaṭṭārikā</s>), I manifest the textual composition extending down to <s>Vaikharī</s>, with its many divisions of scriptural, worldly, and other [discourse]. As has been said:

body.text: Q: ... sarvataś ca yaḥ
body.translated_text: "...and who [is] everywhere,"

body.text: iti / prathamaparyantabhuvi parābhaṭṭārikātmani tatprasarātmani ca parāparādevatāvapuṣy anuttaradhruvapadavijṛmbhaiva / tad āhur nijavivṛtau śrīsomānandapādāḥ kathayāmity uccārayāmy utkalikāta iti / tathāham eva sarvasyāntaś cidrūpeṇa kathayāmīti / tad evāsmābhir yuktyupadeśasaṃskārair nirmalayya hṛdayaṅgamīkṛtam /
body.translated_text: Thus. On the ground extending from the first to the last, in the form of the supreme Goddess (<s>Parā Bhaṭṭārikā</s>) and in the form of her emanation as the <s>Parāpara</s> deity, there is nothing but the expansion of the unsurpassed eternal state (<s>anuttara-dhruva-pada</s>). Therefore the revered <s>Somānanda</s> states in his own commentary: "'I declare' — 'I utter from exuberance (<s>utkalikā</s>)'." Likewise, "I alone, as consciousness within everything, declare." This very [teaching] has been purified by us through reasoning, instruction, and [spiritual] refinements, and made to enter the heart.

body.text: svarūpaṃ cāsya parameśvarasya sadya iti / ya eva ca parameśvaro bhairavātmākulānuttaradhruvadhāmatayoktas tad evedaṃ sarvaṃ sat kaulikavidhirūpam / na hi prakāśavimarśaśuddhabhairavasvarūpātireki kiṃcit bhāvānāṃ sattvam / sattāsaṃbandhārthakriyākāritvādīnām api sattāhetutāparābhimatānām api sattā'yoge tathātvānupapatteḥ sattvāntarārthākriyāntarayoge cānavasthāpatteḥ /prathamata eva tathā vimarśajīvitaprakāśamayatvam eva sattvaṃ, tac ca svātantryavimarśasārāhaṃbhāvabharitam iti bhairavarūpam eva / yad vā sati sadrūpe yasyati yatnaṃ karoti kriyāśaktiprāṇatvāt / tat sadya iti kvipi napuṃsakanirdeśaḥ / sad yad iti kecit guravaḥ paṭhanti / tad uktaṃ śrīsiddhasantāne
body.translated_text: And the own-nature of this Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>) is 'sat' (being). And that very Supreme Lord, who has been described as <s>Bhairava</s>, the unmanifest (<s>akula</s>), the unsurpassed eternal abode — this entire [reality] which exists is of the nature of the <s>kaulika</s> method (<s>vidhi</s>). For there is no being (<s>sattva</s>) of any entity whatsoever apart from the pure <s>Bhairava</s>-nature, which is [the unity of] light (<s>prakāśa</s>) and reflective awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>). Because even of the [criteria of] existence such as connection with being, capacity for causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyākāritva</s>), etc. — which are held by others to be the causes of being — if there is no connection with being, their being such does not hold; and if another being and another causal efficacy [are posited], there is an infinite regress. From the very start, being is nothing but having the nature of light vivified by reflective awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>), and that is filled with the I-sense (<s>ahaṃbhāva</s>) whose essence is the autonomous reflective awareness (<s>svātantrya-vimarśa</s>) — thus it is nothing but the <s>Bhairava</s>-nature. Or alternatively, 'sat' means 'that which moves toward' (<s>yasyati</s>) being — it makes effort — because the power of action (<s>kriyāśakti</s>) is its vital breath. Thus 'sadya' with the <s>kvip</s> suffix, explained in the neuter. Some teachers read 'sad yad'. As stated in the <s>Śrīsiddhasantāna</s>:

body.text: Q: prakāśamānābhāsaiva yad bhūtis tat sad eva hi /
body.translated_text: "The very appearance that shines forth as manifestation — that alone is 'sat' (being)."

body.text: iti / śrīspande 'pi
body.translated_text: Thus. And in the <s>Śrīspanda</s> [śāstra] also:

body.text: Q: ... tad asti paramārthataḥ /
body.translated_text: "...that exists in the ultimate sense."

body.text: iti / śrīsomānandapādair api
body.translated_text: Thus. And by the revered <s>Somānanda</s> also:

body.text: Q: yat sat tat paramārtho hi paramārthas tataḥ śivaḥ /
body.translated_text: "That which is 'sat' (being) — that indeed is the ultimate reality (<s>paramārtha</s>); the ultimate reality is therefore <s>Śiva</s>."

body.text: iti svarūpam uktam / tad uktaṃ \pratika{yaḥ sarvaṃ} iti / asyaiva kriyāśaktiprasaraṃ nirūpayati \pratika{kaulikasiddhidam} iti / kaulikaṃ yat vyākhyātam / tasya siddhiḥ tathātvadārḍhyam / tad yato bhavati / tatra hi paramārthapramātari sakalaṃ kulākulādi tathā bhavati / yatra pratīyamānaṃ sarvaṃ tathātvadārḍhyaṃ bhajate / tad uktam
body.translated_text: Thus has the own-nature been stated. This is expressed by 'who [is] everything' (<s>yaḥ sarvam</s>). He now sets forth the emanation of the power of action (<s>kriyāśakti</s>) of this very [reality] with 'bestower of <s>kaulika</s> accomplishment' (<s>kaulikasiddhidam</s>). The <s>kaulika</s> [principle] that has been explained — its accomplishment (<s>siddhi</s>) is the firmness of its being so (<s>tathātva-dārḍhya</s>). That from which this arises — for in the ultimate knowing subject (<s>paramārtha-pramātṛ</s>), the entire [range of] <s>kula</s>, <s>akula</s>, etc. becomes so. That in which everything perceived attains firmness of being so. As stated:

body.text: Q: kulāt parataraṃ trikam /
body.translated_text: "Higher than <s>kula</s> is <s>Trika</s>."

body.text: iti / anyatrāpi
body.translated_text: Thus. And elsewhere also:

body.text:
Q: vedāc chaivaṃ tato vāmaṃ tato dakṣaṃ tataḥ kulam /
Q: tato mataṃ tataś cāpi trikaṃ sarvottamaṃ param //
body.translated_text: "From the <s>Veda</s>, [one proceeds to] <s>Śaiva</s>; then <s>Vāma</s>; then <s>Dakṣa</s>; then <s>Kula</s>; then the <s>Mata</s>; and then <s>Trika</s>, the supreme and highest of all."

body.text: iti / śrīniśācāre 'pi
body.translated_text: Thus. And in the <s>Śrīniśācāra</s> also:

body.text:
Q: vāmamārgābhiṣikto 'pi daiśikaḥ paratattvavit /
Q: saṃskāryo bhairave so 'pi kule kaule trike 'pi saḥ //
body.translated_text: "Even a teacher consecrated in the <s>Vāma</s> path, who knows the supreme reality, must be [re-]consecrated in <s>Bhairava</s> [tantra], in <s>Kula</s>, in <s>Kaula</s>, and in <s>Trika</s>."

body.text: iti /
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: śrīsarvācare ' pi
body.translated_text: And in the <s>Śrīsarvācāra</s> also:

body.text:
Q: vāmamārgārgābhiṣikto 'pi daiśikaḥ paratattvavit /
Q: kramād bhairavatantreṣu punaḥ saṃskāram arhati //
body.translated_text: "Even a teacher consecrated in the <s>Vāma</s> path, who knows the supreme reality, deserves re-consecration progressively in the <s>Bhairava</s> tantras."

body.text: iti / kramaś caiṣa eva / yathoktam evaṃ yat sarvalokavedasiddhāntavāmadakṣiṇakulamatabhūmiṣu paramārthapramātṛ iti / yathoktam
body.translated_text: Thus. And this is the [proper] sequence. As stated — thus, that which is the ultimate knowing subject (<s>paramārtha-pramātṛ</s>) throughout all the stages of worldly [knowledge], <s>Veda</s>, <s>Siddhānta</s>, <s>Vāma</s>, <s>Dakṣiṇa</s>, <s>Kula</s>, and <s>Mata</s>. As stated:

body.text: Q: yaś ca sarvamayo nityaṃ tasmai sarvātmane namaḥ /
body.translated_text: "And to him who always consists of everything — salutation to that Self of all (<s>sarvātman</s>)!"

body.text: iti / tad evānuttaram / etat sarvaṃ garbhīkṛtyoktaṃ nijavivṛtau somānandapādaiḥ,
body.translated_text: Thus. That alone is the unsurpassed (<s>anuttara</s>). All this has been stated, encompassing everything, by the revered <s>Somānanda</s> in his own commentary:

body.text: Q: kiṃ bahunā sarvam evānuttaram anuttaratvād
body.translated_text: "What more [need be said]? Everything is indeed unsurpassed (<s>anuttara</s>), because of [its] unsurpassed nature."

body.text: iti / ayaṃ tātparyārthaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus. This is the intended meaning.

body.text: ... %Prākṛtam

iti / īdṛg vyākhyānaṃ tyaktvā yad anyair vyākhyātaṃ tatpradarśanaṃ dūṣaṇam / yady api padavākyasaṃskāravihīnaiḥ saha vrīḍāvahā goṣṭhī kṛtābhavati tathāpi sacetaso 'nuttaram avabodhayituṃ tad ekavāraṃ tāval likhyate / \pratika{anuttaram} ityādinā sārdhena ślokena śivaviṣayaḥ praśnaḥ / \pratika{hṛdayasthā} ityādinā ślokena śaktiviṣayaḥ / tathā \pratika{śṛṇudevi} ity atra prativacanagranthe \pratika{uttarasyāpy anuttaram} iti tatrārtha uttaraṃ ca śṛṇv anuttaraṃ ceti / atra yady eṣā trikārthābhiprāyeṇa vyākhyā tan naraviṣayatṛtīyapraśnaprasaṅgaḥ / atha tu yāmalābhiprāyeṇa tatrāpi na dve vastunī śivaśaktyātmake yāmalam ucyate yena pṛthak praśnaviṣayatopapattiḥ / athaśabdārthaś ca na saṃgacchate / sa hi sajātīyaniścayānantaryavṛttiḥ
/ uttarasvarūpāvadhāraṇam antareṇa cānuttaraviṣayasyaikapraśnasyānupapattiḥ / tathāhi keṣucid vṛddhapustakeṣv īdṛk ślokāntaraṃ dṛśyate
body.translated_text: Thus. Having set aside this [correct] interpretation, the exposition and refutation of what others have explained [follows]. Although engaging in debate with those who lack refinement in word and sentence [analysis] is an occasion for embarrassment, nevertheless, in order to make those who are discerning understand the unsurpassed (<s>anuttara</s>), it is written here once. With the verse beginning '<s>anuttaram</s>' (one and a half verses), the question concerns <s>Śiva</s>. With the verse beginning '<s>hṛdayasthā</s>', [the question] concerns <s>Śakti</s>. Then in '<s>śṛṇu devi</s>', in the reply text, '<s>uttarasyāpy anuttaram</s>' — there the meaning is 'hear the answer (<s>uttara</s>) and the unsurpassed (<s>anuttara</s>).' Here, if this interpretation is with the intent of <s>Trika</s> doctrine, then there arises the occasion for a third question concerning 'nara' (the individual). But if with the intent of <s>Yāmala</s>, even there, <s>Yāmala</s> is not said of two separate things of the nature of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s>, so as to justify them being separate subjects of inquiry. Moreover, the meaning of the word 'atha' does not fit [their interpretation], for it functions in the sense of immediate succession to a cognition of the same kind. And without ascertaining the nature of the 'answer' (<s>uttara</s>), the single question regarding the unsurpassed (<s>anuttara</s>) would not be justified. For indeed, in certain old manuscripts, a different verse is seen:

body.text:
Q: śrutaṃ deva mahājñānaṃ trikākhyaṃ parameśvara /
Q: uttaraṃ ca tathā jñānaṃ tvatprasādāvadhāritam //
body.translated_text: "O God, O Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>)! I have heard the great knowledge called <s>Trika</s>, and also the knowledge called <s>Uttara</s>, which has been ascertained by your grace."

body.text: iti / tasmāt śrīsomānandapādanirūpitavyākhyānusāreṇaiva yad guravaḥ samādikṣan tad eva sarvasya karoti śivam /
body.translated_text: Therefore, that alone which the teachers have transmitted in accordance with the interpretation established by the revered <s>Somānanda</s> — that alone brings about the welfare of all.

body.text:
ity asaṃskṛtadurvyākhyātāmasonmūlanavrataḥ /
ṣaḍardhaśāsanāpūtahṛdaṃbujavikāsakaḥ //
body.translated_text: He whose vow is to uproot the darkness of unrefined, wrongly explained [interpretations], who causes the lotus of the heart to blossom, purified by the teaching of the three-and-a-half [systems],

body.text:
saṃstyānānantapāśaughavilāpakalasadruciḥ /
dīpto 'bhinavaguptena vyākhyābhānuḥ prakāśitaḥ //
body.translated_text: whose splendor dissolves the dense, infinite mass of bonds — this sun of commentary has been illuminated by <s>Abhinavagupta</s>.

body.text: evaṃ yato 'yaṃ kauliko vidhiḥ prabhavati yatra ca pratiṣṭhāpadavīṃ bhajate yanmayaṃ cedaṃ kaulikaṃ tad evānuttaraṃ ity uktam / tatra kas tāvat kauliko vidhiḥ kathaṃ cāsya prasaro 'nuttarāt kathaṃ cātraivāsya pratiṣṭhā kathaṃ cānuttaraikarūpatvam ? yac coktam uttarasyāpy anuttaram iti tat sarvaṃ yuktyāgamasvasaṃvedananiṣkarṣaṇatattvāvabodhāvāptavimarśanipuṇān śiṣyān prati vitatya nirṇinīṣur bhagavān prastauti granthāntaram / etāvaddṛḍhopadeśanirdalitabhedābhimānavikalpānalpasaṃskārāṇāṃ tu sarvam etāvataiva
body.translated_text: Thus it has been said that from which this <s>kaulika</s> method (<s>vidhi</s>) arises, in which it attains the state of foundation, and of which this <s>kaulika</s> [reality] consists — that alone is the unsurpassed (<s>anuttara</s>). Now then, what is the <s>kaulika</s> method? How does it emanate from the <s>anuttara</s>? How does it find its foundation in that very [<s>anuttara</s>]? And how is it of one form with the <s>anuttara</s>? And what was stated as 'the unsurpassed of even the answer' (<s>uttarasyāpy anuttaram</s>) — all of this, wishing to determine at length for disciples who are skilled in reflective awareness gained through the comprehension of reality arrived at by the extraction of reasoning, scripture, and self-experience — the Lord introduces a new section of the text. For those, however, whose false notions of duality have been shattered by firm instruction up to this point, and whose [spiritual] refinements are substantial, for them all [is accomplished] by just this much alone —

body.text: anuttaraṃ katham
body.translated_text: "How is [it] unsurpassed (<s>anuttara</s>)?"

body.text: ityādisārdhaślokayugalanigamitena praśnena
body.translated_text: — with the question concluded in a pair of verses and a half,

body.text: śṛṇu devi
body.translated_text: "Listen, O Goddess (<s>Devi</s>)!"

body.text: ityādinā sārdhaślokanirṇītena cottareṇānuttarapadaprāptivaśāviṣṭajīvanmuktabhāvānāṃ kṛtakṛtyatā / atas tāvanmātra eva dṛḍhapratipattipavitrīkṛtair viśramaṇīyam ity udbhujāḥ phūtkurmaḥ / tad anuttaraparabhairavapadavimaladarpaṇāntarniviṣṭakaulikapadapraviviktaye granthāntaram avatarati ity uktam / tad yathā
body.translated_text: — and with the reply determined in a verse and a half, by attaining the state of the unsurpassed (<s>anuttara-pada</s>), those who are possessed by the condition of liberation-in-life (<s>jīvanmukta</s>) have accomplished their purpose. Therefore, those purified by firm conviction in just that much alone should rest. Thus we exhale with arms outstretched [in relief]. It has been said that a new section of the text is introduced for the purpose of clearly distinguishing the <s>kaulika</s> state, which rests within the stainless mirror of the supreme <s>Bhairava</s> state of the <s>anuttara</s>. That is as follows:

body.text: ParTri 5-9ab:

children.translated_text: "Now, the first <s>tithis</s> (lunar days), all [of them],
are the vowels (<s>svaras</s>), ending with <s>bindu</s> (anusvāra);
within them, through the conjunction of time (<s>kāla-yoga</s>),
<s>Soma</s> (Moon) and <s>Sūrya</s> (Sun) are proclaimed.
The <s>tattvas</s> (principles of reality) beginning with earth (<s>pṛthivī</s>),
ending with <s>Puruṣa</s> — [are distributed] among the five
[consonant] groups beginning with 'ka', in sequence,
ending with 'ma', O virtuous one (<s>suvrata</s>).
The four <s>dhāraṇās</s> (concentrations)
of wind (<s>vāyu</s>), fire (<s>agni</s>), water (<s>salila</s>), and <s>Indra</s> (earth) —
above them is proclaimed the [group] beginning with 'śa',
preceded by the fivefold <s>Brahman</s> (<s>brahma-pañcaka</s>).

body.text: var. 7cd: -ūrdvhaṃ

children.translated_text: This [phonemic emanation], whose root is 'a', proceeding in that order, known
to end with 'kṣa', is declared to be the emanation (<s>sṛṣṭi</s>)
of all <s>mantras</s>
and <s>vidyās</s> (knowledge-formulas), O illustrious one (<s>yaśasvinī</s>).
This is proclaimed as the womb (<s>yoni</s>),
in all tantras, always."

body.text: tatrākulam anuttaram eva kaulikaṃ sṛṣṭirūpam iti nirṇīyate / atha tat sṛṣṭir iti saṃbandhas tad evānuttaraṃ padaṃ sṛṣṭir ity arthaḥ / yady api ca sṛṣṭāv api prāktananayena kālāpekṣi paurvāparyaṃ na syāt tathāpy upadeśyopadeśabhāvalakṣaṇo bhedo yāvat svātmani svātantryāt parameśvareṇa bhāsyate tāvat paurvāparyam apīti tadapekṣayā athaśabdenānantaryam /
body.translated_text: Here it is determined that the unmanifest (<s>akula</s>), the unsurpassed (<s>anuttara</s>) itself, is the <s>kaulika</s> emanation (<s>sṛṣṭi</s>). Now, 'that is the emanation' — this is the connection: that very unsurpassed state (<s>anuttara-pada</s>) is the emanation — such is the meaning. And although in emanation too, according to the earlier method, the sequential order dependent on time would not apply, nevertheless, insofar as the distinction characterized by the relation of teacher and taught is manifested by the Supreme Lord through His autonomy (<s>svātantrya</s>) within His own Self, sequential order does apply. With reference to that, the word 'atha' (now) [indicates] immediate succession.

body.text:
anantaram akulam eva sṛṣṭirūpam iti
yāvat / na tu praśnapratijñābhyām ānantaryam athaśabdenoktam ekapraghaṭṭakagatasajātīyaprameyāpekṣakramatātparyapratītipravaṇatvād
asya / anyathā tūṣṇīṃbhāvāder anantaram idam ity api sarvatra tatprayogāvakāśaḥ / astu, ka ivātra bhavataḥ kleśa ? iti cen na kaś cid ṛte
pratītyabhāvāt / yat tu śrīsomānandapādāḥ
body.translated_text: What follows is: the unmanifest (<s>akula</s>) alone is of the nature of emanation (<s>sṛṣṭi</s>). But the word 'atha' does not indicate succession to the question and the proposition, because this [particle here] is inclined toward the apprehension of the intended sequential order with respect to a homogeneous subject matter occurring within a single continuous passage. Otherwise, [the absurd consequence would follow that] 'this comes after silence,' etc., and there would be occasion for its use everywhere. 'So be it — what difficulty does this pose for you?' If [one says] so — [we reply:] none at all, except for the absence of [correct] understanding. Now, what the revered <s>Somānanda</s> [states]:

body.text: Q: akāraḥ śiva ity uktas thakāraḥ śaktir ucyate /
body.translated_text: "The letter 'a' is said to be <s>Śiva</s>; the letter 'tha' is said to be <s>Śakti</s>."

body.text:
ity āgamapradarśanenātha ity etāvad evānuttaram iti vyācacakṣire thakārasamavyāptikatābhiprāyeṇa sarvatra prathamollāse prasaradanantānantavastusṛṣṭiśaktyabhedarūpatvāt sarvabhūtajīvanarūpaparanādāvalambanarūpatvāc cāthaśabdārthasya / tan nāsmābhir vitatya vivecitaṃ, tādṛśasyāgamasya yato na sākṣād vayam abhijñāḥ / tais tu tathāvidhāgamasākṣātkāribhir anekayuktiśatasahiṣṇutā sūtragranthasya sūtritaiva / dhūlibhedapradarśanam api tenaivābhiprāyeṇa tair itaś cāmutaś ca vitatam / vayaṃ tu tacchāsanapavitritās tadgranthagranthinirdalanābhilaṣitasvātmapavitrabhāvās tair nirṇīteṣv artheṣūdāsīnā eva / dhūlibhedādinā ca kalpitasāmayikalipyapekṣaṇam api bhaved api kasya cit upāyāya, na tu tat sakaladeśakālagataśiṣyaviṣayam iti nāsmabhir vitatya vipañcitam
/ etadanubhavayuktyanupraviṣṭānāṃ ca tad akāryakaraṃ svakalpanābhiś ca sukaram avyavasthitaṃ ca, anyeṣāṃ caitadupadeśānabhijñānāṃ tadupadeśanam apy akiṃcitkaram ity alam anena prakṛtavighnavidhāyinā / prastutam anusarāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: — by showing this scriptural authority, they [<s>Somānanda</s> and his lineage] explained that just this much — 'atha' — is itself the unsurpassed (<s>anuttara</s>), with the intention that [the syllable 'tha'] has co-extensive application [with <s>Śakti</s>], because everywhere, in the first effulgence, it is of the nature of non-difference from the power of emanation of infinite and endless realities, and because [the meaning of] the word 'atha' has the nature of resting upon the supreme <s>nāda</s>, which is the life of all beings.
