This has not been elaborated upon at length by us, since we are not directly acquainted with such a scripture. But by them, who directly perceived such scriptures, the capacity of the <s>sūtra</s> text to bear hundreds of reasonings has been demonstrated. The exposition of the <s>dhūli-bheda</s> (dust-divisions, i.e., diagrammatic analysis) has also been extended here and there by them with that very intention. We, however, purified by their teaching, desiring the purity of our own self through untying the knots of their texts, remain neutral regarding the meanings they have determined. And the consideration of the <s>dhūli-bheda</s> and similar [methods] depending on artificially conventional scripts might serve as a means for someone, but it is not applicable to disciples of all regions and times — therefore it has not been elaborated by us. For those who have entered into the experience and reasoning of this [teaching], that [diagrammatic method] is unproductive, and it is easy [to fabricate] through one's own inventions and is unstable; and for others who are unfamiliar with this instruction, teaching it too would be fruitless. Enough of this, which creates obstacles to the subject at hand. Let us follow the main topic.

body.text: ``a'' ādyo yeṣāṃ svarāṇāṃ yadi vā thakāreṇa sukhoccāraṇārthena saha athādyo yeṣām iti ādyaśabdaś cātra na vyavasthāmātre nāpi sāmīpyādau, api tv ādau bhava ādyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Those vowels (<s>svaras</s>) whose first is 'a' — or, with the letter 'tha' [added] for ease of pronunciation, those whose first is 'atha' — and here the word 'ādya' (first) does not mean merely 'in a fixed position' nor 'in proximity,' but rather 'that which exists at the beginning' — 'ādya' [means] 'born at the origin.'

body.text: tathā hy amīyāṃ varṇānāṃ parāvāgbhūmir iyam iha nirṇīyate yatraivaiṣām asāmayikaṃ nityam akṛtrimaṃ saṃvinmayam eva rūpam /
body.translated_text: For indeed, what is being determined here regarding these phonemes (<s>varṇas</s>) is the ground of supreme Speech (<s>parā vāk</s>), wherein alone their form is non-conventional, eternal, uncreated, and of the very nature of consciousness (<s>saṃvid</s>).

body.text:
saṃvinmaye ca vapuṣi sarvasarvātmakatā satatoditaiva / sā ca parameśvarī parābhaṭṭārikā tathāvidhaniratiśayābhedabhāginy api paśyantyādikāḥ parāparābhaṭṭārikādisphārarūpā antaḥkṛtya tattadanantavaicitryagarbhamayī / na hi tatra yan nāsti tat kvāpy astīti nyāyyam / parāmṛśata ca prathamāṃ pratibhābhidhānāṃ saṃkocakalaṅkakāluṣyaleśaśūnyāṃ bhagavatīṃ saṃvidam / tathāhi yat kiṃcic caram acaraṃ ca tat pāramārthikenānapāyinā rūpeṇa vīryamātrasārātmanā tadudbhaviṣyadīṣadasphuṭatame yadasphuṭatare yadasphuṭādivastuśatasṛṣṭikālo lakṣyamāṇatattadanantavaicitryaprathonnīyamānatathābhāvena saṃvidi bhagavadbhairavabhaṭṭārikātmani tiṣṭhaty eva / tathāvadhānātiśayarūḍhaiḥ sahasaiva sarvajñatābhūmir asaṃkucitaparamārthā
akṛtrimatadrūpā adhiśayyate eva parānugrahapavitritair abhyāsakramaśāṇanigharṣaniṣpeṣitatadapratyayarūpakampādyanantāparaparyāya vicikitsāmalaiḥ, savicikitsair api pratibhātakiyanmātravastudattasaṃkocā na tv akṛtrimā / yad āhuḥ śrikallaṭapādāḥ
body.translated_text: And in the body that is of the nature of <s>saṃvid</s> (consciousness), the state of being the self of everything is ever-arisen. And she, the supreme sovereign, <s>Parā Bhaṭṭārikā</s> (the Supreme Goddess), though partaking of such unsurpassed non-duality, having internalized <s>paśyantī</s> and the rest — which are the unfolding forms of <s>Parāparā Bhaṭṭārikā</s> (the Supreme-cum-non-supreme Goddess) and so on — is pregnant with the infinite variety of all those [levels]. For it is not logically tenable that what does not exist there could exist anywhere else. And one should reflectively apprehend (<s>parāmṛśata</s>) the blessed <s>saṃvid</s> (consciousness) called <s>pratibhā</s> (intuitive flash), the primal one, devoid of even a trace of the impurity of contraction. For thus: whatever is moving or unmoving, that, in its ultimately real and never-departing form, whose essence is sheer potency (<s>vīrya</s>), abides indeed in <s>saṃvid</s> — whose nature is the blessed Lord <s>Bhairava</s> — [whether] in the most slightly unmanifest [stage] from which it will arise, or in the more unmanifest, or at the time of the creation of hundreds of unmanifest objects, with its nature being progressively revealed through the spread of the infinite variety of each. Thus, by those who have ascended through the excellence of attention, the ground of omniscience — whose ultimate reality is uncontracted, whose nature is unartificial — is directly attained by those purified by supreme grace, whose impurities of doubt and other synonymous [afflictions] such as the trembling of non-apprehension have been ground away on the whetstone of progressive practice; even by those who still have doubt, it is touched in a contracted form proportional to whatever limited objects have appeared — but it is not unartificial [for them]. As the revered <s>Kallaṭa</s> has said:

body.text: Q: tuṭipāte sarvajñatvasarvakartṛtvalābha
body.translated_text: [Quote]: "Upon the cessation of the gap (<s>tuṭi</s>), the attainment of omniscience and omnipotence —"

body.text:
iti / evam eṣa svaprakāśaikarūpo 'py artho yuktyā pradarśyate / yad yat svasāmarthyodbhūtottarakālikārthakriyāyogyatādivaśaniḥśeṣyamāṇasatyatāvaśāvāptāvicalasavādavirodhāvabhāsisaṃmatakramikavikalpyamānanīlādiniṣṭhavikalpapūrvabhāvi nirvikalpasaṃvidrūpaṃ tattadvikalpanīyaviruddhābhimatanīlapītādyābhāsāvibhāgi bhavati, yathā citrajñānaśikharasthasaṃvinmecakabodhādi / yat tu tadviruddharūpanīlapītādyābhāsāvibhaktaṃ na bhavati tattadanantasvasāmarthyodbhūtanīlapītādyābhāsavikalpapūrvabhāgy api na bhavati, yathā nīlaikasākṣātkāri jñānam / bhavati cedam astamitodeṣyadubhayavikalpajñānāntarālavarty unmeṣapratibhādiśabdāgamagītaṃ nirvikalpakaṃ sasaṃvādaviruddhābhimatanīlādivikalpapūrvabhāvi / tasmāt tad anantāvabhāsāvibhāgamayam
eveti / ubhayoś ca jñānayor antarālam anapahvanīyāṃ jñānayor bhedād eva / tac ca saṃvidātmakam eva, anyathā tenaiva saṃvitsaṃskārocchede smaraṇādyanusaṃdhānādyayoga iti pratibhākhyasya dharmiṇaḥ sarvavādinaḥ praty avivāda eveti nāsiddhiḥ / saṃketavyutpattikālānavalambanāc cāsyāvikalpatvam eva /
body.translated_text: Thus. In this way, though this reality is of the nature of self-luminosity alone, it is demonstrated through reasoning. Whatever <s>nirvikalpa</s> (non-conceptual) awareness-nature precedes the conceptual cognitions (<s>vikalpa</s>) that determine blue and so forth — cognitions that are sequentially conceptualized, accepted as appearing in agreement, of unshakeable valid correspondence, whose truth-status is exhaustively determined by capacity for subsequent causal efficacy arisen from their own power — that [non-conceptual awareness] is undifferentiated with respect to the appearances of blue, yellow and so forth which are considered mutually contradictory and are the objects of those respective conceptualizations, just as the awareness at the summit of variegated cognition [is undifferentiated with respect to] the apprehension of dark-blue and so on. But what is not undifferentiated from the appearances of blue, yellow, and so forth — which are mutually contradictory forms — that also does not precede the conceptualizations of blue, yellow, etc., which arise through the infinite powers inherent in each respectively, just as a cognition that directly perceives blue alone [does not]. And this [non-conceptual awareness] exists, situated in the interval between conceptual cognitions of the past and the future, celebrated in scripture by the terms <s>unmeṣa</s> (opening forth), <s>pratibhā</s> (intuitive flash), and so on — it is non-conceptual and precedes the conceptual cognitions of blue and so forth that possess valid correspondence with [their objects]. Therefore, it is established that it is of the nature of undifferentiation from infinite appearances. And the interval between both cognitions is undeniable, precisely because of the difference between the two cognitions. And that [interval] is of the nature of <s>saṃvid</s> (awareness) alone; otherwise, if the impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) in awareness were severed by it, there would be no possibility of recollection, synthetic recognition, and so forth. Thus there is no dispute among all philosophical schools regarding the substrate (<s>dharmin</s>) called <s>pratibhā</s>, hence there is no fallacy of unestablished [subject]. And its non-conceptual nature is established because it does not depend on the occasion of learning linguistic conventions.

body.text:
sahajāsāmayikatathāparāmarśayogo hi jaḍavilakṣaṇasaṃvidrūpanāntarīyakaḥ / na vikalpatulyatvaṃ bhedānullāsāt / bhedasāratālambatayā tv arthabhāvaṃ kuryāt / vikalpānāṃ cāvikalpaṃ vinā nodayaḥ, asvātantryāt / asvātantryaṃ ca saṃketādismaraṇopāyatvāt, saṃketādismaraṇaṃ ca tathānubhavaṃ vinā kutaḥ / saṃvidaś ca praṅnyāyena kālādiparicchedābhāva iti ekaiva sā pārameśvarī pratibhā asmaduktimāhātmyakalpitā evaṃvidhaparicchinnasvabhāvāpi sarvātmaiva / madhye 'pi vartamānabhūtabhaviṣyadrūpavikalpāntaraprasavabhūr eva / tathā ca vivekakuśalair ālayavijñānam evam evopagatam / sasaṃvādatvaṃ ca tadanantarabhāvināṃ vikalpānāṃ darśitam eveti nāsiddho hetuḥ sādhyadharmiṇi, na caikāvabhāsivikalpasaṃvibhāgakāriṇi avikalpake vipakṣe sadā
vā kadācid api vā vartate, na ca tato 'sya vyāvṛttiḥ saṃdigdheti na viruddho nānaikāntiko na saṃdigdhavipakṣavyāvṛttiḥ, dṛṣṭāntadharmiṇy api citrajñānādau hetor evam evāsiddhatādidoṣā parihṛtā bhavanty eva / hetudoṣeṣu tu parihṛteṣu dṛṣṭāntādidoṣā niravakāśā eva ityādi bahu nirṇītakalpam aparair eveti kiṃ tadanubhāṣaṇakleśena / siddhaṃ tāvad dhy etat
body.translated_text: For the innate, non-conventional reflective apprehension of that-ness is an inseparable concomitant of the awareness-nature that is distinct from the insentient. It is not equivalent to <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual thought), because differentiation does not shine forth [in it]. However, if it rested upon differentiation as its essence, it would render the object [merely] existent [as differentiated]. And without the non-conceptual, conceptualizations (<s>vikalpa</s>) could not arise, due to their lack of independence (<s>asvātantrya</s>). And their lack of independence is because they depend on the means of recollection of conventions and so forth; and whence could the recollection of conventions and so forth come without such [direct] experience? And since awareness, by the logic [already stated], has no delimitation by time and so on, that one supreme <s>pratibhā</s> (intuitive flash) belonging to the Lord — though appearing with a delimited nature fabricated by the grandeur of our [limited] expression — is indeed the Self of all. Even in the middle [states], it is the very ground for the generation of conceptualizations in the form of past, present, and future. And thus by those skilled in discernment, <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (storehouse consciousness) has been understood in just this way. And the valid correspondence of the conceptualizations that follow it has already been demonstrated — hence the reason is not unestablished with respect to the subject (<s>dharmin</s>); nor does [the reason] ever or sometimes occur in the counter-example (<s>vipakṣa</s>) — namely, in the non-conceptual [awareness] that differentiates a portion of single-appearance conceptual awareness; nor is its exclusion from that [counter-example] doubtful. Therefore it is neither contradicted, nor inconclusive, nor of doubtful exclusion from the counter-example. In the example-substrate too — such as variegated cognition — the defects of unestablished [reason] and so on with respect to the reason are resolved in just the same way. And when the defects of the reason are resolved, the defects of the example and so forth find no scope — much more of this has been conclusively determined by others, so why the trouble of restating it? This much, then, is established:

body.text:
yat prātibhaṃ nikhilavaiṣayikāvabodha-pūrvāparāntaracaraṃ nikhilātmakaṃ tat /
tasyāṃ pralīnavapuṣaḥ paraśaktibhāsi glānir ghaṭeta kim abhāvavaśopakḷptā //
body.translated_text: That intuitive [awareness] (<s>prātibha</s>), which moves in the interstice before and after all objective cognitions, is the Self of all. For one whose body has dissolved in Her, who shines as the supreme power (<s>paraśakti</s>) — how could weariness (<s>glāni</s>), produced by the force of non-existence, befall [such a one]?

body.text:
śarīraprāṇādau paradhanasukhāsvādapaṭalam anālokya svasmin spṛśati hṛdaye glānim asamām /
praviṣṭā ced antar nikhilajagatīsūtisarasā parā devī hanta pravilasatu pūrṇaṃ havir iva //
body.translated_text: Without looking at the spread of others' wealth, pleasure, and so forth pertaining to body, <s>prāṇa</s>, and so on, one touches in one's own heart an incomparable weariness. If the supreme Goddess (<s>parā devī</s>), who is the creative sap of all the worlds, has entered within — ah! — let Her blaze forth fully, like an oblation [into the fire]!

body.text: tad uktaṃ spande
body.translated_text: This has been stated in the <s>Spanda</s> [kārikā]:

body.text:
Q: glānir vilumpikā dehe tasyāś cājñānataḥ sṛtiḥ /
Q: tad unmeṣaviluptaṃ cet kutaḥ sā syād ahetukā // SpaKā_3.8 //
body.translated_text: [Quote]: "Weariness (<s>glāni</s>) is that which plunders the body; its coursing arises from ignorance. If that [ignorance] is destroyed by <s>unmeṣa</s> (the opening forth of awareness), how could that [weariness] exist, being without cause?" (<s>Spandakārikā</s> 3.8)

body.text: var: a:: viluṇṭhikā>
body.translated_text: [Variant reading: <s>viluṇṭhikā</s> for <s>vilumpikā</s>]

body.text: iti /
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text:
Q: ekacintāprasaktasya yataḥ syād aparodayaḥ /
Q: unmeṣaḥ sa tu vijñeyaḥ svayaṃ tam upalakṣayet // SpaKā_3.9 //
body.translated_text: [Quote]: "When one is absorbed in a single thought, from which there arises another [thought] — that is to be known as <s>unmeṣa</s> (the opening forth); one should perceive it by oneself." (<s>Spandakārikā</s> 3.9)

body.text: iti ca /
body.translated_text: And thus.

body.text:
Q: māyīyakārmamalamūlam uśanti tāvad ajñānanāmamalam āṇavam eva bhadrāḥ /
Q: bījaṃ tad eva bhavajīrṇataroḥ parasmin saṃvinniśātadahane dahate kṣaṇena //
body.translated_text: [Quote]: "The blessed ones declare that what is rooted in <s>māyīya</s> (relating to <s>māyā</s>) and <s>kārma</s> (relating to action) <s>mala</s> (impurity) is indeed the <s>āṇava mala</s> (impurity of finitude), called ignorance — that alone is the seed of the tree of existence worn old [by transmigration]; in the fire of <s>saṃvid</s> (awareness), sharpened to a keen edge, it burns in an instant."

body.text: yathāhuḥ
body.translated_text: As they have said:

body.text: Q: malam ajñānam icchanti saṃsārāṅkurakāraṇaṃ /
body.translated_text: [Quote]: "They consider <s>mala</s> (impurity) to be ignorance, the cause of the sprout of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence)."

body.text: iti / tad evoktam
body.translated_text: Thus. That itself has been stated:

body.text: Q: tadunmeṣaviluptaṃ cet ... /
body.translated_text: [Quote]: "If that [ignorance] is destroyed by <s>unmeṣa</s>..."

body.text: iti / evam eva ca vyākhyātam adaḥ / anyathā glāner vilopakatvam asyāś cājñānāt saraṇam ajñānasya conmeṣeṇa vilopa iti kiṃ kena saṃśliṣṭam iti nṛpanirūpaṇaprāyam eva bhavet /
body.translated_text: Thus. And [the verse from the <s>Spandakārikā</s>] has been explained in just this way. Otherwise — that weariness is a plunderer of the body, that its coursing is from ignorance, and that ignorance is destroyed by <s>unmeṣa</s> — what would be connected with what? It would amount to nothing more than a king's [superficial] examination [of unrelated facts].

body.text: tad evaṃ bhagavatī parāvāgbhūmir garbhīkṛtasvasvātantryasattodbhaviṣyatpaśyantyādiviniviṣṭaparāparābhaṭṭārikādiprasarā tadgarbhīkāravaśāvivādaghaṭitasakalabhūtabhuvanabhāvādiprapañcaprabodhaikyacamatkārasārā parameśvarabhairavabhaṭṭārakāvirbhāvaprathitatathāvidhādbhūtabhūtaparamārthasvarūpā svātmavimaladarpaṇanirbhāsitānantasṛṣtisthitisaṃhāraikyamayamahāsṛṣṭiśaktir ādikṣāntarūpā athādyā ityādinā granthena niḥśeṣaṃ bhagavatā nirṇīyata iti sthitam /
body.translated_text: Thus, the blessed ground of <s>parā vāk</s> (supreme Speech) — having absorbed within herself her own <s>svātantrya</s> (absolute freedom), from whose very existence will arise <s>paśyantī</s> and the rest, pervading through the expansion of <s>Parāparā Bhaṭṭārikā</s> (the Supreme-cum-non-supreme Goddess) and so on; whose essence is the wonder of the unified awakening of the entire manifold of beings, worlds, states of existence, and so forth — [a manifold] incontrovertibly established by virtue of its being contained within her; whose own nature as supreme reality of such wondrous character is made manifest through the appearance of the blessed Lord <s>Bhairava</s>; whose power of the great creation — consisting of the unity of the infinite [cycles of] creation, maintenance, and dissolution reflected in the spotless mirror of her own Self — has the form [extending] from the initial [phoneme] <s>a</s> to the final <s>kṣa</s> — she, the primordial one, is conclusively determined in her entirety by the blessed [author] through the text beginning with 'and the first' (<s>athādyā</s>). This is established.

body.text: tad evaṃ sthite granthārtho nirṇīyate / akārādivisargāntaṃ śivatattvam / kādiṅāntaṃ dharādinabho 'ntaṃ bhūtapañcakam / cādiñāntaṃ gandhādiśabdāntaṃ tanmātrapañcakam / ṭādiṇāntaṃ pādādivāgantaṃ karmākṣapañcakam / tādināntaṃ ghrāṇadiśrotrāntaṃ buddhikaraṇapañcakam / pādimāntaṃ mano'haṃkārabuddhiprakṛtipuruṣākhyaṃ pañcakam /
body.translated_text: Now, the meaning of the text is determined as follows, given what has been established. From <s>a</s>-kāra to <s>visarga</s> is the <s>Śiva tattva</s>. From <s>ka</s> to <s>ṅa</s> is the pentad of elements (<s>bhūtapañcaka</s>) — from earth (<s>dharā</s>) to space (<s>nabhas</s>). From <s>ca</s> to <s>ña</s> is the pentad of subtle elements (<s>tanmātrapañcaka</s>) — from smell (<s>gandha</s>) to sound (<s>śabda</s>). From <s>ṭa</s> to <s>ṇa</s> is the pentad of organs of action (<s>karmākṣapañcaka</s> / <s>karmendriya</s>) — from the feet (<s>pāda</s>) to speech (<s>vāk</s>). From <s>ta</s> to <s>na</s> is the pentad of cognitive faculties (<s>buddhikaraṇapañcaka</s> / <s>jñānendriya</s>) — from the organ of smell (<s>ghrāṇa</s>) to the organ of hearing (<s>śrotra</s>). From <s>pa</s> to <s>ma</s> is the pentad called mind (<s>manas</s>), ego (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>), intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), <s>prakṛti</s> (primal nature), and <s>puruṣa</s> (the individual self).

body.text: vāyvādiśabdavācyā yādayo vakārāntā rāgavidyākalāmāyākhyāni tattvāni / dhārayanti pṛthagbhūtatayābhimānayantīti dhāraṇāni / dvāv atra ṇicau prayojyaprayojakabhāvadvairūpyāt / tathāhi dhriyante svātmany eva sarve bhāvāḥ prakāśātmani paramaparipūrṇe pade bhairavātmani sarvātmani / yathoktaṃ śivadṛṣṭau
body.translated_text: The <s>tattvas</s> (principles) denoted by the sounds beginning with <s>vā</s> — that is, <s>ya</s> and the others up to <s>va</s> — are those called <s>rāga</s> (attachment), <s>vidyā</s> (limited knowledge), <s>kalā</s> (limited agency), and <s>māyā</s>. [The term] <s>dhāraṇā</s> (that which sustains/maintains): they sustain [beings] by causing the conceit of separate existence. There are two causative suffixes (<s>ṇic</s>) here, on account of the twofold nature of the caused and the causer. For thus: all entities are sustained in one's own Self alone — in the luminous (<s>prakāśātman</s>) state of <s>Bhairava</s>, which is supremely full, which is the Self of all. As stated in the <s>Śivadṛṣṭi</s>:

body.text:
Q: ātmaiva sarvabhāveṣu sphurannirvṛtacidvapuḥ /
Q: aniruddhecchāprasaraḥ prasaraddṛkkriyaḥ śivaḥ //
body.translated_text: [Quote]: "The Self alone, shining forth in all entities, whose body is blissful consciousness, whose flow of will is unobstructed, whose seeing and acting radiate forth — [that is] <s>Śiva</s>."

body.text: iti / yathoktaṃ spande
body.translated_text: Thus. As stated in the <s>Spanda</s> [kārikā]:

body.text: Q: yatra sthitam idaṃ sarvaṃ
body.translated_text: [Quote]: "In whom all this is established —"

body.text:
iti / evaṃ svātmany eva prabhāsvare prakāśanena dhriyamāṇān bhāvān dhārayati svayam aprakāśībhāvena jaḍatāsvabhāvedaṃbhāvāspadatāprāpaṇena prakāśayati parameśvara eva / punar apy ahaṃbhāvenaivācchādayati / tad iyaṃ bhagavatsadāśiveśadaśā śuddhavidyāmayī ekena ṇicā dhvanitā / tatrāpi ca yad idantāyā ahantayācchādanaṃ tadācchādanīyedantopapattāv upapadyate, na ca śuddhaparameśvaracinmayarūpāpekṣaṃ bhinnaprathātmakam idantākhyaṃ rūpam upapadyata ity ācchādanīyānupapattau tadvaśena tadācchādakatāpy ahaṃbhāvasya nopapanneti tathāvidheśvarabodhānupapattiḥ / tadanupapattau ca na kiṃcid bhāseta kāraṇābhavād ity uktam asakṛt / bhāsate cedaṃ tadbhāsāvyatirekarahitam api parameśvaraśaktita eva bahiḥ prathate kāraṇāntarāsaṃbhavāt
svasaṃvidi ca saṃvida eva sarvamayatvaprathanāt / tad evaṃ svātmarūpaṃ jagad bhedena bhāsamānaṃ prakāśātmany eva ahamātmani bhāsate sāmānādhikaraṇyenetīyatā etāvad avaśyam evākṣiptaṃ yathā īśvara eva kasyāpi veditur bhinnān vedyān ahantayā paśyati yaś cāsau ko 'pi vedayitā so 'pi bhāsanāt svātmamaya eveti svātmani tathāvidhāḥ śaktīr adhiśete yābhir asau tadaiva bhinnavedyavedakībhāvam upāśnuvīta / rāgādibhir eva ca tathāvidhatvam asyeti rāgādaya eva dhriyamānān bhāvān uktanyāyena dhārayantam īśvaraṃ prati prayojakatāṃ gacchanti / atas tasyaiva puṃstvavyapadeśakāraṇaikabhūtā dvitīye ṇici utpanne dhāraṇaśabdavācyāḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus. In this way, He himself — the Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>) — sustains the entities that are being maintained in His own Self, which is self-luminous, through illumination; [and] He illuminates [them] by bringing them to the condition of objecthood through [their apparent] insentient nature, by [seemingly] not making [them] luminous. And again, He conceals [them] through the very sense of 'I' (<s>ahaṃbhāva</s>). This, then, is the state of the blessed Lord <s>Sadāśiva</s>, consisting of <s>śuddhavidyā</s> (pure knowledge), which is indicated by the one [i.e., first] causative suffix (<s>ṇic</s>). And there too, the concealment of objectivity (<s>idantā</s>) by subjectivity (<s>ahantā</s>) is possible only when there is the occurrence of objectivity to be concealed. But the nature called objectivity (<s>idantā</s>), which is of the character of differentiated manifestation, is not possible with reference to the pure, consciousness-constituted nature of the Supreme Lord — and therefore, when the thing to be concealed is impossible, the concealing nature of the sense of 'I' is also impossible, and thus the realization of such a [level of] the Lord would be impossible. And if that were impossible, nothing at all would appear, due to the absence of a cause — this has been stated repeatedly. Yet this [world] does appear; and though not different from His appearance, it manifests externally through the power of the Supreme Lord alone, since no other cause is possible, and because in one's own awareness, it is awareness itself whose nature as the Self of all is manifest. Thus, the world, whose nature is the Self, though appearing as differentiated, shines in the luminous [consciousness] alone, in the Self characterized as 'I' — through co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>). This much is necessarily implied: that it is the Lord alone who perceives the differentiated objects through the sense of 'I' for some knower or other; and whoever that knower is, he too, by virtue of being illuminated, is of the nature of the Self alone. Thus, [the Lord] presides over such powers within His own Self, by which He simultaneously takes on the state of differentiated object and knower. And it is through <s>rāga</s> (attachment) and the other [<s>kañcukas</s>] alone that such a condition belongs to him — therefore <s>rāga</s> and the rest assume the role of causer with respect to the Lord who sustains the entities being sustained in the manner described. Hence, being the sole cause of the designation of his limited-subjecthood (<s>puṃstva</s>), they are denoted by the word <s>dhāraṇā</s> when the second causative suffix (<s>ṇic</s>) is introduced.

body.text: ṇijutpattāv api sarvatraiva prakṛtyarthānvayānapāyaḥ / dhriyamāṇatayā prakāśamānasyaiva hi dhāryamāṇatā prakāśanāsaṃjñā upapadyate yataḥ / yathoktaṃ mayaiva śivadṛṣṭyālocane
body.translated_text: Even when the causative suffix is introduced, the connection with the meaning of the verbal root is never lost anywhere. For the state of being sustained (<s>dhāryamāṇatā</s>), which is designated as illumination (<s>prakāśana</s>), is logically possible only for that which is appearing as being maintained. As I myself have stated in the <s>Śivadṛṣṭyālocana</s>:

body.text: Q: preryo 'pi sa bhaved yasya śaktatā nāma vidyate /
body.translated_text: [Quote]: "Even that which is to be impelled must be one which possesses the capacity called power."

body.text:
iti / bhartṛharir api
Q: apravṛttasya hi praiṣe pracchāder loḍ vidhīyate /
Q: pravṛttasya yadā praiṣas tadā sa viṣayo ṇicaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus. And <s>Bhartṛhari</s> also [says]: [Quote]: "For when the imperative (<s>loṭ</s>) is prescribed in the sense of command for one who has not yet commenced [action], it concerns concealment and the like; but when the command is for one already engaged [in action], then that is the domain of the causative (<s>ṇic</s>)."

body.text:
iti / tad evaṃ dhāraṇaśabdenāparaśāstreṣu kañcukanāmadheyaprasiddhāny eva tattvānīha nirūpitāni / yad uktaṃ śrītantrasāre
Q: dhārayanti paśoḥ pāśān bhāvān svātmamayāṃs tathā /
Q: vidyāmāyāniyatyādyāḥ śodhyās tena prayatnataḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus. In this way, by the word <s>dhāraṇā</s>, the very <s>tattvas</s> (principles) that are well known in other treatises under the name <s>kañcuka</s> (coverings) are here expounded. As stated in the revered <s>Tantrasāra</s>: [Quote]: "<s>Vidyā</s> (limited knowledge), <s>māyā</s>, <s>niyati</s> (determinism), and the others — they sustain the bonds of the bound soul (<s>paśu</s>) and likewise the entities that are of the nature of the Self. Therefore they should be purified with effort."

body.text: iti / yat tu śrīsomānandapādair dhāraṇaśabdenāṅgāni nirūpitāni pakṣāntarāśrayaṇena tatra parapakṣasarvadṛśyatvaprathanam ātmany abhiprāyaḥ / teṣāṃ hīdṛśī śailī
body.translated_text: However, that the revered <s>Somānanda</s> has expounded the limbs [of yoga] by the word <s>dhāraṇā</s>, adopting an alternative interpretation — his intention there is the manifestation of all that is to be seen from the rival position within one's own Self. For such is the method of those [masters]:

body.text:
Q: svapakṣān parapakṣāṃś ca niḥśeṣeṇa na veda yaḥ /
Q: svayaṃ sa saṃśayāmbhodhau nimajjaṃs tārayet katham //
body.translated_text: [Quote]: "One who does not know completely both one's own positions and rival positions — how can such a one, himself sinking in the ocean of doubt, ferry [others] across?"

body.text: iti / śādikṣāntaṃ mahāmāyāvidyeśvarasadāśivaśaktyākhyaṃ tattvapañcakam / tathā hi māyātattvasyopari vidyātattvādhaś ca avaśyaṃ tattvāntareṇa bhāvitavyaṃ yatra vijñānākalānāṃ sthitiḥ / yathoktam
body.translated_text: From <s>śa</s> to <s>kṣa</s> is the pentad of <s>tattvas</s> called <s>mahāmāyā</s>, <s>vidyā</s> (pure knowledge), <s>īśvara</s>, <s>sadāśiva</s>, and <s>śakti</s>. For thus: between the <s>māyā tattva</s> above and the <s>vidyā tattva</s> below, there must necessarily be posited an intermediate principle, where the <s>vijñānākalas</s> (those freed from intellect [but not from <s>mala</s>]) have their abode. As stated:

body.text: Q: māyordhve śuddhavidyādhaḥ santi vijñānakevalāḥ //
body.translated_text: [Quote]: "Above <s>māyā</s> and below <s>śuddhavidyā</s> (pure knowledge), there exist the <s>vijñānakevalas</s> (those isolated in pure awareness)."

body.text: iti / tathā hi mahāmāyābhāve māyāpade pralayakevalānām avasthitiḥ vidyāpade ca vidyeśvarādīnām iti kim iva tad vijñānakevalāspadaṃ syāt / ata eva vidyāpadapracyutānām apy eṣāṃ bhedamayabhāvarāśigatabhinnavedyaprathānudayān māyīyābhidhānamalānullāse
body.translated_text: For thus: in the absence of <s>mahāmāyā</s>, the <s>pralayakevalas</s> (those dissolved at cosmic dissolution) would have their station at the level of <s>māyā</s>, and the <s>vidyeśvaras</s> (lords of knowledge) and others at the level of <s>vidyā</s> — then what would serve as the abode of the <s>vijñānakevalas</s>? Precisely for this reason, even though they have fallen from the level of <s>vidyā</s>, since the manifestation of differentiated objects pertaining to the mass of states characterized by differentiation does not arise [for them], and since <s>māyīya mala</s> (impurity pertaining to <s>māyā</s>) does not manifest [in them] —

body.text: Q: tatra vijñānakevalo malaikayuktaḥ
body.translated_text: [Quote]: "There, the <s>vijñānakevala</s> is endowed with a single <s>mala</s> (impurity) —"

body.text: ity ajñānātmakāṇavamalāvalambitvaṃ śrīpūrvaśāstre kathitam / ta eva śuddhavidyāpadānugrahād bodhitā mantratadīśādibhāvabhāgino bhavantīti tatraivoktaṃ
body.translated_text: Thus, their dependence on <s>āṇava mala</s> (the impurity of finitude), which is of the nature of ignorance, has been stated in the revered <s>Pūrvaśāstra</s> (the earlier scripture, i.e. the <s>Mālinīvijayottara</s>). Those very ones, when awakened through the grace of the level of <s>śuddhavidyā</s> (pure knowledge), become partakers of the states of <s>mantra</s>, <s>mantreśvara</s> (lord of <s>mantras</s>), and so on. As stated there as well:

body.text: Q: vijñānakevalān aṣṭau bodhayām āsa pudgalān /
body.translated_text: [Quote]: "He awakened eight <s>vijñānakevala</s> souls —"

body.text: ityādinā
body.translated_text: And so forth, [continuing with]:

body.text: Q: mantramaheśvareśatve saṃniyojya...
body.translated_text: [Quote]: "Having appointed [them] to the lordship of <s>Mantra</s> and <s>Mantreśvara</s>..."

body.text: ityādinā ca / keṣu cit tu śāstreṣu sā mahāmāyā bhedamalābhāvopacārād vidyātattvaśeṣatayaiva nirṇīyate / kvacit punar ajñānamalasadbhāvoparodhān māyātattyapucchatayā yathā keṣu cit śāstreṣu
body.translated_text: And so forth. However, in certain treatises, that <s>mahāmāyā</s> is determined to be merely a subdivision of the <s>vidyā tattva</s>, through the figurative attribution of the absence of <s>bheda-mala</s> (impurity of differentiation, i.e. <s>māyīya mala</s>). In other [treatises], again, it is [treated as] the tail-end of the <s>māyā tattva</s>, on account of the obstruction constituted by the presence of <s>ajñāna-mala</s> (the impurity of ignorance, i.e. <s>āṇava mala</s>), just as in certain treatises:

body.text: Q: rāgatattvaṃ puṃsy eva lagnam
body.translated_text: [Quote]: "The <s>rāga tattva</s> (principle of attachment) is attached to <s>puruṣa</s> (the individual self) itself —"

body.text: iti na pṛthak parāmṛṣṭam, yathā vehaiva śrītrikāgameṣu niyatikālau na pṛthaṅ nirūpitau / atra mate vidyādyanāśritaśivāntaṃ brahmapañcakaṃ nirṇeṣyate caitat / eṣāṃ ca tattvānaṃ bṛhattvaṃ bṛṃhakatvaṃ ca prāyo bhedasamuttīrṇatvāt saṃsārasūtikartṛtvāc ca / evam etāni catustriṃśattattvāni prakriyātmanā sthitāny akāram eva ādirūpatayā bhajante / tatredaṃ vicāryate / prathamataḥ śivatattvam avarge, tato bhūtānītyādi yāvad ante śaktitattvam iti ko 'yaṃ sṛṣṭisaṃhārajñaptisthityavatārakramāṇāṃ madhyāt kramaḥ / sarvatra ca śrīmālinīvijayottarasiddhātantrasvacchandādiśāstreṣu kṣakārāt prabhṛty avargāntaṃ pārthivādīnāṃ śivāntānāṃ tattvānāṃ niveśa uktaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus it is not separately examined, just as here in the sacred <s>Trika</s> scriptures, <s>niyati</s> (determinism) and <s>kāla</s> (time) are not separately treated. In this system, the fivefold group of <s>Brahman</s> from <s>Vidyā</s> onward up to <s>Śiva</s> will be determined — and this too. And the greatness (<s>bṛhattva</s>) and expansiveness (<s>bṛṃhakatva</s>) of these <s>tattvas</s> is mostly because they transcend difference and because they are the progenitors of <s>saṃsāra</s>. Thus these thirty-four <s>tattvas</s>, established in their procedural form, partake of the letter 'a' alone as their primordial form. Now this is examined here: first the <s>Śiva-tattva</s> in the <s>avarga</s>, then the elements and so on, up to the <s>Śakti-tattva</s> at the end — what is this order among the orders of creation, withdrawal, knowledge, abiding, and descent? And everywhere in the sacred scriptures — <s>Mālinīvijayottara</s>, <s>Siddhatantra</s>, <s>Svacchanda</s>, and others — the placement of <s>tattvas</s> from earth onward up to <s>Śiva</s> is stated beginning from the letter 'kṣa' up to the <s>avarga</s>.

body.text:
Q: ādyaṃ dhārikayā vyāptaṃ tatraikaṃ tattvam iṣyate /
Q: ekam ekaṃ pṛthak kṣārṇaṃ padārṇam anuṣu smaret //
body.translated_text:
Quote: 'The first is pervaded by <s>dhārikā</s>; there one <s>tattva</s> is accepted.
One should remember each <s>kṣa</s>-letter separately, the <s>pada</s>-letter in the <s>anu</s>-[letters].'

body.text:
ityādinā / tatraiva ca punar bhinnayonimālinībhaṭṭārikānusāreṇa phakārādīnām abhinnayonimātṛkāniveśāvāptatattvāntarasthitīnām api
Q: phe dharātattvam uddiṣṭaṃ dādijhānte 'nupurvaśaḥ /
Q: trayoviṃśaty abādīni /
ityādinā pārthivāditattvayojanā nirūpitā / punar api ca tatraiva śrīvidyātrayānusāreṇa
body.translated_text: and so on — the assignment of <s>tattvas</s> beginning with earth is set forth. And again there itself, following the threefold <s>Vidyā</s>:

body.text: Q: niṣkale padam ekārṇaṃ tryarṇaikārṇadvayaṃ dvaye /
body.translated_text: Quote: 'In the partless, the one-lettered <s>pada</s>; the three-lettered and one-lettered pair in the two [others].'

body.text: iti parāparābhaṭṭārikānusāreṇa oṃkāraṃ śivatattvam aghore ity atra śaktitattvam ityādikrameṇa pārthivāditattvanirūpaṇā yojitā / śrīmadaparābhaṭṭārikābhiprāyeṇa ca
body.translated_text: Thus, following <s>Parāparā Bhaṭṭārikā</s>, the <s>Śiva-tattva</s> is assigned to <s>Oṃkāra</s>, and at 'aghora' the <s>Śakti-tattva</s>, and so on — the determination of <s>tattvas</s> beginning with earth is arranged in that order. And according to the intent of the blessed <s>Aparā Bhaṭṭārikā</s>:

body.text:
Q: sārdhenāṇḍadvayaṃ vyāptam ekaikena pṛthag dvayam /
Q: aparāyāḥ samākhyātā vyāptir eṣā vilomataḥ //
body.translated_text:
Quote: 'A pair of cosmic eggs is pervaded by one and a half; each pair separately by one.
This pervading of <s>Aparā</s> is declared in reverse order.'

body.text: ityādinā phaṭkāre pārthivaprākṛtāṇḍadvayaṃ, huṃkāre māyīyaṃ, hrīṃkāre śāktam aṇḍaṃ ceti tattvaniveśaḥ / śrīparābhaṭṭārikāvyāptinirūpaṇe ca
body.translated_text: And so on — in 'phaṭ' the earthly and <s>prākṛta</s> pair of cosmic eggs, in 'huṃ' the <s>māyīya</s> [egg], and in 'hrīṃ' the <s>śākta</s> cosmic egg — such is the placement of <s>tattvas</s>. And in the determination of the pervading of <s>Parā Bhaṭṭārikā</s>:

body.text:
Q: sārṇena tritayaṃ vyāptaṃ triśūlena caturthakam /
Q: sarvātītaṃ visargeṇa parā vyāptir udāhṛtā //
body.translated_text:
Quote: 'The triad is pervaded by the syllable; the fourth by the trident.
That which transcends all, by <s>visarga</s> — this is declared as the pervading of <s>Parā</s>.'

body.text:
ity anyathaiva prakriyāyojanaṃ nirūpitam / punar api mātṛkāsadbhāvaratiśekharakuleśvarādimantrabhaṭṭārākādyabhiprāyeṇānyathānyathā ca / aparatantreṣv apy evam eva viparyastaprāyaṃ bahu bahuśo nirūpitam / tat punar iha sarvam evānyatheti paridṛśyata iti mahān ayam āgamavidaḥ svakaṭakakṣobha iva sarvavināśakaḥ samudbhūtaḥ / na ca sāṃketikam idaṃ yena puruṣecchāvaśopakalpitena rūpeṇa cānyathānyathā nirūpyamāṇam iha saṃgataṃ bhavet, yathā dākṣiṇātyāḥ cauraśabdena odanaṃ vyapadiśanti, saindhavās tu tenaiva dasyum, odanaṃ tu krūraśrutyā, tayā tu kāśmīrikā vituṣitayavagodhūmataṇḍulān iti / sāṃketikatve hy anavasthitatvād apāramārthikatvāc ca śodhyaśodhakabhāvādyanupayogād anirūpaṇīyatvam eva syāt / saṃketasyāpi paramārthasattaiva
/ na hi saṃketo nāma anyaḥ kaś cid ṛte parameśvarecchātaḥ / prasiddho hi naḥ saṃketo bhagavadicchāprakalpitas tannāmākṣaralipyādigatāpyāyanādikarmavidhijanitatacchāntikādiphalasaṃpatter iti cet / tarhy ekenaiva saṃketena sarvavastusaṃpattau kiṃ saṃketāntarāśrayeṇa / tadāśrayaṇe vā svaśāstritaśāstrāntarīyalaukikapārṣadadaiśikaghanakṛtapratipuruṣaniyatādyanantasaṃketaniveśapūrvakaṃ tad api nirūpyam eva / na tāvadbhir upayogaḥ, etāvataiva kāryasiddhir ity api nirakṣarakukṣikuharair ucyamānaṃ śrūyamāṇaṃ ca śobhata eva /
body.translated_text: Thus a completely different procedural arrangement is set forth. And again, according to the intent of the <s>Mātṛkā</s>, <s>Sadbhāva</s>, <s>Ratiśekhara</s>, <s>Kuleśvara</s>, and other <s>mantra-bhaṭṭārikā</s> deities, it is set forth differently in each case. And in other <s>tantras</s> too, much that is mostly inverted has been set forth in many ways. Now here all of this appears to be otherwise again — thus this great [source of] confusion has arisen for those who know the scriptures, like a tumult in one's own army that destroys everything. And this is not merely conventional, such that, being set forth differently by different people according to forms fabricated by the will of individuals, it could be consistent here — just as southerners designate cooked rice by the word 'caura' (thief), while the people of Sindh designate a robber by that same word but call rice by the harsh-sounding [word], while Kashmiris use that [harsh word] for dehusked barley and wheat grains. For if it were conventional, since convention is unstable and non-ultimate, the relationship of purifier and purifiable and so on would be useless, and there would be nothing to determine at all. The ultimate reality of convention itself is real. For convention is nothing other than the will of the Supreme Lord. We know well that convention is fabricated by the Lord's will, since the performance of prescribed rituals of nourishment and so on pertaining to His names, letters, scripts, and so forth yields results such as pacification. If so, then when all things are accomplished by one single convention alone, what need is there to resort to another convention? And if one does resort to that, then this too must be determined, preceded by the placement of the infinite conventions — those established in one's own scripture, those of other scriptures, the worldly, the sectarian, the regional, the dense, the person-specific, the fixed, and so on — of endless number. That so many are not needed, that the purpose is accomplished by just this much — even this, when said and heard by those whose bellies are mere hollow caves without letters, is indeed splendid!

body.text:
avikalā bhagavadicchā na vicārapadavīm adhiśete iti ced alaṃ granthadhāraṇavācanavyākhyānavicāraṇādimithyāyāsena, parityājya evāyaṃ gurubhāraḥ, tūṣṇīṃbhāvaśaraṇair eva stheyam, bhagavadicchaivottāraṇīyam uttārayet / tad icchaiva anugrahātmā evaṃvicāraṇāyāṃ paryavasāyayati / na khalu pādaprasārikayaiva sukhaṃ sayānair bhuñjānaiś ca svayam avimṛśadbhiḥ svāpekṣatīvratarādiparameśvarānugrahotpannādhikādhikasūkṣmatamavimarśakuśaladhiṣaṇāpariśīlanaparāṅmukhair vā sthātavyam iti / tat sarvadā vimṛśyam idaṃ vartata iti etāvan na jahīmaḥ / tad atrāvadhārya sthīyatāṃ yāvat pariharāmaḥ sarvam idaṃ kiṃ cin na vastutaś codyajātaṃ parameśvaryāṃ parāvāgbhuvy anuttaradurghaṭakāritātmakanirapekṣasvātantryasārāyāṃ
pāratantryāṃśaleśamātraparamāṇunāpy anuparaktāyām iti / prāyaḥ prāg eva pratisamāhitam adaḥ / tathāpi vistarataḥ parihriyate / yat tāvad uktaṃ śivatattvaṃ tataḥ pṛthivītyādīti ko 'yaṃ krama iti / tan na kaś cit krama iti brūmaḥ / akramaṃ yad etat paraṃ pārameśvaraṃ vicitraṃ garbhīkṛtānantavaicitryaṃ svātantryaṃ trikārtharūpaṃ tad evaitat / tathā hi yeyam aparā parāparā parābhaṭṭārikā pārameśvarī bhairavīyā sattā sā sadāśivatattvānāśritaśaktitattvasyāpy uparivṛttis tadantasyāpy āsanapakṣīkṛtatvāt / tathā hi
body.translated_text: If one objects: 'The complete will of the Lord does not submit to the path of investigation' — then enough with the vain labor of holding, reciting, explaining, and investigating texts! This heavy burden should simply be abandoned; one should take refuge in silence alone; the Lord's will alone will uplift whomever it will uplift. But it is that very will, whose nature is grace, that brings one to rest in such investigation. Indeed, one should not stand with legs outstretched, comfortably reclining, eating, not reflecting on things oneself, nor turning away from the cultivation of increasingly subtle reflective intelligence produced by the Supreme Lord's grace that is more intense according to one's own fitness. Therefore, this is always to be reflected upon — this much we do not abandon. So let it be firmly determined here, while we set aside all of this: not a single objection is really substantive when directed against the Supreme Goddess, the ground of <s>Parā Vāk</s> (Supreme Speech), whose essence is the sovereign freedom of the nature of <s>anuttara</s> (the Supreme) — accomplishing the impossible — who is not tinged even by the slightest atom of a fraction of dependence. Most of this has indeed been settled already. Nevertheless, it is resolved in detail. Now, as to what was said — 'the <s>Śiva-tattva</s>, then earth and so on — what is this order?' — to that we say: there is no order whatsoever. That which is this supreme, belonging to the Supreme Lord, variegated, having absorbed infinite variety within itself, sovereign freedom, of the nature of the meaning of <s>Trika</s> — that alone is this. For thus, the blessed <s>Aparā</s>, <s>Parāparā</s>, and <s>Parā Bhaṭṭārikā</s>, the supreme <s>Bhairavī</s> existence — she is situated even above the <s>Śakti-tattva</s>, which is not dependent on <s>Sadāśiva-tattva</s> and below, because she has made even that her seat. For thus:

body.text: Q: īśvaraṃ ca mahāpretaṃ prahasantam acetanam /
body.translated_text: Quote: '<s>Īśvara</s> too, the great corpse, laughing, without consciousness,'

body.text: ity anena sadāśivāntam āsanaṃ nādāntapakṣaniviṣṭaṃ śrīpūrvaśāstropasaṃhṛtam
body.translated_text: by this [verse], the seat extending up to <s>Sadāśiva</s>, situated within the domain of <s>nādānta</s>, is concluded in the sacred <s>Pūrvaśāstra</s> —

body.text: Q: ity etat sarvam āsanam
body.translated_text: Quote: 'All this is the seat,'

body.text: ity uktvā
body.translated_text: having stated this,

body.text: Q: tasya nābhyutthitaṃ śaktiśūlaśṛṅgatrayaṃ smaret
body.translated_text: Quote: 'One should contemplate the three peaks of the power-trident risen from its navel.'

body.text: iti śaktivyāpinīsamanātmakaśṛṅgatrayam uktaṃ, tatrāpy aunmanasordhvakuṇḍalikāpadaparamadhāma sitakamalatrayarūpatayā nirūpitam ity etat paramāsanaṃ parāparyantatvād iti / tadupari ca devīnāṃ sthitir iti /
body.translated_text: Thus the three peaks consisting of <s>Śakti</s>, <s>Vyāpinī</s>, and <s>Samanā</s> are stated. And even there, the supreme seat is determined in the form of three white lotuses as the stages of <s>Unmanā</s>, <s>Ūrdhvakuṇḍalikā</s>, and the supreme abode, because it is the ultimate limit of <s>Parā</s>. And above that is the station of the Goddesses.

body.text: tat paraṃ paśyantyākhyaṃ jñānaśakter eva paryantadhāma nādākhyarūpam atikramaṇīyatvenaiva sthitam / yathoktaṃ śivadṛṣṭau
body.translated_text: That supreme abode called <s>Paśyantī</s> is the ultimate domain of the power of knowledge alone, having the form called <s>nāda</s>, established as that which must be transcended. As stated in the <s>Śivadṛṣṭi</s>:

body.text:
Q: athāsmākaṃ jñānaśaktir yā sadāśivarūpatā /
Q: vaiyākaraṇasādhūnāṃ sā paśyantī parā sthitiḥ //
body.translated_text:
Quote: 'Now our power of knowledge, which is the <s>Sadāśiva</s> form —
for the grammarians and correct speakers, she is <s>Paśyantī</s>, the supreme station.'

body.text: iti / pratyagātmani hi buddhiḥ paśyantī rudradevatā paraṃ sadāśivajñānaśaktāv eva anāśritaśivaśaktyātmani viśrāmyati / mano'haṃkārayor brahmaviṣṇudevatayor vaikharīmadhyamāpade patyor īśasadāśivakriyāśaktipadam eva parā pratiṣṭhābhūr iti tāvad āgamasiddhaṃ svasaṃvedanabṛṃhitaṃ ca / tat paśyantyupari parābhūmir bhagavatī yatra sarvam abhedenaiva bhāti ca vimṛśyate ca / yady api hi vidyāpade māyāpade 'py abhedena bhāsanā sthitāpi tatra vimarśo 'nyathā / vidyāpade hīdam iti pramātṛprameyajātam ekato 'hamātmani saṃkrāmet tadācchāditaṃ vimṛśyate
body.translated_text: For the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), which is <s>Paśyantī</s>, whose deity is <s>Rudra</s>, rests in the inward Self, precisely in the supreme power of knowledge of <s>Sadāśiva</s>, whose nature is the non-dependent <s>Śiva-Śakti</s>. For <s>manas</s> (mind) and <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego), whose deities are <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>, who preside over the stages of <s>Vaikharī</s> and <s>Madhyamā</s> — the domain of the power of action of <s>Īśa</s> and <s>Sadāśiva</s> alone is the supreme ground of establishment. This much is established by scripture and confirmed by self-experience. Above <s>Paśyantī</s>, the ground of <s>Parā</s>, the blessed Goddess, where everything shines in non-difference and is reflected upon in non-difference. For although at the level of <s>Vidyā</s> and even at the level of <s>Māyā</s>, manifestation in non-difference persists, the reflective awareness there is otherwise. For at the level of <s>Vidyā</s>, the totality of knowers and knowables, being unified on one side in the Self, is reflected upon as covered by that:

body.text: Q: aham idam
body.translated_text: Quote: 'I am this.'

body.text: iti / tad etat samāne cidātmany adhikaraṇe ubhayaṃ pratibimbitam abhedenaivāvabhāsamānaṃ sāmānādhikaraṇyam uktam / ata eva
body.translated_text: This is what is called <s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s> (co-referentiality) — both reflected in the same substratum of consciousness, shining in complete non-difference. And therefore:

body.text:
Q: īśvarāvasthāyāṃ parāparātmikāṃ daśāṃ bhāvā bhajante, yathaiva māyādhvany aparāṃ, na tu
saiva parāparaśaktir aparā vā
body.translated_text: Quote: 'In the state of <s>Īśvara</s>, things partake of the <s>parāparā</s> (supreme-non-supreme) condition, just as in the course of <s>Māyā</s> they partake of the <s>aparā</s> (non-supreme) condition; but it is not that the <s>parāparā</s> power itself is the <s>aparā</s>.'

body.text: iti yad īśvaratattvaṃ praty abhihitaṃ śrīmadutpaladevapādais tat pradarśitāgamaviparyāsaśaṅkāyuktam iti na mantavyam / mantramaheśādiṣu tu rūpaṃ bodhaikaparamārtham api aparabodhaikaparamārthād anyad
body.translated_text: What was stated by the blessed <s>Utpaladeva</s> regarding the <s>Īśvara-tattva</s> — this should not be thought to be tainted by the suspicion of contradicting the scripture shown above. But in the <s>Mantramāheśvaras</s> and others, the form, though having consciousness alone as its ultimate reality, is different from that whose ultimate reality is non-supreme consciousness alone:

body.text: Q: aham aham idaṃ punar idam eva
body.translated_text: Quote: 'I, I; this again is only this.'

body.text: iti saṃvit / vijñānākalānāṃ tu bodhaikaparamārthe 'pi rūpe
body.translated_text: Such is the awareness. But for the <s>vijñānākalas</s>, even in the form whose ultimate reality is consciousness alone:

body.text: Q: nāhaṃ nedam
body.translated_text: Quote: 'Not I, not this.'

body.text: iti saṃvidaprabodhād aham ity eva tatra prabuddham / pralayakevalinām idam aham ity aprabuddham eva / atra māyāpade ca tannirvikalpakatābhāsena yady apy asti tathāvidha eva prāṇabhūto vimarśas tathāpi tadrūpavyavahārakasya tatprasādāsāditasattākasyāpi tadavyatiriktasyāpi paścāttanasya vimarśasya
body.translated_text: Due to the non-awakening of awareness, only 'I' is awakened there. For the <s>pralayakevalins</s>, 'this' and 'I' remain entirely unawakened. And here at the level of <s>Māyā</s>, even though there exists, through the appearance of its non-conceptual nature, a reflective awareness of precisely that kind which is the life-breath, nevertheless for the subsequent reflective awareness — which belongs to one who transacts in that form, whose existence is obtained by its grace, and who is non-different from it —

body.text: Q: idaṃ śarīrādy aham, ahaṃ yo'sau jñātā, idaṃ ghaṭādikam, idaṃ yat tat jñeyam
body.translated_text: Quote: 'This body and so on is I; I am he who is the knower; this pot and so on is this; this is what is the knowable.'

body.text:
iti bhedenaiva vimarśarūpatayā vyavahāro vikalpātmaiva / tatra tu tathāvidhatve kāraṇāntarāsaṃvedanāt kalpyamāne 'pi ca kāraṇe punar api tathāvidhabodhāvinirbhāgamātraparyavasānat tasyaivāvikalpasaṃvidātmanas tathāsāmarthyaṃ tathāsāmarthyayogād eva ca tadanantavaicitryātmakatvam ity aiśvaryam anapāyi siddhyet / asyāṃ ca sattāyām aiśvaryam anapetaṃ yato vaikharyātmani evaṃ māyīye vedye 'pi vā madhyamāmaye dhāmni bhāsanātireky api saṃbhāvya evaṃ vimarśaḥ / atra tu parasaṃvidi yathaiva bhāsā tathaiva vyavahāramayo 'pi vimarśaḥ / tena jala iva jalaṃ jvālāyām iva jvālā sarvathābhedamayā eva bhāvā bhāsante, na tu pratibimbakalpenāpi / kevalaṃ yāvad eṣāpi parameśvarī upadeśāya nirūpyate tāvad adharasattākḷptā tathā bhavati / evaṃ ca bhāsātmakaṃ bhairavarūpaṃ
svataḥsiddham anādi prathamaṃ sarvataḥ caramaṃ ca sarvataś ca vartamānam iti kim aparaṃ tatrocyatām / tattvabhāvavikāsam ātmamayam ātmaikyenaiva svaprakāśaṃ prakāśayati tathaiva ca vimṛśaty anapetatathācamatkāratve 'pi / yac ca tat tathā vimarśanaṃ tad bhāvimāyīyānantasṛṣṭisaṃhāralakṣakoṭyarbudaparārdhasākṣātkāriṇi bhāsane bhavet tathārūpam eva bhavati / tathābhavac ca tad yadi sṛṣṭau prāthamikaṃ mādhyamikaṃ vā padaṃ bhāsanād vimṛśet tatpūrvasya taduttaravyabhicāraṇāśaṅkāsaṃbhāvanānapagamād aparipūrṇam aprathitetarabhāvarāśi khaṇḍitābhedaṃ katham anirvyūḍhaparabhairavamahādhāmasamāśritādhastanapaśyantyādiniṣṭhabhedāsūtraṇakalaṅkaṃ tathāvidhavastvapoṣaṇavasanāmamātrībhūtaparābhaṭṭārikārūpaṃ
tat kim api rūpaṃ bhavet / etādṛśadhārārohaṇābhāve ca na kiṃ cit idaṃ vijṛmbhamāṇaṃ bhāseta iti na vrajatv apūrṇatā mā prathiṣṭha bhāvarāśir abhedakathā khaṇḍyatāṃ mā nirvākṣīd bhairavāśrayatā bhedakalaṅkam udvahatu nāmadheyamātreṇa paratvam iti vaktuṃ yuktam /
body.translated_text: Thus the transaction, being in the form of reflective awareness in difference alone, is of the nature of conceptual thought (<s>vikalpa</s>) alone. But there, when a different cause for such a condition is postulated due to the non-perception [of the real cause], and even for that postulated cause the inquiry terminates in mere non-separation from that very non-conceptual consciousness, then precisely that non-conceptual consciousness possesses such capacity; and by virtue of possessing such capacity, it possesses the nature of infinite variety — thus lordship (<s>aiśvarya</s>) would be established as never-departing. And in this state of being, lordship is not absent, since even in the knowable that belongs to <s>Māyā</s> or in the domain of <s>Vaikharī</s> or <s>Madhyamā</s>, it is conceivable that manifestation exceeds [difference], and such is reflective awareness. But here, in the supreme consciousness, just as is the manifestation, so too is the reflective awareness — including the transactional. Therefore, just as water in water, as flame in flame, things shine as entirely non-different in every way — not even in the manner of a reflection. Only insofar as this Supreme Goddess is being described for the sake of instruction, having been constituted with a lower level of being, she becomes so. Thus the <s>Bhairava</s>-form, consisting of manifestation, self-established, beginningless, first in every respect and last in every respect and present in every respect — what more can be said about it? It illuminates the unfolding of <s>tattvas</s> and existences, which is identical with itself, by identity with itself, as self-luminous; and it reflects upon them in the same way, even while the wonder of that nature is undiminished. And whatever that reflective awareness is, it would be of precisely such a form in the manifestation that directly perceives ten million, hundred million, and trillion future creations and withdrawals belonging to <s>Māyā</s>. And if that, in creation, were to reflect upon the first or middle stage as distinct from the manifestation, then — since the suspicion that what preceded it might deviate from what follows it could not be removed — being incomplete, with the remaining mass of existences not having become manifest, with its non-difference broken, how could it be the form of <s>Parā Bhaṭṭārikā</s>, who has become a mere garment for the nourishment of such a reality, having attained the character of the lower stations of <s>Paśyantī</s> and the rest with their stain of threading difference, not having ascended to the great abode of supreme <s>Bhairava</s>? And without such an ascending stream, nothing of this that is unfolding would shine at all. So let not incompleteness prevail; let the mass of existences not become manifest; let the discourse of non-difference be broken; let <s>Bhairava</s>-nature not be realized; let the stain of difference be borne; let supremacy be by name alone — it is proper to say so!

body.text:
tad etad eva bhavati saṃgacchate ca yadi prathamataraṃ sarvacarame evamābhāsā patantī tatraiva vimarsenāpi padaṃ bandhayet / sa hi caramo bhāgas tathā tāvat svātmarūpaṃ bibhrat tatsvātmarūpanāntarīyakatāsvīkṛtatadanantanijapūrvapūrvatarādibhāgāntaro bhāsamāno vimṛśyamānaś ca pūrṇa eva / tatpurvo 'pi bhāgas taduttarabhāgapṛṣṭhapātivṛttapūrvaparipūrṇabhāsāsāravimarśatādātmyāt taduttararūpaparipūrṇatām ajahat svayaṃ ca svarūpanāntarīyakatāhaṭhakṛṣṭasvapūrvapūrvatarādibhāgāntarābhogo bhāsamāno vimṛśyamānaś ca tathaivākhaṇḍita ity evaṃ tatpūrvapūrvagatā bhāsā tattaddvitrādinijanijottarabhāgabhāsā vibhāge labdhabhairavabhāvasvabhāvāvyabhicārānurodhabalasvīkṛtasvasvapūrvabhāgacamatkāra ekaikam api paraṃ pūrṇā bhavati
yāvat svaprakāśanijabhairavābhimatanikaṭataravarti rūpaṃ / tad eva svecchāviśrāntidhāma vā bhairavākhyaṃ vapuḥ / svayam eva tadvimarśakuśalā bhavata prasaṃkhyānaparāḥ / hradagiritaruprabhṛtyupādhisaṃkocena rahite tadvaty api vāraṇyānīpradeśe durād akhaṇḍitā dṛṣṭir evam evākhaṇḍitatām upāśnuvānā bhairavabodhānupraveśaṃ prati saṃpradāyatām āsādayeta /
body.translated_text: But this alone comes about and is coherent: if, falling upon the manifestation of such a nature in the very first [moment] which is the ultimate last, [awareness] would establish its footing there by reflective awareness as well. For that last part, while bearing its own essential nature, shining and being reflected upon as containing within itself all its own prior, more prior, and so on parts through the inseparability from its own nature — is indeed complete. The part prior to it too, through identity with the reflected awareness of the prior, complete manifestation whose essence has fallen upon the back of its subsequent part — not abandoning its completion through its subsequent form — itself shining and being reflected upon as containing the expanse of its own prior, more prior, and so on parts forcibly drawn in by the inseparability from its own nature — is likewise unbroken. Thus the manifestation proceeding through each prior and prior part, having in the partition [of each part] obtained the non-deviation from the <s>Bhairava</s>-nature gained through its own respective subsequent two, three, and so on parts — each one singly is also supremely complete, up to the form nearest to that which is the self-luminous, own-most cherished <s>Bhairava</s>. That alone is the abode of repose in one's own will, the body called <s>Bhairava</s>. Be skilled yourselves in reflecting upon it, devoted to contemplation! Just as in the open forest terrain, free from delimiting conditions such as lakes, mountains, and trees, an unbroken gaze from afar — even so, attaining such unbrokennness, [the gaze] would arrive at the authentic tradition of entry into <s>Bhairava</s>-consciousness.

body.text: Q: nirvṛkṣagiribhittyādau deśe dṛṣṭiṃ vinikṣipet /
body.translated_text: Q: One should cast one's gaze upon a place devoid of trees, mountains, walls, and so forth /

body.text:
ityādi / anyathā bhāgaśaḥ pāte prathamabhāgād ārabhya yadi vā niravayavam evaitat ka iva aparasaṃvedanebhyo 'purṇābhimatebhyo viśeṣaḥ / viśeṣas tu garbhīkṛtānantavaicitryacamatkārakṛta ivāpūrṇasaṃvidantarebhyaḥ pūrṇābhimatasaṃvedanasyeti svayam eva jānantu sopadeśāh pārameśvarāḥ / parameśaśaktipātakiraṇāvikasite tu paśujanahṛdayakuśeśaye na asmadīyair vacanaśatair apy atitīkṣṇābhidheyasūcibhir api saṃbhedo 'tha vikāso 'tha vitarītuṃ śakyaḥ / ghaṭe 'pi evam eva paripūrṇo dṛṣṭipātaḥ / tatrāpi hy avikalpā saṃvit jhagiti caramabhāga eva nipatati / tatas tu kramād vikalpasaṃvida āyāntya ācaramanikaṭabhāgād antastarām antastamāṃ cānupraviśantīti kim anyena / tad evam evehāpi śivatattvaṃ sadā avikalpam eva vikalpasūti svātantryasarasam
anādi sarvādibhūtaṃ siddham / atra tāvan na vimatiḥ / tat tu paripūrṇaṃ tathā bhavati yadi sarvacaramāṃ pārthivīm eva bhuvam adhiśete / dharāsaṃvid dhi tathā dharāṃ viṣayatayāpy abhedenābhāsayed vimṛśec ca yadi tatsvarūpasarvasvāvabhāsavimarśayoḥ vyāpriyeta /
body.translated_text: ityādi / Otherwise, if the gaze falls part by part, beginning from the first portion, or if this [experience] is entirely without parts, what distinction would there be from other cognitions deemed incomplete? The distinction, however, is as if produced by the <s>camatkāra</s> (rapture) of having absorbed infinite variety within itself — this is how the cognition deemed complete differs from other incomplete cognitions — let those who have received instruction, the devoted followers of the Supreme Lord, know this for themselves / But in the lotus of the heart of the bound soul (<s>paśu</s>), which has not been caused to bloom by the rays of the grace-descent (<s>śaktipāta</s>) of the Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśa</s>), even by hundreds of our words, even by the extremely sharp needles of expressed meaning, neither piercing nor blossoming can be brought about / With regard to a pot too, the casting of the gaze is equally complete in just the same way / For there too, non-conceptual (<s>avikalpā</s>) consciousness (<s>saṃvit</s>) falls all at once upon the very last portion; then gradually, as conceptual cognitions (<s>vikalpa-saṃvid</s>) arise, they enter inward and ever more inward from the portion nearest to the last — so what more need be said? / Thus in exactly this way here too, the <s>Śiva-tattva</s> (Śiva-principle) is established as eternally non-conceptual, yet pregnant with the capacity to give birth to conceptualization, whose essence is the sap of <s>svātantrya</s> (absolute autonomy), beginningless, the source of all things / On this point there is no dispute / But it becomes completely full (<s>paripūrṇa</s>) only when it presides over the very last level of reality, namely the earthly plane (<s>pārthivī bhū</s>) itself / For the consciousness that is <s>dharā</s> (earth) can manifest earth as its object and yet in non-difference, and can reflectively appropriate it (<s>vimṛśet</s>), only if it operates through both the manifestation (<s>avabhāsa</s>) and reflective awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>) of the entire essential nature of that [earth-principle] /

body.text:
svarūpasatattvaṃ cāsyāḥ paripūrṇaprasaratsvātantryakḷptāprarūḍhabhedatatpūrvakaikarasabhedāvabhāsatadvaśoditasakucaccitsvātantryasattāmayamāyāgrāhakatadgrāhyacakrāvibhedātmakpradhānatadvikāradhītattvatatpariṇāmātmakāhaṃkāratanmūlakāraṇapūrvakatanmātravargaprasṛtakhādijalāntabhūtavargādharavṛttitayāvasthānam / sā hi yāvad ākṣepeṇaiva vartamānā tāvat svarūpasatattvaiva / yāvad eva pañcaguṇatvāt tanmātrāṇy ākṣipet tāvat tāny ākṣipyamāṇāni nijasvarūpopakḷptaye samākṣiptaprāktanaprātiṣṭhikamūlāntaraparamparānubandhisvakapūrvakamūlāny eva / na hy
Q: upādānābhimatakāraṇasvarūpānanvayaḥ kāryasattāyāṃ syāt
iti nyāyyam / nimittakāraṇādīni kathaṃ cin nānvīyur ity ucyetāpi kadā cit / etac ca prakṛtavighātakam anyatra tadabhidhānapravaṇe śāstre niṣkuṣya niṣkuṣitam asmābhir eveti neha vitatam /
body.translated_text:
And the true essential nature of this [earth-consciousness] is its abiding in the manner of a substratum, through the following succession: the <s>bhedas</s> (differentiations) that have not yet arisen, fashioned by the <s>svātantrya</s> (autonomy) of completely full expansion, and the preceding unitary relish of those [not-yet-arisen differentiations]; the manifestation of differentiation arising under the power of that, and the contracted <s>cit-svātantrya</s> (consciousness-autonomy) that arises under its sway; the existence constituted by <s>māyā</s> (illusion) whose nature is that contracted autonomy; the undivided totality of the grasper (<s>grāhaka</s>) and the circle of the grasped (<s>grāhya</s>) belonging to that [<s>māyā</s>]; the <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) whose nature is non-differentiation of those, and the transformations thereof; the <s>buddhi-tattva</s> (intellect-principle) and its modifications; the <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego-principle) that is a transformation of that; the group of <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) preceded by the root cause (<s>mūla-kāraṇa</s>) grounded in that; and the group of gross elements beginning with <s>ākāśa</s> (space) and ending with <s>jala</s> (water) that have issued forth from them / For as long as [earth-consciousness] exists by way of containing [all these] within itself, just so long is it truly its own essential nature / Insofar as it draws in the <s>tanmātras</s> by virtue of their fivefold quality, those <s>tanmātras</s>, being drawn in, have as their own root — for the purpose of constituting their own essential nature — the entire chain of prior foundational roots that were previously drawn in / For indeed,
Q: it is not logically tenable that the material cause (<s>upādāna-kāraṇa</s>), in its essential nature, would fail to continue into the existence of the effect
— this is the principle / One might sometimes say that efficient causes (<s>nimitta-kāraṇa</s>) and the like do not in some manner continue [into the effect] / But this [objection], which obstructs the matter at hand, has been thoroughly uprooted by us elsewhere, in the treatise devoted to expounding that topic — so it is not elaborated here /

body.text: tad evaṃ prathamaṃ tāvad dharā tato 'pi jalaṃ tathaiva svarūpasākalyena bhāsamānaṃ vimṛśyamānaṃ ca tadbhāsāvimarśacamatkāram antaḥkṛtatathāvidhadharaṇitattvasaṃskārasattākaṃ pūrayed eveti yāvad ante saiva pūrṇasaṃvidbhagavatī śivātmaiva / tad anenaivopadeśayuktinayena
body.translated_text: Thus, first of all <s>dharā</s> (earth), then <s>jala</s> (water) as well, each shining forth and being reflectively appropriated in the totality of its own nature, would fill up the <s>camatkāra</s> (rapture) of that shining-and-awareness, a rapture whose existence is constituted by the impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) of each such earth-principle internalized within — until in the end that [consciousness] is none other than the blessed complete consciousness (<s>pūrṇa-saṃvid-bhagavatī</s>), whose very nature is <s>Śiva</s> / Therefore, by this very method of instruction and reasoning —

body.text:
Q: pradeśamātram api brahmaṇaḥ sarvarūpam ekaikatrāpi ca tattve ṣaṭtriṃśattattvamayatvaṃ
śāstreṣu nirūpitam / evaṃ ca śrīspandaśāstropadeśo
body.translated_text:
Q: Even a mere point of <s>Brahman</s> contains all forms, and in each and every <s>tattva</s> (reality-principle) there is the nature of all thirty-six <s>tattvas</s>
— this has been established in the scriptures / And thus the teaching of the sacred <s>Spandaśāstra</s> —

body.text:
Q: didṛkṣayeva sarvārthān yadā vyāpyāvatiṣṭhate /
Q: tadā kiṃ bahunoktena svayam evāvabhotsyate //
body.translated_text:
Q: When, with the mere desire to see, one pervades and abides in all objects,
Q: then — what need of many words? — one will know of oneself //

body.text: ity ayaṃ hṛdayaṃgamīkartavyaḥ / carameṇa pādena tad evātra sūcitam iti kim anyat / yac ca yena vinā na bhavati tat tāvatsvarūpaṃ yathā śiṃśapātvaṃ vṛkṣatvasvarūpaṃ pārameśasvātantryātirohitaniyativijṛmbhāyām / yat tu yāvatsvarupaṃ na bhavati tat tena vinā bhavaty eva yathā vṛkṣatvam ṛte śiṃśapātvāpavādaḥ /
body.translated_text: — this [teaching] should be taken to heart / By the last quarter-verse, precisely this has been indicated here — what more is there to say? / Moreover, that without which something does not exist constitutes its essential nature up to that point, just as <s>śiṃśapā</s>-ness (being an Ashoka tree) is the essential nature of tree-ness, within the domain of the rule-expansion that is not concealed by the <s>svātantrya</s> (autonomy) of the Supreme Lord / But that which is not [a thing's] essential nature up to that extent can indeed exist without it, just as tree-ness [can exist] apart from <s>śiṃśapā</s>-ness — this is the exception /

body.text:
na bhavanti ca dharādīny uttarottaratattvāni jalādi pūrvapūrvaṃ vineti tāvatsvarūpāṇy eva / dharā hi na jalaṃ vinā bhavet sruter eva kāṭhinye darśanād ity evaṃkrameṇa bhūtāni tanmātrair vinā katham, tāny api indriyajṛmbhayā vinā, indriyāṇy api tattathāvidhādhyavasāyena vinā / sarvāṇi caitadādyāvibhaktānvitasūkṣmarūpamūlakāraṇavinākṛtāni na bhavanti / mūlaprakṛtir api bhogyā bhoktāraṃ tadbhogyavibhāgabhāgitvād eva saṃkucitaṃ saṃkocavaśād eva ca svātmārohitakālakalādipāśajālaṃ saṃvidātmakaṃ cāntareṇa kathaṃ / saṃvidaś cākhaṇḍarūpāyāḥ kathaṃ saṃkocakāraṇasvātantryaṃ māyāparaparyāyaṃ vinā saṃkucitatvam / svātantryaṃ ca saṃkoce 'saṃkucitatāsāratatsaṃkocatāratamyākṣepi bhavad īṣadasaṃkucitāsaṃkuciteṣaḍvikāsivikasvararūpaṃ
virahayya naiva bhavet / sarvam eva cedaṃ prathamānaṃ svatantraparipūrṇaprathāsārabhairavaṃ vinā kiṃ cid eva neti svasaṃvitsiddho 'yaṃ tattvakramaḥ / srutir api jalātmikā kāṭhinyaṃ vinā kveti dharāpi pūrvikā salile 'stv iti kathyamānam api kiṃ naś chedayet / pratyuta paripūrṇasarvātmakabhairavabhaṭṭārakātmakaparāsaṃvitparipoṣaṇāyaiva syāt / sarvaś cāyaṃ parāparābhaṭṭārikādirūpapaśyantyādisattāsamayodbhaviṣyadīṣatsphuṭasphuṭatarāditattvabhedānusāreṇa parābhaṭṭārikāmahasi taducitenaiva vapuṣā virājate / tatra hi niḥśvasyeva / haste draviṇam asan na kva cid api syāt / bhaviṣyad api vastu caramam api prathamaprakāśe bhāsetaiva / kevalam ekarasatadbhedasārasphuṭarūpāpekṣayā bhaviṣyattā / tathā hi bhaviṣyati kalkī haniṣyaty adharmaparān ityādi
yadi na prakāśitaṃ tat kathaṃ purāṇeṣu nibaddham / kvacana sarge babhūva kalkī tathaiva vyadhita iti cet kiṃ sa evāsāv anya eva vā, anyaś ced aprakāśo 'sau, sa eva cet kathaṃ kālabhedaḥ / akālakalitaś cet katham iva /
body.translated_text:
And <s>dharā</s> (earth) and the other successively higher <s>tattvas</s> (reality-principles) such as <s>jala</s> (water) and so forth do not exist without their respective prior ones — hence they are essentially constituted by them up to that point / For <s>dharā</s> (earth) could not exist without <s>jala</s> (water), since hardness is observed to arise from moisture alone — and by the same progressive reasoning, how could the gross elements exist without the <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements), or those without the unfolding of the sense-faculties (<s>indriyas</s>), or the sense-faculties without the determinate cognition (<s>adhyavasāya</s>) of that kind belonging to them? And none of these, beginning with that [earth], can exist without the root cause (<s>mūla-kāraṇa</s>) whose nature is the subtle form that is undifferentiatedly connected with them from the start / And <s>mūla-prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) too, being the enjoyed (<s>bhogyā</s>), how could it exist without the enjoyer (<s>bhoktṛ</s>) — who is contracted precisely because of participating in the division of that enjoyment, and who, by virtue of that very contraction, has the net of fetters such as <s>kāla</s> (time), <s>kalā</s> (limited agency), and so on superimposed upon himself — and without that which is of the nature of consciousness (<s>saṃvid-ātmaka</s>)? And how could consciousness (<s>saṃvid</s>), whose nature is undivided, be contracted without <s>svātantrya</s> (autonomy) — which is synonymous with <s>māyā</s> — as the cause of contraction? And <s>svātantrya</s> in the mode of contraction could never exist without being that whose own nature is the slightly uncontracted, the uncontracted, the six-fold expanded and the blossomed — [all arising] through its drawing in of the gradations of contraction and the essence of non-contraction within that contraction / And this entire [universe] as it manifests would be nothing whatsoever without <s>Bhairava</s>, whose essence is autonomous, completely full manifestation — this hierarchy of <s>tattvas</s> is established through one's own direct awareness (<s>sva-saṃvit-siddha</s>) / Even moisture (<s>sruti</s>), whose nature is water, where would it be without hardness? — thus even the statement that <s>dharā</s> (earth), being prior, resides in <s>salila</s> (water) — does it not cut through [our doubt]? On the contrary, it serves precisely to nourish the supreme consciousness (<s>Parā-saṃvit</s>) whose nature is the blessed <s>Bhairava</s>, who is completely full and the Self of all / And this entire [manifestation], in accordance with the differentiation of <s>tattvas</s> that are somewhat clear, clearer, and so on, which arise at the time of the existence of <s>Paśyantī</s> and the other [levels of speech] whose nature is [that of] <s>Parāparā Bhaṭṭārikā</s> (the Supreme-and-non-Supreme Goddess) and so forth — all this shines in the radiance of <s>Parā Bhaṭṭārikā</s> (the Supreme Goddess) with precisely the form appropriate to it / For there, as if upon an exhalation / If there is no wealth in hand, it exists nowhere at all / Even a future entity, even the very last [in the series], would shine in the primordial Light / It is merely its futurity that [appears], in relation to the clear form whose essence is the differentiation of that unitary relish / For consider: "<s>Kalkī</s> will arise and will destroy the adherents of <s>adharma</s>" and so forth —
if this were not illuminated [in the primordial Light], how could it be recorded in the <s>Purāṇas</s>? If one objects that in some [previous] creation <s>Kalkī</s> did come into being and did act thus — then is this the same [<s>Kalkī</s>] or a different one? If different, then he is unmanifest [in this creation]; if the same, how [can there be] difference of time? And if he is not conditioned by time, then how indeed [can he be future]? /

body.text:
cittvād viśvarūpatvād iti cet tarhy akālakalite saṃvidātmani satataviśvaśaktyaviyukte svātantryavaśasaṃkocavikāsāvabhāsitasaṃhṛtisṛṣṭisatāvirūddhaikarūpatadātmakavapuṣi parameśvare 'smajjihvāgrahṛdayānapāyini bhairavabhaṭṭārake sarvam astīty asmābhir upanyasyamānam eva muktamandākṣaṃ kathaṃ nādriyate vivṛtatarakaṇṭham eva vā svayam eva na nirṇīya nirūpyate / tasmāt śivatattvam idam anādyantaṃ svayaṃ prathamānaṃ pūrṇatātmakanirapekṣatāmātrasatattvasvātantryasāram antaḥkroḍīkṛtyātmataikaparamārthaṃ tattvajātaṃ parasaṃvidi satatoditatvāt sarvāvirodhitvān nikhilānugrāhakatvāc ca avasthāśabdavyapadeśāsahiṣṇau yāvad akālakalitam āsīnaṃ bhairavarūpam avatiṣṭhate tāvad etacchāstrasamucitenaiva mahāsṛṣṭyādirūpeṇa
na tu mitasṛṣṭyādikrameṇa---iti siddham / sa eṣa eva saṃpuṭayoge asmadgurūṇāṃ saṃpradāyaḥ śuddhaparasattayā sarvasyaiva ekaikatattvasya nikhilasya ca tattvaughasya saṃpuṭīkaraṇāt / vakṣyate cāpy etat /
body.translated_text:
If one says: because [the Supreme] is of the nature of consciousness (<s>cit</s>) and because it is of the nature of the universe — then in that case, within the Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>), who is of the nature of consciousness, not conditioned by time, eternally inseparable from the power of the universe, whose body is the non-contradictory unity of creation and dissolution that are manifested and withdrawn through the force of <s>svātantrya</s> (autonomy) in contraction and expansion, who never departs from the tongue, grasp, and heart of us — in <s>Bhairava Bhaṭṭāraka</s>, all exists — how is it that what is being set forth by us is not heeded with open eyes, or why is it not determined and established by [the objectors] themselves with fully open throat? / Therefore, this <s>Śiva-tattva</s> (Śiva-principle), without beginning or end, self-manifesting, whose essence is the <s>svātantrya</s> (autonomy) that is the true reality of mere self-sufficiency constituting complete fullness (<s>pūrṇatā</s>), having gathered within itself the host of <s>tattvas</s> (reality-principles) whose supreme meaning is identity with its own nature — because it is eternally arisen in the supreme consciousness (<s>para-saṃvid</s>), because it is non-contradictory with everything, and because it is the bestower of grace upon all — it abides in the form of <s>Bhairava</s>, not conditioned by time, intolerant of being designated by the word "state" (<s>avasthā</s>), and with a form appropriate to this scripture, namely that of the great creation (<s>mahā-sṛṣṭi</s>) and so forth,
not by the sequence of limited creation and so forth — this is established / This is indeed the tradition (<s>saṃpradāya</s>) of our teachers regarding the <s>saṃpuṭa-yoga</s> (union of the two [hemispheres/covers]) — the interlocking of each and every <s>tattva</s> and of the entire flood of <s>tattvas</s> by means of the pure supreme reality (<s>śuddha-para-sattā</s>) / And this will be stated further /

body.text: paśyantīdaśāyāś cārabhya bhedāsūtraṇātmāṃśāṃśollāsa iti tataḥ prabhṛty eva śodhyaśodhakabhāva iti tāvad vyavasthānāpahnavanīyā / yathoktam
body.translated_text: And beginning from the level of <s>Paśyantī</s>, there is the efflorescence of aspects and sub-aspects whose nature is the threading-forth of differentiation (<s>bheda-sūtraṇa</s>) — hence from that point onward there obtains the relationship of that-which-is-to-be-purified and that-which-purifies (<s>śodhya-śodhaka-bhāva</s>) — this much, at least, is an arrangement that cannot be denied / As it has been said —

body.text:
Q: yat sadāśivaparyantaṃ pārthivādyaṃ ca suvrate /
Q: tat sarvaṃ prākṛtaṃ jñeyaṃ vināśotpattisaṃyutam //
body.translated_text:
Q: That which extends up to <s>Sadāśiva</s>, and that which begins with <s>pṛthivī</s> (earth), O virtuous one,
Q: all that is to be known as natural (<s>prākṛta</s>), conjoined with destruction and origination //

body.text:
ityādi / paśyantī ca parāparābhaṭṭārikāsatattvā paraśakter eva svātmaśaktir darpaṇakalpā yatra tat parābhaṭṭārikāsvarūpam eva cakāsti pratibimbavat / yac ca rūpaṃ sadā bimbe pratibimbe caikatāparamārthaṃ mukhaparāmarśamātram iva na tat pratibimbitam ucyate tanmātrasattvād eva / yat tu tatrānyathā tathā ca bhāti mukhākāra iva pūrvāparavāmadakṣiṇatādiviparyayād etad evāpi tad evāpi tad eva pratibimbitam ucyate tac ca tatsamānadharmaiva bhavati na tu vijātīyam / evaṃ ca paśyantīsatattvaparāparāvimalamukurikāyāṃ tattattathāvidhoktakramapūrṇapṛthivyāditattvasāmagrīnirbharamantas tathāvidhasahajākṛtrimapāramārthikānapāyikādiparāmarśakroḍīkāreṇaiva vartamānam api
śrīparābhaṭṭārikāvapuḥ pratibimbam arpayat svarūpānyathātvāsahiṣṇukādiparāmarśānanyathābhāvenaiva tatparaikarūpaṃ parāmṛśyaṃ dharaṇyambhaḥprabhṛti tathollasadbhedasūtraṇatayā sajātīyāyāṃ vimalāyāṃ ca yāvat pratibimbayati tāvad dharāditattvānāṃ viparyāsa evopajāyate /
body.translated_text:
ityādi / And <s>Paśyantī</s>, whose true reality is <s>Parāparā Bhaṭṭārikā</s> (the Supreme-and-non-Supreme Goddess), is the self-directed power (<s>svātma-śakti</s>) of the supreme <s>Śakti</s> herself, like a mirror, in which the essential nature of <s>Parā Bhaṭṭārikā</s> (the Supreme Goddess) shines as if in a reflection (<s>pratibimba</s>) / Now, that form which is always in the prototype (<s>bimba</s>) and whose ultimate reality is identity with [the form in] the reflection — being as it were a mere apprehension of the face [itself] — that is not called "reflected," precisely because only that much [i.e. the identical form] exists / But that which appears there [in the reflection] otherwise and yet also thus — like the form of a face with its reversal of front and back, left and right — this too, which is also indeed that [original], is what is called "reflected," and it possesses the same properties as that [original], not being of a different kind / Thus, in the <s>Paśyantī</s>-reality that is the stainless mirror of <s>Parāparā</s>, the body of the glorious <s>Parā Bhaṭṭārikā</s> (Supreme Goddess) — though it exists through the very act of gathering into itself the authentic, innate, ultimate, and imperishable reflective awareness (<s>parāmarśa</s>) of that kind, with its interior replete with the full complement of <s>tattvas</s> (reality-principles) such as <s>pṛthivī</s> (earth) and so forth, complete in the aforesaid sequence —
when it casts its reflection, the object to be reflectively apprehended, namely <s>dharaṇī</s> (earth), <s>ambhas</s> (water), and so forth, is perceived as identical with that [Supreme] precisely because the reflective awareness of [its] intolerance of any alteration of its own nature [undergoes] no alteration — yet insofar as [these tattvas] gleam forth in the manner of threaded differentiation, being reflected in that [mirror] which is of the same kind and stainless — to that extent a reversal (<s>viparyāsa</s>) of the <s>dharā</s> (earth) and other <s>tattvas</s> arises /

body.text:
yat parasaṃvidi śaktitattvaṃ tad eva parāparātmani pṛthivītattvaṃ, yat tu dharātattvaṃ tac chaktitattvam iti kṣakārāt prabhṛti dharādīnāṃ sthitiḥ / bhagavadbhairavabhaṭṭārakas tu sadā pūrṇo 'nantasvatantra eva na viparyasyate jātucid api cidrūpātirekādyabhāvād ityuktaṃ bahuśaḥ / parātmani parāmarśe parāmarśaikatattvāny eva tattvāni parāmarśaś ca kādikṣāntaśāktarūpaparamārtha iti tatra abheda eva / parāparāyāṃ tu bhedābhedātmakatā pratibimbanyāyena / sā ca parāparā parāmarśamayī kādikṣāntavarṇamālāśarīrā yāvat svordhvavyavasthitaparābhaṭṭārikāniviṣṭatattvapratibimbāni dhārayati tāvat teṣv evāmāyīyāśrautakādikṣāntaparamārthaparāmarśeṣūrdhvādharaviparyāsena tattvāni saṃpadyante ūrdhvabimbādharapratibimbadhāmasvabhāvamahimnā---iti
tātparyam / tataḥ pṛthivī kṣakāra ityādi śodhyarūpāpekṣayā na kiṃcid viruddham / tatrāpi paradaśānapāyāt eṣa eva kādivarṇasaṃtānaḥ / tatraiva ca svāṃśodrekāt svāṃśāntarvartimadhyamāpadollāsāt svarūpavartamānavaikharīrūpaprāvaṇyāc ca varṇamantrapadarūpatā śodhyāṃśavṛttir ity āstām / aprakṛtam etan nirṇītaṃ ca mayaiva śrīpūrvaprabhṛtipañcikāsu / yad apy uktaṃ śrīmālinībhaṭṭārikānusāreṇa
body.translated_text:
