What is the <s>Śakti-tattva</s> (power-principle) in the supreme consciousness (<s>para-saṃvid</s>), that itself becomes the <s>pṛthivī-tattva</s> (earth-principle) in the <s>Parāparā</s> aspect; and what is the <s>dharā-tattva</s> (earth-principle) [in <s>para-saṃvid</s>], that becomes the <s>Śakti-tattva</s> — thus the arrangement of <s>dharā</s> (earth) and the other [tattvas] proceeds from the phoneme <s>kṣa</s> onward / But the blessed <s>Bhairava Bhaṭṭāraka</s> is forever full, infinitely autonomous — he is never reversed at any time, because there is no excess over or absence of the nature of consciousness (<s>cit</s>) — this has been stated many times / In the supreme reflective awareness that is <s>Parā</s>, the <s>tattvas</s> are nothing other than the single reality of reflective awareness itself, and reflective awareness is the ultimate reality of the <s>Śākta</s> form [of the alphabet] from <s>ka</s> to <s>kṣa</s> — hence there [in <s>Parā</s>] there is pure non-difference / In <s>Parāparā</s>, however, there is the nature of difference-in-non-difference (<s>bhedābheda</s>), according to the principle of reflection (<s>pratibimba-nyāya</s>) / And that <s>Parāparā</s>, being constituted of reflective awareness, having as her body the garland of phonemes (<s>varṇa-mālā</s>) from <s>ka</s> to <s>kṣa</s> — insofar as she bears the reflections of the <s>tattvas</s> established in <s>Parā Bhaṭṭārikā</s> who is stationed above her, to that extent the <s>tattvas</s> are accomplished within those very reflective awarenesses from <s>ka</s> to <s>kṣa</s> — which are supra-<s>māyic</s>, trans-Vedic, and of ultimate reality — in an inversion of above and below, by the very glory of the nature of the upper prototype (<s>bimba</s>) and the lower reflection (<s>pratibimba</s>) —
this is the purport / Therefore, "<s>pṛthivī</s> (earth) is the phoneme <s>kṣa</s>" and so forth — from the standpoint of the aspect that is to be purified (<s>śodhya</s>), nothing is contradicted / Even there, because the supreme state (<s>para-daśā</s>) never departs, this very sequence of phonemes from <s>ka</s> onward [obtains] / And there itself, due to the preponderance of its own aspect, due to the emergence of the <s>Madhyamā</s> level existing within its own sub-aspects, and due to the tendency toward the <s>Vaikharī</s> form that exists in its own nature — there arises the character of <s>varṇa</s> (phoneme), <s>mantra</s>, and <s>pada</s> (word), which pertains to the aspect that is to be purified — but let that rest / This is not the topic at hand, and it has been determined by me in the commentaries (<s>Pañcikās</s>) on the sacred <s>Pūrva</s> [Śāstra] and others / As for what has also been said, following the sacred <s>Mālinī Bhaṭṭārikā</s> —

body.text: Q: anyathā cānyathā sthitiḥ
body.translated_text: Q: And [there is] an arrangement otherwise and [yet] otherwise /

body.text: iti tad api nirṇīya nirūpyamāṇaṃ vimṛśantu trikopadeśavisīrṇājñānagranthayaḥ pārameśvarāḥ / anāśritaśaktyātmakapaśyantīparamakoṭim atikramya pārameśvaryāṃ parasaṃvidi devatās tisra iti yad uktaṃ tat tāvan na prasmartum arhanti tatrabhavantaḥ /
body.translated_text: — let those devoted to the Supreme Lord, whose knots of ignorance have been loosened by the teaching of the <s>Trika</s>, determine and examine that as well / Having transcended the supreme limit of <s>Paśyantī</s>, whose nature is the unattached power (<s>anāśrita-śakti</s>), what has been said — that in the supreme consciousness (<s>para-saṃvid</s>) of the Lord, the goddesses are three — that, at the very least, those venerable ones should not forget /

body.text: evaṃ ca parasaṃvidantarvartini madhyamāpade parāparābhaṭṭārikāvijṛmbhāspade sthitir vimṛśyate / madhyamā tāvat svādhikārapade kriyāśaktyātmany aiśvare pade sphuṭavedyapracchādakavedanarūpā vācye vācakaṃ tatrāpi ca vācyam adhyasyate /
body.translated_text: Thus the arrangement within the <s>Madhyamā</s> level, which exists within the supreme consciousness (<s>para-saṃvid</s>) and which is the domain of the efflorescence of <s>Parāparā Bhaṭṭārikā</s> (the Supreme-and-non-Supreme Goddess), is being examined / Now, <s>Madhyamā</s>, in the domain of its own jurisdiction, in the lordly station whose nature is the power of action (<s>kriyā-śakti</s>), has the nature of cognition that conceals the clearly known object; upon the signified (<s>vācya</s>) it superimposes the signifier (<s>vācaka</s>), and upon the signifier too it superimposes the signified /

body.text: viśvatra vācye viśvātmani vācakam api yadi viśvātmaiva tad evaṃ parasparācchādanalolībhāvātmā nirvahed adhyāso na tv anyathā / na hi tricaturaṅgulanyūnatāmātre 'pi paṭaḥ paṭāntarācchādakaḥ syāt / viśvātmakatvaṃ ca parasparasvarūpavyāmiśratayā syāt / bījātmanāṃ svarāṇāṃ vācakatvaṃ yonirūpānāṃ ca vyañjanānāṃ vācyatvaṃ krameṇa śivaśaktyātmakatvāt
body.translated_text: If everywhere the signifier (<s>vācaka</s>) too is of the nature of the universe, just as the signified (<s>vācya</s>) is of the nature of the universe, then this mutual superimposition (<s>adhyāsa</s>) would proceed as an essence of reciprocal concealment — but not otherwise / For a cloth that falls short by even three or four finger-breadths could not cover another cloth / And the universal nature [of both] would consist in the mutual interpenetration of their respective essential natures / The vowels (<s>svaras</s>), being of the nature of <s>bīja</s> (seed), have the character of signifiers (<s>vācaka</s>); and the consonants (<s>vyañjanas</s>), being of the nature of <s>yoni</s> (womb), have the character of the signified (<s>vācya</s>) — because they are respectively of the nature of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s> —

body.text: Q: bījam atra śivaḥ śaktir yonir ity abhidhīyate /
body.translated_text: Q: The <s>bīja</s> (seed) here is called <s>Śiva</s>, and <s>Śakti</s> is called the <s>yoni</s> (womb) /

body.text: iti / tathā
body.translated_text: iti / Likewise —

body.text:
Q: bījayonyātmakād bhedād dvidhā bījaṃ svarā matāḥ /
Q: kādibhiś ca smṛtā yoniḥ ... //
body.translated_text:
Q: Due to the division into <s>bīja</s> (seed) and <s>yoni</s> (womb), [the phonemes are] twofold: the vowels (<s>svaras</s>) are considered the <s>bīja</s>,
Q: and the <s>yoni</s> is held to be [constituted] by [the consonants] beginning with <s>ka</s> ... //

body.text:
iti śrīpūrvaśāstranirūpaṇāt / śiva eva hi pramātṛbhāvam atyajan vācakaḥ syāt prameyāṃśāvagāhinī ca śaktir eva vācyā / bhede 'pi hi vācakaḥ pratipādyapratipādakobhayarūpapramātṛsvarūpāvicchinna eva prathate / śivātmakasvarabījarūpā śyānataiva śāktavyañjanayonibhāvo bījād eva yoneḥ prasaraṇād iti samanantaram eva nirṇeṣyāmaḥ / ata eva ca svarātmakabījavyāmiśrībhāvaś ced yoneḥ tat samastaphalaprasavo hanta niryatna ity apavargabhogāv akṛṣṭapacyāv eva bhavato bījavarṇo 'pi svātmani yonivarṇo yonivarṇo 'pi tathaiveti kiṃ kasya bhedakam iti kathyamānaṃ nāsmān ākulayet ye vayam ekāṃ tāvad anantacitratāgarbhiṇīṃ tāṃ saṃvidātmikāṃ giraṃ saṃgirāmahe / māyīye 'pi vyavahārapade laukikakramikavarṇapadasphuṭatāmayī ekaparāmarśasvabhāvaiva
pratyavamarśākāriṇī prakāśarūpā vāk / anyaiś caitat prayatnasādhitaro iha ca etāvadupadeśadhārādhiśayanaśālinām aprayatnata eva siddhyatīti nāsmābhir atra vṛthā vaiyākaraṇagurugṛhagamane pūtaśarīratāviṣkriyāmātraphale nirbandho vihitaḥ / evam eva navātmapiṇḍaprabhṛtiṣv api mālāmantreṣv api ca kramākramapūrvāparādibhedacodyapratividhānaṃ siddham eva /
body.translated_text: Thus it is established in the revered <s>Pūrvaśāstra</s> (prior scripture). <s>Śiva</s> himself, without abandoning his nature as the knowing subject (<s>pramātṛ</s>), becomes the signifier (<s>vācaka</s>), and <s>Śakti</s> alone, penetrating the aspect of the object of knowledge (<s>prameya</s>), is the signified (<s>vācya</s>). For even in differentiation, the signifier manifests as inseparable from the essential nature of the knowing subject, which has the form of both the expressed and the expressor. The very densification (<s>śyānatā</s>) of the <s>Śiva</s>-natured vowel-<s>bīja</s> (seed) form is the state of the <s>Śākta</s> (Śakti-related) consonant-<s>yoni</s> (womb) — since the <s>yoni</s> emanates from the <s>bīja</s> itself, as we shall determine immediately after. And therefore, if the <s>yoni</s> attains a state of intermixture with the vowel-natured <s>bīja</s>, then the bringing forth of all fruits becomes effortless indeed — thus <s>apavarga</s> (liberation) and <s>bhoga</s> (enjoyment) ripen of themselves as if self-sown; a <s>bīja</s>-<s>varṇa</s> (seed-phoneme) is also a <s>yoni</s>-<s>varṇa</s> (womb-phoneme) within itself, and a <s>yoni</s>-<s>varṇa</s> is likewise the same — so what distinguishes what from what? Let what is being said not confuse us who, for our part, swallow whole that one <s>saṃvid</s> (consciousness)-natured speech which is pregnant with infinite variety. Even in the domain of <s>Māyā</s>-based conventional usage, speech — consisting of the clarity of worldly sequential phonemes and words — is of the nature of a single reflective awareness, producing recognition (<s>pratyavamarśa</s>), and is of the form of <s>prakāśa</s> (luminosity). Others achieve this with great effort, but here for those who recline upon the flowing stream of just this much instruction, it is accomplished effortlessly — hence we have not insisted upon futile visits to the houses of grammarian teachers, the sole fruit of which is a display of bodily purification. In exactly this way, with regard to the <s>navātma</s> (nine-self), <s>piṇḍa</s> (aggregate), and other garland-<s>mantras</s> as well, the resolution of objections concerning distinctions of sequence and non-sequence, prior and posterior, is already established.

body.text: evaṃ bhagavatī māliny eva mukhyapāramārthikamadhyamādhāma śaktisatattvam / ata evoktaṃ śrīpūrvaśāstre
body.translated_text: Thus the blessed <s>Mālinī</s> herself is the supreme, ultimate, intermediate, and lower <s>śakti-tattva</s> (principle of Śakti). Therefore it is said in the revered <s>Pūrvaśāstra</s> (prior scripture):

body.text:
Q: yatheṣṭaphalasaṃsiddhyai mantratantrānuvartinām /
Q: nyasec chāktaśarīrārthaṃ bhinnayoniṃ tu mālinīm //
body.translated_text:
Q: For the attainment of desired fruits, for those who follow the <s>mantra</s>-<s>tantra</s> (system),
Q: one should place (<s>nyāsa</s>) the <s>Mālinī</s>, which has separated <s>yoni</s> (womb-phonemes), for the purpose of the <s>Śākta</s> body. //

body.text: iti / bhinnayonitvaṃ ca nirṇītam / anyatrāpi
body.translated_text: Thus. And the state of having separated <s>yoni</s>s has been determined. Elsewhere also:

body.text:
Q: na puṃsi na pare tattve śaktau mantraṃ niveśayet /
Q: jaḍatvān niṣkriyatvāc ca na te bhogāpavargadāḥ //
body.translated_text:
Q: One should not place a <s>mantra</s> in the <s>puṃs</s> (male principle), nor in the supreme <s>tattva</s> (reality), nor in <s>Śakti</s>;
Q: because of their inertness and actionlessness, they do not grant <s>bhoga</s> (enjoyment) or <s>apavarga</s> (liberation). //

body.text:
iti / evaṃ ca sthite sarvasarvātmakatvād yad eva ``na ṛ ṛ ḷ ḷ3 tha ca dha ī ṇa u ū ba ka kha ga'' ity abhihitehatyaparasaṃvidam apekṣya krameṇa śrotraṃ nādātmakabhāvarūpaṃ yonyātma amṛtāpyāyakāriṇi bījacatuṣkāpyāyabhūmau patitaṃ bṛṃhitatvam avāpya jhaṭiti grahaṇātmakarasasatattvarasanāmayatvaṃ pratipadya dharaṇyākāragandhaviśeṣībhūya tatraiva sparśakaraṇatāṃ śritvā etāvac ca śāktaṃ yaunaṃ dhāma īśānabījenādhisthāya vāgātmani karaṇaśaktau pratiphalitaṃ tato 'pi karaṇaśakter unmeṣordhvāśrayaṇabījarūpatayā buddhirūpāṃ śāktayonim adhiśayya pṛthivyaptejoyonisamāviṣṭam / paśyantīrūpānusṛtyā tu grahaṇātmakavāṇirūpāyāṃ tatraiva bījeṣu prasṛtya cākṣuṣyāṃ bhuvi tatsāmānyāśuddhavidyākaraṇe
tatsarvāntyakaraṇe ca ghrāṇe sthitvā īśānabījenākramya śrotraśaktim ālambyonmeṣordhvabījayogena ānandendriyayonigaṃ sadāśiveśvaraśuddhavidyāmayaṃ bhavati -- iti sarvāgramadhyāntagāmitvenāparicchinnam anantaśakti śivatattvam atroktaṃ bhavati / mālinyām ihatyaparasaṃvidanusṛtyā paśyantyātmakasattānusṛtyā ca krameṇa vāyur māyā gha sādākhyam / nabhaḥ kalā ca ṅa īśvaraḥ / icchaiva śaktimayī i śuddhavidyā / anuttara eva svatantro 'haṃbhāvaḥ a śivākhyo māyā / aśuddhavidyā gandhaś ca va kalā / prakṛtiḥ pādendriyaṃ ca bha aśuddhavidyā / kālaḥ sparśaś ca ya rāgaḥ / pāyur ahaṃkṛc ca ḍa niyatiḥ / hastau manaś ca ḍha kālaḥ / ānandendriyaṃ buddhiś ca ṭha puruṣaḥ / sparśaḥ kālaś ca jha prakṛtiḥ / śabdaḥ pumān
ca ña dhīḥ / rūpaṃ niyatiś ca ja ahaṃkṛtam / niyatī rūpaṃ ca ra manaḥ / pādendriyaṃ prakṛtiś ca ṭa śrotram /
body.translated_text: Thus. And this being so, since everything is the essence of everything — that which has been stated as "na ṛ ṛ ḷ ḷ tha ca dha ī ṇa u ū ba ka kha ga" — considering the <s>apara-saṃvid</s> (lower consciousness) of this context, sequentially: the ear, being of the nature of <s>nāda</s> (sound-vibration), having the <s>yoni</s>-nature, falls upon the ground of nourishment of the four <s>bīja</s>s (seeds) that cause the flowing of <s>amṛta</s> (nectar), and having attained expansion, suddenly attains the nature of the tongue — the <s>rasanā</s> (organ of taste), whose essence is the <s>rasa-tattva</s> (principle of taste) characterized by grasping — and having become particularized as smell in the form of earth, and having there assumed the nature of the organ of touch — and this much constitutes the <s>Śākta</s> (Śakti-related) and <s>yauna</s> (yoni-related) abode — presiding through the <s>Īśāna</s>-<s>bīja</s> (seed of the Lord), it is reflected in the faculty of speech (<s>vāk</s>), the instrumental <s>śakti</s>; from there too, by virtue of the <s>bīja</s>-form of the upward-ascending unfolding (<s>unmeṣa</s>) of the instrumental <s>śakti</s>, having rested upon the <s>Śākta</s>-<s>yoni</s> in the form of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), it is pervaded by the <s>yoni</s>s of earth, water, and fire. But following the <s>paśyantī</s> (visionary) level, extending into the <s>bīja</s>s there in the form of <s>vāṇī</s> (speech) characterized by grasping, in the visual faculty, in earth, in the instrument of <s>aśuddha-vidyā</s> (impure knowledge) which is the universal of that, and in the sense of smell which is the final instrument of all that — having stationed itself and then advancing through the <s>Īśāna</s>-<s>bīja</s>, resting upon the power of hearing, through the conjunction of the upward-ascending <s>bīja</s> of <s>unmeṣa</s> (unfolding), it enters the <s>yoni</s> of the <s>ānanda</s>-<s>indriya</s> (bliss-faculty) and becomes constituted of <s>Sadāśiva</s>, <s>Īśvara</s>, and <s>Śuddhavidyā</s> — thus what is stated here is the <s>Śiva-tattva</s> (Śiva-principle), unlimited by virtue of pervading all beginnings, middles, and ends, possessed of infinite <s>śakti</s>. In the <s>Mālinī</s>, following the <s>apara-saṃvid</s> (lower consciousness) of this context, and following the being-nature of <s>paśyantī</s> (the visionary level), sequentially: wind is <s>Māyā</s>, gha is <s>Sadākhya</s> (Sadāśiva); space and <s>kalā</s> are ṅa, which is <s>Īśvara</s>; <s>icchā</s> (will) itself, filled with <s>śakti</s>, i is <s>Śuddhavidyā</s>; the supreme (<s>anuttara</s>) itself, the autonomous I-sense, a is <s>Śiva</s>-named <s>Māyā</s>; <s>aśuddhavidyā</s> (impure knowledge) and smell are va, which is <s>kalā</s>; <s>prakṛti</s> (nature) and the locomotive faculty are bha, which is <s>aśuddhavidyā</s>; <s>kāla</s> (time) and touch are ya, which is <s>rāga</s> (attachment); the excretory organ and <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego) are ḍa, which is <s>niyati</s> (necessity); the hands and <s>manas</s> (mind) are ḍha, which is <s>kāla</s>; the <s>ānanda-indriya</s> (bliss-faculty) and <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) are ṭha, which is <s>puruṣa</s> (self); touch and time are jha, which is <s>prakṛti</s>; sound and <s>puruṣa</s> are ña, which is <s>buddhi</s>; form and <s>niyati</s> are ja, which is <s>ahaṃkāra</s>; <s>niyati</s> and form are ra, which is <s>manas</s>; the locomotive faculty and <s>prakṛti</s> are ṭa, which is the ear;

body.text:
mano hastaś ca pa tvak / raso rāgaś ca cha netre / rāgo rasaś ca la rasanā / ānandaśaktiḥ śaivī ā ghrāṇam / vidyā tejaś ca sa vāk / visargaśaktiś ca aḥ karau / īśo jalaṃ ca ha pāyuḥ / māyā vāyuś ca ṣa ānandendriyam / sādākhyaṃ pṛthivī ca kṣa pādau / pumān śabdaś ca ma śabdaḥ / kalā nabhaś ca śa sparśaḥ / baindavī śivaśaktiḥ aṃ rūpam / nāsikā tvak ca ta rasaḥ / śivaśaktiḥ sāttvī e gandhaḥ / saiva dīrghā ai nabhaḥ / tathaiva vāyutejasī o au / netre rasaś ca da āpaḥ / ahaṃkṛt pāyuś ca pha pṛthivī / atraiva ca yathoktaṃ śarīraniveśa ity evaṃ sarvasarvātmakatvaṃ nirvyūḍhaṃ bhavet / parābhaṭṭārikaiva hi proktanayena paśyantyāṃ pratibimbaṃ svakam arpayamāṇā tatsamakālam eva svātmatādātmyavyavasthitamadhyamādhāmni
bhinnayonitām aśnuvānā tattadyonibījaparasparasaṃbhedavaicitryasyānantyād asaṃkhyenaiva prakāreṇa tattatkulapuruṣādibhedenāparigaṇanabhedabhāginī māliny eva / yathoktam
body.translated_text: <s>manas</s> (mind) and the hands are pa, which is skin; taste and <s>rāga</s> (attachment) are cha, which is the eyes; <s>rāga</s> and taste are la, which is the tongue; <s>ānanda-śakti</s> (bliss-power), which is <s>Śaivī</s> (of Śiva), ā is the nose; <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) and fire are sa, which is speech; <s>visarga-śakti</s> (emissive power) aḥ is the hands; <s>Īśa</s> (the Lord) and water are ha, which is the excretory organ; <s>Māyā</s> and wind are ṣa, which is the <s>ānanda-indriya</s> (bliss-faculty); <s>Sadākhya</s> (Sadāśiva) and earth are kṣa, which is the feet; <s>puruṣa</s> and sound are ma, which is sound; <s>kalā</s> and space are śa, which is touch; the <s>Baindavī</s> (bindu-related) <s>Śiva-Śakti</s> aṃ is form; the nose and skin are ta, which is taste; <s>Śiva-Śakti</s>, which is <s>sāttvī</s> (of the nature of sattva), e is smell; the same in its long form ai is space; likewise wind and fire are o and au; the eyes and taste are da, which is water; <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego) and the excretory organ are pha, which is earth. And here in this very context, the placement in the body as stated — thus the nature of everything being the essence of everything is fully demonstrated. For the supreme <s>Parā Bhaṭṭārikā</s> (the supreme Goddess) herself, casting her own reflection in <s>paśyantī</s> (the visionary level) according to the method described, and simultaneously attaining the state of separated <s>yoni</s>s in the intermediate and lower levels established as identical with her own self — because of the infinity of the variety of mutual intermingling of the respective <s>yoni</s>s and <s>bīja</s>s, she partakes of innumerable divisions in the form of distinctions of respective <s>kula</s>-<s>puruṣa</s>s (clan-beings) and the like — she is none other than <s>Mālinī</s>. As it is said:

body.text:
Q: anantaiḥ kuladevais tu kulaśaktibhir eva ca /
Q: mālinīṃ tu yajed devīṃ parivāritavigrahām //
body.translated_text:
Q: With innumerable <s>kula</s>-deities and <s>kula</s>-<s>śakti</s>s (clan-powers),
Q: one should worship the goddess <s>Mālinī</s>, whose body is surrounded by her retinue. //

body.text:
iti / anenaiva ca krameṇa bahir bhuvaneṣu tattveṣu śārīreṣu ca cakreṣu abhyāsaparo yogī tattatsiddhibhāg yatraiva dehe prāṇe vā bhavati /
yathā kāś cid evauṣadhyaḥ samudbhūya kiṃcid eva kāryaṃ vidadhate
tathā kācid eva samudbhūya bhāvanā mantranyāsahomādigatir vā
kāṃcid eva siddhiṃ vitaret, atrāpi yāvan niyativyāpārānatikramāt /
tathā hi pratiśāstram anyathā cānyathā ca varṇaniveśapuraḥsaraṃ nijanijavijñānasamucitatatattadvarṇabhaṭṭārakaprādhānyena tattadvarṇaprāthamyānusārāyātaniyataparipāṭīpiṇḍitavarṇasamūharūpaḥ prastāro ni rūpitaḥ -- tata eva ca mantroddhāro nirūpitaḥ -- tām eva mātṛkārūpatāṃ
tathāvidhavīryadānopabṛṃhitamantrasphurattādāyinīṃ darśayituṃ, yathā śrīnityātantreṣu aikārātmakamohanabījaprādhānyahetuḥ / paranādātmaniveśaprādhānyāt tadanusārāpatitaśrīmannādiphāntakrameṇaiva
niveśaḥ / atra kulapuruṣāṇāṃ kulaśaktīnāṃ ca eṣa eva niveśa abhiprāyo na ca varṇamantrādiguptimātram eva phalam / tathā śrīvājasaneyatantre varṇān yathocitaṃ niveśyoktam
body.translated_text:
Thus. And in this very sequence, the <s>yogī</s> who is devoted to practice in the external worlds, in the <s>tattva</s>s (principles), and in the bodily <s>cakra</s>s (centers), partakes of the respective <s>siddhi</s>s (attainments) in whatever body or <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) he may be.
Just as certain herbs, having sprung up, accomplish only a particular effect,
so too a particular <s>bhāvanā</s> (contemplation), or a practice of <s>mantra</s>-<s>nyāsa</s> (placement), <s>homa</s> (oblation), and so forth,
may bestow only a particular <s>siddhi</s> (attainment) — and even here, only insofar as the operation of <s>niyati</s> (cosmic necessity) is not transgressed.
For thus, in each scripture, in one way or another, preceded by the placement of phonemes, with the predominance of the respective presiding deity of the respective phonemes appropriate to one's own particular knowledge, the arrangement — a collection of phonemes assembled in a fixed sequence following the primacy of the respective phonemes — has been set forth; and from that very arrangement the extraction of <s>mantra</s>s has been determined — in order to demonstrate that very <s>Mātṛkā</s> (Mother-alphabet) nature, which bestows the flashing forth of <s>mantra</s>s nourished by the granting of such potency. Just as in the revered <s>Nityā</s>-<s>tantra</s>s, the reason for the predominance of the <s>mohanabīja</s> (seed of delusion) whose essence is the phoneme ai; due to the predominance of the placement in the form of the supreme <s>nāda</s> (resonance), the placement follows in the sequence beginning with the revered <s>nāda</s> and ending with pha. Here, this very placement is the intended meaning regarding the <s>kula-puruṣa</s>s (clan-beings) and <s>kula-śakti</s>s (clan-powers), and the fruit is not merely the concealment of the phoneme-<s>mantra</s>s and so forth. Likewise, in the revered <s>Vājasaneya-tantra</s>, having placed the phonemes as appropriate, it is said:

body.text:
Q: ity etan mātṛkācakraṃ divyaṃ viṣṇupadāspadam /
Q: jñātaṃ gurumukhāt samyak paśoḥ pāśān nikṛntati //
body.translated_text:
Q: This is the divine <s>Mātṛkā-cakra</s> (circle of the Mother-alphabet), the abode of <s>Viṣṇupada</s> (the station of Viṣṇu);
Q: properly known from the mouth of the <s>Guru</s> (teacher), it cuts the bonds of the <s>paśu</s> (bound soul). //

body.text: iti / tathā śrītrikahṛdaye 'pi
body.translated_text: Thus. And likewise in the revered <s>Trikahṛdaya</s> (Heart of the Triad) also:

body.text: Q: cakraśūlāmbujādīnāṃ prāṇināṃ saritaṃ nṛṇām //
body.translated_text: Q: Of <s>cakra</s>s (discs), <s>śūla</s>s (tridents), <s>ambuja</s>s (lotuses), and other such things, of living beings, of rivers, of people, //

body.text: Q: āyudhānāṃ ca śaktīnām anyasyāpi ca kasya cit //
body.translated_text: Q: of weapons, of <s>śakti</s>s (powers), and of whatever else there may be, //

body.text:
Q: yo niveśas tu varṇānāṃ tadvīryaṃ tatra mantragam /
Q: tena guptena te guptāḥ śeṣā varṇās tu kevalāḥ //
body.translated_text:
Q: whatever placement of phonemes there is, the potency of that resides in the <s>mantra</s> therein;
Q: by that concealed one, they are concealed — the remaining phonemes are mere letters. //

body.text: iti / tathāhi mantrāṇām akṣaramātrānanyathābhāve 'pi teṣām eva śāstreṣv āṇavaśāktaśāmbhavādivibhāgenānyathātvaṃ yathā māyābījasya praṇavasya sarvasyāmṛtabījasya vaiṣṇavaśaivavāmādiśāstreṣu yathā vā catuṣkalabhaṭṭārakasya kālottarādau śrīmaducchuṣmaśāstre ca / atra ca kulapuruṣabahubhedaprakaṭanāyām abhiyuktānām upāyo likhyate
body.translated_text: Thus. For although the <s>mantra</s>s consist of nothing other than mere syllables, in the scriptures those very same ones are differentiated through the distinctions of <s>āṇava</s> (pertaining to the individual), <s>śākta</s> (pertaining to Śakti), <s>śāmbhava</s> (pertaining to Śiva), and so forth — as for example the <s>Māyā-bīja</s> (seed of Māyā), the <s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ), and the <s>Amṛta-bīja</s> (seed of immortality) in the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>, <s>Śaiva</s>, <s>Vāma</s>, and other scriptures; or as with the four-<s>kalā</s> Lord in the <s>Kālottara</s> and the revered <s>Ucchuṣma-śāstra</s>. And here, the method employed by the adepts for demonstrating the many divisions of <s>kula-puruṣa</s>s (clan-beings) is written:

body.text:
Q: pūrve pareṣām apare pare pṛṣṭhavad eva ca /
Q: pūrve 'pi ca yathāpūrvaṃ mātṛkāyā vidhir mataḥ //
body.translated_text:
Q: The prior ones become the posterior ones' [counterparts], the posterior ones likewise become the prior ones' as if placed behind;
Q: and the prior ones also [remain] in their original order — such is the rule of <s>Mātṛkā</s> (the Mother-alphabet). //

body.text: Q: etenaivānusāreṇa bhinnayonisvarūpataḥ //
body.translated_text: Q: By this very method of following, through the nature of having separated <s>yoni</s>s, //

body.text: Q: śāktā hy asaṃkhyā devīyaṃ paraivottaramālinī //
body.translated_text: Q: the <s>Śākta</s> (Śakti-related) ones are innumerable — this divine one is the supreme and ultimate <s>Mālinī</s>. //

body.text:
Q: ūrdhvādho viniviṣṭeṣu bhedasaṃkhyeṣu dhāmasu /
Q: ekaṃ bindur athāpi prāg anyeṣu prāktanāntyagām //
body.translated_text:
Q: Among the abodes placed above and below, with countable distinctions,
Q: one is <s>bindu</s> (point); or else, placed first, in the others it moves from the foremost to the last, //

body.text:
Q: svapṛṣṭhagāṃ ca tāṃ saṃkhyāṃ viniveśyaikataḥ kṣipet /
Q: asmādanyair bhavet saṃkhyā spṛṣṭair iṣṭaiḥ punaḥ kramaḥ //
body.translated_text:
Q: and placing that count which follows one's own back into one, one should cast it;
Q: from those other than this, the count arises from those touched and desired; then again the sequence. //

body.text: yathoktaṃ kulaśaktīnāṃ vidhir ānantyavedana iti / tad etena vidhinā ye kulapuruṣaśaktiyogino niradhikārībhūtāḥ, yathoktam
body.translated_text: As stated, the rule of <s>kula-śakti</s>s (clan-powers) is the realization of infinity. Thus, by this method, those who are united with <s>kula-puruṣa</s>s and <s>śakti</s>s and have become without further qualification — as it is said:

body.text: Q: brahmādistambaparyante jātamātre jagaty alam //
body.translated_text: Q: In the world from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a blade of grass, as soon as it is born, //

body.text:
Q: mantrāṇāṃ koṭayas tisraḥ sārdhāḥ śivaniyojitāḥ /
Q: anugṛhyāṇusaṃghātaṃ yātāḥ padam anāmayam //
body.translated_text:
Q: three and a half <s>koṭi</s>s (tens of millions) of <s>mantra</s>s, appointed by <s>Śiva</s>,
Q: having graced the aggregate of individual souls, have gone to the state free from affliction. //

body.text: iti mantramahesvarāḥ, na tu mantrāḥ, teṣāṃ svalayāvasare anāmayapadaparyantatābhāvaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus they are <s>Mantramāheśvara</s>s (great lords of mantras), not mere <s>mantra</s>s; for at the time of their dissolution, there is no end to the state of the affliction-free abode.

body.text: tebhyo naiva mantroddhāras tasya niṣphalatvāt / tata eva
body.translated_text: From them there is no extraction of <s>mantra</s>s, since that would be fruitless. Therefore:

body.text: Q: abhinnayonimadhye tu nādiphāntaṃ kalau yuge /
body.translated_text: Q: But within the undivided <s>yoni</s> (womb), from <s>nāda</s> to pha, in the <s>Kali</s> age, //

body.text: iti / tad evaṃ bhagavatī parāparābhaṭṭārikā padabhedaśālinī madhyamayā mukhyayā vṛttyā bhagavanmālinīrūpaivānantāparigaṇapradarśitavaiśvarūpyasvasvarūpāpīti / tatrāpi ca tathaiva svātmani sarvātmakatvenāṃśatrayodrekād varṇapadamantrātmakatvam / etac ca śodhanakaraṇabhāveneti mantavyam / paśyantyaṃśollasanto hi pāśāḥ sūkṣmā eva śodhyā bhavanty antarlīnatva eva pāśatvāt / uditoditavijṛmbhāmayaśāktaprasare tu madhyamāpade śodhanakaraṇataivāntarlīnapaṭamalāpasaraṇe bāhyasthūlamalasyeva /
body.translated_text: Thus the blessed <s>Parāparā Bhaṭṭārikā</s> (the supreme-and-non-supreme Goddess), possessing the distinctions of levels, through <s>Madhyamā</s> (the intermediate level of speech) as her principal mode, is indeed of the form of the blessed <s>Mālinī</s>, whose own essential nature has been demonstrated as displaying a cosmic variety that is infinite and beyond enumeration. And there too, in her own self, due to the predominance of three aspects by virtue of being the self of all, there is the nature of <s>varṇa</s> (phoneme), <s>pada</s> (word), and <s>mantra</s>. And this should be understood as functioning in the capacity of purification (<s>śodhana</s>). For the <s>pāśa</s>s (bonds), flashing forth from the <s>paśyantī</s> aspect, being subtle, are to be purified precisely in their state of inner absorption, since it is in the state of being absorbed within that bondage consists. But in the <s>Śākta</s> expansion where the <s>madhyamā</s> level unfolds with fully arisen efflorescence, the function of purification is like the removal of externally gross impurity when the internally absorbed stain is being removed.

body.text:
tatparābhaṭṭārikāsaṃvidantargataṃ tu vaikharīpadaṃ vimṛśyate / na hi tatraiva vaikharyā asaṃbhavaḥ / tathā hi bālā dvitrair varṣair yady api sphuṭībhūtasthānakaraṇā bhavanti tathāpy eṣāṃ māsānumāsadinānudinam eva vā vyutpattir adhikādhikarūpatām etīti tāvat sthitam / tatra yadi madhyamāpade tathāvidhavaikharīprasarasphuṭībhaviṣyatsthānakaraṇāvibhāgavarṇāṃśasphuraṇaṃ na syāt tad aharjātasya bālakasya māsajātasya saṃvatsarajātasya vā vyutpattau na viśeṣaḥ syāt / madhyamaiva sā vyutpattyā viśiṣyata iti cet katham iti carcyatām tāvat / sṛnvann eva tāñ śabdān paśyaṃś cārthān vyutpadyate vamāṃś ca śrūyamānān eva parāmṛśec chrūyante ca vaikharīmayāḥ, teṣu ca asau rūpa eva jātyandhavat / tasmād antarmadhyamāniviṣṭasthānakaraṇādimayī
asty eva vaikharī / mūke 'py evam eva / sarvātmakatvaṃ ca saṃvido bhagavatyā evoktam / evaṃ ca vaikharīpadam eva madhyamādhāmalabdhavijṛmbhaṃ svāṃśe parasparavaicitryaprathātmani sphuṭavācyavācakabhāvollāse jāte tattvajālam antaḥkṛtya yāvad āste tāvad aparābhaṭṭārikā / tadantarvartimadhyamāpadollāse parāparā / paśyantyullāse ca svarūpato bhagavatī devī ceti śodhakabhāvena sthitiḥ traidham evāvatiṣṭhate / sodhako hi viśvātmā vitatarūpo vaitatyaṃ caivam eva bhavatīty uktam /
body.translated_text: Now the <s>Vaikharī</s> (externally manifest speech) level contained within the consciousness of the supreme <s>Parā Bhaṭṭārikā</s> (Goddess) is examined. For the impossibility of <s>Vaikharī</s> existing there is not the case. For thus: although children become clear in their points of articulation and organs of pronunciation after two or three years, nevertheless their proficiency increases month by month, day by day, assuming ever greater and greater form — this much is established. Now if at the <s>Madhyamā</s> level there were no flashing forth of the phoneme-aspect with its as-yet-undifferentiated points of articulation and organs of pronunciation that will become manifest through the expansion of <s>Vaikharī</s> of such a kind, then there would be no difference in the proficiency of a day-old infant, a month-old one, or a year-old one. If one says that it is <s>Madhyamā</s> itself that becomes distinguished through proficiency, then let that be examined. For one who hears those very sounds and sees the objects gains proficiency, and one who vomits would recognize the very sounds being heard — and what is heard consists of <s>Vaikharī</s>, and in regard to those, one who is in that form alone is like one born blind. Therefore there certainly exists a <s>Vaikharī</s> consisting of points of articulation, organs of pronunciation, and so forth, situated within the inner <s>Madhyamā</s>. The same applies even to one who is mute. And the nature of consciousness as being the self of everything has been declared by the blessed Goddess herself. And thus, the <s>Vaikharī</s> level itself, having gained its efflorescence at the intermediate and lower levels, in its own aspect — when the clear manifestation of the relation between signified and signifier unfolds, whose nature is the display of mutual variety — so long as it remains having internalized the web of <s>tattva</s>s (principles), it is <s>Aparā Bhaṭṭārikā</s> (the lower Goddess). When the <s>Madhyamā</s> level within that unfolds, it is <s>Parāparā</s> (the supreme-non-supreme). And when <s>Paśyantī</s> (the visionary level) unfolds, it is in its own essential nature the blessed <s>Devī</s> (Goddess) herself — thus the existence as purifier abides in a threefold manner. For the purifier, being the self of the universe, has an extended form, and extension is indeed of this very nature, as has been stated.

body.text: śodhanaṃ prati tu karaṇatvaṃ kartur eva svasvātantryagṛhītasaṃkocasya śāktamahimaviśrāntasya bhagavataḥ / śodhyatā tu saṃkocaikarūpasya saptatriṃśātikrāntatrikaikarūpabhairavabhaṭṭārakāvinirbhaktaparābhaṭṭārikātulyakakṣyaparāparādevatākṣobhātmakasadāśivajñānaśaktivisphāritapaśuśaktirūpapaśyantīdhāmaprathamāsūtritabhedātmano narātmanaḥ pāśajālasyeti nirṇayaḥ / yathoktaṃ śrīsomānandapādaiḥ śivadṛṣṭau
body.translated_text: With respect to purification, however, the instrumentality belongs to the agent himself — the blessed Lord who has assumed contraction through his own <s>svātantrya</s> (absolute freedom) and who reposes in the glory of <s>Śakti</s>. But what is to be purified is the web of <s>pāśa</s>s (bonds) whose nature is exclusively that of contraction — belonging to the human soul (<s>nara</s>), whose essence is differentiation, first projected at the <s>Paśyantī</s> (visionary) level, which is the form of the <s>paśu-śakti</s> (power of the bound soul) expanded by the <s>jñāna-śakti</s> (power of knowledge) of <s>Sadāśiva</s>, whose nature is the agitation of the <s>Parāparā</s> deity of equal rank with <s>Parā Bhaṭṭārikā</s> (the supreme Goddess), who is undifferentiated from <s>Bhairava Bhaṭṭāraka</s> (the Lord Bhairava), whose singular form is the Triad that transcends the thirty-seven [tattvas] — such is the determination. As stated by the revered <s>Somānanda</s> in the <s>Śivadṛṣṭi</s>:

body.text:
Q: asmadrūpasamāviṣṭaḥ svātmanātmanivāraṇe /
Q: śivaḥ karotu parayā namaḥ śaktyā tatātmane //
body.translated_text:
Q: May <s>Śiva</s>, who is absorbed in our own essential nature, through the supreme <s>Śakti</s>,
Q: accomplish the removal of the self by the self — homage to Him who is of that very nature! //

body.text: iti / sarvakriyākalāpe evaṃrūpatāsūcakatvaṃ śivadṛṣṭau / tatrāpi cottarottaraṃ śodhyasodhakānām api vigalanam /
body.translated_text: Thus. In the entire range of activities, the indication of such a nature is shown in the <s>Śivadṛṣṭi</s>. And there too, the successive dissolution of both the purifiable and the purifier, one after another.

body.text:
Q: tyaja dharmam adharmaṃ ca ubhe satyānṛte tyaja /
Q: ubhe satyānṛte tyaktvā yena tyajasi tat tyaja //
body.translated_text:
Q: Abandon <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) and <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness); abandon both truth and falsehood;
Q: having abandoned both truth and falsehood, abandon that by which you abandon. //

body.text:
iti / tad iyam etāvatī dhārā yac chodhanam api śodhyam eveti śrīṣaḍardhaśāstre eva eka utkarṣaḥ / tisṛṇām api cāsāṃ yugapat sthitir bhavaty eva / vakti hy anyat vikalpayaṃś cānyat jalpaty avikalpam eva anyat paśyati / atra tu paripūrṇa eva tāvati bhagavān bhairava evetyādy anubhavasaṃpradāyopadeśapariśīlanenāsyārthasya svasaṃvinmayasyānapalāpanīyatvāt / na tad yugapat api tu tathāsauksmyād alaksaṇam iti yaugapadyābhimānaḥ śirīṣakusumapallavasatavyatibheda iveti cet keyaṃ khalu bhāṣā yugapad iti / samānakālam iti ced antarmukhe samvidātmani proktanayena kaḥ kālaḥ tasya jñeyarūpaprāṇagamāgamādimayābhāsatadabhāvaprāṇatvāt / jñeyopādhigato'pi jñānam avaskandet sa iti cej jñeyasya svātmani bhāsāmaye 'nyathā vā kasya niveśo jñānamukhe noktaḥ / itaretarāśrayasaṃplavaḥ
svato bhedād ityādy api sarvam ucyamānaṃ jñānamukham evāpatet tathā ca sa eva doṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus, this is the full extent of the stream — that the purifier too is itself the purifiable. This is the one excellence found in the sacred <s>Ṣaḍardhaśāstra</s> (Trika scripture) alone. Moreover, the three [levels of speech] do indeed exist simultaneously. For one says one thing, while conceptualizing (<s>vikalpayan</s>) another, and while uttering yet another, one perceives something altogether non-conceptual (<s>avikalpam</s>). But here, the blessed Lord <s>Bhairava</s> is utterly complete in just that much — and so on — because, through the cultivation of the teaching of the experiential tradition, this meaning, which is constituted by one's own consciousness (<s>svasaṃvid</s>), cannot be denied. If it be objected that this is not simultaneous but rather, due to such subtlety, is imperceptible — so that the notion of simultaneity is like the interpenetration of <s>śirīṣa</s> flower petals and threads — then what indeed does the word "simultaneous" mean? If it means "occurring at the same time," then in the inward-facing Self whose nature is consciousness (<s>saṃvid</s>), what is time, according to the doctrine already stated? For time has its life-breath in the appearance and non-appearance of the coming and going of the life-breath whose form is the knowable. Even if [time] obtained through the limiting adjunct of the knowable were to overpower knowledge — if one says so — then for the knowable, whose abode in the Self (which is the mass of manifestations) or otherwise has not been stated as having entry through the portal of knowledge, there is a collapse into mutual dependence. Everything stated beginning with "from intrinsic difference" and so on would fall into the portal of knowledge alone, and thus the same fault applies.

body.text:
bahutarakusumapallavasatavyatibhedo 'pi cāneka ity ucyamāne sarvatra sūkṣmaparamāṇvantāvayavayogān nāsti karma ity āpatet / na cānusaṃdhānaṃ jñānābhāvena saha syād anusaṃdhāyāḥ smṛtibhede tasyāś cānubhavopajīvitve 'nubhavābhāvābhāvāt / vitatya ca vicāritaṃ mayaitat padārthapraveśanirṇayaṭīkāyām iti kim iha vṛthāvāgjālena prakṛtopadeśavighnaparyavasāyinā / evaṃ bhagavaty aparā sodhakabhāvena sthitā parā parāparāpi ca yatra bhagavatīnām aghoradīnāṃ śaktīnāṃ sthitir yadyogād vijñānākalasādhakayogino mantramahesādirūpeṇāghorādyāḥ saṃpannāḥ / brahmyādiśaktyanugraheṇaiva sādhakāṇavo brahmaviṣṇvādayaḥ / parameśvaro hi bhairavabhaṭṭārakaḥ samagraśaktipuñjaparipūrṇanirbharavapur nijaśaktiniveśanayā brāhmyādīn
svātantryāt karoti iti kim anyat / evaṃ śodhakasyāpi śodhyatvam ity anya utkarṣaḥ
body.translated_text: Moreover, even the interpenetration of a greater number of flower petals and threads — when it is said to be "multiple" — would everywhere lead to the conclusion that there is no action, due to the conjunction of parts down to the subtlest atoms. Nor could there be a synthesis (<s>anusaṃdhāna</s>) together with the absence of knowledge, because in the difference of memory — which is the faculty of synthesis — and given that memory depends on experience, there would be no absence of the absence of experience. I have discussed this at length in my commentary on the <s>Padārthapravesanirṇaya</s>, so what is the use here of a useless web of words that only obstructs the teaching at hand? Thus, the blessed <s>Aparā</s> (non-supreme speech) abides in the role of purifier, as do <s>Parā</s> (supreme) and <s>Parāparā</s> (supreme-non-supreme) — where the powers of the blessed Goddesses <s>Aghorā</s> and the rest abide; by whose union the <s>vijñānākala</s> practitioner-yogins have attained the forms of <s>Mantramāheśvara</s> and the rest beginning with <s>Aghorā</s>. Through the grace of the powers of <s>Brahmī</s> and the rest alone, the atomic souls who are practitioners become <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and the rest. For the supreme Lord, the venerable <s>Bhairava</s>, whose body is replete and overflowing with the entire mass of powers, through the disposition of His own powers, creates <s>Brahmī</s> and the rest out of His own absolute freedom — what more [need be said]? Thus the purifier too is itself purifiable — this is the other excellence.

body.text: Q: ... kulāt parataraṃ trikam /
body.translated_text: Quote: "... beyond <s>Kula</s> is <s>Trika</s>."

body.text:
iti sthityā / tataś ca śodhyaśodhanaśodhakānāṃ sarvatraiva tryātmakatvāt trikam anapāyi yathoktaṃ mayaiva stotre
Q: ... yatra trikānāṃ tritayaṃ samasti /
body.translated_text: Such is the established position. And therefore, since the purifiable, the act of purification, and the purifier everywhere possess a threefold nature, <s>Trika</s> never departs. As I myself have stated in my hymn: Quote: "... where the triad of <s>Trikas</s> is present."

body.text: iti / na caivam anavasthā sarvasyāsya bhagavatparasaṃvidekamayatvāt /
body.translated_text: Thus there is no infinite regress, because all of this is constituted solely by the supreme consciousness (<s>saṃvid</s>) of the Lord.

body.text: Q: ... yena tyajasi tat tyaja
body.translated_text: Quote: "That by which you renounce — renounce that [too]."

body.text: / ity evam eva mantavyam / śodhanam api antataḥ śodhako 'pi vā bhedāṃśocchalattāyāṃ pāśātmakatvāt śodhya eva / śodhanaṃ ca paramārthataḥ sarvamalaploṣacaturabhairavasaṃvidabhedihutavaha eva sarvasyānupraveśe paripūrṇataiva / yad vaksyati
body.translated_text: This is exactly how it should be understood. The act of purification, or ultimately even the purifier, when there is a surge of the aspect of difference, is itself the purifiable, being of the nature of a bond (<s>pāśa</s>). And purification, in the ultimate sense, is simply the fullness [attained] through the entry of everything into the fire of the consciousness of the four <s>Bhairavas</s> — which is non-different, which consumes all <s>malas</s> (impurities). As will be stated:

body.text: Q: evaṃ yo vetti tattvena ... /
body.translated_text: Quote: "Thus one who knows in truth..."

body.text: ityādi / tat parasaṃvidekamayaparāparādidevatānaṃ sarvātmakatvāt
body.translated_text: and so forth. Since the deities <s>Parā</s>, <s>Aparā</s>, and the rest, who are constituted solely by the supreme consciousness (<s>saṃvid</s>), possess the nature of everything —

body.text: Q: parāparāṅgasaṃbhūtā yoginyo 'ṣṭau mahābalāḥ /
body.translated_text: Quote: "<s>Yoginīs</s>, eight in number, of great strength, born from the limbs of <s>Parāparā</s> —"

body.text:
ityādivacanāl laukikaśāstrāntarīyādivācyavācakānantyam api saṃgṛhītam / tad evaṃ kṛtakariṣyamāṇādyanantasaṃketagarbhīkāreṇaivāyaṃ śodhyaśodhakabhāvo na cānavasthā na cātiprasaṅgo nāvyaptir na saṃketitasyāpāramārthikateti sthitam / evaṃ sthite prakṛtam anusarāmaḥ / akārādyā eva kālayogena somasūryau yau tau tadantaḥ prakīrtitāv iti saṃbandhaḥ/ tacchabdena prāktanaślokoktam akulaṃ bhairavātma parāmṛśyate / tenākulam evāntargṛhītakalanākaṃ kulaśakter atraiva niveśāt / kalanātmikā hi vimarśaśaktiḥ / tām antareṇākulam api turyātītaṃ nāma na kiṃ cit sauṣuptapadāviṣṭatvāt turyānantaratāyā api samānatvāt / vimarśaśaktiś ca parā parameśvarī bhairavabhaṭṭārakasya niratiśayasvātantryātmikā
pūrṇakṛśatadubhayātmakatadubhayarahitatvenāvatiṣṭhate / tatra yady api na kaś cid atra kramayaugapadyodayakalaṅkaḥ proktopadeśanayenaitāvatyāḥ parābhaṭṭārikāsaṃvido 'nantāgāmipralayodayātmakasvasvabhāvavimarśaikaghanatvāt
body.translated_text: by such statements, the infinity of the signifier and signified belonging to worldly language, other scriptures, and so on is also comprehended. Thus, by the very act of internally encompassing the infinite conventions — past, present, future, and so on — this relationship of purifiable and purifier [is established]; and there is no infinite regress, no overextension, no under-extension, and the conventionally designated is not unreal — this is established. This being established, let us follow the topic at hand. The vowels beginning with "a," by the yoga of time, are <s>Soma</s> (moon) and <s>Sūrya</s> (sun) — "those two are declared within it" — this is the syntactic connection. By the word "that," the <s>Akula</s> (the uncategorized absolute) spoken of in the preceding verse, whose nature is <s>Bhairava</s>, is referred to. Therefore <s>Akula</s> itself, having internally absorbed the power of <s>Kula</s> (the categorized), encompasses <s>Kula-śakti</s> within itself. For the power of reflective awareness (<s>vimarśa-śakti</s>) is of the nature of <s>kalanā</s> (creative activity). Without her, even <s>Akula</s>, called <s>Turyātīta</s> (beyond the fourth state), would be nothing, being sunk in the condition of deep sleep, since even the state beyond the fourth would be equivalent [to unconsciousness]. And the power of reflective awareness is the supreme Goddess (<s>Parā Parameśvarī</s>), the absolute freedom of the venerable <s>Bhairava</s>, abiding as full, as diminished, as both of these, and as devoid of both. There, although there is no stain whatsoever of sequence or simultaneity of arising — since, according to the doctrine taught, this much of the consciousness of the supreme <s>Parā Bhaṭṭārikā</s> is a single mass of self-reflective awareness of her own essential nature in the form of infinite future dissolutions and creations —

body.text:
Q: svatantraḥ paripūrṇo 'yaṃ bhagavān bhairavo vibhuḥ /
Q: tan nāsti yan na vimale bhāsayet svātmadarpaṇe //
body.translated_text: Quote: "This Lord <s>Bhairava</s>, autonomous, complete, all-pervading — there is nothing that He would not cause to shine in the stainless mirror of His own Self."

body.text: iti nītyā kramayaugapadyāsahiṣṇusvātmarūpamadhya eva yāvat kramākramāvabhāsas tāvat tadanusāreṇāyaṃ kramo vicāraṇīyaḥ, akramasya tatpūrvakatvena saṃvidy eva bhāvāt pratipādanāyās tu sarvathaiva sakramatvāt / tathā ca sarva evāyaṃ vāgrūpaḥ parāmarśaḥ kramika eva, antaḥsaṃvinmayas tv akrama eveti sadaiveyam evaṃvidhaiva evam eva vicitrā pārameśvarī parābhaṭṭārikā / tatas tatkramānusāreṇa ``at'' ityādivyapadeśaḥ / evaṃ parameśvarasya svātmanīcchātmikā svātantryaśaktir anunmīlitabhāvavikāsā tathāvidhāntarghanasaṃvitsvabhāvavimarśasārā ``a'' ity ucyate / sa cāvasthā iccheti vyapadeśyā iṣyamānānudrekā tata evānuttarasattāparāmarśātmikaiva eṣā /
body.translated_text: by this principle, even as [consciousness] rests in the center of its own nature which cannot tolerate sequence or simultaneity, insofar as there is manifestation of sequence and non-sequence, this sequence must be examined in accordance with that. For non-sequence exists precisely as consciousness, being preceded by that [sequence], while instruction is in every case sequential. And thus all this reflective awareness, being of the nature of speech, is entirely sequential; but insofar as it is constituted by inner consciousness (<s>saṃvid</s>), it is entirely non-sequential — and so always, in this very manner, infinitely variegated, is the supreme <s>Parā Bhaṭṭārikā</s>. Therefore, in accordance with that sequence, the designation "a-t" and so on [is given]. Thus, the Lord's power of freedom (<s>svātantrya-śakti</s>), whose nature is will (<s>icchā</s>), directed toward His own Self, with the unfolding of entities not yet opened out, having the essence of reflective awareness of inner dense consciousness of that nature — is called "a." And that state, designated as will (<s>icchā</s>), is that in which the desired has not yet surged forth; hence it is simply the reflective awareness of the being of the <s>Anuttara</s> (unsurpassable absolute).

body.text:
parameśvaraḥ satataṃ svasvarūpāmarśako 'kulaśaktipadātmakam api rūpam āmṛśan yady api kulaśaktīr anuyātu tathāpi kulaparāmarśato 'sya syād eva viśeṣa iti bhairavaśaktimadvimarśasatteyam / tādṛśy eva punaḥ prasarantī ānandaśaktiḥ ``ā'' iti / prasṛtā paripūrṇecchā ``i'' iti / icchaiva bhāvijñānaśaktyātmakasvātantryeṇa jighṛkṣantī īśanarūpā ``ī'' iti / unmiṣantī tu jñānaśaktir iṣyamāṇasakalabhāvonmeṣamayī ``u'' iti / unmiṣattaiva unmimiṣatām api antaḥprāṇasarvasvarūponmeṣottaraikarūpair api antaḥkaraṇavedyadeśīyāsphuṭaprāyabhedāṃśabhāsamābhiḥ saṃkocavaśenonībhūtānuttarasaṃvit sarvabhāvagarbhīkāreṇānaṅgadhainavīrūpaparadevatāyā ūḍhorūpā ūḍhasakalabhāvarāśiḥ susphuṭā prasṛtā jñānaśaktiḥ
``ū'' iti / tad evam ete parameśvarasya bhairavasya dve śaktī, prathamā svarūpaparipūraṇārūpatvāt pūrṇā cāndramasīśaktyavyatirekāc ca sahomayā vartata iti somarūpā svānandaviśrāntibhāvā icchākhyā kalanā mahāsṛṣṭivyapadeśyā, yad vakṣyate ``tatra sṛṣṭiṃ yajed'' iti / dvitīyā tu tatsvarūpabhāvarāśirecanānupraveśād riktā tadrecanād eva kṛśā bhāvamaṇḍalaprakāśanaprasāraṇavyāpārā sūryarūpā svarūpabhūtakulasaṃvitsaṃjihīrṣātmikā mahāsaṃhāraśaktir jñānākhyā / tatrāpi ca prasaratatprāktanarūpaparyālocanāvasāt svātmani yathākramaṃ somasūryarūpatāyugalakabhāvena svasaṃvidātmakaṃ bhāvākhyaṃ ca rūpam apekṣya viparyayo 'pi somasūryātmakasṛṣṭisaṃhṛtikalanayoḥ / na cātrānavasthā jñānecchayor api prasarāprasarāntarādirūpatvaṃ,
tayor api prasarāprasarayor icchājñānaprasarāprasarāntarādiparikalpanāprasaṅgād iti vācyam / upasaṃharata bāhyavibhramabhramabhramaṇaṃ tāvat, anupraviśata sūkṣmāṃ vimarśapadavīm / yāvad dhi ghaṭādāv api vijñānaṃ jāyate tāvad eva jñeyaghaṭādyaṃśakarburīkṛtasvayaṃprathaṃ jñānaṃ prathata eva / tatrāpi ca tadrūpakarburībhāve ghaṭādiprathamasūkṣmollāso'pi saṃvedya ekabhāvodgamasya anyataḥ kutaś cid abhāvasya prathamānatvāt /
body.translated_text: The supreme Lord, who constantly reflects upon His own essential nature, while reflecting upon the form that belongs to the station of <s>Akula-śakti</s> — even if He were to follow the <s>Kula-śaktis</s>, still, from the reflective awareness of <s>Kula</s>, there would indeed be a distinction for Him — thus this is the existence of the reflective awareness of <s>Bhairava</s> possessing <s>Śakti</s>. That very [awareness], when expanding further, is <s>Ānanda-śakti</s> (power of bliss) — "ā." The expanded full will is "i." Will itself, through the autonomy whose nature is the power of knowledge born of existence, grasping forth, in the form of sovereignty (<s>Īśana</s>) — is "ī." The power of knowledge (<s>Jñāna-śakti</s>), opening out, consisting of the opening out of all entities that are being desired — is "u." That very opening-out, while opening out those [entities] that are [still] opening, having as its single form the subsequent opening of the essential nature of all [things] within as the inner life-breath, yet with aspects of indistinct differentiation belonging to the domain of what is apprehended by the inner organ — through contraction, the <s>Anuttara</s>-consciousness that has become compressed, by the act of encompassing all entities within itself, in the form of the supreme deity <s>Anaṅgadhanavī</s> — is the embraced form, the fully embraced mass of all entities, the clearly manifest, expanded power of knowledge (<s>Jñāna-śakti</s>) — "ū." Thus these are the two powers of the supreme Lord <s>Bhairava</s>: the first, being of the nature of not being the fulfillment of one's own essential nature, is full — and because it does not differ from the lunar power, it contains <s>Soma</s> (the moon) within it; hence it is of <s>Soma</s>-form, resting in its own bliss, called will (<s>icchā</s>), the creative activity (<s>kalanā</s>) designated as the great creation (<s>mahāsṛṣṭi</s>) — as will be stated: "therein one should worship the creation." The second, however, through the entry into and pouring out of the mass of entities belonging to that essential nature, is empty; through that very pouring out it is diminished; its function being the illumination and expansion of the sphere of entities — it is of <s>Sūrya</s> (solar) form, whose nature is the desire to draw back the <s>Kula-saṃvid</s> (consciousness of the totality) that constitutes its own nature — it is the power of the great withdrawal (<s>mahāsaṃhāra-śakti</s>), called knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>). Moreover, within that too, by force of the contemplation of its own prior form as it expands, with respect to its own Self, through the paired nature of <s>Soma</s>-form and <s>Sūrya</s>-form in due sequence, and with regard to the form called existence (<s>bhāva</s>) that is of the nature of its own consciousness — there is also a reversal of the <s>Soma</s>- and <s>Sūrya</s>-natured creative activities of creation and withdrawal. Nor is there an infinite regress here, since even will and knowledge have the form of expansion and non-expansion and so on; if it be objected that for those [states of] expansion and non-expansion too, there would be the contingency of imagining further expansion and non-expansion of will and knowledge — withdraw for now the spinning of external delusion! Enter the subtle path of reflective awareness. For whenever cognition arises even with regard to a pot and so on, precisely then does knowledge manifest itself — self-luminous yet variegated by the aspect of the knowable pot and so on. And even there, in that variegation by the form [of the knowable], the first subtle flash of the pot and so on is also experienced, since the arising as one [unified experience] cannot be preceded by the non-existence of anything from elsewhere.

body.text: saṃvida eva svātantryaṃ bhāvojjigamiṣātmakam īśanaṃ svasaṃvitpramāṇalabdham eva / tadbhāvānucayarūpā saṃvidghanā paripūrṇā svātantryasattāpi saṃvedyā / svātmany ānandaghano bhavaṃs tathā svatantraḥ syād ity ānando 'pi nāpahnavanīyaḥ / anuttaraś ca śaktimān avyapadeśyaparacamatkārasāro bhairavabhaṭṭārakaḥ sarvatra kartṛtvena bhāsata eva / tatrāpi tv anuttarānandeccheśanonmeṣaṇonatvanimeṣāṇāṃ svarūpavimarśe teṣāṃ vicchedavicāraṇena jñānabhūmim adhiśayānānāṃ tā eva bhagavatyaḥ saṃvicchaktayaḥ samāpatanty ananyā eva svayaṃ saṃvidaḥ, paripūrṇatvenābhedāt saṃvedyopādheś ca bhedakatvāt tasya dehasaṃvedyamātratayaiva bhāvāt / ata eva śrītantrasāre nijottamāṅgacchāyā tattvam ity uktam
body.translated_text: The freedom of consciousness (<s>saṃvid</s>) itself, whose nature is the desire for the arising of entities, sovereignty (<s>Īśana</s>), is obtained precisely through the instrument of one's own consciousness. The dense consciousness, full, whose form is the accumulation of those entities, and whose nature is the existence of freedom — is also experienced. Being a mass of bliss within one's own Self, one is thus autonomous — so bliss too cannot be denied. And the <s>Anuttara</s> (unsurpassable), the possessor of power (<s>Śaktimān</s>), the venerable <s>Bhairava</s>, whose essence is the supreme wonder beyond designation — always shines everywhere as the agent. Yet even there, when in the self-reflective awareness of <s>Anuttara</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, <s>Icchā</s>, <s>Īśana</s>, <s>Unmeṣa</s>, diminishment (<s>Ūnatva</s>), and <s>Nimeṣa</s> (closing), through the examination of their mutual distinction, those who rest upon the ground of knowledge — for them, those very blessed powers of consciousness (<s>saṃvicchaktayaḥ</s>) converge, being none other than consciousness itself. [This is] because of non-difference through completeness, and because it is the limiting adjunct of the knowable that creates differentiation, and that [knowable] exists merely as what is experienced as the body. Therefore, in the sacred <s>Tantrasāra</s>, the shadow of one's own head is called the <s>tattva</s> (reality) —

body.text:
Q: svapadā svaśiraśchāyāṃ yadval laṅghitum īhate /
Q: pādoddeśe śiro na syāt tatheyaṃ baindavī kalā //
body.translated_text: Quote: "Just as one attempts to step over the shadow of one's own head with one's own foot — the head would not be at the location of the foot; such is this <s>Baindavī Kalā</s> (the creative power of the Bindu)."

body.text:
iti / tad evaṃ ṣaṭkaṃ pravṛttaṃ jñānaśaktyantam / kriyāśaktis tu prasarantī vicāryate / icchājñāne eva parasparasvarūpasāṃkaryavaicitryacamatkāramayapūrvāparībhūtasvarūpaparigrahe saṃrambhasārā kriyā / tatra yad yad anyavyāmiśritasāṃkaryam anyasaṃbandhād eti tat tad anāmarśanīyaśūnyaprāyasvarūpākramaṇapuraḥsarīkāreṇa tathā bhavati plavānām iva bhekādiḥ / tatrānuttarānandātmakaṃ vapur na vyapasarati, avyapadeśyarūpatvāt sarvajñāneṣu sarvādhāravṛttitvena paryavasatiparyantabhittirūpatvāt, api tu kramasahiṣṇutvāt saṃrambha icchaiveśanāntā svātmany anuttarānandapade ca prasaraṇakṣamā / tataḥ saiva śūnyātmakaṃ svaṃ vapur avagāhamānā bhāsvaraṃ rūpaṃ tejomayam iva prathamaṃ gāhate ``ṛ ḥ'' iti / atra hi ``i ī'' ityanugamo bhāsvararūparephaśrutyanugamaś
ca katham apahnūyatām / yathāha bhagavān puṣpadantaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus the group of six [vowels] has proceeded, ending with the power of knowledge (<s>Jñāna-śakti</s>). Now the power of action (<s>Kriyā-śakti</s>), as it expands, is to be examined. When will and knowledge themselves, in the appropriation of their own essential nature which has become prior and subsequent through the wonder of the mutual intermingling and variegation of each other's forms — [then] action, whose essence is intensity (<s>saṃrambha</s>), [arises]. In that process, whatever mutual intermingling with another arises from relation with another — that comes about through the precedence of the approach to one's own essential nature, which is virtually void and beyond reflective awareness, like frogs and such among aquatic creatures. There, the body whose nature is <s>Anuttara</s> and <s>Ānanda</s> does not depart, because it is of an undesignable nature, and because in all cognitions it abides as the substratum of all, being the ultimate ground-wall at the end of repose. Rather, because it can tolerate sequence, the intensity that is will itself, extending up to sovereignty (<s>Īśana</s>), is capable of expanding both into its own <s>Anuttara-Ānanda</s> station and into its own Self. Then that very [will], entering into its own nature which is void, first takes on a luminous form, as if consisting of light — "ṛ." For here, how can the continuation of "i" and "ī" and the continuation of the <s>repha</s> sound in its luminous form be denied? As the blessed <s>Puṣpadanta</s> has stated:

body.text: Q: raśrutisāmānyād vā siddham
body.translated_text: Quote: "Or it is established by the commonality of the <s>ra</s>-sound."

body.text: iti / śūnye hi niścale rūpe anupravivikṣāyāṃ bhāsvararūpasaṃvittisopānākramaṇaṃ sthitam eva /
body.translated_text: For when there is the desire to enter into a form that is void and motionless, the ascent of the stairway of luminous consciousness is already established.

body.text:
tato niścalarūpānupraveśāt pārthivarūpasatattvaniścalatātmakalakāraśrutyanugame ḷ ḷ3 iti / tathā ca paryante īśanarūpataiva samagrabhāvātmasvarūpollaṅghanena dīrghataraṃ plutvā niścalāṃ śūnyāṃ sattām etīti plutatvam eti ``ḷvarṇasya dīrghā na santi'' iti nyāyāt / avarṇādīnāṃ tu dīrghasyaiva dīrghataratā plutatvaṃ / tac ca prāṅnītyā dīrghatvam eva pṛthag aparyeṣaṇīyam ity āstāṃ tāvat / etac catuṣkaṃ śūnyarūpatānupraveśād dagdhabījam iva ṣaṇṭharūpaṃ bhaṇyate na tu sarvathā bījarūpatvābhāvāt, bījayonyātmakaśivaśaktyubhayātirekinaḥ kasya cid apy abhāvāt, śrīpūrvādiśāstreṣu cānabhidhānāt / laukikasukhādiṣu caivaṃvidhaiva viśrāntir ānandarūpeti tad evāmṛtabījacatuṣkam ity uktam / tad evam iccheśanaṃ cānandavapuṣi
anuttaraparadhāmani ca prāgbhāvini svarūpād apracyāviny anupraviśya ``a ā i ī iti e'', na tu viparyaye, yathoktam ``avarṇa ivarṇe e'' iti / anupraveśe cānuttarapadānupraveśe syād api kaś cid viśeṣaḥ / ānandapadānupraveśe hi sphuṭatā / anuttaradhāmasaṃbhede tu sūkṣmatā tadapekṣayā / tathāhi bhagavān bhujagavibhur ādiśat
body.translated_text: Then, from entry into the motionless form, through the continuation of the <s>la</s>-sound — which has the nature of the stability of the earth-<s>tattva</s>'s motionless reality — [we get] "ḷ" and long "ḷ." And thus, at the end, the very nature of sovereignty (<s>Īśana</s>), having leaped further by transcending one's own essential nature consisting of the totality of entities, reaches the motionless, void existence — hence it attains the <s>pluta</s> (protracted) state; [but] by the rule that "the ḷ-vowel has no long forms," [this is only notional]. For the vowels beginning with "a," the protracted state is simply the prolongation of the already long form. And that long form, by the principle stated earlier, is not to be sought as something separate — let that rest for now. This group of four, due to entering into the void nature, is called "eunuch-form" (<s>ṣaṇṭha</s>) — like a burnt seed — but not because it entirely lacks seed-nature, since there is no absence whatsoever of anything that would be beyond the seed-and-womb nature of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s>; and because it is not mentioned in the sacred <s>Pūrvādi-śāstras</s> [as seedless]. And in worldly pleasure and the like, repose of precisely this kind is of the nature of bliss — hence that very [group] is called the "four ambrosia-seeds." Thus, will and sovereignty, entering into the body of bliss (<s>Ānanda</s>) and into the supreme abode of <s>Anuttara</s> — which pre-exists and does not deviate from its own nature — [produce] "a ā i ī," thus "e"; but not in the reverse [order], as stated: "a-vowel [combines with] i-vowel [to form] e." In this entry, there might be some distinction in the entry into the <s>Anuttara</s> station: for in the entry into the <s>Ānanda</s> station there is clarity, whereas in the merging with the <s>Anuttara</s> abode there is subtlety in comparison. As the blessed Lord <s>Bhujaṅgavibhu</s> (Patanjali/Sesha) has taught:

body.text: Q: chandogānāṃ sātyamugrirāṇāyanīyā ardham ekāram ardham okāraṃ cādhīyate /
body.translated_text: Quote: "The <s>Sātyamugri-Rāṇāyanīya</s> [branch] of the <s>Chandogas</s> recite half as <s>e-kāra</s> and half as <s>o-kāra</s>."

body.text:
iti / loke'pi prākṛtadeśabhāṣādau sphuṭa eva pracuro niveśaḥ / pārameśvareṣv api ekāraukārayor ekāraukārāpekṣayā yad dhrasvatvam aṅgavaktrādiviniyoge dṛśyate tad evam eva mantavyam ardhaikārārdhaukārabhiprāyeṇa / evam ``e'' iti bījaṃ sthitam / etad api tathāśabalībhūtaṃ saṃvidvapus tathaiva tad eva rūpam anuvasat ``a ā e'' iti ai / evam unmeṣe'pi vācyam ``a ā u ū iti o'' / ``a ā o iti au'' / kevalam unmeṣo jñānaśaktyātmā prasaran yady api śūnyatāvagāhanam kuryāt tathāpi asyeśanecchātmakobhayarūpapraveśa eva śūnyatā, iccheśanayos tu svaparivṛttirūpaṃ nāstīty uktanayenaiva sthitiḥ / evam icchājñāne anuttarasvarūpānupraveśena prāptopacaye paścāt parityajya tathāvidhopādhiparispandasattām abhedasattārohaṇacinmayapuruṣatattvasatattvavedanārūpabindumātrāvaśeṣeṇa
vapuṣā tathānuttarapada līne ``aṃ'' iti /
body.translated_text: Thus. Even in the world, in <s>Prākṛta</s>, regional languages, and so on, the placement [of these sounds] is clearly abundant. And even in the <s>Pārameśvara</s> [tradition], the shortness that is seen in 'e' and 'o' relative to 'e' and 'o' [proper] in the assignment of limbs, faces, and so on — that too should be understood in just this way, with the intention of half-'e' and half-'o'. Thus 'e' is established as a seed-syllable. This too, being variegated in the same way as the body of consciousness, following that very same form — 'a, ā, e' — becomes 'ai.' Similarly for <s>unmeṣa</s> (opening/expansion) also it should be stated: 'a, ā, u, ū — thus o'; 'a, ā, o — thus au.' Only, <s>unmeṣa</s>, being of the nature of the power of knowledge, when it expands, even though it might plunge into voidness, nevertheless for this [consciousness] the entry into both forms — which are of the nature of <s>īśana</s> (lordship) and <s>icchā</s> (will) — is itself the voidness; but for <s>icchā</s> and <s>īśana</s>, there is no form of self-transformation — thus the situation is just as stated. Thus, when <s>icchā</s> and <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), having obtained their fullness through entry into the <s>anuttara</s> (supreme) nature, thereafter relinquish the existence of such conditioned vibration and, with a body that is mere <s>bindu</s> (point) — of the form of the awareness of non-difference, consciousness-constituted, ascending to the being of non-difference, the <s>puruṣa-tattva</s> and <s>sat-tattva</s> — dissolve into the <s>anuttara</s> state, [the result is] 'aṃ.'

body.text: tathāhi aukāre eva kriyāśaktiparispandaḥ parisamāpyate itīcchājñānayor atraivāntarbhāvāt triśūlarūpatvam asya ṣaḍardhaśāstre nirūpitam
body.translated_text: For thus: in 'au' itself the vibration of the power of action (<s>kriyā-śakti</s>) reaches completion; therefore, since <s>icchā</s> and <s>jñāna</s> are included here within it, its trident-form is determined in the scripture of the six half-[verses]:

body.text: Q: ...trisūlena caturthakam /
body.translated_text: Quote: '...by the trident, the fourth.'

body.text: ityādyuddeśeṣu / binduḥ punar vedanāmātraśeṣataiva sarvasya / vedanāmātrāvaśeṣam api viśvaṃ yadā svātmany ekagamanāya visṛjati svātmanaś ca sakāśāt tannirmāṇena visṛjati sa eva parameśvaraḥ, prathamaṃ śaktimadrūpapradhānatayā, idānīṃ tu śāktavisargapradhānatayā ``aḥ'' iti / aukāraparyante hi nirbharībhūte kriyāśaktiprasare etāvad anupraviṣṭam / anuttarapadasya bhairavabhaṭṭārakasya svarūpasatattvasyecchājñānakriyātmakaśaktiparispandādimadhyāntabhāgā ullilasiṣollasattollasitatāsvabhāvāḥ sūkṣmatamaprasaṃkhyānagṛhītatāvadbhūmikādhirūḍhayogijanasphuṭalaksaṇīyāḥ śrīsvacchandādiprakriyāśāstreṣu prabuddhaprasaraṇāvaraṇādirūpatvenoktāḥ / ata eva śivadṛṣṭiśāstre saptamāhnike
body.translated_text: And so on, in these designations. The <s>bindu</s> (point), moreover, is the mere remainder of feeling (<s>vedanā</s>) of everything. When even the universe, which has been reduced to mere feeling, is emitted for the sake of becoming one with one's own Self, and when from one's own Self it is emitted by creating that [universe] — that is <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord) himself: first with the predominance of the <s>śaktimat</s> (power-possessing) form, and now with the predominance of the <s>śākta visarga</s> (the emission belonging to <s>Śakti</s>) — thus 'aḥ.' For when the expansion of the power of action has become fully replete at the culmination of 'au,' this much has entered into it. The initial, middle, and final portions of the vibration of power — whose nature is <s>icchā</s>, <s>jñāna</s>, and <s>kriyā</s> — of the <s>anuttara</s> state, of <s>Bhairava Bhaṭṭāraka</s>, of the reality of His own essential nature, have the character of about-to-flash, flashing, and having-flashed; they are clearly discernible by yogis who have ascended to the corresponding levels, grasped through the most subtle contemplation; in the sacred procedural scriptures such as the <s>Svacchanda</s> and others, they are spoken of as having the form of awakened expansion, concealment, and so on. And therefore, in the seventh chapter of the <s>Śivadṛṣṭi</s> scripture:

body.text:
Q: sunirbharatarāhlādabharitākārarūpiṇi /
Q: nilīnaśaktitritaye parātmany anubhāvanāt //
body.translated_text:
Quote: 'Having the form filled with the most intense delight,
from the realization in the supreme Self in which the triad of powers is absorbed.'

body.text: ityādi
body.translated_text: And so on —

body.text: Q: tasyāpi śaktir mṛtpiṇḍaghaṭavad viśvarūpatām /
body.translated_text: Quote: 'His power too, like a lump of clay [becoming] a pot, [assumes] the form of the universe.'

body.text: gatā ... //
body.translated_text: And so on.

body.text: ityantaṃ nirūpya
body.translated_text: Having determined this up to [the verse ending with that],

body.text: Q: ekam eva hi tat tattvaṃ na saṃkhyāto 'tiriktatā /
body.translated_text: Quote: 'There is indeed only one <s>tattva</s>; there is no excess beyond number.'

body.text: iti yac chivatattvam eva anantavicitrasvātantryasphārasphuraṇaśakticamatkārabharitatopāttabhairavabhāvaṃ nirṇītaṃ tatrāyam evoktakramaḥ / saṃpradāyaprathamāhnike 'pi
body.translated_text: Thus that which is the <s>Śiva-tattva</s> alone — filled with the wonder of the power of the flash of the expansion of infinite and variegated sovereign freedom, having thereby assumed the <s>Bhairava</s> nature — has been determined; and this very order as stated [applies] there. In the first chapter of the <s>Saṃpradāya</s> [tradition] also:

body.text:
Q: sa yadāste cidāhlādamātrānubhavatallayaḥ /
Q: tadicchā tāvatī tāvaj jñānaṃ tāvat kriyā hi sā //
body.translated_text:
Quote: 'When He abides absorbed in the experience of the mere delight of consciousness,
that is His <s>icchā</s> (will) — that much; that much is <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge); and that is <s>kriyā</s> (action).'

body.text:
Q: susūkṣmaśaktitritayasāmarasyena vartate /
Q: cidrūpāhlādaparamo nirvibhāgaḥ paraḥ sadā //
body.translated_text:
Quote: 'He abides in the equilibrium of the exceedingly subtle triad of powers.
Supreme in the delight of consciousness, without division, He is the supreme, always.'

body.text: iti / tathā
body.translated_text: Thus. And likewise:

body.text:
Q: ...ghaṭaṃ jānāti yāvasā /
Q: jānāti jñānam atraiva niricchor vedanakṣatiḥ //
body.translated_text:
Quote: '...knows the pot by that force.
Knowledge [rests] right here; for one without will, there is loss of feeling.'

body.text:
Q: aunmukhyābhāvatas tasya nivṛttir nirvṛtiṃ vinā /
Q: dveṣye pravartate naiva na ca vetti vinā citim //
body.translated_text:
Quote: 'Due to the absence of orientation toward [it], there is cessation of that without delight;
[consciousness] never engages with what is repugnant, nor does it know without awareness.'

body.text: iti / tathā
body.translated_text: Thus. And likewise:

body.text:
Q: yata icchati taj jñātuṃ kartuṃ vā secchayā kriyā /
Q: tasyāḥ pūrvāparau bhāgau kalpanīyau purā hi yā //
body.translated_text:
Quote: 'Since it wills to know or to do that — with will there is action;
its prior and posterior parts are to be posited, for that which previously'

body.text:
Q: tatkarmanirvṛtiprāptir aunmukhyaṃ tadvikāsitā /
Q: na caunmukhyaprasaṅgena śivaḥ sthūlatvabhāk kvacit //
body.translated_text:
Quote: 'attains the accomplishment of its object — that orientation, that expansion of it.
And there is no occasion that <s>Śiva</s> ever becomes gross through the occasion of orientation.'

body.text: ityādi / etad āgamasarvasvaprāṇatayaiva yuktiyuktatayā hṛdayaṃgamīkṛtam / sa eṣa parameśvaro visṛjati viśvam, tac ca dharādiśaktyantaṃ kādikṣāntarūpam ity etavatī visargaśaktiḥ ``ṣoḍaśī kalā'' iti gīyate
body.translated_text: And so on. This has been made intelligible to the heart through reasoning, as it is the very life-breath of all scripture. That very <s>Parameśvara</s> emits the universe; and that [universe] extends from earth to <s>Śakti</s>, having the form of 'ka' to 'kṣa' — this much is the power of <s>visarga</s> (emission), which is celebrated as 'the sixteenth <s>kalā</s>':

body.text: Q: puruṣe ṣoḍaśakale tām āhur amṛtāṃ kalām /
body.translated_text: Quote: 'In the <s>puruṣa</s> of sixteen <s>kalās</s>, they call her the immortal <s>kalā</s>.'

body.text: iti eṣā hi na saṃkhyeyā nāpi vaidantikī dṛg api tu śaivy eva / visargaśaktir eva ca parameśvarī paramānandabhūmibījam / evaṃ hy akārādirūpaṃ ghanatāpattyā yonirūpatāṃ gṛhītvā svarūpāpracyutaṃ tad eva svasvarūpa eva yonirūpe saṃkrāmad visargapadam ity ucyate / yathoktam
body.translated_text: For she is not to be enumerated, nor is she the Vedāntic view, but rather the <s>Śaiva</s> view alone. And the power of <s>visarga</s> itself is the Supreme Goddess, the seed of the ground of supreme bliss. For thus, the form beginning with 'a,' having attained the nature of the womb (<s>yoni</s>) through arriving at density, not deviating from its own essential nature — that very thing, transitioning into its own essential nature which has the form of the womb, is called the state of <s>visarga</s> (emission). As stated:

body.text:
Q: sa visargo mahādevi yatra viśrāntim ṛcchati /
Q: guruvaktraṃ tad evoktaṃ śakticakraṃ tad ucyate //
body.translated_text:
Quote: 'That <s>visarga</s>, O great Goddess, in which [everything] comes to rest —
that alone is called the mouth of the <s>guru</s>; that is called the circle of <s>śaktis</s>.'

body.text: ityādi / akārasyaiva ghanatā kavargaḥ, kaṇṭhyatvāt / ikārasya cavargaḥ, tālavyatvāt / ukārasya pavargaḥ, auṣṭhyatvāt / ṛkārasya tavargaḥ, mardhanyatvāt, ḷkārasya tavargaḥ, dantyatvāt / yaśau cavargasyāntaḥ, raṣau ṭavargasya, lasau tavargasya, vakāro'pi tapavargayoḥ / ghanatā bodhasyāmūrtasyāpi cinmātrasyāpi kriyāśaktirūpataiva / sā coktanītyā śaktiṣaṭkakrameṇaivopajāyate / tena pañca prasṛtāḥ ṣaḍguṇitās triṃśat, ṣaḍbhiḥ saha ṣaṭtriṃśad bhavantīti /
body.translated_text: And so on. The density of 'a' itself is the <s>ka-varga</s>, because of being guttural. Of 'i,' the <s>ca-varga</s>, because of being palatal. Of 'u,' the <s>pa-varga</s>, because of being labial. Of 'ṛ,' the <s>ṭa-varga</s>, because of being cerebral. Of 'ḷ,' the <s>ta-varga</s>, because of being dental. 'Ya' and 'śa' are within the <s>ca-varga</s>; 'ra' and 'ṣa' of the <s>ṭa-varga</s>; 'la' and 'sa' of the <s>ta-varga</s>; 'va' also of the <s>ta-</s> and <s>pa-vargas</s>. The density of consciousness, even though it is formless, even though it is pure awareness alone, is indeed of the nature of the power of action (<s>kriyā-śakti</s>). And that [density], by the stated method, arises precisely through the sequence of the sixfold <s>śaktis</s>. Therefore, five [vargas] multiplied by six make thirty; with the six [antaḥsthas and ūṣmans] they become thirty-six.

body.text: tad evaṃ śivabījam eva svātantryād ghanībhūtatayā kvacid vapuṣi śāktarūpe kusumatayā tiṣṭhad yonir ity abhidhīyate / tad eva hi puṣpaṃ purvoktanayena grāhyagrāhaṇagrāhakakoṇatrayamayaṃ vastutaḥ prasūtipadaṃ bījasaṃmiśratayaiva bhavati, tadaiva puṣparūpatvāt, anyadā tu yogyatayaiva tathāvyapadeśaḥ / tathā ca tat kusumam eva trikoṇatayā yonirūpam / tat sphuṭībhūtavibhaktagrāhyādirūpasomasūryāgnisṛṣṭisthitisaṃhṛtīḍāpiṅgalāsuṣumnādharmādharmaśabalādikoṇatritayā pārameśvarī bhairavī bhaṭṭārikā mudrā tadrūpayonyādhāratayā yonir iti nirdiṣṭā / tathā ca śrīkubjikāmate khaṇḍacakravicāre amum evārthaṃ pradhānatayādhikṛtyādiṣṭam
body.translated_text: Thus, the seed of <s>Śiva</s> alone, by its sovereign freedom, standing in a densified form sometimes in the body of <s>Śakti</s>-form as a blossom, is called the womb (<s>yoni</s>). For that very flower, by the aforementioned method, consisting of the triangle of grasped (<s>grāhya</s>), grasping (<s>grāhaṇa</s>), and grasper (<s>grāhaka</s>), is in reality the seat of generation — being mixed with the seed alone. For only then does it have the form of a flower; at other times, it is designated so only by capacity. And thus, that very blossom, being triangular, is the womb-form. The Supreme <s>Bhairavī Bhaṭṭārikā</s>, who is the <s>mudrā</s> — having the triangle of corners that are the distinctly manifested and differentiated forms of graspable and so on, of <s>Soma</s>-<s>Sūrya</s>-<s>Agni</s>, of creation-sustenance-dissolution, of <s>Iḍā</s>-<s>Piṅgalā</s>-<s>Suṣumnā</s>, of <s>dharma</s>-<s>adharma</s>-and-mixed — is designated as the womb by virtue of being the support of such a womb-form. And thus, in the <s>Śrī Kubjikāmata</s>, in the examination of the <s>khaṇḍacakra</s>, this very meaning is primarily addressed and taught:

body.text: Q: māyopari mahāmāyā trikoṇānandarūpiṇī / %not in ed. of KuMa? for Mahāmāyā \cf \RauSuSam 4:28cd: māyopari mahāmāyā sarvakāraṇakāraṇam; = \agama{Niśvāsaguhya} 7.253ab
body.translated_text: Quote: 'Above <s>Māyā</s>, the great <s>Mahāmāyā</s>, triangular, of the form of bliss.'

body.text: ityādi / ata eva tathāvidhabījakusumaikaghanabhāvaśivaśaktisaṃghaṭṭaḥ svayaṃ svātmanaiva pūjya ity upadiṣṭaṃ śrītrikatantrasāre
body.translated_text: And so on. Therefore, the union of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s>, which is the single dense unity of such a seed and blossom, is to be worshipped by oneself through one's own Self — as taught in the sacred <s>Trikatantrasāra</s>:

body.text:
Q: śivaśaktisamāpattyā śivaśaktighanātmakaḥ /
Q: śivaśaktisamāpatti trikaṃ saṃpūjayet param //
body.translated_text:
Quote: 'Through the union of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s>, being of the nature of the dense unity of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s>,
one should worship the supreme <s>Trika</s> through the union of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s>.'

body.text:
iti / evaṃ ca ghanībhāvo 'pi vaikharīrūpe yady api sphuṭībhavati tathāpi sarvasarvātmani parāvāgvapuṣi mukhyatayāvatiṣṭhate / tatra paraṃ kaṇṭhoṣṭhasthānakaraṇāny api sarvasarvātmakam eveti viśeṣaḥ / tathā hy antar api saṃjalpet paśyed iti sphuṭa evānubhavo bhedaś ca sthānādikṛta eva, śrutyekaprāṇatvāt varṇānāṃ / kiṃ bahunā / bālo'pi vyutpādyamāno 'ntas tathārūpatayā vimṛśati bhāvajātaṃ, viparyayeṇa saṃśayenāpi vā vimṛśati / avacchedaṃ tāvat saṃvedayata eva / sa ca vāgvimarśakṛta eva / ata eva saṃvāravivārālpaprāṇamahāprāṇatāśvāsanādānupradānādiyogo'pi cāntas tathāsamucitasvabhāvaḥ syād eva, anyathā sasthāneṣu bhedāyogāt / antarhitakaraṇaśaktayo'pi syur eva, śṛṇomy aśrauṣaṃ paśyāmy adrākṣaṃ saṃkalpayāmi
samakalpayam ityāder api saṃkalpasyānyathāvaicitryāyogāt / tad anayā yuktyā nibhālitayāntar adhikam adhikam anupraviśya pariśīlayata tāṃ samvidaṃ yatra sarvasarvātmakabodhaikaghanakaṇṭhauṣṭhādidhāmni tathāvidhabodhaikaghanavimarśātmakasvātantryasāramahāmantrarūpavarṇabhaṭṭārakaniveśaḥ /
body.translated_text: And thus, although densification becomes manifest in the <s>Vaikharī</s> form, nevertheless it primarily abides in the body of <s>Parā Vāk</s> (Supreme Speech), which is the Self of all in all respects. The special point there is that the supreme [level] — even the places of articulation such as throat and lips — is the Self of all in all respects. For thus, even internally one would converse and see — this is a clear experience; and the differences are made by place of articulation and so on alone, because phonemes have audibility as their sole life-force. What more? Even a child being instructed reflects internally upon the totality of things in that very form, or reflects upon them contrarily, or with doubt. At the very least, one experiences delimitation. And that [delimitation] is made by linguistic reflection alone. Therefore, even internally the conjunction of closed and open [articulation], of unaspirate and aspirate, of breathing in and breathing out and so on, would indeed be of a nature appropriate to that [internal level] — otherwise, there would be no differentiation in the same places. Even internally there would be powers of sense-organs: 'I hear,' 'I heard,' 'I see,' 'I saw' — and 'I intend,' 'I intended' — even this variety of conceptual thought would be impossible otherwise. Therefore, by this reasoning well-contemplated, entering more and more inward, cultivate that consciousness where, in the domain of throat, lips, and so on that is the single dense mass of the awareness that is the Self of all in all, there is the placement of the lord of phonemes (<s>varṇa-bhaṭṭāraka</s>) — whose nature is the great <s>mantra</s>, whose essence is sovereign freedom, whose form is the single dense mass of awareness of that very nature.

body.text:
bodhaikaghanatānirviśeṣatāyām idaṃ sthānam, idaṃ karaṇam, ayaṃ varṇa iti kathaṃkāraṃ vibhāga iti ced yad evaṃ svātantryaṃ tathāvidhe svātmani ghaṭo 'yam, sukham idam, jñānam idam, jñātāham ity avabhāsayati tasyaivaṃvidhacitratararūpāvabhāsena ko vā kiyān vā prayāsaḥ / ata eva sarve pāṣāṇatarutiryaṅmanuṣyadevarudrakevalimantratadīśatanmaheśādikā ekaiva parabhaṭṭārikābhūmiḥ sarvasarvātmaiva parameśvararūpeṇāste iti tadvicitrasthānādisārvātmyanirviṣṭasphuṭāsphuṭavyaktāvyaktādirūpaśabdaśarīrā mantra vīryam iti gīyate/ tathā hi vīṇāvipañcīkacchapikāmurujādiṣu sa eva svano 'nyato 'nyato deśād apy udbhavann ekasthāna iti kathyate / evaṃ tāramadhyamandreṣv api tatsthāyisvaraikātmye 'pi vācyam / ata eva ca sa eva varṇaḥ kva cit prāṇini
