sthānāntarasamullāsy api bhavati yathā dhvāṃkṣeṣu kakāraṭakārarephā uccarantaḥ sarva evodarapāyukaṇṭhatālunirvartyā upalabhyante / avyaktatve 'pi ta eva tāvantaḥ śabdatvāt śabdasya ca mātṛkātirekino 'bhāvāt / mātṛkātireky api avyaktaḥ śabdo 'nupayogān na saṃgṛhīta ity apy ayuktam / avyaktavarṇarūpasyāpi maurujasāmudrādidhvanitasya hlādaparitāpakāritvam api asty eveti ko 'nyo 'bhimata upayogaḥ / pārameśvare 'pi avyaktadhvaner mukhyatayaiva prāyaśo mantratvaṃ nirūpitam ardhacandrādīnām eva mantravyāptisāratvenābhidhānāt / tatra ca
body.translated_text: If one objects: 'In the non-differentiated, single dense mass of consciousness, how can there be division as "this is the place, this is the organ of articulation, this is the phoneme"?' — then: just as that very sovereign freedom illuminates in its own Self of such a nature 'this is a pot,' 'this is pleasure,' 'this is knowledge,' 'I am the knower' — what effort or how much effort is there for it to manifest such increasingly variegated forms? Therefore, all — stones, trees, animals, humans, gods, <s>Rudras</s>, <s>Kevalins</s>, <s>Mantras</s>, their Lords, their Great Lords, and so on — are one single ground of <s>Parā Bhaṭṭārikā</s>, the Self of all in all respects, abiding in the form of <s>Parameśvara</s>; and having as their sound-body the clearly and unclearly manifest, the distinct and indistinct forms pervading the universality of such variegated places of articulation and so on, they are celebrated as the power of <s>mantras</s> (<s>mantra-vīrya</s>). For thus, in the <s>vīṇā</s>, <s>vipañcī</s>, <s>kacchapikā</s>, <s>muruja</s>, and other [instruments], that very sound, even though arising from different places, is spoken of as being of one place. Similarly, it should be said regarding the high, middle, and low [registers] — even though the note abiding there is of one nature. And therefore, that very phoneme, in some living being, manifests even from a different place of articulation — just as in crows, the sounds 'ka,' 'ṭa,' and 'ra' are all perceived as being produced from the belly, anus, throat, and palate. Even in their indistinct form, they are precisely that many [phonemes], because they are sound, and because sound does not exist beyond the <s>Mātṛkā</s> (the mother-alphabet). And it is not correct to say that sound beyond the <s>Mātṛkā</s>, being indistinct, is not included because it is useless — for even the sound of drums, the ocean, and so on, though of indistinct phonemic form, does indeed produce delight and torment — so what other desired utility [is needed]? Even in the supreme [level], the <s>mantra</s>-nature of indistinct sound is established primarily in most cases, since the <s>ardha-candra</s> (half-moon) and the rest alone are stated as the essence of <s>mantra</s>-pervading. And there:

body.text: Q: nirodhinīm anuprāptaḥ śabdaḥ śumaśumāyate /
body.translated_text: Quote: 'The sound, having reached <s>Nirodhinī</s>, makes a whispering hum.'

body.text: ityādy uktam / ghaṇṭākāṃsyādidhvanīnāṃ śrotraghaṭṭanādīnāṃ ca nādopadeśe nirūpaṇāt
body.translated_text: And so on is stated. Because in the teaching on <s>nāda</s>, the sounds of bells, gongs, and so on, and the striking of the ears are determined:

body.text:
Q: hayo heṣati yadvac ca dānta udravatīva ca /
Q: siṃho garjati yadvac ca uṣṭraḥ sītkurute yathā //
body.translated_text:
Quote: 'Just as a horse neighs, and a tamed [elephant] trumpets,
and a lion roars, and a camel hisses,'

body.text:
Q: tathodīrya paśoḥ prāṇān ākarṣanti balādhikāḥ /
Q: mahāmantraprayogo 'yam asādhyākṛṣṭikarmaṇi //
body.translated_text:
Quote: 'so, having aroused [them], the more powerful ones draw out the <s>prāṇas</s> (life-breaths) of the bound soul.
This is the application of great <s>mantras</s> in the act of attraction of the unattainable.'

body.text: ity uktaṃ guhyayoginītantre / tatropāyamātram etat / vastutas tv āntara evāsau nādātmā mantra iti tu kathyamānaṃ bhavadbhir api asmābhir api vyaktavarṇamālādimantreṣv api na na saṃcārayituṃ śakyate /
body.translated_text: Thus it is stated in the <s>Guhyayoginītantra</s>. There, this is merely the means. In reality, however, that inner <s>nāda</s>-natured <s>mantra</s> — this, which is being stated by you and by us alike, cannot but be applied even in <s>mantras</s> of distinct phonemic alphabets and so on.

body.text:
tasmād avyakto varṇātmaiva śabdo yathā vidūragato'pi ghaṭo ghaṭa eva iti sthitam / sa ca prāṇabheryādibhedena sthānāntaram api anusaran sa evety api sthitam / ata evedanīṃ sarvabhūtarutajñānaṃ yac cheṣamuninā bhagavatopadiṣṭaṃ taddhṛdayaṃgamībhūtaṃ, anyathā śabdārthapratyayānāṃ ya itaretarādhyāso yaś ca dhyānadhāraṇāsamādhisaṃyamena tatpravibhāgaparyantaparalābhaḥ sa katham asphuṭavarṇarūpatvātirekivihagādikūjitajñānāya paryavasyet / yadā tu ta eva varṇā varṇānām eva ca paramārthato 'rthatādātmyalakṣaṇaṃ vācakatvam tadā yuktyāta eva vihagādirutajñānam / bheryādiśabdā api hy arthavanta eva jayājayasūcakatayopadeśād vihagādirutavat / tadabhiprāyeṇaiva śikṣāsūtrakārasūtrāṇi havisarjanīyāv urasyāv ekeṣāṃ radanamūlam ekeṣām
ityādīni vācakībhavanti na tv aparathā kathaṃcid api / ata eva kiṃcid vaicitryam ālambyānyatvam anyatvaṃ cāśaṅkamānaiḥ visarjanīyāj jihvāmūlīyopadhmānīyau, anunāsikebhyaḥ pañcayamān, ḍakāraḍhakārayaralavakṣakārebhyaḥ tān eva laghuprayatnatarān bhedenābhimanya catuḥṣaṣṭir varṇā uktāḥ / anyatvaṃ cātra svaravyañjanayor iva ṛvamaraśabdayoḥ / śrītrikaratnakule 'pi uktam
body.translated_text: Therefore, it is established that sound is of the nature of phonemes alone, even when indistinct — just as a pot, even when far away, is still a pot. And it is also established that [sound], even when following a different place through the differentiation of breath, drums, and so on, is the same. And therefore, the knowledge of all creature-sounds, which was taught by the blessed Lord to the sage <s>Śeṣa</s>, becomes intelligible to the heart; otherwise, the superimposition of word, meaning, and cognition upon one another, and the attainment of their ultimate discrimination through the <s>saṃyama</s> (concentration) of meditation, <s>dhāraṇā</s>, and <s>samādhi</s> — how could this culminate in the knowledge of the cries of birds and other creatures, which exceed the form of distinct phonemes? But when those are indeed phonemes, and the denotative capacity of phonemes is ultimately of the nature of identity with their objects — then by reasoning alone, the knowledge of the sounds of birds and other creatures [follows]. For sounds of drums and so on are indeed meaningful, since they are taught as indicative of victory and defeat, just like the sounds of birds and other creatures. And with that very intention, the <s>sūtras</s> of the author of the <s>Śikṣā-sūtra</s> — 'the <s>havisarjanīyas</s> are chest [sounds] for some; root of the teeth for others' — and so on become denotative; but not otherwise in any way. Therefore, by those who, seizing upon some variety, suspect otherness upon otherness, the <s>jihvāmūlīya</s> and <s>upadhmānīya</s> [are derived] from <s>visarjanīya</s>; the five <s>yamas</s> (nasal stops) from the nasals; and from 'ḍa,' 'ḍha,' 'ya,' 'ra,' 'la,' 'va,' 'kṣa,' and 'ka' — those very same [sounds] with lighter articulation, considering them as different — sixty-four phonemes are stated. And the otherness here is like that of vowels and consonants, [or] of the words <s>ṛ</s>, <s>vama</s>, and <s>ra</s>. In the sacred <s>Trikaratnakula</s> also it is stated:

body.text:
Q: aṣṭāṣṭakavibhedena mātṛkā yā nirūpitā /
Q: tad eva kulacakraṃ tu tena vyāptam idaṃ jagat //
body.translated_text:
Quote: 'The <s>Mātṛkā</s>, which is determined as having the division of eight groups of eight —
that alone is the <s>kulacakra</s> (circle of <s>kula</s>); by that, this universe is pervaded.'

body.text: iti / mātṛkājñānabhede vistarato nirūpitam etat / iha tu tatprakriyānabhiniveśaḥ, pūrṇataikasāratvāt / tad evaṃ sarvatrāyam īdṛśaḥ saṃvidanupraveśakramaḥ / padārthaḥ saṃkalpyamānaḥ sākṣātkriyamāṇo vāmāyīyāsāṃketikasvarūpabhūtaśuddhavimarśātmaparavāṅmantramahāmahasi tāvat pratiṣṭhāṃ bhajate yatra sarvavādibhir avikalpā daśā gīyate / tac ca paramamantramahaḥ pṛthivyādau śuddhavyāmiśrādipāramārthikabījapiṇḍarūpakādivarṇātmakam eva, anyathā merubadarajalajvalanabhāvābhāvaghaṭasukhanirvikalpajñānānīty ekam eva sarvaṃ syāt / vikalpo 'pi tatprasādotthaḥ tām eva saraṇim anusaret,
body.translated_text: Thus. This has been explained in detail in the section on the differentiation of <s>Mātṛkā</s>-knowledge. Here, however, there is no insistence on that procedure, since [the text's] sole essence is fullness. Thus, everywhere the order of the entry of consciousness (<s>saṃvid</s>) is of this kind: an object being intended or being directly experienced rests first in the great radiance of the supreme speech-<s>mantra</s>, whose nature is pure reflective awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>), which constitutes the non-<s>māyic</s>, non-conventional (<s>asāṃketika</s>) essential nature—where all schools proclaim the state beyond conceptual construction (<s>avikalpā daśā</s>). And that supreme <s>mantra</s>-radiance, in [the case of] earth and the like, is of the nature of syllables (<s>varṇa</s>) alone—in the forms of seeds (<s>bīja</s>), clusters (<s>piṇḍa</s>), and figures (<s>rūpaka</s>), whether pure, mixed, or ultimate in reality. Otherwise, <s>Meru</s>, jujube-fruit, water, fire, being, non-being, pot, pleasure, and non-conceptual cognition—all would be one and the same. Even conceptual thought (<s>vikalpa</s>), arising by the grace of that [supreme mantra-radiance], follows that very path,

body.text:
na tu pratyuta tatsvarūpaṃ bhindyāt / tathā ca yad eva tad asāṃketikaṃ mantravapus tad eva anyonyavicitrarūpaṃ paśyadbhiḥ sarvajñaiḥ saṃketopāyam upāsyatayā upadiśyate / tatraiva cāsāṃketike vāṅmahasi tathā khalu māyīyāḥ saṃketāḥ patanti yathā ta evāmāyīyāsaṃketitamantratādātroyaṃ pratipadyante / tathāsvarūpapratipattir eva hi teṣāṃ vācakatābhāvo nānyaḥ kaś cit / atra ca sphuṭam abhijñānam abhyāsavasāt / sāṃketikatām āpanno ciratarapūrvavṛttagośabdaparāmarśas tathaiva saṃketakāle goparāmarśo 'py anyo'māyīyāsāṃketikaparāmarśadhāmany eva nipatati / yāvat bālasyāpijanmāntarānusaraṇe 'pi citsvabhāvasyādau sthitaivāsaṃketikī sattā, anyathānavasthānāt / evam eva khalu saṃketagrahaṇopapattir nānyathetīśvarapratyabhijñāṭīkāyām api
śrīmadutpaladevapādair nirṇītam / atra cānupraveśayuktiḥ
body.translated_text: but does not, conversely, fragment its essential nature. And accordingly, that very non-conventional <s>mantra</s>-body is taught by the omniscient ones—who perceive the mutually variegated forms [of things]—as something to be meditated upon through the device of convention (<s>saṃketa</s>). And indeed, in that very non-conventional radiance of speech, <s>māyic</s> conventions fall in such a way that they attain identity with the non-<s>māyic</s>, non-conventional <s>mantra</s>. For their denotative capacity (<s>vācakatā</s>) is nothing other than the attainment of their own true nature—there is no other [basis for it]. And here, clear recognition [of this] comes through the force of practice. A cognition of the word 'cow' (<s>go</s>), long accustomed through prior usage, having acquired conventionality, [and] the cognition of 'cow' at the time of [establishing] convention—these are both different, [yet both] fall within the very domain of the non-<s>māyic</s>, non-conventional reflective awareness. Inasmuch as even for an infant, in following [impressions from] other births, since [consciousness] is of the nature of <s>cit</s> (awareness), the non-conventional existence is established from the very beginning; otherwise there would be infinite regress. In exactly this way the acquisition of convention is justified—not otherwise. This has been determined by the revered <s>Utpaladeva</s> in the commentary on the <s>Īśvarapratyabhijñā</s> as well. And here the reasoning for [this] entry [of awareness into convention] is [given by the verse]:

body.text:
Q: paśyaty anyac chṛṇoty anyat karoty anyac ca jalpati /
Q: cintayaty anyad ābhuṅkte tatrāsāṃketikī sthitiḥ //
body.translated_text: One sees one thing, hears another, does yet another, and speaks [another]; one thinks something else, eats [something else]—therein lies the non-conventional state.

body.text: iti / bhaṭṭārakaśrīśrīkaṇṭhapādāḥ
body.translated_text: Thus. The revered lord <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s>

body.text: Q: mano'py anyatra nikṣiptaṃ cakṣur anyatra pātitam
body.translated_text: also said: 'The mind is placed on one thing, the eye is cast elsewhere'—

body.text: ityādy apy avocan / tad apy asāṃketikamantravapuḥ svabījam anudhāvad anuttarapadaparyavasāyi bhavati / tad apy anuttarapadaṃ satatatathāvidhānantasamudāyavaicitryasaṃrambhasāraṃ visargadṛṣṭyā prasarad eva, visargasyaiva hakalāparyantatayā prasarāt tasyā api hakārākhyaśaktikuṇḍalinyāḥ svarūpabhedātmakabindusvarūpadvāreṇānuttarapada eva saṃkramāt, svarūpa eva viśrāmyati / ekākṣarasaṃvit kila svarūpata eva deśakālakalanopādhānādinairapekṣyeṇaiva prāguktatattvapūrṇatānayena jhagiti visargabhūmau dhāvati / visargabhūmiśleṣa evānandeccheśanonmeṣatatprasṛtitadvaicitryakriyāśaktimayānām ākārādīnāṃ sthitiḥ /
body.translated_text: and so on. That too—the non-conventional <s>mantra</s>-body—pursuing its own seed, culminates in the <s>anuttara</s>-state (the Ultimate). And that <s>anuttara</s>-state, whose essence is the profusion of the variety of the endless aggregate [of manifestations] that is ever thus, spreads forth in the aspect of <s>visarga</s> (emission). [This is] because <s>visarga</s> itself spreads forth as terminated by the <s>ha</s>-<s>kalā</s>; and because that [<s>ha</s>-<s>kalā</s>] too—the <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s>-power called <s>hakāra</s>—passes into the <s>anuttara</s>-state itself through the door of the <s>bindu</s> (point), which is of the nature of differentiation from its own essential nature, [and thus] rests in its own nature. The one-syllable consciousness (<s>ekākṣara-saṃvit</s>), by its very nature, without dependence on the imposition of spatial-temporal division and the like, rushes instantaneously to the plane of <s>visarga</s> (emission) by the previously stated method of fullness of reality (<s>tattva</s>). In the very embrace of the <s>visarga</s>-plane lies the abiding of <s>ā</s> and the other [vowels], which are composed of the powers of <s>ānanda</s> (bliss), <s>icchā</s> (will), <s>īśana</s> (lordship), <s>unmeṣa</s> (opening forth), their expansion, their variety, and <s>kriyā</s> (action).

body.text: sa eva visargaḥ svasattānāntarīyakatayaiva tathaivātibharitayā sattayā prasaran drāg ity eva hakalāmayaḥ saṃpadyate / hakalāmayatāsaṃpattir eva vastutaḥ kādisattānantatattvajālasthitiḥ / hakalaiva ca punar api bindāv anupraviśanty anuttarapada eva paryavasyatīty ekaivādvayaparipūrṇarūpā saṃvedanasattābhaṭṭārikeyaṃ parā bhagavatī parameśvarī, na tv atra kramādiyogaḥ kaś cit / tad etad ucyate ``aham'' iti viparyaye tu saṃhṛtau ``maha'' iti / dvaidham api ceyam ekaiva vastutaḥ saṃvit / evam eṣa sa sarvatra ghaṭasukhādiprakāśe 'pi svātmaviśrāntisarvasvabhūto 'hambhāvaḥ / yathoktam
body.translated_text: That very <s>visarga</s>, spreading forth with an existence that is inseparable from its own being and yet overflowing with that very fullness, becomes composed of the <s>ha</s>-<s>kalā</s> instantaneously. The attainment of <s>ha</s>-<s>kalā</s>-nature is in reality the abiding of the net of infinite realities (<s>tattvas</s>) [in the form of] the existence of <s>ka</s> and the subsequent [consonants]. And the <s>ha</s>-<s>kalā</s> again, entering into the <s>bindu</s>, culminates in the <s>anuttara</s>-state itself. Thus this single, non-dual, perfectly full awareness-existence—the sovereign Lady (<s>Bhaṭṭārikā</s>)—is the supreme Goddess, the supreme Sovereign; yet no relation of sequence or the like [truly applies] here. This is expressed as '<s>aham</s>' (I); and in reverse—in withdrawal—as '<s>maha</s>' (the great). And though twofold, this is in reality one single consciousness. In this way, this I-sense (<s>aham-bhāva</s>), whose entire essence is repose in one's own Self, [is present] everywhere, even in the manifestation of a pot, pleasure, and the like. As stated:

body.text: Q: prakāśasyātmaviśrāntir ahaṃbhāvo hi kīrtitaḥ /
body.translated_text: The repose of luminosity (<s>prakāśa</s>) in itself is indeed declared to be the I-sense (<s>aham-bhāva</s>).

body.text: iti / sa ca vastutaḥ sarvātmakaḥ samanantaranirṇītanītyā -- iti parābhaṭṭārikānuviddho bhairavātmaka eva / yathoktaṃ mayaiva stotre
body.translated_text: Thus. And that [I-sense] is in reality the Self of all, by the method just determined—thus it is pervaded by the supreme Lady (<s>Parā Bhaṭṭārikā</s>) and is of the nature of <s>Bhairava</s> himself. As stated by me in [my] hymn:

body.text: Q: viśvatra bhāvapaṭale parijṛmbhamāṇa

children.text:
Q: vicchedaśūnyaparamārthacamatkṛtir yā /
Q: tāṃ pūrṇavṛtty aham iti prathanasvabhāvāṃ
children.translated_text: the supreme wonder (<s>camatkṛti</s>) that is without interruption, whose nature is manifestation as the full activity 'I'—
to that Goddess, the state of abiding in one's own Self, spontaneously [arising], I bow.

body.translated_text: Expanding everywhere in the canvas of [all] entities,

body.text: iti / eṣa eva śrīvāmanaviracite dvayasaṃpattivārtike upadeśanayo boddhavyaḥ / tena sthitam etad akāra eva sarvādyaḥ / yatrāpi harṣaghaṭanīlādau hakārādyā api varṇās tatrāpi tathāvidhānantanijapūrvāparavarṇasamākṣepa eva, anyathā tasyaiva hādeḥ samudayāyogāt / te param ākṣipyamāṇatvād evāntamilīnā vikalpagocaratvam aprāptāḥ, ata eva sarvatra vijñāne sarvā eva devatāḥ samam eva samudāyaṃ dadhatyaś citrāṃ saṃvittivṛttiṃ vartayanti / tad anenaivāśayena kālādhikārādāv ekasminn eva prāṇe prāṇaṣoḍaśāṃśe 'pi vā ṣaṣṭitaddviguṇādyabdodayapūrvakaṃ mātṛrudralokapālagrahanāgādīnām udayapralayāś citrā nirūpitāḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus. This very instructional method is to be understood in the <s>Dvayasaṃpattivārtika</s> composed by the revered <s>Vāmana</s>. Therefore, it is established that <s>a</s>-<s>kāra</s> alone is the first of all. Even where <s>ha</s>-<s>kāra</s> and other letters [appear to come first]—as in [the cognitions of] joy, pot, blue, and the like—even there, it is precisely the gathering up of one's own infinite prior and subsequent letters of that very kind [that occurs]; otherwise, that very <s>ha</s> and the rest would be incapable of forming an aggregate. But those [other letters], by virtue of being attracted [into the aggregate], are dissolved within and do not reach the domain of conceptual thought. For this very reason, in every cognition, all the deities equally constitute the aggregate and operate the variegated functioning of awareness. With this very intent, in the section on Time and the like, within a single <s>prāṇa</s> (breath) or even in a sixteenth part of a <s>prāṇa</s>, the variegated arising and dissolution of <s>mātṛs</s> (mothers), <s>Rudras</s>, world-protectors, planets, <s>nāgas</s>, and the like have been described, preceded by the arising of sixty [units], their double, and so on up to a year.

body.text:
tac citrānantodayapralayamaya eva dvitīyo 'pi prāṇacārādir ity akālakalitam eva tattvaṃ vastutaḥ paramārthaḥ, yadi param etāvanmātraṃ māyīyādhyavasāyānadhyavaseyam iti nāstitābhimānakāri parasaṃvidi tu tatkālaṃ bhāsate eva / ata evaikasyām eva jñānakalanāyāṃ paśyaty anyad vikalpayaty anyad ityādyupadeśena yad uktam devatātrayādhiṣṭhānaṃ tat sarvatraivānapāyi / sarvāṇy eva ca saṃvedanāni vastuto 'ham iti paramārthāni vimarśamayāny eva / tad evaṃ sthitam etad viśvam antaḥsthitam ānandaśaktibharito vaman grasamānaś ca visarga eva parameśvaro ghanībhūya hakārātmatāṃ pratipadyānantasaṃyogavaicitryeṇa kṣarūpatām apy eti / sa evaiṣa dūtyatmakaśāktayonisaṃghaṭṭasamucitavarṇātmakakṣobhaḥ / anāhatanādadaśāśrayaṇena
madhyamasauṣumnapadocchalattattadanantabhāvapaṭalātmā visargo viśliṣyan dhruvadhāmni anuttarapada eva praviśatīti prāg apy uktam eta / amī cākārādyāḥ sthitimantaḥ prāṇe tuṭiṣoḍaśakādisthityā ekāṃ tuṭiṃ saṃdhīkṛtyārdhārdhabhāgena pralayodayayor bahir api pañcadaśadinātmakakālarūpatāṃ tanvate iti tithayaḥ kalāś coktāḥ / ṣoḍaśy eva ca kalā visargātmā viśliṣyantī saptadaśī kalā śrīvādyādiśāstreṣu nirūpitā
body.translated_text: Since the second [moment] of the movement of <s>prāṇa</s> and so on is also composed of that very variegated, infinite arising and dissolution, the reality (<s>tattva</s>) is in truth unconditioned by time—that is the ultimate truth (<s>paramārtha</s>). If, however, only this much—that which is not to be determined by <s>māyic</s> determination—gives rise to a nihilistic attitude, [know that] in the supreme consciousness it shines at that very time. For this very reason, by the teaching 'one sees one thing, conceptualizes another' and so on, what has been stated—that which is the presiding [function] of the triad of deities—is never absent anywhere in a single act of cognitive division (<s>jñāna-kalanā</s>). And all cognitions are in reality of the nature of 'I'—ultimate, consisting of reflective awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>). Thus it is established: this universe is contained within. The supreme Lord, filled with the power of bliss (<s>ānandaśakti</s>), emitting and swallowing [the universe], is <s>visarga</s> (emission) itself, [who] having become condensed, attains the nature of <s>ha</s>-<s>kāra</s>, and through the variety of infinite unions also reaches the form of <s>kṣa</s>. This very [emission] is the agitation (<s>kṣobha</s>) consisting of the letters appropriate to the contact of the <s>Śākta</s> womb (<s>yoni</s>) whose nature is the <s>Dūtī</s> (Messenger-power). Resting on the state of the unstruck sound (<s>anāhata-nāda</s>), the <s>visarga</s>, whose nature is the canvas of those various infinite entities arising in the middle <s>suṣumnā</s> path, separating, enters the permanent abode—the <s>anuttara</s>-state itself—as has been previously stated. And these <s>ā</s>-<s>kāra</s> and other [vowels], abiding in the <s>prāṇa</s> in [units of] sixteen <s>tuṭis</s> and the like, making one <s>tuṭi</s> the juncture and through halving and halving again [extending] outward in the form of dissolution and arising, externally unfold the form of time consisting of fifteen-day [fortnights]—hence [they are called] <s>tithis</s> (lunar days) and <s>kalās</s> (phases). And the sixteenth <s>kalā</s> itself, being of the nature of <s>visarga</s>, separating, is described in the <s>Śrīvādya</s> and other scriptures as the seventeenth <s>kalā</s>:

body.text: Q: sā tu saptadaśī devī hakārārdhārdharūpiṇī /
body.translated_text: That seventeenth Goddess is of the form of half of the half of <s>ha</s>-<s>kāra</s>.

body.text: iti / visargasya hakārārdhatvāt tato'pi viśleṣasyārdhatvād iti niravayavasyaikavarṇasya katham eṣā vikalpanā iti ced asmatpakṣe sarvam evānavayavaṃ cinmayaikāvabhāsanānatirekāt, tathāpi ca svātantryād eva avayavāvabhāse 'py anavayavataivānapāyinī, tathehāpi astu ko virodhaḥ / evam eva varṇopapattiḥ, aparathā dantyoṣṭhyakaṇṭhyatālavyādivarṇeṣu kramaprasārī pavana āghātakaḥ kathaṃ kaṇṭhaṃ hatvā tālv āhantīti / yugapadāpūrakatve 'pi samānakālatā syāt, yatra kaṇṭhaghāṭotthaṃ rūpaṃ tat tu tālvāhatijaṃ sarvatra saṃbhavati / śvāsanādayoś ca paścātpratīyamānatayānupradānatvam ucyate / dvimātratrimātreṣu ca dvikādiyogo garbhīkṛtaikadvayādir eva /
body.translated_text: Thus. Because <s>visarga</s> is half of <s>ha</s>-<s>kāra</s>, and the separation from that is again half [of that]—if one objects: how is such division possible for a single, partless letter?—in our view, everything is partless, since there is nothing beyond the manifestation of a single consciousness (<s>cinmaya</s>). And yet, through sheer autonomy (<s>svātantrya</s>), even in the manifestation of parts, partlessness is never lost. Let it be so here too—what contradiction is there? In exactly this way the derivation of letters [is to be understood]. Otherwise, in dental, labial, guttural, palatal, and other letters, how could the breath (<s>pavana</s>), which spreads sequentially as the striker, having struck the throat, [then] strike the palate? Even if [one posits] simultaneous filling, there would be simultaneity [of all sounds], in which case the form arising from striking the throat would be possible everywhere from the palatal strike too. And [the properties of] aspiration, nasality, and the like are said to be secondary accompaniments (<s>anupradāna</s>) because they are perceived afterwards. And in two-<s>mātrā</s> and three-<s>mātrā</s> [vowels], the conjunction of two, etc., is one in which one or two [units] are contained within.

body.text: tathaiva mātrake 'py ardhamātrādiyogaḥ saṃvedyaḥ, yathoktaṃ bhaṭṭanārāyaṇena
body.translated_text: Likewise, even in a [single] <s>mātrā</s> (mora), the conjunction of half-<s>mātrā</s> and the like is to be experienced. As stated by <s>Bhaṭṭa Nārāyaṇa</s>:

body.text: Q: praṇavordhvārdhamātrāto 'py aṇave mahate namaḥ /
body.translated_text: Salutation to the minute and the great [Lord], from the upper half-<s>mātrā</s> of <s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ)!

body.text:
iti / iha tu pañcāśadvarṇā viśvam api vā akramam ekam eva / kva cit tu matādiśāstreṣu visargaviśleṣasyaivānuttarapadasattālambanenāṣṭādaśī kalā ity abhyupagamaḥ / tad evam etāḥ kalā eva hlādanāmātracittavṛttyanubhāvakāḥ ``svarā'' ity uktāḥ / svarayanti śabdayanti sūcayanti cittaṃ svaṃ ca svarūpātmānaṃ rānty evam iti parapramātari saṃkrāmayantaḥ dadati svaṃ cātmīyaṃ kādiyonirūpaṃ rānti bahiḥ prakāśayanto dadatīti svarāḥ / eta eva hi cittavṛttisūcakā nādātmakāḥ karuṇāśṛṅgāraśāntādikāṃ cittavṛttim ākrandanacāṭukastutyādau kevalā vā yonivarṇaniviṣṭā vā tiryaktattadaharjātādiṣv api prathamata evāpatantaḥ saṃketavighnādinairapekṣyeṇaiva saṃvidāsannavartitvāt svarakākvādirūpatām aśnuvānāḥ prakāśayantīty
arthadharmā udāttādaya upadiṣṭāḥ, teṣām eva cittavṛttyanubhāvakaṣaḍjādisvarūpatvāt /
body.translated_text: Thus. Here, however, the fifty letters—or indeed the universe—are one single [reality] without sequence. But in some doctrinal scriptures, by the separation of <s>visarga</s> resting on the <s>anuttara</s>-state existence, an eighteenth <s>kalā</s> is accepted. Thus, these <s>kalās</s> alone, which cause the experience of the mental states called <s>hlāda</s> (joy) and the like, are called '<s>svaras</s>' (vowels/tones). They sound forth (<s>svarayanti</s>), indicate (<s>sūcayanti</s>) the mind, and they convey (<s>rānti</s>) their own self-nature to the supreme knower, and they give forth (<s>dadati</s>) their own [product]—the womb-form of <s>ka</s> and the rest—[and] <s>rānti</s>, [meaning] they externally illuminate and give—hence [they are called] <s>svarāḥ</s>. For these very [vowels], being of the nature of <s>nāda</s> (resonance) and indicative of mental states, manifesting the mental states of compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), erotic love (<s>śṛṅgāra</s>), peace (<s>śānta</s>), and the like—in weeping, flattery, praise, and so on—either alone or stationed in womb-letters (consonants), even in animals, children just born, and the like, falling [upon awareness] first of all, regardless of impediments to convention, due to their proximity to awareness—assuming the form of intonation (<s>svara</s>), voice-modulation (<s>kāku</s>), and the like—they illuminate [those states]. Therefore, the <s>udātta</s> (raised) and other [accents] are taught as properties of meaning, since they are of the nature of <s>ṣaḍja</s> and other [musical notes] that cause the experience of mental states.

body.text: evaṃ sarvatra saṃvedane sarvā evaitā vaicitryacaryācāracaturāḥ śaktaya ādikṣāntāḥ samāpatantyo 'hamahamikayā akramam eva bhāsamānāḥ kalanāmayatayaiva jñānakramasaṃkramaṇam eva diśyamānaṃ deśam utthāpayantyaḥ,
body.translated_text: Thus, in every cognition, all these powers—from <s>a</s> to <s>kṣa</s>—skilled in the conduct of variegated play, falling simultaneously, shining without sequence through their mutual vying, raising up the manifesting space through the very fact of being acts of division (<s>kalanā</s>), which constitutes the passage through the sequence of cognition;

body.text: Q: anyathā meruparamāṇvor aviśeṣāt
body.translated_text: by the principle that 'otherwise there would be no distinction between <s>Meru</s> and an atom,'

body.text: iti nyāyena garbhīkṛtadeśātmakavaicitryaṃ kriyāvaicitryātmakaṃ kramarūpaṃ kālaṃ bahiryojanayollāsayantyaḥ svātmani yuñjānatvena grasamānāḥ prollāsasamaye 'pi riktarūpatayā udyogāvabhāsasaṃkrāmavilāpanarūpeṇa dvādaśātmikāṃ kṛśarūpatām āśrayantyas tadgṛhītapramadādigatodyogādikalācatuṣṭayaparipūrṇatayāpy aṅkurībhūya sālasaṃ ṣoḍaśātmakabharitapūrṇarūpatayā praviśantyo 'ntar bahiś ca tad amṛtānandaviśrāntirūpaṃ camatkārasattāsārakalācatuṣkaṃ visṛjantya evaṃvidhām eva pūrṇakṛśātmakadolālīlāṃ nirviśamānāḥ somasūryakalājālagrasanavamanacaturāḥ /
body.translated_text: externally projecting and displaying the sequential form that is time—whose nature is the variety of action characterized by the variety of space contained within [each cognition]—while devouring [time] by yoking it into themselves; even at the time of effulgent manifestation, assuming a thin form of twelve [phases] in the aspect of emptiness, through the forms of effort, appearance, transition, and dissolution; then, by the fullness of the fourfold <s>kalā</s> consisting of effort, and the like—which pertain to the seized [object], the woman (<s>pramadā</s>), and other states—sprouting forth, entering inward and outward with languid fullness in the complete sixteen-fold form; emitting that fourfold <s>kalā</s> whose essence is the wonder-existence of repose in that nectar-bliss—thus engaging in this very play of oscillation (<s>dolā-līlā</s>) between fullness and thinness—[these powers are] skilled in the swallowing and emitting of the net of the <s>Soma</s> (moon) and <s>Sūrya</s> (sun) <s>kalās</s>.

body.text: akāram evāditayā madhye ca kādiyonijātam avasāne ca binduṃ dadhatī ``aham'' ity eṣaiva bhagavatī sṛṣṭiḥ /
body.translated_text: Placing <s>a</s>-<s>kāra</s> alone as the beginning, the womb-born [consonants] from <s>ka</s> onwards in the middle, and <s>bindu</s> at the end—this is 'I' (<s>aham</s>)—this very [syllable] is the blessed creation (<s>sṛṣṭi</s>).

body.text: tad uktaṃ śrīsomānandapādair nijavivṛtau ``aṃ a ity eṣaiva vikṛtāvikṛtarūpā mātṛkā'' ityādi / te tu ``a'' ity etad anuttaram ākārādyāś ca tithayaḥ, yad vā bindur aṃkāraḥ akārādyās tithayas tadanto visarga ity api vyācakṣate / tad eva saṃvitsatattvaṃ ``spanda'' ity upadiśanti / spandanaṃ ca kiṃciccalanam / svarūpāc ca yadi vastvantarākramaṇaṃ tac calanam eva na kiṃcittvam, no cet calanam eva na kiṃcit / tasmāt svarūpa eva kramādiparihāreṇa camatkārātmikā ucchalattā ūrmir iti matsyodarītiprabhṛtiśabdair āgameṣu nidarśitaḥ spanda ity ucyate, kiṃciccalanātmakatvāt / sa ca śivaśaktirūpaḥ sāmānyaviśeṣātmā / tad vyākhyātam, ādyās tithayaḥ bindvavasānagāḥ kālayogena somasūryau tasyaivākulasyāntaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus it is stated by the revered <s>Somānanda</s> in his own commentary: '<s>aṃ a</s>—this very [combination] is the <s>Mātṛkā</s> in both modified and unmodified form,' and so on. And they [explain]: '<s>a</s>'—this is the <s>anuttara</s> (Ultimate); and the <s>ā</s>-<s>kāra</s> and other [vowels] are the <s>tithis</s> (lunar phases). Or, the <s>bindu</s> is <s>aṃ</s>-<s>kāra</s>, the <s>a</s>-<s>kāra</s> and other [vowels] are the <s>tithis</s>, and the <s>visarga</s> ending in them [constitutes the whole]—so they also explain. That very reality of awareness (<s>saṃvit-satattva</s>) they teach as '<s>spanda</s>' (vibration). And <s>spandana</s> is a slight movement (<s>kiṃcit calana</s>). If from one's own nature there is a movement toward another entity, that is movement proper, not 'slightness'; and if there is no [movement toward another], then there is no movement at all. Therefore, in one's own nature alone, without the involvement of sequence and the like, the surging forth—the wave (<s>ūrmi</s>)—whose nature is wonder (<s>camatkāra</s>), is what is indicated in the scriptures by the terms <s>matsyodarī</s> and the like, and is called <s>spanda</s>, because it is of the nature of a slight movement. And that is of the form of <s>Śiva</s>-<s>Śakti</s>, the nature of universal and particular. This has been explained: the first <s>tithis</s>, culminating in <s>bindu</s>, [and] through conjunction with time, <s>Soma</s> (moon) and <s>Sūrya</s> (sun) [reside] within that very <s>akula</s> (transcendent).

body.text: pṛthivyādīni ca yāvad brahmapañcakaṃ tāvat teṣāṃ svarāṇām antaḥ / kathaṃ / kramāt / atha ca kramasyādanaṃ bhakṣaṇaṃ kālagrāsaḥ tathā kṛtveti kriyāviśeṣaṇaṃ ca / sobhane vrate bhoge riktatve bhoganivṛttau ca pūrṇatve suvrate / āmantraṇam apy etat evaṃ vyākhyeyam /
body.translated_text: And from earth onwards up to the fivefold <s>Brahman</s> (<s>brahmapañcaka</s>)—all that is within those <s>svaras</s> (vowels). How? Sequentially (<s>kramāt</s>). And yet, the devouring (<s>adana</s>) of sequence is its consumption (<s>bhakṣaṇa</s>), [which is] the swallowing of time (<s>kālagrāsa</s>); 'having done thus' is an adverbial qualifier of the action. In the beautiful observance (<s>sobhane vrate</s>), in enjoyment (<s>bhoge</s>), in emptiness (<s>riktatve</s>), in the cessation of enjoyment, and in fullness (<s>pūrṇatve</s>)—in the auspicious vow (<s>suvrate</s>). The vocative address too is to be explained in this manner.

body.text:
evam amūlā akāramūlā avidyamānamūlā cānāditvāt / sa kramo yasyāḥ praśleṣeṇātadrūpaḥ / anyathārūpo 'pi kramo yasyāḥ tathāpy amūlā / amūlasya yad ātananam ātat tatas tad eva ca kramo yasyāḥ / eṣa cājñeyā jñātṛrūpā, eṣaiva ca jñeyā, anyasyābhāvāt / avidyamānaṃ kṣāntaṃ tuṣṇīm āsanam avirataṃ sṛṣṭyādirūpatvena asyām / ākṣāṇām aindriyakāṇām ante samīpe prāg aparyavasānā yā bhaved iti / upacārād ākṣāntā sṛṣṭir apūrvam āharaṇaṃ svātmānupraveśātmasvarūpaṃ saṃhārarūpaṃ yasyām / eṣaiva ca śivātmakabījaprasararūpāṇāṃ mananatrāṇadharmānāṃ sarveṣām eva vācyavācakādirūpavarṇabhaṭṭārakātmanāṃ mantrāṇāṃ śaktyātmakayonispandānām, sarvāsāṃ tadbījodbhūtānāṃ
vedanārūpāṇāṃ vidyānām iyaṃ samā sarvatrānūnādhikā sarveṣu tantreṣu tantraṇāsu ca sarvāsu kriyāsu sarvakālaṃ ca sarvaṃ dadatī siddhisaṅgham / akhyātā aprakaṭā / akhyātirūpatāṃ māyīyām uddiśya bhedo varṇānāṃ / tathā hi ta eva śuddhamantrarūpā varṇāḥ prathamaṃ pañcavidhaviparyayāśaktyādirūpapratyayātmakabhāvasṛṣṭitām etya svarūpam āvṛṇvate /
body.translated_text: Thus [the <s>Mālinī</s>] is rootless (<s>amūlā</s>) — having <s>a-kāra</s> as its root, having a non-existent root, because it is beginningless (<s>anādi</s>). The sequence (<s>krama</s>) of which, through coalescence (<s>praśleṣa</s>), is of a different nature — even though the sequence is of another form, it is still rootless. The spreading out (<s>ātatam</s>) of that which is rootless — that itself is the sequence of which [the <s>Mālinī</s> consists]. And this [<s>Mālinī</s>] is unknowable, being of the nature of the knower; and this itself is also the knowable, since there is nothing else. In it, the quiescent (<s>kṣānta</s>), the silent resting, is non-existent [as separate], since it unceasingly takes the form of creation and so forth. That which would be beyond the end of the sense-letters (<s>ākṣa</s>), i.e., near the sensory [phonemes], before [them], without limit — thus, figuratively speaking, the <s>ākṣāntā</s> creation is a novel bringing forth, whose own nature is the absorption into one's own Self, having the form of dissolution (<s>saṃhāra</s>). And this itself is the [source] of all <s>mantras</s> — which are of the nature of the <s>varṇa</s>-lords in the form of the signified and signifier, possessing the qualities of meditation (<s>manana</s>) and protection (<s>trāṇa</s>), being the expansion of seeds (<s>bīja</s>) whose essence is <s>Śiva</s> — and of all <s>vidyās</s> (cognitions), which are born from those seeds and are of the nature of awareness, which are the pulsations (<s>spanda</s>) of the womb (<s>yoni</s>) whose essence is <s>Śakti</s>. This [<s>Mālinī</s>] is equal (<s>samā</s>) everywhere, neither deficient nor excessive, in all <s>tantras</s>, in all systematic arrangements, in all rituals, and at all times, granting the entire collection of <s>siddhis</s> (attainments). [She is] unmanifest (<s>akhyātā</s>), not openly revealed. With a view to the <s>māyīya</s> (illusory) state of non-manifestation, there is differentiation of the <s>varṇas</s> (phonemes). For those very <s>varṇas</s>, which are of the nature of pure <s>mantras</s>, first enter into the state of creation of conceptual constructs (<s>pratyaya</s>) in the form of the five <s>viparyayas</s> (misconceptions), incapacity (<s>aśakti</s>), and so forth, and thereby veil their own true nature.

body.text:
Q: pañca viparyayabhedā bhavanty aśaktiś ca karaṇavaikalyāt /
Q: aṣṭāviṃśatibhedā tuṣṭir navadhāṣṭadhā siddhiḥ //
body.translated_text:
Q: The five varieties of <s>viparyaya</s> (misconception) arise, and <s>aśakti</s> (incapacity) due to deficiency of the instruments;
Q: twenty-eight varieties [of <s>aśakti</s>], <s>tuṣṭi</s> (contentment) is ninefold, and <s>siddhi</s> (attainment) is eightfold. //

body.text: iti hy eta eva pratyayāḥ pāśavasṛṣṭirūpāḥ pāśā mukhyatayā, yathoktam
body.translated_text: Thus indeed these very <s>pratyayas</s> (conceptual constructs), having the form of creation belonging to the bound soul (<s>paśu</s>), are principally the bonds (<s>pāśas</s>), as stated:

body.text:
Q: svarūpāvaraṇe cāsya śaktayaḥ satatotthitāḥ /
Q: yataḥ śabdānuvedhena na vinā pratyayodbhavaḥ //
body.translated_text:
Q: And for concealing his own nature, the powers (<s>śaktis</s>) are constantly arising,
Q: since without the interpenetration of word (<s>śabda</s>), there is no arising of conceptual constructs (<s>pratyaya</s>). //

body.text: iti / tathā
body.translated_text: Thus. And likewise:

body.text: Q: parāmṛtarasāpāyas tasya yaḥ pratyayodbhavaḥ /
body.translated_text: Q: The loss of the nectar-essence of the Supreme (<s>parāmṛtarasa</s>) — that which is the arising of conceptual constructs (<s>pratyaya</s>) for him —

body.text: ityādi / evaṃ pratyayasṛṣṭitvāntarālīkaraṇena sphuṭaśrūyamāṇaśrutyātmakakramābhāsamānamāyīyavarṇasṛṣṭir ādyapāramārthikaśuddharūpāliṅgitā tattatkāryaphalaprasavadāyinī nirūpitā śrīpūrvaśāstre /
body.translated_text: and so forth. Thus, by rendering intermediate the creation of conceptual constructs (<s>pratyaya</s>), the <s>māyīya</s> (illusory) creation of <s>varṇas</s> (phonemes) — which appears as a clearly audible sequence of sounds — embraced by the primordial pure form of ultimate reality, bestowing the fruits and results of their respective effects, has been set forth in the glorious <s>Pūrvaśāstra</s> (Mālinīvijayottara).

body.text: Q: sarvaśāstrārthagarbhiṇyai .../
body.translated_text: Q: To her who is pregnant with the meaning of all <s>śāstras</s> (scriptures)... /

body.text: ity evaṃvidhayā
body.translated_text: Thus, by means of such [a <s>Mālinī</s>]:

body.text:
Q: anayā saṃprabuddhaḥ san yoniṃ vikṣobhya śaktitaḥ /
Q: tatsamānaśrutīn vamāṃs tatsaṃkhyān asṛjat prabhuḥ //
body.translated_text:
Q: Being fully awakened by means of this [<s>Mālinī</s>], having agitated the womb (<s>yoni</s>) through <s>Śakti</s>,
Q: emitting [phonemes] of equal sound to those, equal in number, the Lord (<s>Prabhu</s>) created [them]. //

body.text: ityādi,
body.translated_text: and so forth,

body.text: Q: te tair āliṅgitāḥ santaḥ sarvakāmaphalapradāḥ /
body.translated_text: Q: Those [<s>bījas</s>], being embraced by those [<s>yonis</s>], become bestowers of the fruits of all desires. /

body.text: ityādi / evam ākhyātā aprakaṭāpi māyāndhānāṃ sarvadaiva khyātā / prakāśā śuddhavedanātmikā / yaśaḥ sarvatra svasvabhāvātmakaprabhāvaprakhyāprasarānirodho yasyā ity āmantraṇaṃ śobhanavrate itivat / tad ayam atra saṃkṣepārthaḥ /
body.translated_text: and so forth. Thus proclaimed — even though unmanifest, she is always manifest to those blinded by <s>Māyā</s>. She is luminous (<s>prakāśā</s>), whose essence is pure awareness (<s>śuddhavedanā</s>). Glory (<s>yaśas</s>) — everywhere there is no obstruction to the radiant expansion whose nature is her own essential power — this is the vocative address ["O you of beautiful vow" (<s>śobhanavrate</s>)], like [an exclamation of praise]. This, then, is the summary of the meaning here:

children.translated_text: Whose sole characteristic is the wonder (<s>camatkāra</s>) of immersion in the singular essence of absolute freedom (<s>svātantrya</s>),

children.text: parā bhagavatī nityaṃ bhāsate bhairavī svayam //
children.translated_text: the supreme (<s>parā</s>) Goddess (<s>Bhagavatī</s>), <s>Bhairavī</s>, eternally shines forth of her own accord. //
That uninterrupted, ever-arisen [light] which is the inseparability from her own radiance —
through [entities] ranging from <s>Sadāśiva</s> down to earth, horizontal [creatures], blue, yellow, pleasure, and so forth, //
manifesting through their own natures, possessing the capacity for self-expansion,
the form of consciousness (<s>saṃvid</s>) expands, whose essence is self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>). //
Self-awareness (<s>svasvasaṃvedana</s>) by name is described as the means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>);
it shines equally in children, animals, and the omniscient alike. //
The senses, the threefold <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body), the sequence of the supreme Word (<s>paravāc</s>),
conformity (<s>sārūpya</s>), erroneous connection (<s>anyathāyoga</s>), dependent origination (<s>pratītyānudaya</s>), restraint (<s>yama</s>) — //
all of this, of which [self-awareness is the basis], is established merely as a doorway;
that is declared to be self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>), consisting of uninterrupted expansion. //
Even for those who have no acquaintance with even the mere names such as senses, threefold [body], and so on,

children.text: teṣām api tiraścāṃ hi samā saṃvit prakāśate //
children.translated_text: even for animals, consciousness (<s>saṃvit</s>) shines forth equally. //
Thus, luminosity (<s>bhāsā</s>) by its very nature is reflective awareness of one's own essence (<s>svarūpāmarśana</s>);

children.text: svarūpāmarśanaṃ yac ca tad eva paravāgvapuḥ //
children.translated_text: and that reflective awareness of one's own essence is itself the body of the supreme Speech (<s>Parāvāk</s>). //
Due to the variegated nature of that, [the supreme Speech] consists of variegated expansion;

children.text: prathane pāratantryaṃ hi na jātu bhajate kva cit //
children.translated_text: in [its] expansion, it never, anywhere, partakes of dependence (<s>pāratantrya</s>). //
Since there is no dependence, how can convention (<s>saṃketa</s>), obstruction (<s>pratyūha</s>), and the like have any standing?
Therefore, the reflective awareness of one's own nature (<s>svasvarūpavimarśana</s>) is free from convention, //
transcending place, time, <s>kalā</s> (limited agency), <s>Māyā</s>, location, destruction, and action,
perfectly complete of its own accord, [encompassing] everything, distinct from all [limited] forms, //
characterized solely by the true impressions (<s>satsaṃskāra</s>) of the innate great consciousness (<s>mahāsaṃvit</s>),
this form, whose essence is <s>Śuddhavidyā</s> (Pure Knowledge), being of a dual nature as 'I' (<s>aham</s>). //

children.text: tad eva mātṛkārūpaṃ dharādīnāṃ nijaṃ vapuḥ /
children.translated_text: That itself is the form of <s>Mātṛkā</s>, the intrinsic body of earth (<s>dharā</s>) and the rest;
that is the ultimate <s>a-kāra</s>, due to its nature of fluidity and viscosity, //
it is said to be of the nature of seed (<s>bīja</s>) and womb (<s>yoni</s>), having the form of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s>;
from the union (<s>saṃghaṭṭa</s>) of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s>, due to their mutual overflowing, //
the mutual absorption (<s>parasparasamāpatti</s>) that bestows bliss upon the world,
whose true being is the ultimate reality [extending] from the innermost to the furthest extent of the universe — //

children.text: yad vīryam iti nirṇītaṃ tad visleṣaṇayojanāt /
children.translated_text: that which is ascertained as <s>vīrya</s> (potency), through separation and conjunction,

children.text: visarga iti tat proktaṃ dhruvadhāma tad ucyate //
children.translated_text: is called <s>visarga</s> (emission); that is said to be the eternal abode (<s>dhruvadhāma</s>). //
For the attainment of the state of <s>Anuttara</s> (the Unsurpassable), this is the easily accomplished method.

children.text: asmād eva tv amāyīyād varṇapuñjān nirūpitā //
children.translated_text: From this very non-<s>māyīya</s> [source], the collections of <s>varṇas</s> (phonemes) have been set forth; //

children.text: māyām ālambya bhinnaiva śrīpūrve sṛṣṭir ākṣarī /
children.translated_text: resorting to <s>Māyā</s>, the phonemic creation (<s>ākṣarī sṛṣṭi</s>) in the glorious <s>Pūrvaśāstra</s> is indeed differentiated,
having the nature of producing conceptual constructs (<s>pratyaya</s>) differentiated into fifty divisions, //
by its very nature having the form of bondage (<s>bandha</s>), consisting of the concealment of one's own nature;
within this very [differentiated creation] are contained those <s>Khecarīs</s> (sky-moving powers) whose nature is objects of experience. //
They weave the variegated <s>saṃsṛti</s> (worldly existence), consisting of <s>karma</s>, <s>Māyā</s>, and <s>āṇava</s> [<s>mala</s>];
in the equality of this [differentiated creation], by its very nature, consisting of pure <s>Bhairava</s>-hood, //

children.text: proktaṃ prāg eva jīvatve muktatvaṃ pārāmārthikam /
children.translated_text: has been declared previously the liberation (<s>muktatva</s>) that is ultimate reality even while living (<s>jīvatva</s>);

children.text: bhinnāyā varṇasṛṣṭeś ca tad abhinnaṃ vapuḥ param //
children.translated_text: and of the differentiated <s>varṇa</s>-creation, that undifferentiated supreme form, //

children.text: vīryam ity uktam atraiva yad guptyā mantraguptatā /
children.translated_text: is called <s>vīrya</s> (potency) right here, by whose secrecy the secrecy of <s>mantras</s> is maintained;

children.text: tad etad aham ity eva visargānuttarātmakam //
children.translated_text: that is precisely 'I' (<s>aham</s>), of the nature of <s>visarga</s> (emission) and <s>anuttara</s> (the Unsurpassable). //

children.text: svasvabhāvaṃ paraṃ jānañ jīvanmuktaḥ sakṛd budhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Knowing this as one's own supreme nature, the wise one is <s>jīvanmukta</s> (liberated while living) at once;
those desirous of <s>siddhis</s> (attainments) and the like, by that [<s>aham</s>] threaded through deliberately contracted [forms], //
<s>yogins</s> worship the 'I' (<s>aham</s>) in the navel, the <s>kuṇḍalinī</s>, the heart, and the space [above];

children.text: tad etat kila nirṇītaṃ yathāgurvāgamaṃ manāk //
children.translated_text: this has been ascertained here, according to the teacher's tradition, in brief. //

children.text: enāṃ saṃvidam ālambya yat syāt tat pṛcchyatāṃ svavit /
children.translated_text: Resting upon this consciousness (<s>saṃvid</s>), whatever may arise, let one's own knower be questioned;
not by this much alone has it been weighed — only a portion of the path has been shown. //

children.text: iyatīti vyavacchindyād bhairavīṃ saṃvidaṃ hi kaḥ /
children.translated_text: Who could delimit the consciousness of <s>Bhairavī</s> as 'this much'?
This much is the descent of power (<s>śaktipāta</s>) that has manifested in us. //
By us who are qualified, this has been made manifest;
for us or for others, now or at another time, //

children.text: bhavaty abhūtvā bhavitā tarkaḥ sūkṣmatamo 'py ataḥ /
children.translated_text: there arises, having not existed before, and will arise, even the subtlest reasoning (<s>tarka</s>),
which is radiant like the sun in the illuminations of all the components of <s>yoga</s>. //

children.text: śrīpūrvaśāstre nirṇīto yena muktaś ca mocakaḥ /
children.translated_text: That which has been ascertained in the glorious <s>Pūrvaśāstra</s>, by which one is both liberated and a liberator —

children.text: etat tu sarvathā grāhyaṃ vimṛśyaṃ ca parepsubhiḥ //
children.translated_text: this must be grasped and contemplated in every way by those who seek the Supreme. //
Setting aside for a moment the envy that is so easy for mortals, by the discerning,

children.text: ālocanakṣaṇād ūrdhvaṃ yad bhaved ātmani sthitiḥ /
children.translated_text: from the very moment of contemplation onward, whatever abidance in the Self there may be, //
by that, the clouds and [obscuring] creepers of the sun of consciousness (<s>cidarka</s>) subside of their own accord. //

body.text: evam uttarasyāpy anuttaram iti yad uktaṃ yo 'sāv ``uttarasya'' ity aṃśenopāttaḥ kulātmā śāktaḥ sṛṣṭiprasaraḥ sa vistarato nirṇītaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus, regarding what was said that even the <s>uttara</s> (subsequent) has an <s>anuttara</s> (unsurpassable) — that which was taken up by the portion [of the verse reading] 'of the <s>uttara</s>' — the <s>Śākta</s> (power-related) expansion of creation whose essence is <s>kula</s> (totality) has been ascertained in detail.

body.text: tac cottaram api yathānuttaraṃ tathā nirūpitam / idānīṃ tv anuttaram eva svarūpeṇa vistarato vicārapadavīm apekṣate /evaṃ vidhyanuvādau nirvahataḥ, yady anūdyamāno vidhīyamānaś cāṃśaḥ svarūpato lakṣitau syātām, yathā yad eva śivanāmasmaraṇam etad eva samastasaukhyocchalanam iti dvāv apy aṃśau lakṣyau / iha tu yady apy anuttaraṃ nāma anyad vastu kiṃcin nāsti, anyatve tasyāpy uttaratve evābhipātāt, tathāpi svātantryakḷptopadeśyopadeśakabhāvābhiprāyeṇeyaṃ vyavasthā ity uktaṃ prāk / tataś ca vistarato 'nuttarasvarūpanirūpaṇāya granthāntarāvatāraḥ / tan nirūpayati /
body.translated_text: And that <s>uttara</s> (subsequent) too has been established as being <s>anuttara</s> (unsurpassable). Now, however, <s>anuttara</s> itself, in its own essential nature, requires detailed examination along the path of inquiry. Thus the injunction and the restatement are carried out: if the portion being restated and the portion being enjoined were identified in their own nature — as for instance, that which is the remembrance of the name of <s>Śiva</s> is itself the overflowing of all happiness — then both portions are identified. But here, although there is indeed nothing whatsoever other than <s>anuttara</s> — since anything that were other would itself fall into the category of <s>uttara</s> (surpassable) — nevertheless, with the intention of the relationship of teacher and taught established through absolute freedom (<s>svātantrya</s>), this arrangement [is made], as was stated before. Therefore, for the detailed examination of the nature of <s>anuttara</s>, [there is] the commencement of another section of the text. He sets that forth:

body.text: ParTri 9cd-18ab:

children.translated_text: Endowed with fourteen, O blessed one (<s>bhadre</s>),
conjoined with the lord of <s>tithis</s> (lunar days) and the end [phoneme],
the third <s>Brahman</s>, O fair-hipped one (<s>suśroṇi</s>),
[is] the heart (<s>hṛdaya</s>) of <s>Bhairava</s>.
This, one not born of a <s>yoginī</s>,
nor a [mere] <s>Rudra</s>, obtains clearly.
The heart (<s>hṛdaya</s>) of the God of gods (<s>Devadeva</s>),
instantly bestowing <s>yoga</s> and liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) —
when its utterance (<s>uccāra</s>) is properly performed,
the great host of <s>mantras</s> and <s>mudrās</s>
immediately becomes subject to him,
[this being] characterized by possession (<s>āveśa</s>) of one's own body.
He who remembers [it] for a <s>muhūrta</s> (forty-eight minutes),
sealed with the <s>cumbaka</s> [<s>mudrā</s>],
that person then binds to his body
the host of <s>mantras</s> and <s>mudrās</s>.
Past and future matters —
when asked, he speaks of them too.
Within one <s>prahara</s> (three hours), whatever is desired,
uttering [it] in the form of the deity (<s>devatā</s>),
he directly sees, without doubt,
[that deity] drawn forth by the powers of <s>Rudra</s>.
In merely two <s>praharas</s>,
the one who remembers becomes established in the sky (<s>vyomasthaḥ</s>).
In three [<s>praharas</s>], all the Mothers (<s>Mātaraḥ</s>),
the <s>Yogeśvarīs</s> of great power,
<s>Vīras</s>, <s>Vīreśvaras</s>, <s>Siddhas</s>,
and the powerful host of <s>Śākinīs</s>,
having come and given the pledge (<s>samaya</s>),
impelled by <s>Bhairava</s>,
they bestow the supreme <s>siddhi</s> (attainment),
or whatever fruit is desired.
By this, the <s>Siddhas</s> were perfected and will be perfected,
and practitioners of <s>mantras</s> (<s>mantriṇaḥ</s>) accomplish [their aims].
Whatever is in the <s>Bhairava Tantra</s>,
everything is accomplished by means of this.

body.text:
bhairavarūpasya viśvasya pradarśitayuktyāgamanirūpitaparāparābhaṭṭārikāsvabhāvaḥ śāktaḥ / tasya hṛdayaṃ sāraṃ śivarūpaṃ parameśvaryā śrīmatparābhaṭṭārikayā samāliṅgitam / bhairavaśabdena viśvasya sarvasarvātmakatāvapuḥ śaktirūpam / tatsahitasyātmanaḥ pratyekasya bhedasya nararūpasya etāvac chivātmakaṃ hṛdayam / pareṇābhedena sarvātmakatāyā eva tena tayā ca vināsya bhedasyaivāyogad ity uktaṃ prāk / ``susroṇi'' ity āmantraṇam / śobhanaṃ māyātmakatāyām apy anapetaṃ śuddhacinmayaṃ yad etat śroṇyāṃ hṛdayaṃ yonirūpam uktaṃ tan no 'ntaḥkṛtasakalamantramaheśāditiryaksthāvarāntapramātṛjālasyāmātmano 'smākam iti samucitāpatitavyapadeśasya bhairavātma pūrṇatāmayam antargataviśvavīryasamucchalattātmakavisargaviśleṣānandaśaktyaikaghanaṃ
brahma bṛhad vyāpakaṃ bṛṃhakaṃ bṛṃhitaṃ ca, na tu vedāntapāṭhakāṅgīkṛtakevalaśūnyavādāvidūravarti brahmadarśane iva / etac ca tṛtīyaṃ narādyapekṣayā śivaparaikarūpam / ata evāmīṣu śāstreṣv atra ca mukhyatayā tad eva hṛdayaṃ pūjyatayopadiṣṭam / ananupraviṣṭatathāvīryavyāptisārahṛdayā api tāvanmātrabāhyācārapariśīlanenaiva kramavaśaśithilībhavacchithilitavidaladvidalitapāśavaniyamabandhanā etaddhṛdayavyāptiṃ svayam eva samadhiśerate / na hy etaddhṛdayānupraveśa eva ``etaddhṛdaye 'nupraviṣṭo 'smi, iyaṃ devī parā'' ity etacchābdavikalpakalpyaḥ, asya ca pratyuta hṛdayāntaramārgaṇād ity uktaṃ vistarataḥ, api tu
body.translated_text: The <s>Śākta</s> [aspect], whose nature is <s>Parāparā Bhaṭṭārikā</s> as established through the reasoning and scripture that have been demonstrated, belongs to the universe whose form is <s>Bhairava</s>. Its heart (<s>hṛdaya</s>), the essence, having the form of <s>Śiva</s>, is embraced by the Supreme Goddess, the glorious <s>Parā Bhaṭṭārikā</s>. By the word '<s>Bhairava</s>' is [meant] the <s>Śakti</s>-nature of the universe, the body of the omnitude of all things. Of the Self united with that [<s>Śakti</s>], of each individual differentiated entity in the form of the limited being (<s>nara</s>), this much is the heart whose essence is <s>Śiva</s>. Through the Supreme, through non-difference, since the omnitude itself — without it [<s>Śiva</s>] and without her [<s>Śakti</s>] — would render this very differentiation impossible, as was stated before. '<s>Suśroṇi</s>' (O fair-hipped one) is a vocative address. Beautiful — even in the state of <s>Māyā</s>, not departed from the pure essence of consciousness — that which has been called the heart in the womb-form (<s>yoni</s>) as the hip (<s>śroṇī</s>), that is not [merely] ours — [it belongs to] the Self that has internalized the entire network of cognizing subjects from the great lords of <s>mantras</s> down to immobile beings and animals — 'of us' is the designation that has appropriately fallen [upon us] — having the nature of <s>Bhairava</s>, consisting of fullness, one compact mass of <s>visarga</s>-<s>śakti</s> (the power of emission) whose nature is the overflowing of the potency (<s>vīrya</s>) of the universe contained within, the bliss of separation [and union]. <s>Brahman</s> — great, all-pervading, nourishing, and nourished — but not as in the vision of <s>Brahman</s> accepted by the reciters of <s>Vedānta</s>, which is not far from mere voidism (<s>śūnyavāda</s>). And this is the 'third' in relation to <s>nara</s> (individual) and the rest, being the supreme singular form of <s>Śiva</s>. For this very reason, in these scriptures and here, it is that very heart which is principally taught as worthy of worship. Even those who have not entered into the heart of the essence of such <s>vīrya</s>-pervasion, merely through the cultivation of external practice to that extent, with their bonds of fetters and restrictions becoming gradually loosened, split, and shattered through the progressive force [of practice], attain of their own accord the pervasion of this heart. For this very entry into the heart is not [to be conceived as] 'I have entered into this heart, this is the supreme Goddess (<s>Parā Devī</s>)' — as something to be constructed by such verbal conceptualization (<s>śābdavikalpa</s>); and indeed, because of seeking the interior path of the heart [rather than conceptualizing it], as has been stated in detail. Rather:

body.text:
Q: saṃkocayanti hṛdayaṃ nahi śāstrapāśā no saṃvidaṃ kaluṣayed yad ayaṃ ca lokaḥ /
Q: samyaksvabhāvapadavīparipūrṇarūpā saivollasallayabharā bharitā sthitiḥ syāt //
body.translated_text:
Q: The bonds of scripture do not contract the heart, nor does this world taint consciousness;
Q: that state which is full of the form of the path of one's own true nature, filled with the surging weight of flashing forth and dissolution — that alone would be [true] abidance. //

body.text: yad uktaṃ mayaiva stotre
body.translated_text: As I myself have said in the hymn (<s>stotra</s>):

body.text:
Q: bhagavadbhaktyāvesād viśadatarasaṃjātamanasām
Q: kṣaṇenaiṣāvasthā sphuṭam adhivasaty eva hṛdayam /
body.translated_text:
Q: For those whose minds have become most clear through immersion in devotion to the Lord (<s>Bhagavat</s>),
Q: this state clearly takes up residence in the heart in an instant. /

body.text: iti / ata eva koṇeṣu pūjyās tisraḥ / madhye devī parānandabhairavanirmathanarūpā nityānandarasaprasareṇaiva kṣobhātmakavisargeṇa iti devatānāṃ saṃpradāyaḥ / yāmalayoge vīrāṇām apy ānandendriyanityānandakṣobhātmakadūtīsaṃghaṭṭajeneti / ekavīratāyam api svarūpānandaviśrāntiyogena / puṃso 'pi ānandendriyaniḥsaraṇadhāma trikoṇaṃ kandādhoviniviṣṭaṃ cittaniveśād ānandakṣobhaprasavaṃ karoti tadindriyamūlatatparyantasaṃghaṭṭaghanatāyām / atroktam
body.translated_text: Thus. For this very reason, the three [goddesses] are to be worshipped in the corners [of the triangle]. In the center, the Goddess, whose form is the churning of <s>Parānanda</s> (supreme bliss) and <s>Bhairava</s>, through the emission (<s>visarga</s>) characterized by agitation (<s>kṣobha</s>) by means of the continuous flow of the essence of eternal bliss (<s>nityānandarasa</s>) — this is the tradition (<s>saṃpradāya</s>) regarding the deities. In the <s>yāmala</s> union (coupling), for the <s>vīras</s> (heroes) as well, through the agitation of bliss-sense-organ-eternal-bliss generated by the contact with the <s>Dūtī</s> (female messenger). In the practice of the single hero (<s>ekavīratā</s>) also, through the repose in the bliss of one's own nature through <s>yoga</s>. For the male practitioner also, the triangle — the abode of the emission of the bliss-sense-organ — established below the bulb (<s>kanda</s>), produces the generation of bliss-agitation through the settling of consciousness, in the compactness of the contact between the root and the extremity of that sense organ. Here it is stated:

body.text:
Q: vahner viṣasya madhye tu... /
iti / evam ānandayoga eva hṛdayapūjā, yathoktaṃ trikatantrasāre
body.translated_text:
Q: In the middle of fire and poison... /
Thus. In this way, the worship of the heart (<s>hṛdayapūjā</s>) is nothing but the union of bliss (<s>ānandayoga</s>), as stated in the <s>Trikatantrasāra</s>:

body.text:
Q: ānandaprasaraḥ pūjā tāṃ trikoṇe prakalpayet /
Q: puṣpadhūpādigandhais tu svahṛtsaṃtoṣakāriṇīm //
body.translated_text:
Q: The expansion of bliss (<s>ānandaprasara</s>) is worship; one should establish it in the triangle;
Q: with flowers, incense, fragrances, and the like, [making it] one that produces satisfaction in one's own heart. //

body.text: iti / sarvaṃ hi mudrādvayānuviddham, jñānakriyāśaktisāratvat / kevalaṃ devatāsu jñānamudrā antar udriktā, kriyāmudrā bahiḥ, vīreṣu viparyayaḥ / anupraveśas tu samatayā viparyayāc ca / anenaivābhiprāyeṇa jñānaśaktyātmake liṅge kriyāśaktisamarpaṇam uktam /
body.translated_text: Thus. For everything is pervaded by the two <s>mudrās</s>, since the essence is <s>jñānaśakti</s> (power of knowledge) and <s>kriyāśakti</s> (power of action). Only, in the case of the deities, the <s>jñānamudrā</s> (gesture of knowledge) predominates internally, and the <s>kriyāmudrā</s> (gesture of action) externally; in the case of the <s>vīras</s> (heroes), it is the reverse. Entry (<s>anupraveśa</s>), however, is through equality and also through reversal. It is with this very intention that the offering of <s>kriyāśakti</s> (power of action) into the <s>liṅga</s> whose essence is <s>jñānaśakti</s> (power of knowledge) has been stated.

body.text: evam etat caturdaṣasu yutaṃ saṃśliṣṭaṃ pañcadaśātmakaṃ tithīśāntena visargeṇa ṣoḍaśenānvitam / yad vā caturdaśasahitaṃ yutaṃ yugmaṃ ṣoḍaśa / tithīnāṃ pañcadaśānām īso visargaḥ tasyāntaḥ saptadaśy anuttarakalā, tadanvitaṃ hṛdayam / sarvāṇi ghaṭasukhādīni vastūni tām eva bījasattāṃ paramārtharūpeṇākrāmantīty uktaṃ vistarataḥ / atas tad eva hṛdayam /
body.translated_text: Thus this [heart], combined with the fourteen [vowels], conjoined, having fifteen as its nature, is endowed with the sixteenth <s>visarga</s> (emission) which is the lord of the <s>tithis</s> (lunar days). Alternatively, combined with fourteen, the pair that is joined is sixteen. The lord of the fifteen <s>tithis</s> is <s>visarga</s>; beyond its end is the seventeenth <s>kalā</s> (phase) of <s>anuttara</s> (the unsurpassable), and the <s>hṛdaya</s> (heart) is endowed with that. All entities such as pot, pleasure, and so forth penetrate that very seed-existence in the form of ultimate reality -- this has been stated in detail. Therefore, that alone is the <s>hṛdaya</s>.

body.text: evaṃ ṣoḍaśadhā hṛdayam etat /
body.translated_text: Thus, this <s>hṛdaya</s> (heart) is sixteenfold.

body.text: 1) tatrānuttarānusāreṇa yad etad brahma sāmarasyaṃ vedyavedakayoḥ, catasṛṇāṃ daśānām udyogādīnāṃ samāhāro 'vibhāgabhūḥ prāthamikī, tayā yutam avibhāgi / ya ete tithīnām īśā ūkārāntāḥ tatprabhavatvād anyasyeti hy uktam / tesāṃ tithīśānām antā amṛtavarṇāḥ catvāraḥ / taiḥ samyag anvitam / tac ca tṛtīyaṃ narādyapekṣayā śivarūpaṃ param / vedakaś catasṛbhir daśābhir ullasan vedyam eva tābhir āpyāyakautukātmanā tā evāmṛtakalāḥ svātmani ekīkurvan vedyavedakakṣobhasamāpattyā aikātmya lakṣaṇaṃ prasaṃkhyānenābhyāsena vā gamyaṃ bhairavātmano viśvahṛdayam anuttaraṃ praviśet / yathoktam
body.translated_text: 1) In accordance with <s>anuttara</s> (the unsurpassable) and <s>anusāra</s> (the nasal resonance), that which is the state of equipoise (<s>sāmarasya</s>) of <s>Brahman</s> between the known and the knower -- the aggregate of the four phases (<s>daśās</s>) beginning with <s>udyoga</s> (arising), whose ground is non-differentiation, is primary; combined with that, it is undivided. Those who are the lords of the <s>tithis</s>, ending in <s>ū</s>-sounds, since others originate from them -- so it has been said. The ends of those lords of <s>tithis</s> are the four <s>amṛtavarṇas</s> (immortal phonemes). It is properly endowed with those. And that third [aspect], in relation to the series beginning with <s>na</s>-[class consonants], is the supreme <s>Śiva</s>-nature. The knower, shining forth through the four phases, nourishing the known through them in the spirit of delightful augmentation -- those very <s>amṛtakalās</s> (immortal phases) -- unifying them within oneself, through the convergence of the agitation of known and knower, one should enter the <s>hṛdaya</s> (heart) of the universe, which is <s>anuttara</s> and whose nature is <s>Bhairava</s>, whose characteristic is oneness, to be attained through <s>prasaṃkhyāna</s> (contemplative enumeration) or <s>abhyāsa</s> (practice). As it has been stated:

body.text: Q: sarvabhūtastham ātmānaṃ sarvabhūtāni cātmani / iti /
body.translated_text: [One should see] oneself as abiding in all beings, and all beings in oneself.

body.text: 2) icchollasattātmany ānandaśaktau yad etat saṃhṛtyanusṛtyā kriyāśaktim apekṣya tṛtīyaṃ rūpam icchātma tad eva prākkoṭāv iṣyamāṇadyakaluṣaṃ brahma / catur ye daśa catvāriṃśad bhairavabhedāpekṣayā parabhairavaparaśaktitrayasahitāni tattvāni, yathoktam
body.translated_text: 2) In <s>ānandaśakti</s> (the power of bliss), which is the nature of the surge of <s>icchā</s> (will), that which is the third form -- having the nature of will, having withdrawn and traced back to <s>kriyāśakti</s> (the power of action) -- that very <s>Brahman</s> at the initial point [is] tinged with the desired object. The fourteen [times] four, that is, the forty <s>tattvas</s> (principles) together with the three [aspects of] supreme <s>Bhairava</s> and supreme <s>Śakti</s>, from the perspective of the divisions of <s>Bhairava</s> -- as it has been stated:

body.text:
Q: ṣaṭtriṃśac chodanīyani śodhako bhairavaḥ paraḥ /
Q: paraṃ trikaṃ tu karaṇaṃ dīkṣeyaṃ pāramārthikī //
body.translated_text: "Thirty-six are to be purified; the purifier is the supreme <s>Bhairava</s>; the supreme triad is the instrument; this <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) is the ultimate one."

body.text: ityādi / tair yutam / ānandaśaktir hi prāgapararūpā pūrṇā / katham / tithīśair bījaiḥ tadantaiś ca yonirūpadharādibhiḥ samanvitam iti kriyāviśeṣaṇam / tad eva hṛdayam / sarvatrātra sakṛdvibhātaṃ prasaṃkhyānagamyaṃ rūpaṃ mukhyataḥ tatrayogyānāṃ tu paraśaktipātapavitritānāṃ vṛthaindrajālikakalanālālasānāṃ vā yogābhyāsa iti mantavyam /
body.translated_text: And so forth. Combined with those. For <s>ānandaśakti</s> (the power of bliss) is full, being of the nature of both prior and subsequent. How? 'Endowed with the <s>bījas</s> (seed-syllables) that are lords of the <s>tithis</s>, and with their endings, and with the <s>yoni</s>-forms (womb-forms) beginning with <s>dharā</s> (earth)' -- this qualifies the action. That itself is the <s>hṛdaya</s> (heart). Everywhere here, the form that flashes forth at once, attainable through <s>prasaṃkhyāna</s> (contemplative enumeration), is primary; but for those suited to the threefold [practice], who are purified by the descent of supreme <s>śakti</s>, or for those delighting in the play of illusory magical fabrication, it should be understood as <s>yogābhyāsa</s> (yogic practice).

body.text: 3) icchābhiprāyeṇa tṛtīyam icchā / tac ca bṛṃhitam iṣyamāṇenābhinnena pūrṇaṃ brahma / caturdaśa catvāriṃśat / yutāni vibhāgabhāñji yato 'nantaram / yutaśabdo vibhaktavācy api yutasiddhatvād ityādau / tithīśvarasyākulamayānuttarakalātmano 'ntaḥ ānandaḥ tasyānu paścāt / samyagitaṃ bhodamayam /
body.translated_text: 3) The third is <s>icchā</s> (will) according to the intention of will. And that, augmented by the desired which is non-different, is full <s>Brahman</s>. Fourteen [times] forty. Combined, they possess division, since what follows [is sequential]. The word 'combined' (<s>yuta</s>) also denotes 'separated,' since it is established [in that sense] in usages like <s>yutasiddha</s> and so forth. Within the lord of <s>tithis</s>, whose nature is the <s>anuttarakalā</s> (unsurpassable phase) pervaded by <s>akula</s>, there is <s>ānanda</s> (bliss); after that, following it, [comes] that which is of the nature of awareness.

body.text: 4) īśānāpekṣayā tṛtīyam icchārūpaṃ prasaravaśād bṛhadbhūtam īśānatāpannam / caturdaśānāṃ catvāriṃśata uktāyā yutaṃ parasparavyāmiśratā yatra / tithīśvarasyākulamayānuttarakalātmano 'ntaḥ saṃhṛtiḥ kulaśaktiprathamaspandaḥ / tenānvitam /
body.translated_text: 4) The third, in relation to <s>Īśāna</s>, is of the nature of <s>icchā</s> (will), which has become expanded through the force of emanation, having attained <s>Īśāna</s>-hood. Of the fourteen [times] forty as stated, 'combined' means where there is mutual interpenetration. Within the lord of <s>tithis</s>, whose nature is the <s>anuttarakalā</s> pervaded by <s>akula</s>, there is withdrawal (<s>saṃhṛti</s>), the first vibration of <s>kulaśakti</s>. It is endowed with that.

body.text: 5) unmeṣātmakajñānaśaktiyogena tṛtīyaṃ brahmeśānam eva yadā caturdaśānāṃ tasyā eva tattvacatvāriṃśato yutaṃ prathamavibhāgo yatra tathāvidhaṃ bhavati / tathā tithīśāntena kulaśaktiprathamaspandena samyak prarurukṣutayā anvitam / saṃśabdo 'tra bharaṇāpekṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: 5) When through the union with <s>jñānaśakti</s> (the power of knowledge) whose nature is <s>unmeṣa</s> (opening forth), the third <s>Brahman</s>-<s>Īśāna</s> itself [arises], and the forty <s>tattvas</s> of that very fourteen are 'combined' -- meaning where the first division occurs, it becomes of that nature. Likewise, it is properly endowed with the end of the lord of <s>tithis</s>, the first vibration of <s>kulaśakti</s>, in the manner of being about to ascend. The prefix <s>sam</s>- here implies sustenance.

body.text: 6) tajjñānaśaktikriyāśaktimadhyakoṭirūpaprāṅnirṇīta-ūkārakalālambitoḍhatāruḍhyā yad etat brahma yat kiṃcic carācaraṃ tad aśuddhaśuddhāśuddhasṛṣṭyapekṣayā tṛtīyaṃ śuddhasṛṣṭyātmakam ata eva tithīśvarair hṛdayabhūtatayā tadantaiś ca kādikṣāntaiḥ samanvitam /
body.translated_text: 6) Through the ascent by means of clinging to the <s>ū-kalā</s> (the phase of <s>ū</s>), which is of the nature of the middle point between <s>jñānaśakti</s> (the power of knowledge) and <s>kriyāśakti</s> (the power of action), as previously determined -- that which is <s>Brahman</s>, whatever is moving and unmoving, that is the third in the sense of pure creation, in relation to the triad of impure, pure-impure, and pure creation. Therefore it is endowed with the lords of <s>tithis</s> as its heart-essence, and with their endings, the consonant classes from <s>ka</s> to <s>kṣa</s>.

body.text: 7) atha śūnyacatuṣkānusṛtyā caturṇāṃ dharādīnāṃ daśā vināśātmikā vidyate yatra tad vyoma / tena yutaṃ tṛtīyaṃ brahmecchākhyaṃ tithīśvarasyārkasya antena bāhyena tejasānvitam /
body.translated_text: 7) Now, in accordance with the fourfold void (<s>śūnyacatuṣka</s>), that in which there exists the phase of destruction of the four [elements] beginning with <s>dharā</s> (earth) -- that is <s>vyoman</s> (space). Combined with that, the third [aspect] called <s>Brahman</s>-<s>icchā</s> (Brahman-will) is endowed with the external radiance of the sun, which is the end of the lord of <s>tithis</s>.

body.text: 8) vyākhyātakrameṇa tṛtīyaṃ brahmeśanam / etad api evam eva /
body.translated_text: 8) By the method already explained, the third is <s>Brahman</s>-<s>Īśāna</s>. This too is exactly the same.

body.text: 9) tṛtīyaṃ brahmecchākhyam / caturṇāṃ nabhaḥprabhṛtīnām antadaśā yatra sā dharā / tayā yutaṃ samanvitaṃ tithīśāntasya vahnes tejaso yad anusaradrūpaṃ tena sahitaṃ vyomātma /
body.translated_text: 9) The third is called <s>Brahman</s>-<s>icchā</s> (Brahman-will). The final phase of the four [elements] beginning with <s>nabhas</s> (space) -- that is <s>dharā</s> (earth). Combined with that, it is endowed with the form that follows the radiance of fire, which is the end of the lord of <s>tithis</s> -- [thus it is] of the nature of space.

body.text: 10) tathaiva tṛtīyaṃ brahma caturdaśayutaṃ tithīśāntasamanvitaṃ paripūrṇaśūnyarūpaplutyā bhairavātma / icchā khalu nijasvabhāvabhūteśanasahitā vedyabhūmer vyomasattāṃ yadākrāmati tadā kiṃcitprakāśabhuvi viśramya jhaṭity aparyantāṃ kāṣṭhapāṣāṇaprāyāṃ niścalāṃ vyomabhūmim anupraviśati yatrāpavedyasuṣuptamahāvyomānupraviṣṭān yoginaḥ praty ucyate
body.translated_text: 10) Similarly, the third <s>Brahman</s>, combined with the fourteen, endowed with the end of the lord of <s>tithis</s>, through the flooding of the form of complete void, is of the nature of <s>Bhairava</s>. Indeed, when <s>icchā</s> (will), accompanied by <s>īśana</s> (lordship) which belongs to its own essential nature, penetrates the spatial existence of the ground of objectivity, then resting momentarily on the ground of slight luminosity, it suddenly enters the boundless, immovable ground of space, inert like wood and stone -- regarding which, to <s>yogins</s> who have entered the great space of the unknowable deep sleep, it is said:

body.text: Q: bherīkāṃsyaninādo 'pi vyutthānāya na kalpate / ityādi /
body.translated_text: "Even the sound of a drum or cymbal is unable to bring about awakening." And so forth.

body.text: 11) adhunoktavyāpti yad etat paraspararūpasāṃkaryavaicitryaṃ śaktīnāṃ taduddeśena / evam icchā yadānuttarapadapraveśaśālinī bhavati, yathā śaktikṣobhasya rasanāder anantaraṃ, tatrocyate vilambitamadhyadrutānāṃ cidviśeṣaspandānāṃ sattvādiyogajuṣāṃ catuḥśabdopalakṣitā caturthī daśā yatrāsti sāmānyaspandarūpā tad akulaṃ / tenākulenānuttareṇa yutaṃ tṛtīyaṃ brahmecchātma īśanasahitaṃ tithīśasyākārasyāntenānandaśaktyātmanā anvitam /
body.translated_text: 11) Now, that mutual intermingling and variety of forms among the <s>śaktis</s> (powers), with reference to which the aforementioned pervasion [was described] -- when <s>icchā</s> (will) thus becomes possessed of entry into the state of <s>anuttara</s> (the unsurpassable), as happens immediately after the agitation of <s>śakti</s> [expressed through] tasting and so forth -- there it is said: the fourth phase, characterized by the four sounds, in which there is the general vibration, among the specific vibrations of consciousness that are slow, medium, and rapid, associated with <s>sattva</s> and the other [<s>guṇas</s>] -- that is <s>akula</s> (the unconditioned). Combined with that <s>akula</s>, which is <s>anuttara</s>, the third <s>Brahman</s>, whose nature is <s>icchā</s> (will), accompanied by <s>īśana</s> (lordship), is endowed with the end of the <s>ā</s>-sound which is the lord of <s>tithis</s>, whose nature is <s>ānandaśakti</s> (the power of bliss).

body.text: 12) tad api tathaiva punar api parāṃ sattām anupraviśati yadā tadā bhairavātma paripūrṇaṃ dīrghībhūtaṃ / no 'smākam iti pūrvavat / ata evaitad eva bījayugmam evaṃvidhabījavaicitryānupraveśād ācchādaprasavasamartham iti kāmavāktattvopayogenocyate
body.translated_text: 12) That too, in the same manner, once again enters the supreme existence; when it does so, it becomes of the nature of <s>Bhairava</s>, full, elongated. 'Not ours' -- as before. Therefore, this very pair of <s>bījas</s> (seed-syllables), through the entry into such variety of <s>bījas</s>, is capable of producing coverings [and manifestations] -- thus, in connection with the principle of <s>kāmavāk</s> (the speech of desire), it is said:

body.text: Q: kāmena kāmayet kāmān kamaṃ kāmeṣu yojayet /
body.translated_text: "One should desire desires through desire, and one should join desire with desires."

body.text: ityādi
body.translated_text: And so forth.

body.text: Q: e-okāragataṃ bījaṃ vāgvidhānāya kevalam /
body.translated_text: "The <s>bīja</s> (seed-syllable) contained in the <s>e</s> and <s>o</s> sounds is solely for the purpose of the arrangement of speech."

body.text: ityādi /
body.translated_text: And so forth.

body.text: 13) pañcamaṣaṣṭha ... varṇadvayena ... /
body.translated_text: 13) By means of the pair of phonemes, the fifth and sixth [aspects] ...

body.text: 14) ... yad uktaṃ ``caturdaśayutaṃ tṛtīyaṃ brahma tithīśāntasamanvitaṃ'' tad eva bhairavātmānuttarapadānupraviṣṭam /
body.translated_text: 14) ... What was stated as 'the third <s>Brahman</s>, combined with fourteen, endowed with the end of the lord of <s>tithis</s>' -- that very [<s>Brahman</s>], having entered the state of <s>anuttara</s> (the unsurpassable), is of the nature of <s>Bhairava</s>.

body.text: 15) etad brahma catvāriṃśadyutam uktanītyā tithīśāntasamanvitaṃ bhairavātma vedanarūpatayā bindvātmakaṃ hṛdayam /
body.translated_text: 15) This <s>Brahman</s>, combined with forty in the manner stated, endowed with the end of the lord of <s>tithis</s>, of the nature of <s>Bhairava</s>, having the nature of <s>bindu</s> (the point) through its form as sensation -- [that is] the <s>hṛdaya</s> (heart).

body.text: 16) sakalam idaṃ tattvajālaṃ bhairavātmatayocchalad ata eva bahir visṛjyamānaṃ bṛṃhitaṃ brahma visargātmakam / bahiḥsthitaṃ ca bhairavātmatayaikībhūtaṃ bhedātmakavyavacchedadāridryāpasaraṇena sarvasarvātmakapadaprāptyā bṛṃhitam iti visargapadam / nirṇītaṃ caitad avadhānena /
body.translated_text: 16) This entire web of <s>tattvas</s> (principles), surging forth as the nature of <s>Bhairava</s>, and therefore being emitted outward -- that is augmented <s>Brahman</s>, whose nature is <s>visarga</s> (emission). And when established externally, it becomes unified as the nature of <s>Bhairava</s>, augmented through the departure of the poverty of differentiated limitation, through the attainment of the state where everything is the self of everything -- thus it is the state of <s>visarga</s>. And this has been determined with careful attention.

body.text: evaṃ ṣoḍaśātmikā bījavyāptir uktā / yonivyāptis tu prativarṇaṃ prāg evoktā / vargīkaraṇābhiprāyeṇa tu nirūpaṇīyā / bālyayauvanasthāviradehāntaragrahaṇarūpadaśācatuṣṭayasamāhāramayaṃ pāñcabhautikam antas tithīśāntena praveśanirgamanātmanā prāṇāpānarūpeṇa yutam / tṛtīyaṃ ca puryaṣṭakātma / brahma bṛhattvāc ca śūnyam / atra ca yad dhṛdayaṃ śaktyātma / ta ete sarva eva śarīraprāṇapuryaṣṭakaśūnyaturyaśaktirūpā bodhātmakabījasātiśayaghanatākramaprāptakramikatathābhāvā bāhyātmabhūtātmātivāhikātmāntarātmaparamātmavyapadeśyāḥ pramātāraḥ / etad bhairavātma hṛdayam / praveśopāyo 'tra -- sarvāḥ pramātṛbhūmīr anavacchedenākramet /
body.translated_text: Thus the sixteenfold pervasion of the <s>bīja</s> (seed) has been stated. The pervasion of the <s>yoni</s> (matrix), however, has been stated earlier with respect to each phoneme. But it should be examined with the intention of classification. That which consists of the five elements, constituting the aggregate of the fourfold phases of childhood, youth, old age, and the assuming of different bodies -- internally combined with the end of the lord of <s>tithis</s> in the form of <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s> (inhalation and exhalation), the nature of entry and exit. And the third is of the nature of <s>puryaṣṭaka</s> (the subtle body). <s>Brahman</s>, being vast, is the void. And herein the <s>hṛdaya</s> (heart) is of the nature of <s>śakti</s>. All these -- having the forms of body, <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>puryaṣṭaka</s>, void, <s>turya</s> (the fourth state), and <s>śakti</s> -- attaining gradual progression through the increasing density of the seed whose nature is consciousness -- are the knowing subjects designated as <s>bāhyātman</s> (external self), <s>bhūtātman</s> (elemental self), <s>ativāhikātman</s> (transmigrating self), <s>antarātman</s> (inner self), and <s>paramātman</s> (supreme self). This, of the nature of <s>Bhairava</s>, is the <s>hṛdaya</s>. The means of entry here is: one should traverse all the grounds of subjectivity without limitation.

body.text: antarbahiṣkaraṇatrayodaśakaṃ prakṛtyā saha ca /
body.translated_text: The thirteen inner and outer instruments (<s>karaṇas</s>), together with <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature),

body.text: caturdaśa catvāriṃśat tadyutaṃ dviguṇitam aśītiḥ / tithayaḥ pañcadaśa / īśā rudrā ekādaśa / antāḥ kālās trayaḥ /
body.translated_text: are fourteen [times] forty; combined and doubled, [that is] eighty. The <s>tithis</s> (lunar days) are fifteen. The lords are the eleven <s>Rudras</s>. The ends are the three <s>kālas</s> (times).
