body.text: evaṃ dvādaśottaraśatamarmagatasthūlasūkṣmaparaśāktaspandarūpamantravīryavikāsasphurīkṛtavisargavisleṣaṇasaṃghaṭṭakṣobhātmikāṃ śarīrasattām eva bhairavarūpāṃ pariśīlayed yugapanniveśasaṃpradāyayuktyā /
body.translated_text: Thus, one should cultivate the very existence of the body as the form of <s>Bhairava</s> -- [that body] which is of the nature of the agitation through the contact, separation, and emission made manifest by the expansion of <s>mantravīrya</s> (mantra-potency) in the form of the gross, subtle, and supreme <s>śākta</s> vibration situated in the one hundred and twelve vital points (<s>marmas</s>) -- through the method of the tradition of simultaneous installation.

body.text:
catasro madhurakaṣāyatiktāmladaśā yasya madyasurāsavādes tat / tithīśāntam ubhayavisargātmadravyam / samanvitaṃ tadindriyadvayāntarvarti / kusumaśabdavācyaṃ malaṃ tṛtīyam / brahma jagadindhanadāhaśeṣaṃ bhasma / bhairavātma bharitākāram āpyāyakam ambu / hṛdayaṃ ca sarvendriyāntarvarti rasāśyānobhayarūpam / tad etāni dravyāṇi yathālābhaṃ bhedamalavilāpakāni / tathāhi dṛśyate evāyaṃ kramo yad iyaṃ saṃkocātmikā śaṅkaiva samullasantī rūḍhā phalaparyantā saṃsārajīrṇataroḥ prathamāṅkurasūtiḥ / sā cāprabuddhān prati śuddhāśuddhādīnāṃ sthitir bhaved iti prabuddhaiḥ kalpitā bālān prati ca / kalpyamānāpi ca teṣāṃ rūḍhā vaicitryeṇaiva phalati / ata eva vaicitryakalpanād eva sā bahuvidhā dharmādiśabdanirdeśyā pratiśāstraṃ
pratideśaṃ cānyānyarūpā, yathoktam
body.translated_text: That which has the four tastes -- sweet, astringent, bitter, and sour -- such as wine, <s>surā</s>, fermented drink, and so forth; the substance whose nature is the twofold <s>visarga</s> (emission), which is the end of the lord of <s>tithis</s>; endowed with that, situated between both sense organs; the third is impurity (<s>mala</s>), denoted by the word 'flower' (<s>kusuma</s>); <s>Brahman</s> is ash, the remainder after the burning that fuels the world; of the nature of <s>Bhairava</s>, having the form of fullness, nourishing -- that is water (<s>ambu</s>); and the <s>hṛdaya</s> (heart) is situated within all the senses, of the twofold nature of <s>rasa</s> (taste/essence) and viscous substance. These substances, according to availability, dissolve the impurity of differentiation. For indeed this sequence is observed: this very contraction in the form of fear (<s>śaṅkā</s>), rising up, established and reaching its fruition, is the first sprouting of the tree of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) grown old. And that, for the unawakened, would be the persistence of pure, impure, and mixed [states] -- so it is conceived by the awakened for the sake of the immature. And even when being conceived, it bears fruit for them in manifold variety alone. Therefore, through the very fabrication of variety, it is manifold, to be designated by terms such as <s>dharma</s> and the like in each <s>śāstra</s> (treatise) and in each region, taking different forms. As it has been stated:

body.text: Q: glanir vilumpikā dehe. . . / iti /
body.translated_text: "Debility, which is destructive in the body..." and so forth.

body.text: seyaṃ yadā jhaṭiti vigalitā bhavati tadā nirastapāśavayantraṇākalaṅko bhairavahṛdayānupraviṣṭo bhavatīti sarvathaitadabhyāse yatitavyam / śrītilakaśāstre 'yaṃ bhāvaḥ / śrībhargaśikhāyām api uktam
body.translated_text: When this [contraction of fear] suddenly dissolves, then one becomes free of the blemish of the bonds and constraints of the noose and enters the <s>hṛdaya</s> (heart) of <s>Bhairava</s> -- therefore one should strive in every way for the practice of this. This is the purport in the <s>Śrītilakaśāstra</s>. It has also been stated in the <s>Śrībhargaśikhā</s>:

body.text: Q: vīravrataṃ cābhinanded yathāyogaṃ tathābhyaset /
body.translated_text: "One should delight in the <s>vīravrata</s> (the vow of the hero) and practice it according to proper method."

body.text: ityādi / śrīsarvācāre 'pi
body.translated_text: And so forth. And in the <s>Śrīsarvācāra</s> also:

body.text:
Q: ajñānāc chankate mūḍhas tataḥ sṛṣṭiś ca saṃhṛtiḥ /
Q: mantrā varṇātmakāḥ sarve varṇāḥ sarve śivātmakāḥ //
body.translated_text: "The fool is fearful due to ignorance; from that [arise] creation and dissolution. All <s>mantras</s> are of the nature of phonemes; all phonemes are of the nature of <s>Śiva</s>."

body.text:
Q: peyāpeyaṃ smṛtā āpo bhakṣyābhakṣyaṃ tu pārthivam /
Q: surūpaṃ ca virūpaṃ ca tat sarvaṃ teja ucyate //
body.translated_text: "What is drinkable and non-drinkable is declared to be water; what is edible and inedible is the earthy [element]; beautiful form and ugly form -- all that is said to be fire."

body.text:
Q: spṛśyāspṛśyau smṛto vāyuś chidram ākāśa ucyate /
Q: naivedyaṃ ca nivedī ca naivedyaṃ gṛhṇate ca ye //
body.translated_text: "What is touchable and untouchable is declared to be wind; the opening is said to be space. The offering and the offerer, and those who receive the offering --"

body.text:
Q: sarvaṃ pañcātmakaṃ devi na tena rahitaṃ kvacit /
Q: icchām utpādayed ātmā kathaṃ śaṅkā vidhīyate //
body.translated_text: "Everything is of fivefold nature, O <s>Devī</s>; nothing is devoid of that. The self should generate will -- how can fear be prescribed?"

body.text: iti / śrīvīrāvaliśāstre 'pi ayam evābhiprāyaḥ / uktaṃ ca kramastotre
body.translated_text: Thus. In the <s>Śrīvīrāvalīśāstra</s> also, this very intention [is expressed]. And it has been said in the <s>Kramastotra</s>:

body.text:
Q: sarvārthasaṃkarṣaṇasaṃyamasya yamasya yantur jagato yamāya /
Q: vapur mahāgrāsavilāsarāgāt saṃkarṣayantīṃ praṇamāmi kālīṃ //
body.translated_text: "I bow to <s>Kālī</s> who draws together -- she whose body, out of passionate delight in the great devouring, draws together -- for the restraint of the world, [she who is] the restraint of the restrainer (<s>Yama</s>), the restrainer of the one who controls the restraint that contracts all objects."

body.text: iti / vyākhyātaṃ caitan mayā taṭṭīkāyām eva kramakelau vistarataḥ / ata eva ṣaḍardhaśāstreṣv eṣaiva kriyā prāyo niyantraṇārahitatvena pūjā / tatparipūraṇāyaiva sarvadravyālābhāt saṃvatsaramadhye catus trir dviḥ sakṛd vā pavitrakavidhir uktaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus. And I have explained this in detail in the <s>Kramakelī</s>, the commentary on that [<s>Kramastotra</s>]. Therefore, in the scriptures of the six half-[systems], this very action is predominantly worship, being free from restriction. For the fulfillment of that [worship], in the absence of all [required] substances, within the course of a year, four times, three times, twice, or once, the <s>pavitrakvidhi</s> (purificatory rite) has been prescribed:

body.text:
Q: kriyāyāḥ pūraṇārthāya yāgājñāpūraṇāya ca /
Q: catuḥ sakṛd vā yaḥ kuryān na pavitraṃ sa niṣphalaḥ //
body.translated_text: "For the completion of ritual action, and for the fulfillment of the command of sacrifice, one who performs [it] four times, or once -- without the purificatory [rite], he is fruitless."

body.text: iti / vijñānakramo vistarata uktaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus. The progression of knowledge (<s>vijñānakrama</s>) has been stated in detail.

body.text: jātīnāṃ ca brāhmaṇādīnāṃ nāsti sthitiḥ kalpitatvāt upadeśavyaṅgateti tu durbuddhīn paśūn pratyāyayed iti ca bhagavatā mukuṭasaṃhitāyāṃ vistarato nirṇītam / iha tu ayatnasiddham eva /
body.translated_text: And for the castes (<s>jātis</s>) such as <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and others, there is no [fixed] existence, because they are fabricated -- 'and the implied [meaning] of instruction' -- thus the Lord has determined in detail in the <s>Mukuṭasaṃhitā</s>, in order to convince the dull-witted <s>paśus</s> (bound souls). But here it is self-established without effort.

body.text: guṇā icchādyā nirṇītāḥ caturdaśasvarebhyaḥ /
body.translated_text: The qualities (<s>guṇas</s>) such as <s>icchā</s> (will) and so forth have been determined from the fourteen vowels.

body.text: okāra-aṃkāramadhyagaḥ / tithīśānto visargaḥ / tṛtīyaṃ brahma ṣahamadhyagam / etad bījaṃ vastuto viśvasya / tathāhi yat kiṃcit sat pārthivaprākṛtamāyīyarūpaṃ bhāsate tad icchāyāṃ jñāne vā kriyāyāṃ vā patitam api sarvātmakatvāt trikarūpaṃ paratra śivapade visṛjyate sarvaṃ ca śivapadād visṛjyate ity aviratam eṣa eva prabandho nirvikalpakaḥ / vikalpo 'pi pramadārātiprabhṛtir evaṃkāry abhūt, ata evaṃkārī bhavati, evaṃkārī bhaviṣyatīti vartamānakālatrayānusaṃdhito 'bhedaparamārthatayaiva visarga iti pratyuta mokṣamayaśivabhūmir eva sadaiva daivadagdhānāṃ saṃsārabhayamarumahāṭavī saṃpannā /
body.translated_text: Situated between the <s>o</s>-sound and the <s>aṃ</s>-sound; the <s>visarga</s> (emission) is the end of the lord of <s>tithis</s>; the third <s>Brahman</s> is situated in the middle of <s>ṣa</s> and <s>ha</s>. This is the <s>bīja</s> (seed) of the universe in reality. For whatever exists, appearing as earthly, pertaining to <s>Prakṛti</s>, or pertaining to <s>Māyā</s> in form, whether it has fallen into <s>icchā</s> (will), <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), or <s>kriyā</s> (action), being of the nature of all, it is of the form of the triad and is emitted in <s>Śiva</s>'s supreme state; and everything is emitted from <s>Śiva</s>'s state -- thus this uninterrupted flow is <s>nirvikalpa</s> (free of conceptual construction). Even conceptual thought (<s>vikalpa</s>), beginning with notions of beloved and enemy, has acted thus, acts thus, and will act thus -- being connected with the three present times, the <s>visarga</s> (emission) is indeed of the ultimate nature of non-difference. Therefore, the ground of <s>Śiva</s>, consisting of liberation, is forever accomplished; [yet] for those burned by fate, the desert wilderness of the fear of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) appears rich [with terrors].

body.text:
Q: jalāt sphūrjajjvālājaṭilavaḍavāvahninivahaḥ sudhādhāmnaḥ purṇād bhayasadanadambholidalanā /
Q: vikalpād aiśvaryaprasarasaraṇeḥ saṃsṛtidaraḥ kiyac citraṃ citraṃ hatavidhivighātāt prasarati //
body.translated_text: "From water, a mass of <s>vaḍavā</s>-fire blazing with flickering flames; from the full moon of nectar, the shattering of the thunderbolt that is the abode of fear; from <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual thought), the terror of <s>saṃsṛti</s> (transmigration) [arising] from the path of the expansion of sovereignty -- how wondrous, how wondrous that it spreads forth from the destruction of what has been destroyed by fate!"

body.text: īśvarapratyabhijñāyām apy uktam
body.translated_text: In the <s>Īśvarapratyabhijñā</s> also it has been stated:

body.text:
Q: sarvo mamāyaṃ vibhava ity evaṃ parijānataḥ /
Q: viśvātmano vikalpānāṃ prasare 'pi maheśatā //
body.translated_text:
Q: "All this splendor is mine" — for one who knows thus,
Q: even in the expansion of <s>vikalpas</s> (mental constructs), the sovereignty of the <s>Maheśvara</s> (Great Lord) belongs to the one whose self is the universe.

body.text: iti / yathā cākṛtimadhya eva caturbhujatrinayanapūrṇakṛśādyā ākṛtayo dravyamadhye ca surāsavādyā balād eva tāṃ sattāṃ samadhiśāyayantīva lipyakṣarāṇīva satyavarṇabhūmim ity utkarṣabhāgitvam eṣām, evaṃ sarvavarṇamadhye 'pi ayaṃ varṇaḥ / tathāhi sakāras tāvat paramānandāmṛtasvabhāva ullasan eva samastaṃ varṇajālam ākṣipya ullasati / yad yat satyasukhasaṃpatsattādīnāṃ pāramārthikaṃ vapuḥ sītkārasamullāsaśephakampavarāṅgasaṃkocavikāsopalakṣyam / tad eva hi satyādīnām amāyīyaṃ vastuto rūpam / tathāhi parahṛdayagrahaṇeṅgitanipuṇā gaganagavayagavādyanantapadaprāṅmadhyāntabhāvino 'pi gakārādimātrād evābhīṣṭaṃ cinvate, tāvati satyapade 'nupraveśāt / evam ekaikasyaiva varṇasya vāstavaṃ vācakatvam / yathoktam
body.translated_text: iti / Just as among forms, the forms of four-armed, three-eyed, full, thin, and so forth, and among substances, wine, liquor, and the like, forcefully cause that very existence to preside — like written letters upon the ground of true <s>varṇas</s> (phonemes) — thus demonstrating the superiority of these, so too among all <s>varṇas</s>, this <s>varṇa</s> (phoneme) is supreme. For indeed, the <s>sa-kāra</s> (letter 'sa'), whose nature is the nectar of supreme bliss (<s>paramānanda</s>), flashing forth, draws in the entire web of <s>varṇas</s> and radiates. Whatever is the ultimate form of true bliss, authentic prosperity, being, and so forth — that which is indicated by the hissing sound (<s>sītkāra</s>), the excitement, the trembling of the phallus, the contraction and expansion of the excellent limbs — that alone is the non-<s>māyic</s>, real form of truth and the rest. For indeed, those who are skilled in grasping another's heart through gestures, from the mere <s>ga-kāra</s> and the like, even of words like <s>gagana</s> (sky), <s>gavaya</s> (wild ox), <s>go</s> (cow), and countless others that have prior, middle, and final states, discern what is desired, because of entry into that much of the real word. Thus, each and every <s>varṇa</s> has genuine expressive power (<s>vācakatva</s>). As it is stated —

body.text: Q: śabdārthapratyayānām itaretarādhyāsāt saṃkaraḥ tatpravibhāgasaṃyamāt sarvabhūtarutajñānam /
body.translated_text: Q: "From the mutual superimposition of word, meaning, and cognition, there is commingling; from <s>saṃyama</s> (concentrated discipline) on their distinction, knowledge of the cries of all beings arises."

body.text: iti / ata eva prāyaśo 'mī akāracakārādyā ekavarṇātmāno nipātavibhaktyādayo māyāpade 'pi pāramārthikam iva pramātṛpadalīnam idantāparāṅmukham asattvabhūtaṃ tattanniṣidhyamānasamuccīyamānābhinnarūpaniṣedhasamuccayādikam artham abhidadhati / eṣa eva bhāvas tatrabhavato bhartṛhareḥ, yad āha
body.translated_text: iti / Therefore, mostly these single-phoneme particles, case-endings, and the like — consisting of <s>a-kāra</s>, <s>ca-kāra</s>, etc. — even in the domain of <s>māyā</s>, express meaning as though it were ultimate: merged in the subject-state, turned away from objectivity, of the nature of non-being — negation, conjunction, identity with what is being negated or conjoined, and so forth. This is precisely the view of the venerable <s>Bhartṛhari</s>, who said —

body.text: Q: padam ādyaṃ pṛthak sarvaṃ padaṃ sākāṅkṣam ity api /
body.translated_text: Q: "The first word, each one separately, is said to be a word with expectancy (<s>sākāṅkṣa</s>)."

body.text: iti vākyavicāre / tathā ca vedavyākaraṇe pārameśvareṣu śāstreṣu mantradīkṣādiśabdeṣv akṣaravarṇasāmyān nirvacanam upapannam / tat tu na rūḍhaṃ niyativaśād iti na lokaparyantam / tad evaṃ sakāra īdṛśaḥ / aukāravisargāv api vyākhyātau / tad uktaṃ śrīpūrvaśāstre
body.translated_text: iti / — in the <s>Vākyavicāra</s> ("Inquiry into the Sentence"). And thus in <s>Veda</s>-grammar, in the <s>Pārameśvara</s> (divine) scriptures, in words such as <s>mantra</s>, <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation), and the like, etymology is well-established on account of the identity of syllables and <s>varṇas</s> (phonemes). But this is not merely conventional, nor is it dependent on fixed necessity alone, and hence it does not extend merely to worldly usage. Thus such is the <s>sa-kāra</s>. The <s>au-kāra</s> and <s>visarga</s> have also been explained. As stated in the glorious <s>Pūrvaśāstra</s> (Prior Scripture) —

body.text:
Q: sārṇena tritayaṃ vyāptaṃ triśūlena caturthakam /
Q: sarvātītaṃ visargeṇa parā vyāptir udāhṛtā //
body.translated_text:
Q: "By the <s>sa-kāra</s>, the triad is pervaded; by the trident (<s>triśūla</s>), the fourth;
Q: by the <s>visarga</s> (emission), which transcends all, the supreme pervasion is declared."

body.text: iti / tathā
body.translated_text: iti / Likewise —

body.text:
Q: siṣyeṇāpi tadā grāhyā yadā saṃtoṣito guruḥ /
Q: śarīradravyavijñānaśuddhikarmaguṇādibhiḥ //
body.translated_text:
Q: "The <s>śiṣya</s> (disciple) should receive it only when the <s>guru</s> is satisfied,
Q: through purity of body, wealth, knowledge, action, qualities, and the like."

body.text:
Q: bodhitā tu yadā tena guruṇā hṛṣṭacetasā /
Q: tadā siddhipradā jñeyā nānyathā viravandite //
body.translated_text:
Q: "When one is instructed by that <s>guru</s> with a joyful heart,
Q: then it is known to bestow <s>siddhi</s> (attainment), not otherwise, O honored one among heroes."

body.text: iti / anyatrāpi
body.translated_text: iti / Elsewhere also —

body.text: Q: ekaṃ sṛṣṭimayaṃ bījam ... /
body.translated_text: Q: "The one <s>bīja</s> (seed), consisting of creation ..."

body.text: iti / ata evālekhyaṃ pustake iti niyamaḥ / śrīpūrvaśāstre 'pi
body.translated_text: iti / For this very reason there is the rule that it should not be written in a book. In the glorious <s>Pūrvaśāstra</s> also —

body.text: Q: vāmajaṅghānvito jīvaḥ pāramparyakramāgataḥ /
body.translated_text: Q: "The living being (<s>jīva</s>), accompanied by the left shank, has come down through the succession of tradition (<s>paramparā</s>)."

body.text: iti / ihāpi vakṣyate
body.translated_text: iti / Here too it will be stated —

body.text: Q: yathā nyagrodhabījasthaḥ... /
body.translated_text: Q: "Just as what dwells within the seed of the banyan tree (<s>nyagrodha</s>)..."

body.text:
iti /
tad etad bhairavātmano hṛdayaṃ mālinyapekṣayā nakārāt vastutas tv akārād yoginyāś ca visargaśakter jātaḥ / prādurbhūtapramātṛbhāvo rudro rodhako drāvakaś ca pāśānāṃ, sa eva nā puruṣaḥ, etat sphuṭaṃ labhate, na tv arudro nāpi ayoginīgarbhasaṃbhavaḥ / sadyoyogo bhairavaikātmyam / sa eva mokṣo nirṇītaḥ / taṃ dadātīti yo labhate sa evaṃvidho nānyaḥ / yaś caivaṃvidhaḥ sa sphuṭaṃ labhate / evaṃ hṛdayam eva labhate sadyoyogavimokṣadam eveti sarvato niyamaḥ /
body.translated_text:
iti /
This is the heart (<s>hṛdaya</s>) of <s>Bhairava</s>: with reference to <s>Mālinī</s>, it arises from the <s>na-kāra</s>, but in reality from the <s>a-kāra</s>, and from the <s>visarga-śakti</s> (emissive power) of the <s>Yoginī</s>. <s>Rudra</s>, having manifested the nature of the cognizing subject, is the one who blocks and dissolves the bonds (<s>pāśas</s>). He alone, as <s>nā</s>, is the <s>Puruṣa</s> (Person). He clearly obtains this — but not one who is not <s>Rudra</s>, nor one who is not born from the womb of the <s>Yoginī</s>. Immediate union (<s>sadyoyoga</s>) is identity with <s>Bhairava</s>. That alone has been determined as liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>). The one who gives it — he who receives it is of this very nature and no other. And whoever is of this nature clearly obtains it. Thus, one obtains the very heart that grants immediate union and liberation — this is the rule in every respect.

body.text: mantrā varṇabhaṭṭārakā laukikapārameśvarādirūpā mananatrāṇarūpā avikalpasaṃvinmayāḥ / mudrāś ca sakalakaracaraṇādikaraṇavyāpāramayāḥ kriyāśaktirūpāḥ / tatkṛto gaṇaḥ samūhātmā paraśaktyekarūpaḥ / svasyātmanaḥ prāṇapuryaṣṭakaśūnyāder dehasya ya āveśo jhaṭiti parasvarūpānupraveśena pāratantryātmakajaḍatātirodhānena svatantrakartṛtānuviddhapramātṛtodayaḥ / tathā svaṃ svabhāvaṃ padārthasya dadātīti svadā / īhā icchādyā kriyāntā / tayā āveśaḥ / tad eva lakṣaṇaṃ yatra / tathā kṛtvā ya udeti so 'sya bījasyoccāre ūrdhvacaraṇe sthitau satyām / asya akārasya / yathaitat tathā nirṇītaṃ bahuśaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Mantras</s> are the sovereign <s>varṇas</s> (phonemes), having both worldly and <s>Pārameśvara</s> (supreme divine) forms, consisting of contemplation (<s>manana</s>) and protection (<s>trāṇa</s>), made of thought-free consciousness (<s>avikalpa-saṃvid</s>). <s>Mudrās</s> are constituted by the activities of all instruments — hands, feet, and the rest — having the form of <s>kriyā-śakti</s> (power of action). The group (<s>gaṇa</s>) produced by these is a collective entity, one in nature with the supreme <s>Śakti</s>. The <s>āveśa</s> (possession/penetration) of one's own self — whose body is <s>prāṇa</s>, the subtle body (<s>puryaṣṭaka</s>), the void, and so forth — is the sudden entry into one's supreme nature, the concealment of inert dependency being overcome, and the arising of the cognizing subject imbued with autonomous agency. Likewise, <s>svadā</s> means "it gives its own nature" to an object. <s>Īhā</s> (endeavor) ranges from <s>icchā</s> (will) to <s>kriyā</s> (action). Through that, there is <s>āveśa</s>. That is the defining characteristic where this occurs. Having done thus, that which arises — when the utterance of this <s>bīja</s> (seed-syllable), its upward movement, is established — pertains to this <s>a-kāra</s>. How this is so has been determined many times.

body.text: sadya ity anena sat ity apy anupraveśaḥ sūcyate / tanmukhatāṃ tatpararūpaprādhānyam eti, na tu paśūnām iva tadrūpaṃ pratyuta tirodhatte /
body.translated_text: By the word <s>sadya</s> ("immediately"), the word <s>sat</s> ("being/truth") is also indicated as entering into it. It attains orientation toward that — the predominance of that supreme nature — but it does not, as in the case of <s>paśus</s> (bound souls), conceal that very nature; rather, the opposite.

body.text: ata eva muhūrtaṃ, akālakalitatve 'pi parakalanāpekṣayā unmeṣamātram, yaḥ smaraty anusaṃdhatte sa eva vyākhyātaṃ mantramudrāgaṇaṃ saṃbadhnāti svātmany ekīkaroty advayataḥ / katham / cumbakena viśvasparśakena śāktena rūpeṇābhitaḥ sarvato mudritaṃ mudraṇaṃ kṛtvā / tur avadhāraṇe / ya eva śāktaspandamudrita evaṃvidhatattvamayaśivarūpānusaṃdhāyakaḥ sa evaivaṃ karoti na tu naraikarūpaḥ pāṣānādiḥ / yad atītaṃ yac cānāgataṃ yad anartharūpaṃ prāg anyābhāvād itarad api sa eva kathayati kathāparyantatāṃ nayati saṃkalpanāt / katham /
body.translated_text: Therefore, <s>muhūrta</s> (a moment) — even though not conditioned by time, with reference to the supreme reckoning it is a mere flash of opening (<s>unmeṣa</s>) — whoever remembers, whoever contemplates, he alone binds together — that is, unifies within his own self in a non-dual manner — the explained <s>mantra</s>, <s>mudrā</s>, and <s>gaṇa</s>. How? By means of the <s>cumbaka</s> (magnet), the <s>Śākta</s> (pertaining to <s>Śakti</s>) form that touches the universe, having sealed (<s>mudrita</s>) it on all sides. The particle <s>tu</s> is for emphasis. Only one who is sealed by the pulsation of <s>Śakti</s> (<s>śakti-spanda</s>), who contemplates this <s>Śiva</s>-nature constituted of such reality — he alone does this, not a mere human form, a stone, or the like. Whatever is past, whatever is yet to come, whatever is of the nature of non-purpose — since prior to anything else's existence nothing else exists — he alone narrates, brings to the conclusion of the narrative, through <s>saṃkalpana</s> (creative volition). How?

body.text:
Q: pṛṣṭaḥ praśno jñīpsā pṛṣṭaṃ tad yasyāsti sa tathā /
Q: yad eva kila jñīpsati tat tad evāntargataṃ bahiṣkurute //
body.translated_text:
Q: "Inquiry is the question, the desire to know; that which is asked — whoever possesses it, he is thus.
Q: Whatever indeed one desires to know, precisely that, which is internal, one brings forth externally."

body.text: yathoktam
body.translated_text: As it is stated —

body.text:
Q: yathecchābhyarthito dhātā jagrato 'rthān hṛdi sthitān /
Q: somasūryodayaṃ kṛtvā saṃpādayati dehinaḥ //
body.translated_text:
Q: "Just as the Creator (<s>Dhātā</s>), requested according to one's desire, for one who is awake, the objects established in the heart,
Q: having caused the rising of <s>Soma</s> and <s>Sūrya</s>, bestows upon the embodied being."

body.text:
ityādi / eko hy asau smaraṇotprekṣaṇādāv api tāvān eva vartamāno
na sto bhūtabhaviṣyatī / yathoktaṃ
body.translated_text:
ityādi / For this one, even in the acts of remembering and imagining, remains of exactly that extent —
he does not become past or future. As stated —

body.text: Q: kālobhayāparicchinnam ... ityādi /
body.translated_text: Q: "Not delimited by either aspect of time ..." ityādi /

body.text: prāgbhāvata evānadhikarūpasya punar idaṃ jānāti karoti ityādisaṃkocāsahiṣṇoḥ sakṛdvibhātatvam / ata evoktaṃ bhūtādyapekṣayā vartamānakālasya tadabhāve vastuto 'prasakter akālakalitam eva vastutattvam iti hy uktam asakṛt / sa eva tu kālaśaktim avabhāsayati citrām
body.translated_text: From prior non-existence itself, for one whose form is beyond limitation, who cannot tolerate the contraction of "now he knows this, now he does this," there is a once-and-for-all shining forth. Therefore it is said: since in the absence of the past and future, the present time has no real applicability — the reality of things is not conditioned by time at all — this has been stated repeatedly. Yet it is He alone who manifests the variegated power of time (<s>kāla-śakti</s>) —

body.text:
Q: kiṃ ca jāgrati kasmiṃścid ghaṭikābhimatāpi yā /
Q: tasyām eva pramātāraḥ svapnagāś citratājuṣaḥ /
Q: dinapraharavarṣādivaicitryam api cinvate //
body.translated_text:
Q: "Moreover, in some waking state, even that which is regarded as a mere <s>ghaṭikā</s> (unit of time),
Q: within that very span, the cognizing subjects, traversing dreams, partaking of diversity,
Q: discern the variety of days, watches, years, and the like."

body.text: iti nītyā /
body.translated_text: iti / — according to this reasoning.

body.text:
prakṛṣṭo haraḥ saṃhāro 'kulākhyas tato 'nantaram abhipretaṃ pretaśabdavācyasadāśivatattvaniviṣṭajñānaśaktyābhimukhyena devatāyā icchāyā rūpaṃ rūpāṇāṃ kalānāṃ sākṣasya sendriyasya rūpasyādanaṃ bhakṣaṇam atanaṃ ca sātatyagamanaṃ kṛtvā rodhanadrāvaṇarūpaśaktibhir ākṛṣṭaṃ paśyaty asaṃdigdhaṃ kṛtvā / etad uktaṃ bhavati yad idaṃ darśanaṃ nāma tat sarvataraṅgapratyastamayākhyākulasattādhirūḍhasyānantamahimasvātantryayogād icchāśaktimataḥ / saivecchā svāntargateṣyamāṇavastuna īṣadasphuṭabhedāvabhāsanarūpajñānaśaktyātmakatām eti / tajjñānaśaktir viśeṣaspandanarūpasamastendriyāṇāṃ bahīrodhanam / etad eva sātatyagamanam / yac ca drāvaṇaṃ tad eva bhakṣaṇam / ete eva vamanabhakṣaṇe darśanasya
sarvaprathaikamayatvāt prathāyāś ca tathāvidhavaicitryayogāt / aniścitobhayālambanatvam api sthāṇupuruṣādāv apy asaṃdigdham eva / evaṃ duṣkṛtamayī parameśaśaktiḥ /
body.translated_text:
The supreme <s>Hara</s> (Destroyer) is dissolution (<s>saṃhāra</s>), called <s>akula</s>; thereafter, the intended form of the <s>Devatā</s> (Deity), of <s>Icchā</s> (Will), directed toward the <s>Jñāna-śakti</s> (power of knowledge) established in the <s>Sadāśiva-tattva</s> — designated by the word <s>preta</s> — having consumed and continuously traversed the forms, the <s>kalās</s> (parts), the form endowed with senses, through the powers of blocking and dissolving, draws it forth and sees it with certainty. What is being said is this: that which is called seeing (<s>darśana</s>) — that belongs to one who has ascended to the state of <s>akula</s>, characterized by the subsidence of all waves, and who, by virtue of infinite sovereign autonomy, possesses <s>Icchā-śakti</s>. That very <s>Icchā</s> (Will) attains the nature of <s>Jñāna-śakti</s> (power of knowledge), which consists in the slightly indistinct manifestation of differentiation in the object desired within oneself. That <s>Jñāna-śakti</s> is the external expression of all the senses in the form of particular vibration (<s>spandana</s>). This is the continuous movement. And what is dissolution (<s>drāvaṇa</s>) is itself the consuming. These are indeed the vomiting and consuming of seeing,
because seeing is primarily of the nature of universal manifestation, and manifestation possesses such variety. Even the state of uncertain dual-object apprehension, as in the case of a post and a person, is itself certain. Thus is the <s>Śakti</s> of <s>Parameśa</s> (the Supreme Lord), pervading even what appears erroneous.

body.text:
evaṃ tv asau parāpararūpasmṛtiśaktimān bhairava ity āha ``praharadvayetyādi'' / evaṃ tu smaran jāyate vyoma vidyate yatra puryaṣṭake śūnye ca tatpramātṛrūpatām ādadhānaḥ / praharopalakṣitaṃ darśanākhyaṃ rūpaṃ yadā punaḥ punaḥ parāmṛśati smaraty api ca prāgvat ``sākṣāt paśyaty asaṃdigdham ākṛṣṭaṃ rudraśaktibhiḥ'' iti saṃbandhaḥ / tāvad dhi tad api darśanam eva ity uktam / evaṃ tu aparātmakavikalpaśaktiyukta ity ucyate / trayeṇeti paśyan smaraṃś ca vyomastho yadā punar api paśyati tad anena praharopalakṣitadarśanatrayeṇa mātaro 'ntaḥpramāṭrmayāḥ parameśaśaktayaḥ tāś ca pramātṛtvād eva siddhāḥ pramātrantaraviṣayasiddhyanapekṣāḥ, tadrūpaikātmyalakṣaṇena yogenaiśvaryam, tathā gṛhītasvātantryāṃśāḥ, mahad
bāhyendriyavṛttyapekṣayā sarvatrāpratihataprasaratvaṃ balaṃ yāsāṃ tā antaḥkaraṇadīdhitayaḥ tā api siddhā eva /
body.translated_text:
Thus, He, <s>Bhairava</s>, possesses the power of memory of the supreme-and-non-supreme nature — this is stated in "<s>praharadvaya</s>" and so forth. Thus remembering, He arises as the sky (<s>vyoman</s>) — that is, He assumes the nature of the cognizing subject in the subtle body (<s>puryaṣṭaka</s>) and in the void. When He again and again touches, remembers the form characterized as seeing, indicated by "<s>prahara</s>" — then as before, "He directly sees with certainty, drawn by the powers of <s>Rudra</s>" — this is the syntactic connection. For that also is indeed seeing — thus it is stated. And thus He is said to possess the <s>vikalpa-śakti</s> (power of determinate thought) of the non-supreme aspect. By the triad — when, seeing and remembering, established in the sky (<s>vyoman</s>), He sees yet again — then by this triad of seeings indicated by "<s>prahara</s>," the <s>Mātṛs</s> (Mothers), who are internally constituted of cognizing subjects, who are the powers of <s>Parameśa</s> — and they are established by virtue of being cognizing subjects themselves, not requiring validation by another subject — through <s>yoga</s> characterized by identity with that nature, there is sovereignty; and they have assumed a portion of autonomy; and the power that is their
unobstructed expansion everywhere, in comparison with the activity of the external senses, constitutes the great strength — these rays of the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) are also established indeed.

body.text:
viśvatra pāśavasāsanayantraṇānirapekṣatayaiva sarabhasapravṛttirūpatvād vīrā buddhikriyendriyākhyās te 'pi siddhā eva / teṣām api cesvarāḥ kādivarṇātmānaḥ te 'pi siddhāḥ / tatkādivarṇoddhāroditaś ca brāhmyādidevatātmā tattaddveṣarāgādicittavṛttirasamayaḥ śaktisamūhaḥ so 'pi siddha eva, ata eva balavān / ete sarve saṃbhūya parājñayā parasya māṃ mānamayīm ``asau paraḥ'' iti vikalpātmikāṃ siddhim / yad vā samīhitaṃ phalam eva ``ahaṃ'' dadati prayacchanti / ajñātārthakriye jñātārthakriye ca eṣa krameṇa vikalpāvikalpayogaḥ / kiṃ bahunā / ye mantriṇo 'parakulāntamantrasiddhā api sādhayanti / api ca te 'py anena hṛdayena setsyanti jīvanmuktāḥ / etena vinā pāramārthikī siddhir na bhavatīti bhāvaḥ / ``yat kiṃcid bhairavetyādi'' / tathā ye siddhāḥ
sādhayanti ca ye ca setsyanti aṇimādiyogāt te 'py anenaiva / na hi etaddhṛdayānupraveśaṃ vinā vyāvahāriky api siddhiḥ, yato bhairave viśvātmani tantre kriyākalāpe yat kiṃcit siddhijātaṃ tad ata eva /
body.translated_text:
Everywhere, because their nature is that of impetuous activity, independent of the restraints of <s>paśu</s>-governance — these are the <s>Vīras</s> (heroes), namely the <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), <s>kriyā</s> (action), and <s>indriyas</s> (senses) — they too are established. And the lords of these are the <s>varṇas</s> (phonemes) beginning with <s>ka</s> — they too are established. And the host of <s>Śaktis</s>, having the nature of <s>Brāhmī</s> and other deities, arising from the extraction of those <s>varṇas</s> beginning with <s>ka</s>, constituting the savor of the respective mental modifications of aversion, attachment, and the like — that aggregate of powers is also established, and therefore powerful. All of these together, by the supreme command, give — that is, bestow — <s>siddhi</s> (attainment) of the supreme, which is the measure-nature (<s>mānamayī</s>) "that is the Supreme" — in the form of <s>vikalpa</s> (determinate thought). Or alternatively, they bestow the desired fruit itself as "I." In the case of both action with unknown purpose and action with known purpose, this is respectively the application of <s>vikalpa</s> (determinate thought) and <s>avikalpa</s> (thought-free awareness). In brief: those <s>mantrins</s> (adepts of <s>mantras</s>) who have attained <s>siddhi</s> in the <s>mantra</s> at the end of the non-supreme lineage (<s>aparakula</s>) — they too accomplish [their aims]. Moreover, they too shall attain perfection through this heart, becoming <s>jīvanmuktas</s> (liberated while living). Without this, ultimate <s>siddhi</s> does not occur — this is the purport. "Whatever in <s>Bhairava</s>" and so forth. Likewise, those who have attained <s>siddhi</s>,
those who are accomplishing, and those who will attain — even through <s>aṇimā</s> and other <s>yogic</s> powers — they too [accomplish] only through this. For without entry into this heart, even conventional <s>siddhi</s> is not possible, since whatever class of <s>siddhi</s> exists in the <s>Bhairava-tantra</s>, which is the self of the universe, in the ensemble of practices — all of that is from this alone.

body.text: evam eṣa parameśvara eva hṛdayātmā evaṃrūpatayā śaktitritayabṛṃhitasatatodayamānasaṃhriyamāṇānantasaṃvidaikyaśālī parikalpitaḥ san adṛṣṭam asaṃdarśanam evākhyātirūpaṃ maṇḍaṃ māyāmalam, maṇḍaṃ ca bhāvānāṃ bhedākhyaṃ sāraṃ lumpati / evam adṛṣṭam etad dhṛdayam aṇḍalopi / catvāry aṇḍāny eva / lopaḥ saṃkocaḥ / tad yogi /
body.translated_text: Thus this <s>Parameśvara</s> (Supreme Lord) Himself, having the nature of the heart (<s>hṛdaya</s>), being of this very form, endowed with the three <s>Śaktis</s>, possessing the unity of infinite consciousness that is perpetually arising and being reabsorbed — having been realized thus, He destroys what is unseen — namely, the stain of <s>māyā</s>, which is of the nature of non-manifestation itself, appearing as false appearance (<s>ākhyāti</s>) — and also the <s>maṇḍa</s> (essence) of entities, namely their differentiation (<s>bheda</s>). Thus this unseen heart is the destroyer of the cosmic eggs (<s>aṇḍa</s>). The four <s>aṇḍas</s> (cosmic eggs) themselves. <s>Lopa</s> (destruction) means contraction. That is what pertains to the <s>yogin</s>.

body.text: evam eṣa vidyāmāyobhayātmā parameśvara eka eva cidghanaḥ, yathoktam
body.translated_text: Thus this <s>Parameśvara</s> (Supreme Lord), one alone, of the nature of both <s>Vidyā</s> (knowledge) and <s>Māyā</s> (illusion), is a solid mass of consciousness (<s>cidghana</s>), as stated —

body.text:
Q: darśanaṃ tu parā devī smaraṇaṃ ca parāparā /
Q: vikalpas tv aparā devī trikaśaktimayaḥ prabhuḥ //
body.translated_text:
Q: "Seeing (<s>darśana</s>) is the supreme <s>Devī</s> (Goddess); memory (<s>smaraṇa</s>) is <s>Parāparā</s> (the supreme-non-supreme);
Q: determinate thought (<s>vikalpa</s>) is the non-supreme <s>Devī</s> (<s>Aparā</s>); the Lord is constituted of the triad of <s>Śaktis</s>."

body.text:
Q: māyāvidye ubhe tasya māyā tu caturaṇḍikā /
Q: vidyā svarūpasaṃvittir anugrahamayī śivā //
body.translated_text:
Q: "<s>Māyā</s> and <s>Vidyā</s> are both His; <s>Māyā</s> is fourfold, pertaining to the four cosmic eggs;
Q: <s>Vidyā</s> is self-awareness (<s>svarūpa-saṃvitti</s>), gracious, of the nature of <s>anugraha</s> (grace), and <s>Śivā</s> (auspicious)."

body.text: iti / yadi tu yogaprādhānyaṃ tadā śrīpūrvādiśāstranirūpitaṃ pūrvam eva vratādi kṛtvā, ``asyoccāre kṛte'' ityādi spaṣṭam eva vyakhyeyam, yato dṛṣṭakāryeṣu niyatiparatantrī kriyākalāpaṃ niyatam evāpekṣate /
body.translated_text: iti / If, however, the emphasis is on <s>yoga</s> practice, then having first performed the <s>vrata</s> (observance) and the like as taught in the glorious <s>Pūrvaśāstra</s> and other scriptures, "upon the utterance of this" and so forth should be explained straightforwardly, since in matters of visible results, one who is dependent on <s>niyati</s> (fixed rule) necessarily requires a prescribed ensemble of practices.

body.text: yoginām api hi nāḍīcakrakaraṇabhāvanāsaṃvedanayuktyā niyama eva /
body.translated_text: For even for <s>yogins</s>, there is indeed a fixed rule involving the method of experiencing <s>nāḍī</s>-<s>cakras</s> (energy channels and centers), the instruments, and contemplation (<s>bhāvanā</s>).

body.text: asyedānīṃ trikārthasya yad uktaṃ
body.translated_text: Now, regarding this meaning of the triad (<s>trika</s>), what has been stated —

body.text: Q: kulāt parataraṃ trikam iti
body.translated_text: Q: "The <s>Trika</s> is higher than <s>Kula</s>"

body.text: sarvottaram anuttaratvaṃ tan nirūpayati /
body.translated_text: — its supremely unsurpassable nature (<s>anuttaratva</s>) is now being established.

body.text: ParTri 18cd-18ef:

children.translated_text: Even one who has not seen the <s>maṇḍala</s> (sacred circle),
whoever knows this in truth,
he shall be a partaker of <s>siddhi</s> (attainment) eternally,
he is a <s>yogin</s>, and he is one who has received <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation).

body.text:
maṇḍalaṃ devatācakram apaśyann apy aprāptamelako 'pi caryāniśāṭanahaṭhādinā, maṇḍalāni śarīranāḍīcakrānucakrarūpāṇi yogābhyāsenāsākṣātkurvann api, trisūlābjādimaṇḍalam adṛṣṭvāpi / nātra maṇḍalādidīkṣopayogaḥ / evam eva kaścit paraśaktipātānugṛhīto vetti yaḥ ``etajjñānam eva hi dīkṣā kānyātra dīkṣā'', ata eva evaṃ jānan vibhunā bhairavabhaṭṭārakeṇa dīkṣitaḥ / ata eva svayaṃgṛhītamantraś cety etad etaddhṛdayātiriktamantraviṣayam / na hi ayaṃ mantro hṛdayamayatvāt, mantramaheśatanmaheśarūpottīrṇatvād asya / pustakeṣv alekhyam evedaṃ hṛdayam iti paraśaktipātānugrahād eva etallābhas tattvata iti nirṇītam / tathā yaḥ kaścid iti jātivratacaryādinairapekṣyam / atra vedanam eva hi pradhānam / sa siddhibhāg
yogī
body.translated_text:
<s>Maṇḍala</s> means the circle of deities. Even one who has not seen it, who has not attained the ritual gathering (<s>melaka</s>) through <s>caryā</s> (observance), nocturnal wandering (<s>niśāṭana</s>), <s>haṭha</s>, and the like; even one who has not directly realized through yogic practice the <s>maṇḍalas</s> that are the <s>nāḍī-cakras</s> and subsidiary <s>cakras</s> of the body; even one who has not seen the <s>maṇḍala</s> of the trident-and-lotus (<s>trisūlābja</s>) and the rest — here the ritual use of <s>maṇḍala</s>-initiation and such is not required. In just this way, whoever, graced by the descent of supreme <s>Śakti</s> (<s>paraśaktipāta</s>), knows — "this knowledge itself is <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation); what other <s>dīkṣā</s> is there?" — therefore, one who knows thus is initiated by the all-pervading Lord <s>Bhairava</s> Himself. Therefore he has spontaneously grasped the <s>mantra</s> — and this pertains to <s>mantras</s> other than this heart. For this <s>mantra</s> is not [merely a <s>mantra</s>], since it is of the nature of the heart, and it transcends <s>Mantra</s>, <s>Mantreśvara</s>, and <s>Mantramaheśvara</s> in form. This heart should indeed not be written in books — the attainment of this comes only through the grace of the descent of supreme <s>Śakti</s>; this is determined as "in truth." And the phrase "whoever" indicates independence from caste, observance, conduct, and the like. Here, knowing itself is primary. He is a partaker of <s>siddhi</s>,
a <s>yogin</s> —

body.text: Q: yogam ekatvam icchanti
body.translated_text: Q: "They desire <s>yoga</s> as oneness."

body.text: iti yataḥ / jñānadānamāyākṣapaṇalakṣaṇā ca tasyaiva dīkṣā / cakāro 'vadhāraṇe tac ca sarvato mantavyam / sa eva siddhibhāg yogī dīkṣitaḥ / siddhibhāg eva yogy eva dīkṣita eva saḥ / tad āha nityam iti /
body.translated_text: Thus, because. And the <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) characterized by the bestowal of knowledge and the destruction of <s>Māyā</s> is His alone. The particle 'ca' is for emphasis, and that should be understood throughout. He alone is the partaker of <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment), He alone is the <s>yogī</s>, He alone is the initiated one. The partaker of <s>siddhi</s> alone, the <s>yogī</s> alone, the initiated one alone is he. Therefore it says 'always.'

body.text: ParTri 19ab:

children.translated_text: "By the mere knowledge of this,"
"one is known by all <s>śaktis</s>."

body.text:
sarvābhir devatābhiḥ sarvaśaktibhiś ca sarvajñair asau jñāyata etaj jānann eva / tair api yat kiṃcit jñāyate tad anena jñatamātreṇa
jñāyata iti prāgvat / sarvābhiḥ śaktibhir iti karaṇe tṛtīyā /
body.translated_text: By all deities and all <s>śaktis</s> — all the omniscient ones — he is known as one who knows this very thing. Whatever is known even by them, that is known by the mere knowledge of this — as stated before. 'By all <s>śaktis</s>' — the instrumental case is in the sense of instrument.

body.text: tathā
body.translated_text: Likewise:

body.text: ParTri 19cd:

children.translated_text: "One becomes equal to the <s>Śākinī</s> clan,"
"even without <s>yoga</s> indeed."

body.text: anena jñātamātreṇa yogam ābhyāsikaṃ māyīyadehapātāvāptatadaikyarūpaṃ ca vināpi śākinīkulasya viśeṣaspandātmanaḥ sāmānyaspandarūpo 'kularūpaḥ śakticakreśvaro bhaved iti /
body.translated_text: By the mere knowledge of this, even without <s>yoga</s> — whether practiced [yoga] or [yoga] of the form of unity attained through the death of the <s>māyīya</s> (illusory) body — one becomes of the nature of the universal vibration of the <s>Śākinī</s> clan, which is of the nature of particular vibration; that is, of the <s>akula</s> nature, the lord of the circle of <s>śaktis</s>.

body.text: kiṃ ca
body.translated_text: Moreover:

body.text: ParTri 20:

children.translated_text: "One ignorant of ritual becomes a knower of ritual,"
"with respect to worship."

body.text: vidhiḥ kriyā jñā jñānam / tad yasya dvayaṃ nāsti sa paśuḥ, yathoktaṃ kiraṇāyām
body.translated_text: <s>Vidhi</s> (ritual) means action; <s>jñā</s> means knowledge. He who lacks both is a <s>paśu</s> (bound soul). As stated in the <s>Kiraṇā</s>:

body.text:
Q: paśur nityo hy amūrto 'jño niṣkriyo nirguṇo 'prabhuḥ /
Q: vyāpī māyodarāntaḥstho bhogopāyavicintakaḥ //
body.translated_text:
Quote: 'The <s>paśu</s> (bound soul) is eternal, formless, unknowing, without action, without qualities, without lordship,
all-pervading, situated within the womb of <s>Māyā</s>, contemplating the means of enjoyment.'

body.text: iti / sa paśur apy anena jñātamātreṇa vidhānaṃ jñā ca yasya sa kartā jñātā ca viṣayasaṃgatikaraṇaṃ prati jāyate / yajanaṃ cāsyāpūrṇam api pūrṇaṃ bhavatīti sarvamayatvād dhṛdayasya / tathāhi
body.translated_text: That <s>paśu</s> too, by the mere knowledge of this, becomes one who possesses both ritual and knowledge — an agent and a knower — with respect to the accomplishment of engagement with objects. And his worship, even if incomplete, becomes complete, because the heart is the nature of all. For thus:

body.text: ParTri 21:

children.translated_text: "Beginning with <s>Kālāgni</s>,"
"up to <s>Māyā</s>, contained in the body of <s>Brahman</s>;"
"<s>Śiva</s>, from <s>Viśva</s> onward, within <s>Ananta</s>;"
"the supreme triad of <s>śaktis</s> is declared."

body.text: kālāgner dharātattvādibhuvanān māyātattvaṃ yāvad brahmaṇaḥ sakārasya dehe / viśvabhuvanād vidyātattvāder ārabhya yāvat śivo 'nāśritaśaktirūpo 'nantasyaukārasyāntaḥ / paraṃ visargātmakaṃ śaktitrayaṃ tac ca param / uktaṃ ca ``sārṇena'' ityādi //
body.translated_text: From <s>Kālāgni</s>, the worlds of the earth-<s>tattva</s> and so on up to the <s>Māyā-tattva</s>, in the body of <s>Brahman</s>, the [letter] 'sa.' From the <s>Viśva</s> world, beginning with the <s>Vidyā-tattva</s> and so on, up to <s>Śiva</s>, who has the form of the non-dependent <s>Śakti</s>, within <s>Ananta</s>, the [letter] 'au.' The supreme triad of <s>śaktis</s>, of the nature of <s>visarga</s> — and that is supreme. And it has been stated: 'By the syllable...' and so on.

body.text: ParTri 22:

children.translated_text: "Whatever abides within that,"
"established in the pure path —"
"the limited soul, purified, swiftly"
"attains lordly knowledge."

body.text: yat kiṃcid vastu vyavasthitaṃ vicitrāvasthaṃ tad dhṛdayabījāntarvarti śuddhaṃ bhavet / tad eva caiśvaraṃ jñānam aṇur aṇyate prāṇiti aṇati nadati parimitoccārāt mūrdhanyo bhagavatprabhāvād acirād eva prāpnoti /
body.translated_text: Whatever entity, established in various states, abides within the heart-seed — it would be pure. And that very lordly knowledge — the limited soul (<s>aṇu</s>) [so called because it] breathes, lives, sounds, emits limited utterance, [the word being] cerebral — by the power of the Lord, attains it swiftly.

body.text: katham /
body.translated_text: How?

body.text: ParTri 23:

children.translated_text: "The impeller of that is to be known as <s>Śiva</s>,"
"the omniscient Supreme Lord,"
"all-pervading, spotless, transparent,"
"satisfied, self-aboding, pure."

body.text: yas taccodako guruḥ sa śiva eva jñeyaḥ / śiva eva taccodakaḥ / sa cājñeyo jñātaiva / svāyatanaḥ svān ayān vijñānarūpān bhāvāṃs tanotīti / sarvaṃ caitad vistarato nirṇītam eva //
body.translated_text: He who is the impeller of that, the <s>guru</s> — he is to be known as <s>Śiva</s> himself. <s>Śiva</s> himself is the impeller of that. And He is unknowable, [yet] already known. 'Self-aboding' (<s>svāyatana</s>) — He extends His own abodes (<s>āyas</s>), which are of the nature of consciousness, as entities. And all this has been determined in detail.

body.text: evaṃ vistaraśo 'bhidhāya tātparyeṇa nigamayati /
body.translated_text: Having stated thus in detail, he concludes with the essential purport:

body.text: ParTri 24-25:

children.translated_text: "Just as in the seed of the banyan tree,"
"the great tree abides in the form of power,"
"so in the heart-seed,"
"this world of moving and unmoving [beings] abides."
"Thus, one who knows in truth —"
"for him the <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) that leads to <s>nirvāṇa</s>"
"comes about, undoubted,"
"devoid of sesame, ghee, and oblations."

body.text: ihāsat tāvan na kiṃcid ity uktam / viśvaṃ ca viśvātmakam iti / tataś ca yathā vaṭabīje tatsamucitenaiva vapuṣāṅkuraviṭapapatraphalādi tiṣṭhatīty evaṃ viśvam idaṃ hṛdayāntaḥ / evaṃparijñānam evāsaṃdigdhā nirvāṇadīkṣā, yathoktam
body.translated_text: Here, first: nothing was non-existent — this has been stated. And the universe is of the nature of all — [this too]. And therefore, just as in the banyan seed, the sprout, branches, leaves, fruit, and so on abide in a form appropriate to it — so this universe [abides] within the heart. Such complete knowledge alone is the undoubted <s>nirvāṇa</s> initiation. As stated:

body.text:
Q: iyam evāmṛtaprāptir ayam evātmano grahaḥ /
Q: iyaṃ nirvāṇadīkṣā ca śivasadbhāvadāyinī /
body.translated_text:
Quote: 'This alone is the attainment of immortality; this alone is the grasp of the Self;
this is the <s>nirvāṇa</s> initiation, the bestower of the true being of <s>Śiva</s>.'

body.text: iti / anyā api dīkṣā bhogān vitareyur api, etatparijñānam eva tu tattvato dīkṣeti tata evātra sarvottaratvam, kulaśāstrebhyo 'pi ādhikyāt / yathā hi tulāṅkeṣūrdhvam ūrdhvaṃ parimite 'pi unnatyavanatiyoge 'nantam antaraṃ parimāṇasya bhavati, evam ūrdhvordhvatattveṣu deśakālabhogasaṃvedanānām anantam evāntaram ity evam evādhikībhavet, ṣaṭtriṃśato 'pi adhikaṃ bhaved iti / yataś ca saṃvedanam eva dīkṣā tad evoktam etatsaṃvidanupraviṣṭau vīro vā yoginī vā nijaparasattāsatatoditāmāyīyabāhyāntaḥkaraṇaraśmidevatādvādaśakacakreśvaraparabhairavabhaṭṭārakātmakanirṇītatattvāharūpānugṛhītau na kṛtadīkṣāv iti /
body.translated_text: Other initiations too may bestow enjoyments (<s>bhogas</s>), but the complete knowledge of this alone is truly <s>dīkṣā</s> — hence its supremacy over all, surpassing even the <s>kula</s> scriptures. For just as on the beam of a balance, even though the measured [quantity] increases higher and higher, the interval of measurement in the conjunction of rising and falling is infinite — so in the successively higher <s>tattvas</s>, the interval of the experiences of space, time, and enjoyment is indeed infinite — thus it would become ever more superior, even exceeding the thirty-six [tattvas]. And since awareness itself is <s>dīkṣā</s>, therefore it has been stated: a hero or a <s>yoginī</s> who has entered into this awareness — who has been graced by the determination of <s>tattvas</s> in the form of the day 'I am,' whose nature is the always-risen, non-<s>māyīya</s> external and internal sense-rays, deities, the circle of twelve, the lord of the circle, and <s>Parabhairava Bhaṭṭāraka</s> himself, arising from the reality of one's own and the supreme — is not [merely] one who has received initiation.

body.text: evam anuttarapadam uttararūpāparityāgenaiva yathā bhavati tathā vyāsasamāsābhyāṃ bhūyasā nirṇītam / adhunā tv idaṃ vaktavyam / ucyate tāvac chāstreṣu
body.translated_text: Thus, how the <s>anuttara</s> (supreme) state comes about without abandoning the form of the answer — this has been determined extensively, both in detail and in summary. But now this must be said. For it is stated in the scriptures:

body.text:
Q: manuṣyadeham āsthāya cchannās te parameśvarāḥ /
Q: nirvīryam api ye hārdaṃ trikārthaṃ samupāsate //
body.translated_text:
Quote: 'Having assumed a human body, those Supreme Lords move concealed;
even those devoid of power who worship the <s>Trika</s> meaning in the heart.'

body.text: iti / tat katham asyopāsā / tathāpi cānuttarasattayātrāpi bhāvyam anuttaratvād eva / sā ca katham ity ākāñkṣāṃ nirṇinīṣur granthāntaram avatārayati /
body.translated_text: So how is the worship (<s>upāsanā</s>) of this [to be performed]? And even so, one should dwell in the <s>anuttara</s> (supreme) existence — precisely because of its supremacy. And how that is [to be done] — wishing to determine [that], he introduces another section of the text:

body.text: ParTri 26-32:

children.translated_text: "On the crown of the head, on the face, and on the heart,"
"on the secret part, and on the body likewise,"
"having performed <s>nyāsa</s> (ritual placement), and having tied the <s>śikhā</s> (tuft),"
"empowered with twenty-seven [recitations of the] <s>mantra</s>,"
"And binding the directions,"
"one by one, of the ten [directions], one should apply;"
"having first given three claps,"
"with sound, for the pacification of obstacles."
"With water empowered by recitation"
"equal in number to the <s>śikhā</s>, one should then sprinkle;"
"flowers and so on, everything in sequence,"
"on a <s>liṅga</s> or alternatively on a <s>sthaṇḍila</s> (ritual ground)."
"With a flower empowered by fourteen [recitations],"
"the preparation of the seat;"
"there the hero should worship the creation,"
"then again the seat."
"Having enclosed the creation,"
"afterward one should commence the worship:"
"perfectly complete with all <s>tattvas</s>,"
"adorned with all ornaments,"
"one should worship the Goddess, <s>Maheśānī</s>,"
"empowered with twenty-seven [recitations of the] <s>mantra</s>;"
"then with fragrant flowers,"
"one should honor [her] according to one's ability."
"One should worship with supreme devotion"
"and offer oneself."
"Thus the worship has been declared;"
"in the fire-rite too, this is the procedure."

body.text: mūrdhādīni bāhye tathocitarūpāṇi / vastutaḥ paraṃ brahmarūpābhihitapañcātmakavyomādidharaṇyāntasatattveśānādisāracidunmeṣecchājñānakriyārūpāṇy eva, mantraliṅgāt, yathā mantrāḥ 1) īśānamūrdhne, 2) tatpuruṣavaktrāya, 3) aghorahṛdayāya, 4) vāmadevaguhyāya, 5) sadyojātamūrtaye iti / tatraitatpañcakāvibhāgātmakam upakramopasaṃhārayoḥ rūpam iti dve, madhye ca prollasati vibhāgatve pañcānām ekaikaśaḥ pañcātmakatā iti pañcaviṃśatiḥ / atraiva mālinyādimantrāṇām anupraveśaḥ /
body.translated_text: The crown of the head and so on are, externally, of their well-known forms. In reality, however, they are the fivefold supreme <s>Brahman</s>-form — the true <s>tattvas</s> from space to earth, whose essence is <s>Īśāna</s> and the rest, of the nature of the flashing forth of consciousness, <s>icchā</s>, <s>jñāna</s>, and <s>kriyā</s> — as known from the <s>mantra-liṅga</s> (scriptural indicator), namely the <s>mantras</s>: 1) <s>Īśāna</s> for the crown, 2) <s>Tatpuruṣa</s> for the face, 3) <s>Aghora</s> for the heart, 4) <s>Vāmadeva</s> for the secret part, 5) <s>Sadyojāta</s> for the body. Now, at the beginning and conclusion, the form is the undivided fivefold nature — thus two; and in the middle, when differentiation unfolds, each of the five has a fivefold nature — thus twenty-five. Herein is the entry of the <s>Mālinī</s> and other <s>mantras</s>.

body.text:
tisraś ca devyāḥ pratyekam icchāditrayayogān navātmatāṃ prāptāḥ punar api sṛṣṭisthitisaṃhṛtivaśāt traidham āpannā iti saptaviṃśatisaṃsmṛtahṛdbījena śikhāyā evaṃrūpadharaṇyantaparikalpanasvātantryarūpāyāḥ paracidbuddhisparśaprāṇabrahmarandhravāharūpair upacaryamāṇāyā bandhanaṃ sarvāvibhāgasāraṃ tādātmyam / mūrdhādiṣu kevaleṣv api pratyekaṃ sarvāṇi vaktrādīni parasparaṃ viśeṣaṇāni / tac ca nirṇītam eva sarvasarvātmakatvanirṇayeṇaiva / diśyamānā ghaṭādyā eva diśaḥ tāś ca svāpekṣayā daśaiva bhavanti / tatrāpy etad eva bandhanam ātmasātkārātmakam / etac ca tālatrayeṇa / tālā pratisthā viśrāntiḥ / tatra sakārādi hṛdayam eva / tāś ca saśabdaṃ madhyamāntam / śabdanaṃ hi śabdaḥ, tac ca madhyamaiva
vaikharyās taccheṣātmakatvād ity uktaṃ bahuśaḥ / eṣā ca vighnānām abhedātmany akhaṇḍite paramātmani khaṇḍanātmakasaṃkocasārabhedakallolakalaṅkānāṃ śāntir abhedabhairavārṇavatādātmyam eva / yad āhuḥ śrīsomānandapādāḥ
body.translated_text: And the three Goddesses, each having attained a ninefold nature through the conjunction of the triad of <s>icchā</s> and the rest, again having assumed a threefold nature through creation, sustenance, and dissolution — thus the binding of the <s>śikhā</s> (tuft) with the heart-seed of twenty-seven recitations — of the <s>śikhā</s> which, being of the nature of the freedom to project [the universe] up to earth in such a form, is served by the channels of the supreme consciousness, intellect, touch, <s>prāṇa</s>, and <s>brahmarandhra</s> — means the identity that is the essence of complete non-differentiation. Even in the crown and so on taken individually, all the face and so on are mutual qualifiers of each other. And this has been determined precisely by the determination of the nature of everything being the Self of all. The directions being indicated are pots and the like themselves; and they, relative to themselves, are indeed ten. There too, this very binding is of the nature of self-assimilation. And this [is done] with three claps. 'Clap' (<s>tāla</s>) means establishment, repose. There, the heart itself beginning with 'sa' and so on. And those [claps are done] 'with sound' — up to <s>Madhyamā</s>. For 'sounding' (<s>śabdana</s>) is sound, and that is indeed <s>Madhyamā</s> itself, because <s>Vaikharī</s> is of the nature of being a remainder of that — this has been stated repeatedly. And this is the pacification of obstacles — of the waves and stains of differentiation whose essence is contraction, which break the unbroken, non-dual supreme Self — [namely,] the very identity with the ocean of the non-dual <s>Bhairava</s>. As the revered <s>Somānandapāda</s> states:

body.text:
Q: asmadrūpasamāviṣṭaḥ svātmanātmanivāraṇe /
Q: śivaḥ karotu nijayā namaḥ śaktyā tatātmane // iti /
body.translated_text:
Quote: 'May <s>Śiva</s>, who is absorbed in our own essential nature, through His own <s>Śakti</s>,
accomplish the removal of the self by the self — homage to that one who is of that very nature!'

body.text: evam eva saptaviṃsatijaptaṃ toyam ity arghapātravidhiḥ / toyam atra sarvam eva hṛdayaṃ dravātma, aniyantritatvād asaṃkocadānāc ca / puṣpaṃ vyākhyātam / liṅgaṃ ca
body.translated_text: In the same way, the water empowered with twenty-seven recitations — this is the procedure of the <s>arghya</s> (oblation) vessel. 'Water' here means the heart in its entirety, being of fluid nature, because of being unrestrained and because of bestowing non-contraction. 'Flower' has been explained. And '<s>liṅga</s>' —

body.text: Q: ...yatra līnaṃ carācaram /

children.text: ity etad api nirṇītam eva / viśvātmani tattve āsikriyāyām adhikaraṇasya kartuś cāsanasya svātantryāt kalpyamānasya svātantryeṇa kalpyamānatvaṃ caturdaśena aukāreṇa, tasyaiva triśūlarūpatvād ity uktam eva / sṛṣṭir ādikṣāntatādātmyamayaṃ hṛdayaṃ śaktir guhyam iti vīratvam / ata eva āsanam api sarvaṃ tatraiva, ādhārādheyayoḥ parasparaikarūpatvāt / yathoktam
children.translated_text: This too has been determined already. In the <s>tattva</s> that is the Self of all, the preparation of the seat — of the substratum and of the agent — being established by sovereign freedom, is [expressed] through the sovereign freedom of being established by the fourteenth [vowel] 'au,' because that very [vowel] has the trident-form — as has been stated. The creation — the heart that is the identity from 'a' to 'kṣa' — is the <s>śakti</s>, the secret, and thus the heroic nature. Therefore, the seat too is entirely there alone, because of the mutual identity of support and supported. As stated:

body.translated_text: Quote: '...in which the moving and unmoving are dissolved.'

body.text: Q: sarvabhūtastham ātmānam ... /
body.translated_text: Quote: 'The Self abiding in all beings...'

body.text:
ityādi / saṃpuṭīkaraṇaṃ sṛṣṭer ādikṣāntāyāḥ pratyekaṃ sarvaśaś ca hṛdayabījena / paratattva evollāsāt saṃhārāc ca na cānavasthety uktam eva / sṛṣṭeś ca saṃpuṭīkaraṇam ubhayasaṃghaṭṭakṣobhānandarūpam / tadutthadravyopayogo 'pi / ktvā atra śabdapratītipaurvāparyamātre / sarvatattvaiḥ suṣṭhv abhedena samyag anapāyitayā pūrṇatvam / sarvatra ca paramāṇāv api yad ā samantāt bharaṇaṃ sarvātmīkaraṇam, sarvair vā ghaṭasukhatiryaṅnaraviriñciviṣṇurudramantrasadāśivādipramātṛrūpair avayavamānair ahamekarasāvayavitvaṃ nirṇītam eva / ata eva viśiṣṭākṛtyāyudhādidhyānam atra noktam, tasya nirmeyatvāt / ārurukṣur etāvattrikārthābhilāṣukaś ca katham ārohatv iti cet kasyāyam arthibhāvaḥ / mā tarhi ārukṣat / siddhātantrādividhim
eva tadāśayenaiva nirūpitataddhyānādisaṃkocam ālambatām / asaṃkocitānuttarapade hy anadhikṛta eva / eṣa eva sadodito yogaḥ / gandhapuṣpādi nirṇītam / yathāśabdaḥ sahārthe, tṛtīyā ca tatraivoktā / parayaiva hṛdayarūpayā pūjayet / katham / bhaktyā tādātmyānupraveśaprahvatātmanā / bhaktyā svayaṃkḷptena pūjyapūjakavibhāgena / pūjyo hi svayaṃ sṛjyate / sa paraṃ svatantracinmayatāparamārtha evānuttarasvātantryabalāt, na ghaṭādir iva jaḍa iti viśeṣo 'tra / tad uktaṃ śrīpratyabhijñāyām
body.translated_text: And so on. The enclosing (<s>saṃpuṭīkaraṇa</s>) of the creation — from 'a' to 'kṣa' — is [done] individually and comprehensively with the heart-seed. Since there is both the flashing forth and the withdrawal into the supreme <s>tattva</s> alone, there is no infinite regress — as has been stated. And the enclosing of the creation is of the nature of the bliss of the agitation of the union of both [Śiva and Śakti]. The use of substances arising from that [is also implied]. 'Having done' (<s>kṛtvā</s>) here [indicates] merely the temporal sequence of the verbal cognition. 'Perfectly full with all <s>tattvas</s>' — completeness through thorough, non-different, complete, non-deviating [union with all tattvas]. And everywhere, even in the atom, the all-encompassing pervading in every direction, the making-one's-own-Self-of-all — or: the oneness of the 'I'-essence, having as its measured parts the knowers in the forms of pot, pleasure, animal, human, <s>Viriñci</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Mantra</s>, <s>Sadāśiva</s>, and so on — has been determined already. Therefore, the meditation upon a specific form with weapons and so on is not stated here, because that is to be constructed [and therefore secondary]. If one asks: 'How should one who aspires to ascend, who desires this much of the <s>Trika</s> meaning, actually ascend?' — whose is this neediness? Then let him not ascend! Let him resort to the procedure of the <s>Siddhatantra</s> and so on — the contraction of meditation and so on determined with that very intention. For in the uncontracted <s>anuttara</s> state, he is indeed without qualification. This alone is the ever-arisen <s>yoga</s>. Incense, flowers, and so on have been determined. The word 'yathā' is in the sense of 'together with'; and the instrumental case is stated there itself. One should worship with the supreme [devotion] alone, which has the form of the heart. How? With devotion (<s>bhakti</s>) — through the humility of entering into identity. With devotion — through the self-made division of worshipped and worshipper. For the object of worship is itself created [by oneself]. And it is supreme — of the ultimate reality of sovereign, consciousness-constituted nature — by the force of <s>anuttara</s> sovereignty alone, not inert like a pot and so on — this is the distinction here. As stated in the sacred <s>Pratyabhijñā</s>:

body.text:
Q: svātantryāmuktam ātmānaṃ svātantryād advayātmanaḥ /
Q: prabhur īśādisaṃkalpair nirmāya vyavahārayet //

children.text: iti / bhaktyā ca lakṣaṇayā / pūjanena paraṃ tattvaṃ lakṣyate / sarvakriyāsv evaṃrūpatāpratyabhijñānam, upāyatvāt, lipyakṣarasyeva māyīyavarṇavyutpattau tasyāpi ca varṇavīryānupraveśa iva / ātmānaṃ nivedayet, anyasya nivedyasyābhāvāt / evaṃ ca ātmānam eva niḥśeṣeṇa niruttarapadaṃ vedayet / anuttarasattānusāreṇātra saṃbhāvanāyāṃ liṅ, satatam evaṃmayatvenaivāvasthiter iti hy uktam, upāsānusāreṇa tu niyogādāv api /
children.translated_text: And with devotion that has the character of indication (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>). Through worship, the supreme <s>tattva</s> is indicated. In all actions, the recognition of such a nature [is the point], because it serves as the means — just as a written letter [serves as means] in the learning of the <s>māyīya</s> (illusory) phoneme, and even that [māyīya phoneme serves] as if entering into the power of the [true] phoneme. 'One should offer oneself' — because there is no other thing to be offered. And thus, one should cause oneself alone to be known completely, to the <s>anuttara</s> (supreme) state. In accordance with the <s>anuttara</s> existence, the optative mood (<s>liṅ</s>) here is in the sense of possibility, since it has been stated that one abides perpetually in the nature of such-ness; but in accordance with worship, [it is used] even in the sense of injunction and so on.

body.translated_text:
Quote: 'Through sovereignty He projects the Self from sovereignty;
the Lord, being of non-dual nature, having fashioned [it] through the conceptions of <s>Īśa</s> and so on, transacts [with it].'

body.text: evam ā samantāt sarvatra sadā yat khyātaṃ pāramārthikaśuddhaśivasvarūpaprathātmikā khyātir iti tad eva yajanam, parabhairavasaṃviddevatāyāḥ pūjanāt tayā ca tādātmyasamyaggamanarūpatākaraṇāt sarvatra ca parimitātmīyātmarūpasvatvanivṛttyā paripūrṇacidghanaśivaśaktyātmakātmīyarūpaparasvatvāpādanātma dānāc ca / etad eva agnikāryaṃ sarvavāsanābījānāṃ sarvapadārthendhanagrāsalāṃpaṭyajājvalyamāne śivasaṃghaṭṭakṣobhakṣubhitaparaśaktyaraṇisatatasamuditaparabhairavamahāmahasi sarvābhiṣvaṅgarūpamahāsnehājyaprājyapratāpe havanād antardāhāt / ayam eva agnikārye vidhir dīkṣāparyanto 'pi, nānyaḥ pṛthak kaścid iti tātparyam /
body.translated_text: Thus, the worship (<s>yajana</s>) is that which is manifested everywhere, always, in every direction — the manifestation whose nature is the shining forth of the ultimate, pure <s>Śiva</s>-nature. [It is worship] because of the worshipping of the deity of <s>Parabhairava</s>-consciousness, and because of the proper, complete entering into identity with her; and everywhere, because of the giving that is the bestowal of the supreme ownership — whose nature is the perfectly full, consciousness-dense <s>Śiva-Śakti</s> Self — through the cessation of the limited ownership of one's own limited self-form. This alone is the fire-rite — because of the offering, the inner burning, in the great radiance of supreme <s>Bhairava</s>, perpetually arisen from the fire-stick (<s>araṇi</s>) of the supreme <s>Śakti</s> agitated by the agitation of the union with <s>Śiva</s>, blazing with the fuel of all entities in the form of devouring all objects, resplendent with the abundant ghee of the great affection that is the form of total embrace. This alone is the procedure in the fire-rite, extending even to <s>dīkṣā</s>; there is no other separate [procedure] — this is the essential purport.

body.text:
svasvarūpaparijñānaṃ mantro 'yaṃ pāramārthikaḥ /
dīkṣeyam eṣa yāgaś ca kriyeyam apy anuttaraḥ //
body.translated_text:
"The complete knowledge of one's own essential nature —
this is the true <s>mantra</s>;
this is <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation), this is worship,
and this is the supreme <s>kriyā</s> (action)."

body.text: ata eva prāg evoktaṃ yathānyatra mantropāsādikriyā uttareṇa jñānagranthenottīryate naivam iheti / yad uktam ``uttarasyāpyanuttaram'' iti sūtre tad evaitadantena granthena nirvyūḍhaṃ hṛdayasyaiva yāgadīkṣākriyārūpatvāt tasya cānuttaratvāt / śrīsomānandapādais tu sruksruvasaṃskārādi sarvaṃsahatvapratipādanenāpy akhaṇḍitatvābhiprāyeṇa nirūpitam / evamādāv aṅgahṛdbhedadhūlibhedādy api tadrūpaṃ yujyate na kiṃcid atra nāpy upapadyate nāpy asti nāpy adharaśāstrapātitvena tadupajīvakatvam iti nirṇītaprāyam eva /
body.translated_text: Therefore, it was stated earlier that unlike elsewhere, where the ritual actions of <s>mantra</s>-worship and so forth are transcended by a subsequent text on knowledge, here this is not the case. What was stated in the <s>sūtra</s> "the <s>anuttara</s> (unsurpassed) even of the subsequent" — that has been fully elaborated by this text up to its conclusion, because the heart itself has the nature of sacrifice, initiation, and ritual action, and because that [heart] is the <s>anuttara</s>. The revered <s>Somānanda</s>, however, demonstrated all this — the consecration of the sacrificial ladle (<s>sruk</s>) and cup (<s>sruva</s>) and so forth — with the intention of showing its unbroken wholeness through establishing the capacity to bear everything. Thus, at the beginning too, the distinctions of limbs and heart, the distinctions of <s>dhūli</s> (dust-rites) and so forth — all that is appropriate as having that very nature; nothing here is inapplicable, nor is there anything that does not obtain, nor is there dependence on lower scriptures — this has been essentially established.

body.text: kim evamupāsāyāṃ bhavatīty avatarati /
body.translated_text: What happens through such worship? He introduces this:

body.text: ParTri 33ab:

children.translated_text: One who has properly performed the rite of worship,
remembering the <s>bīja</s> (seed), attains perfection.

body.text: evam anavarataṃ vyavahāreṣv api bījaṃ smarann eva smaraṇād eva kṛtapūjāvidhiḥ prakarṣeṇānyakulaśāstrādiśaivavaiṣṇavāntaśāstrātirekeṇaiva bhagavadbhairavabhaṭṭārakarūpasamāvīṣṭo nijaparasaṃviccamatkāravaśavinirmitabhāvakriḍāḍambaro jīvanmukta eva prathamoktanayena bhavati ity anubhava evāyam āvartate na tv anyat kiṃcid iti smaraṇam uktam / śrīmataśāstreṣv evam eva / upāsakas tv ananupraviṣṭavīryasattāsārahṛdayo 'pi kramapūjāmāhātmyād bījaṃ saṃyak smaran prāptahṛdayākhyatattvamantravīryaḥ prakarṣeṇa siddhyati kramapūjāmāhātmyād eva /
body.translated_text: Thus, one who remembers the <s>bīja</s> (seed) continuously even in worldly activities — by that very remembering, having performed the rite of worship with excellence, surpassing the other <s>kula</s>-scriptures and the inner doctrines of <s>Śaiva</s> and <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> traditions — becomes fully absorbed in the form of the blessed Lord <s>Bhairava</s>, one whose play of manifested existence is fashioned by the wonder of one's own supreme consciousness (<s>saṃvit</s>), and is indeed a <s>jīvanmukta</s> (liberated while living) according to the method stated at the outset. This is what the word 'remembering' means — it is this very experience that recurs, nothing else whatsoever. So it is in the blessed scriptures as well. However, even a worshipper whose heart has not yet been penetrated by the essence of the power of vitality, by the greatness of the sequential worship (<s>kramapūjā</s>), properly remembering the <s>bīja</s>, having obtained the power of the <s>mantra</s> called the heart-<s>tattva</s> (reality), attains perfection with excellence, precisely through the greatness of the sequential worship.

body.text: tāratamyātiśayāt svayaṃ vā prasannagurubhaṭṭārakavadanakamalād vā mantravīryaṃ hṛdayātmakam āsādayati jīvanmuktaś ca bhavatīti yāvat / atra dvāraparivāragurupūjanaṃ guṇaṃ khaṇḍanāṃ vā na vahati tata eva bhaṭṭapādaiḥ nyarūpi / atra tu kulapārvāṇi pavitraṃ ceti samyaktvaṃ pūjāvidheḥ /
body.translated_text: Through the gradation of degrees of excellence, one obtains the <s>mantra</s>-power, which is of the nature of the heart, either by oneself or from the lotus-mouth of the gracious preceptor (<s>guru-bhaṭṭāraka</s>), and becomes a <s>jīvanmukta</s> — such is the meaning. Here, the worship of the door-guardians, attendants, and preceptor neither adds a quality nor produces a deficiency — this was explained by the revered master (<s>Bhaṭṭapāda</s>). And here, the <s>kulaparvāṇi</s> (sacred junctures of the <s>kula</s>) and the <s>pavitrakam</s> (purificatory rite) constitute the 'propriety' of the rite of worship.

children.text: yatrāntar akhilaṃ bhāti yac ca sarvatra bhāsate /
children.translated_text: Within which everything shines, and which shines in all things —

children.text: sphurattaiva hi sā hy ekā hṛdayaṃ paramaṃ budhā //
children.translated_text: that very radiance alone is indeed the one supreme heart, O wise ones.

children.text: rāsabhī vaḍavā vāpi svaṃ jagaj janmadhāma yat /
children.translated_text: Whether a she-donkey or a mare, the universe which is the birthplace of one's own [creation],
simultaneously expanding and contracting in the heart, one rejoices.
Similarly, within the heart of the central channel (<s>suṣumnā</s>) of the great bliss of both [expansion and contraction],
one should worship the heart that pulsates, whose nature is creation.

children.text: dhyāyan smaran pravimṛśan kurvan vā yatra kutracit /
children.translated_text: Whether meditating, remembering, reflecting, or acting, wherever one may be,

children.text: viśrāntim eti yasmāc ca prollased dhṛdayaṃ tu tat //
children.translated_text: that in which one finds rest and from which the heart springs forth — that is it.

children.text: tad ekam eva yatraitaj jñānaṃ vaikalpikaṃ param /
children.translated_text: That alone is the one in which this highest conceptual knowledge,
the <s>tattvas</s> (principles), the expanse of worlds, <s>Śiva</s> and the other beings down to the bound souls and the mothers —
each one, manifesting its own wondrous inner essential nature in its ultimate reality,

children.text: citrīkurvanta eṣanti tāṃ citraṃ saṃvidaṃ parām //
children.translated_text: they paint that supreme consciousness (<s>saṃvid</s>) as a variegated picture.
In the ten [senses], substances, actions, places, knowledge, and all other [categories],
the transition [of awareness] without any hesitation — this is his ever-arisen worship.
And the mere sequential worship, together with the sacred junctures (<s>kulaparvan</s>) and purificatory rites (<s>pavitrakam</s>),
is declared here in the <s>Trika</s> doctrine as the 'propriety' of worship.

body.text: yathoktam
body.translated_text: As it has been stated:

body.text:
Q: dravāṇām iva śārīraṃ varṇānāṃ sṛṣṭibījakaṃ /
Q: śāsanānāṃ trikaṃ śāstraṃ mokṣāṇāṃ bhairavī sthitiḥ //
body.translated_text: Q: Just as the body is [the essence] of fluids, and the seed of creation is [the essence] of the letters (<s>varṇa</s>), / Q: so the <s>Trika</s> scripture is [the essence] of all doctrines, and the state of <s>Bhairavī</s> is [the essence] of all liberations.

body.text:
Q: upāsāyāḥ samāpattir vratānāṃ vīravṛttitā /
Q: tathaiva parvamadhye tu kulaparvāṇi śāsane //
body.translated_text: Q: <s>Samāpatti</s> (meditative absorption) is [the essence] of all forms of worship, the conduct of the hero (<s>vīravṛtti</s>) is [the essence] of all vows, / Q: and likewise among all sacred junctures, the <s>kulaparvāṇi</s> (kula-junctures) are [the essence] in [this] doctrine.

body.text:
Q: sarveṣāṃ cāpi yāgānāṃ pūraṇāya pavitrakam /
Q: pavitrakaṃ na kurvanti catus trir dviḥ sakṛt tu ye //
body.translated_text: Q: And for the completion of all sacrifices, there is the <s>pavitrakam</s> (purificatory rite). / Q: Those who do not perform the <s>pavitrakam</s> four times, three times, twice, or even once,

body.text: Q: kulaparva na jānanti teṣāṃ vīryaṃ na rohati /
body.translated_text: Q: and do not know the <s>kulaparvan</s> (sacred kula-juncture) — for them the power (<s>vīrya</s>) does not grow.

body.text: iti /
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: evam anuttarasvarūpaṃ vistarato nirṇītam, yatra bhāvanādyanavakāśaḥ / prasaṃkhyānamātram eva dṛḍhacamatkāralakṣaṇahṛdayaṅgamatātmakapratipattidārḍhyaparyantam / yatropāyadhaureyadhārādharan nidhatte siddhiprepsuṣu tu yogo vaktavyaḥ / svātantryānīyamānāsv api dṛṣṭayogasiddhiṣu laukikaprasiddhiniyatyuttaratve 'pi pārameśavyavasthārūpaniyatyanatikramāt, yaduktaṃ śivadṛṣṭau
body.translated_text: In this way, the nature of the <s>anuttara</s> (unsurpassed) has been determined in detail, wherein there is no scope for meditation and the like — [there is] only enumeration (<s>prasaṃkhyāna</s>), extending up to the firmness of conviction characterized by the heart's direct apprehension marked by intense wonder. Where [the teaching] places its foremost current of means for those who desire <s>siddhi</s> (attainment), there <s>yoga</s> (the path of practice) must be spoken of. For even though the yogic attainments that have been perceived are brought about by [the Lord's] absolute freedom, and even though they surpass worldly conventional certainties, there is no transgression of the regularity that has the form of the Lord's own established order. As stated in the <s>Śivadṛṣṭi</s>:

body.text: Q: tathāpi citrakarmārtham upāyo vācya adarāt /
body.translated_text: Q: Nevertheless, for the purpose of the wondrous display, the means should be taught with care.

body.text: iti / tatrāpi cānuttararūpasya nāsti khaṇḍanā kācit, dṛṣṭasiddhīpsāyatnasevātadāptitatphalaviśrāntyāder api paraikamayatvāt, kiṃ tu jīvanmuktāpekṣayā mandaśaktipāto 'sāv ucyeta apūrṇaprāyatvāt /
body.translated_text: And even there, there is no diminishment whatsoever of the <s>anuttara</s> nature, since even the effort of desiring perceived attainments, the practice, the obtaining of those [attainments], and the rest in their fruit — all of that is pervaded by the supreme oneness alone. However, in comparison with the <s>jīvanmukta</s>, this [practitioner] may be called one of lesser descent of power (<s>mandaśaktipāta</s>), because of being mostly incomplete.

body.text: taṃ yogamārgaṃ nirūpayituṃ granthaśeṣo 'vatarati /
body.translated_text: To set forth that path of <s>yoga</s>, the remainder of the text introduces [the following]:

body.text: ParTri 33cd-33ef:

children.translated_text: The <s>bīja</s> (seed) without beginning or end,
blossoming, situated in the middle of the <s>tithis</s> (lunar days),
one should meditate upon [it] as dwelling within the heart-lotus,
one should constantly practice the portion of <s>Soma</s> (the moon).

body.text:
etad eva hṛdayabījaṃ dīpakābhāvād gamāgamaśūnyatvāt satatoditatvāc cānādyantam / tad eva vikasat paripūrṇatvaṃ yātam / tithīnaṃ madhyagaṃ hṛdayatvāt / tad eva saṃkocavikāsadharmopacaritapadmabhāve kande guhye hṛdaiva dhyāyet / kiṃ cāsya dhyānam āha / somāṃśaṃ ṣoḍaśakalātmakaṃ kesararūpam abhitaḥ samantād asyet kṣipet paripūrṇacandrasyāsya hṛtkārṇikāniveśikalayā svasvadvādaśāntagam / puṣpādyudayasthānād āhṛtāmṛtasparśaḥ prodyannādānusāracumbikālakṣaṇakākacañcupuṭamudrāmudritaḥ punas tadupasṛtaśiśirāmṛtarasāsvādavikasvarahārdasomaprasarannādanirmathithasudhāpānapūritacandramāḥ punaḥ sūryakalodayamayo 'nackasakāramātraviśrānto romāñcastobhotpatanabāṣpakampastambhādyanugṛhītadeho
'bhyāsaṃ kuryād iti bhaṭṭadhaneśvaraśarmā /
body.translated_text: This very heart-<s>bīja</s> is without beginning or end because there is no illuminator [other than itself], because it is devoid of coming and going, and because it is ever-arisen. That very [seed], blossoming, has reached fullness. It is situated in the middle of the <s>tithis</s> (lunar phases) because of being the heart. That very [seed], in the form of a lotus characterized by the properties of contraction and expansion, in the <s>kanda</s> (bulb), in the secret [center], one should meditate upon in the heart itself. Moreover, he describes its meditation: one should project (<s>abhitaḥ kṣipet</s>) the portion of <s>Soma</s>, consisting of sixteen <s>kalās</s> (digits), in the form of filaments, all around it; by placing this full moon in the pericarp of the heart, [the breath] reaching one's own <s>dvādaśānta</s> (twelve-finger space above); touched by the nectar drawn from the place where the flower and other [experiences] arise; sealed with the <s>kākacañcupuṭamudrā</s> (crow-beak seal) characterized by the kissing-sound that follows the rising <s>nāda</s> (inner sound); then again, with the moon filled by drinking the nectar churned by the <s>nāda</s> spreading from the heart's <s>soma</s> that blossoms through savoring the cool nectar-essence that flows to it; then again, consisting of the rise of the solar <s>kalā</s>, resting only in the mere <s>sa</s>-sound, the body graced by horripilation, trembling, tears, rigidity, and other [ecstatic signs] — one should practice thus, according to the revered <s>Dhaneśvaraśarman</s>.

body.text: ādyantarahitaṃ sakāramātraṃ ṣoḍaśākārāditithirahitaṃ kalāgrāsakrameṇa hṛdaye 'ntar nikṣipet nālikājalākarṣaṇavat /
body.translated_text: The [seed] without beginning or end — the mere <s>sa</s>-sound, devoid of the sixteen forms beginning with the vowel sounds, the <s>tithis</s> — one should deposit within the heart through the method of gradual absorption of the <s>kalās</s>, like drawing water through a pipe.

body.text: calanakampanaspandanasamāviṣṭamūlādhāratrikonabhadrakandahṛnmukhamudrāsu yugapad eva vilambitamadhyadrutataratadatiśayādidhārāprāptivaśagalitasūryasomakalājālagrāse ādyantarahitaṃ kṛtvā /
body.translated_text: Having made [the seed] without beginning or end by the absorption of the net of solar and lunar <s>kalās</s> that dissolve through attaining the streams of slow, medium, fast, faster, and exceedingly [fast speeds], simultaneously in the <s>mudrās</s> (seals) of the <s>mūlādhāra</s> triangle, the auspicious <s>kanda</s> (bulb), and the opening of the heart, [all] pervaded by movement, trembling, and pulsation —

body.text: ādyantābhyām etadbījaṃ mātṛkāpekṣayā aukārasakārābhyāṃ rahitaṃ viśleṣaṇayuktilabdhavīryaparicayaṃ dhruvaṃ visargātmakaṃ vikasatāṃ pañcadaśānāṃ tithīnāṃ yan madhyaṃ tithirahitam eva grastakālaṃ ṣoḍaśaṃ tato 'pi gacchati yat ``saptadaśī kalā'' ity uktam /
body.translated_text: This <s>bīja</s>, deprived of its beginning and end — with respect to the <s>mātṛkā</s> (alphabet), stripped of the <s>au</s>-sound and the <s>sa</s>-sound — having gained familiarity with the power obtained through the method of separation, permanently of the nature of <s>visarga</s> (emission), that which is the middle of the fifteen blossoming <s>tithis</s>, itself free of <s>tithis</s>, the sixteenth [phase] whose time has been swallowed, and which goes beyond even that — which is called "the seventeenth <s>kalā</s>."

body.text: somasya soḍaśātmakam āmṛtam aṃśaṃ hṛtkamale dhyāyet / tad eva nityam abhyasyed ity asmadguravaḥ / tathā hi sahomayā bhagavatyā saṃghaṭṭātmakasamāpattikṣobheṇa tattvanirmathanātmanā vartata iti somo bhaṭṭārakaḥ / tasya samagrabhavabhāvāvayavinaḥ paripūrṇāhamātmano 'ṃśo nīlasukhādiḥ / tad evam abhyasyati svasvarūpāvartanasṛṣṭisaṃhārāvartacakrākṣamālikayā punaḥ punar āvartayatīti yat satyaṃ bhāvyate sa eva eṣa satatodito hṛdayajapaḥ / saṃbhāvanāyāṃ liṅ /
body.translated_text: One should meditate upon the immortal nectar-portion of <s>Soma</s>, consisting of sixteen [digits], in the heart-lotus.
