That very [practice] one should perform constantly — so say our preceptors. For thus: with the blessed Goddess who is accompanied by the sacrificial fire (<s>sahomā</s>), through the agitation of the <s>samāpatti</s> (absorption) whose nature is union, by means of churning the <s>tattvas</s> (realities) — thus does the Lord <s>Soma</s> exist. His portion, [namely] blue, pleasure, and the like, belongs to Him who is the possessor of all parts of existence, whose self is the fullness of 'I'-consciousness. Thus one who practices in this way, revolving again and again through the garland-wheel of the cycles of creation and dissolution that are the return to one's own nature — that which is truly contemplated, that alone is this ever-arisen recitation (<s>japa</s>) of the heart. The optative mood is used to express possibility.

body.text:
anye tu hṛtsthānād dvādaśāntāntaṃ yaś cāraḥ ṣaṭtriṃśadaṅgulas tatra sūryarūpatayollāsya bahir ardhatuṭimātraṃ viśramya avināśy amṛtākhya vi sargarūpasomakalodaye sapādāṅguladvitayamātrāyāṃ tuṭau tuṭau pratyekaṃ candrakalāparipūraṇe pañcadaśyāṃ tuṭau pūrṇāyāṃ hṛtpadme pūrṇaś ca bhavati / ardhatuṭimātraṃ ca tatrāpi viśrāntiḥ / evaṃ ṣoḍaśatuṭyātmā ṣaṭtriṃśadaṅgulaś cāro bhavati ity avasthāyām ādyantarahitam anastamitatvāt vikasatsu dvitīyādiṣv antargataṃ somāṃśaṃ visargarūpaṃ hṛtpadmamadhye viśliṣya saptadaśātmakaṃ pariśīlanena dhyāyan kalāgrāsābhyāsaṃ kuryād ityādi samādiśan / sarvaṃ caitad yuktam eva mantavyam / atra cāvṛttyānantaṃ vyākhyānaṃ sūtratvād upapannam eva yata uktam
``anantārthasūtraṇāt sūtram'' iti / ``triṃśikā cānuttarasūtram'' iti guravaḥ / evaṃ pūrveṣv api ślokasūtreṣu /
body.translated_text: Others, however, [teach that] the course (<s>cāra</s>) from the heart-center to the <s>dvādaśānta</s> (twelve-finger space) is thirty-six finger-breadths; there, having caused [the breath] to rise in the form of the sun, one rests externally for merely half a <s>tuṭi</s> (time-unit); then in the imperishable <s>visarga</s> (emission) called nectar, at the rise of the lunar <s>kalā</s> of <s>Soma</s>, in each <s>tuṭi</s> measuring two and a quarter finger-breadths, with the filling of one lunar <s>kalā</s> in each <s>tuṭi</s>, at the fifteenth <s>tuṭi</s> when [the moon] is full, one becomes full in the heart-lotus; and there too one rests for merely half a <s>tuṭi</s>. Thus the course consists of sixteen <s>tuṭis</s> and is thirty-six finger-breadths — in this state, [the seed is] without beginning or end because it never sets; among the blossoming [phases] from the second onward, one should meditate upon the <s>Soma</s>-portion in the form of <s>visarga</s>, contained within, in the center of the heart-lotus, and having separated it into its seventeenth [aspect], one should practice the absorption of the <s>kalās</s> through cultivation — thus they instruct. And all of this should be understood as entirely appropriate. Here, the commentary through repetition [of meanings] is indeed fitting because of the <s>sūtra</s>-nature [of the text], since it has been said: "A <s>sūtra</s> is so called because it strings together infinite meanings." "And the Triṃśikā is an <s>anuttara</s>-<s>sūtra</s>" — so say the preceptors. The same applies to the earlier verse-<s>sūtras</s> as well.

body.text: kim ittham abhyāse sati bhavatīty āha
body.translated_text: What happens when one practices in this manner? He says:

body.text: ParTri_34:

children.text: yān yān kāmayate kāmāṃs tān tāñ cchīghram avāpnuyāt /
children.translated_text: Whatever desires one desires, those one swiftly obtains;

children.text: asmāt pratyakṣatām eti sarvajñatvaṃ na saṃśayaḥ //
children.translated_text: from this, omniscience becomes directly manifest — there is no doubt.

body.text: evamabhyāsād yad yat kāmayate tat tad acirād eva tathāvidhasarvamayahṛdayavīryasamucchalitecchāprasarāvaṣṭambhaviśeṣabalodyogasaṃrambhasotsāhaḥ punaḥ punas tatsthitirūḍhirūpābhyāsāt prāpnoti / kiṃ bahunā / sarvajñatvaṃ parabhairavātmakatvam anenaiva deheneti sarvam uktvopasaṃhriyate / paryante hi prasarasyopasaṃhāre viśrāntirūpākulasattāsādane bhairavatā ity uktam asakṛt /
body.translated_text: Through such practice, whatever one desires, that one obtains before long, being full of enthusiastic vigor and forceful exertion through the particular power of the steadying of the outpouring of will that surges forth from the power of the heart which pervades everything in that manner — and through repeated practice in the form of the deepening establishment in that [state], one attains [it]. In brief: omniscience, identity with the supreme <s>Bhairava</s>, in this very body — having said all this, he concludes. For at the culmination, in the withdrawal of expansion, in the attainment of the <s>akula</s> (transcendent) state whose nature is repose, there is <s>Bhairava</s>-hood — this has been stated repeatedly.

body.text: so 'yam upasaṃhāragranthaḥ
body.translated_text: This is the concluding text:

body.text: ParTri 35:

children.translated_text: Thus, the attainment of the fruit of <s>mantras</s> —
this is the <s>Rudrayāmala</s> (the union of <s>Rudra</s> and his Consort).
Through the practice of this, <s>siddhi</s> (perfection) [is obtained],
omniscience is attained.

body.text: mantrāṇāṃ śāstrāntarīyāṇāṃ varṇānāṃ ca phalam evam avāpyate nānyathā / iti samāptau / rudrasya rudrāyāś ca yad yāmalaṃ saṃghaṭṭo nirvibhāgapraśnottararūpasvarūpāmarśanaprasarād ārabhya yāvad bahir anantāparigaṇanīyasṛṣṭisaṃhāraśatabhāsanaṃ yatrāntaḥ, tad etad akulopasaṃhṛtam eveti prasaṃkhyānanigamanam / ``etadabhyāsāt sarvajñatvam'' iti yogaphalanigamanam / satatoditaṃ hy etat sarvasyeti śivam /
body.translated_text: The fruit of <s>mantras</s> belonging to other scriptures and of the <s>varṇas</s> (letters) is thus obtained, and not otherwise — so [it is said] at the conclusion. The <s>yāmala</s> (union) of <s>Rudra</s> and <s>Rudrā</s> — that is, the coupling — [extends] from the arising of the outpouring of self-awareness in the form of non-differentiated question-and-answer, up to where within [that union] shines the external manifestation and dissolution of limitless, innumerable hundreds of creations. That is this — withdrawn into the <s>akula</s> (the transcendent) — such is the conclusion by way of enumeration (<s>prasaṃkhyāna</s>). "Through the practice of this, omniscience [is attained]" — this is the conclusion regarding the fruit of <s>yoga</s>. For this [heart] is ever-arisen as the essence of everything — thus, all is auspicious (<s>śivam</s>).

children.translated_text: Thus, a bee at the lotus-feet of the glorious <s>Maheśvara</s>, who is engaged in uplifting the people who have taken refuge —

children.text: vṛttiṃ vyadhāt trikarahasyavimarśagarbhāṃ kāśmīrikāc cukhalakād adhigamya janma //
children.translated_text: he composed this commentary, pregnant with the insight into the secret of the <s>Trika</s>, having obtained his birth from <s>Cukhala</s> of <s>Kāśmīra</s>.

children.text: etāvad etad iti kas tulayet prasahya śrīśāṃbhavaṃ matam anargalitāś ca vācaḥ /
children.translated_text: "This much is this" — who could forcibly weigh the glorious doctrine of <s>Śambhu</s>, and [whose] words flow unimpeded?

children.text: etat tu tāvad akhilātmani bhāti yan me bhātaṃ tato 'tra sudhiyo na parāṅmukhāḥ syuḥ //
children.translated_text: But this much at least shines within me, who am the Self of all — what has shone forth; therefore, may the wise not turn away from this.

children.text: ajñasya saṃśayaviparyayabhāgino vā jñānaṃ prakamparahitaṃ prakaroti samyak /
children.translated_text: For the ignorant, or for one beset by doubt and error, a work such as this properly produces knowledge free from wavering;

children.text: rūḍhasya niścayavato hṛdayapratiṣṭhāṃ saṃvādinīṃ prakurute kṛtir īdṛśīyam //
children.translated_text: for one who is firmly established, possessed of certainty, it produces a confirmation in the heart that accords [with his realization].
Having ascended to this height of the synthesis of the essence of meaning, one whose heart has ascended to the stream [of consciousness] may reflect even beyond this;

children.text: yady uttaraṃ tad api naiva saheta nedaṃ sopānam etad amalaṃ padam ārurukṣoḥ //
children.translated_text: if there is something further, [this work] would not resist that either, nor would this — for this is the stainless staircase for one who wishes to ascend to the supreme state.

children.text: kasmīreṣu yaśaskarasya nṛpater āsīd amātyāgraṇīḥ śrīmān vallabha ity udāhṛtatanur yaḥ prāgryajanmā dvijaḥ /
children.translated_text: In <s>Kāśmīra</s>, there was the foremost minister of king <s>Yaśaskara</s>, the illustrious one called <s>Vallabha</s>, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> of the highest birth;

children.text: tasya svāṅgabhavaḥ prasiddhipadavīpātraṃ samagrair guṇaiḥ śrīśauriḥ śiśucandracūḍacaraṇadhyānaikaratnākaraḥ //
children.translated_text: his own son, a vessel for the path of renown, endowed with all virtues, was the glorious <s>Śauri</s>, a very ocean of the jewel of meditation on the feet of the moon-crested one [<s>Śiva</s>].

children.text: śīlasyāyatanaṃ parasya yasaso jṛmbhāspadaṃ narmabhūr vātsalyasya samagralokakaruṇādharmasya janmasthitiḥ /
children.translated_text: An abode of virtue, a ground for the expansion of supreme glory, a playground of humor, the very birthplace of compassion-as-<s>dharma</s> toward all the world in its fullness of affection —

children.text: śrīmadvatsalikābhidhā sahacarī tasyaiva bhaktyullasat-prodriktāntaravṛtti śaṅkaranutau yasyā mano jṛmbhate //
children.translated_text: his companion, named the illustrious <s>Vatsalikā</s>, whose inner disposition shone forth with devotion, whose mind blossomed in the praise of <s>Śaṅkara</s>.

Born of that very [couple], one who manifested the creation and maintenance of the world, devoted solely to meditation, worship, and contemplation of <s>Śaṅkara</s>, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Karṇa</s> —

children.text: yo bālye 'py atha yauvane 'pi viṣayāsaktiṃ vihāya sthirām enām āśrayate vimarśapadavīṃ saṃsāranirmūlinīm //
children.translated_text: who, even in childhood and in youth, abandoning firm attachment to sense objects, takes refuge in this path of reflective awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>) that uproots <s>saṃsāra</s>.

children.text: bhrātā mamaiva śivaśāsanarūḍhacittaḥ prepsuḥ parātmani manorathaguptanāmā /
children.translated_text: My own brother, whose mind is established in the doctrine of <s>Śiva</s>, who aspires to the supreme Self, named <s>Manorathagupta</s> —

children.text: yaḥ śāstratantram akhilaṃ pravivektukāmaḥ prāptuṃ paraṃ śivapadaṃ bhavabhedanāya //
children.translated_text: who, desiring to thoroughly examine the entire body of scripture and <s>tantra</s>, [seeks] to attain the supreme state of <s>Śiva</s> for the destruction of worldly existence.
Devoted solely to the scriptures of <s>Śiva</s>, a knower of word, sentence, and valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>),
and the one named <s>Rāmadeva</s>, adorned with the highest birth.
That which has been composed by me, whose heart has grown in the doing of what is dear and beneficial to these [family members],
may that showing of the path serve for the attainment of <s>Śiva</s> by all.
In <s>Antarvedī</s> (Madhyadeśa, the land between the rivers), [one] named <s>Atrigupta</s>, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> of the highest birth, having obtained his origin [there], entered
the glorious land of <s>Kāśmīra</s>, whose surroundings had been purified by innumerable descents of the moon-crested one [<s>Śiva</s>].
In the great lineage of that [<s>Atrigupta</s>], born from <s>Varāhagupta</s>,
one who turned away from the affairs of <s>saṃsāra</s>, whose mind was fixed solely on <s>Śiva</s>, named <s>Cukhala</s>.
From him — who had discerned the entire range of categories — having obtained even the path of embodiment purified by the supreme Lord,
the one named <s>Abhinavagupta</s>, having attained fearlessness, caused this hidden truth of the <s>Trika</s> to enter [the world].

children.text: ye tāvat pravivekavandhyahṛdayās tebhyaḥ praṇāmo varaḥ ke 'py anye praviviñcate na ca gatāḥ pāraṃ dhig etāñ jaḍān /
children.translated_text: To those whose hearts are barren of discrimination — to them, the best [offering] is a salutation; some others do discriminate but have not reached the far shore — shame on those dull ones!

children.text: yas tv anyaḥ pravimarśasārapadavīsaṃbhāvanāsusthito lakṣaiko 'pi sa kaścid eva saphalīkurvīta yatnaṃ mama //
children.translated_text: But if there is even one other person, well-established on the path of appreciating the essence of reflective awareness (<s>pravimarśa</s>), he alone may render my effort fruitful.

children.text: svātmānāṃ pravivektum apy alasatāṃ ye bibhrati prārthanā tān praty ātmakadarthanān na parataḥ kiṃcit phalaṃ soṣyate /
children.translated_text: Those who bear laziness even in discerning their own Self — those self-tormentors — no fruit whatsoever will be derived from others on their behalf;

children.text: viśvasyāsya viviktaye sthiradhiyo ye saṃrabhante punaḥ tān abhyarthayituṃ mayaiṣa vihito mūrdhnā praṇāmādaraḥ //
children.translated_text: But those of steady intellect who strive again for the discernment of this entire universe — to honor them, this respectful salutation has been offered by me with bowed head.

children.text: bhrāmyanto bhramayanti mandadhiṣaṇās te jantucakraṃ jaḍaṃ svātmīkṛtya guṇābhidhānavasato baddhvā dṛḍhaṃ bandhanaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Those of dull understanding, wandering about, cause the inert mass of beings to wander, having made them their own, binding them firmly with bonds dwelling in the designation of qualities;

children.text: dṛṣṭvetthaṃ gurubhāravāhavidhaye yātānuyātān pasūn tatpāśapravikartanāya ghaṭitaṃ jñānatriśūlaṃ mayā //
children.translated_text: Seeing these animals yoked to carrying heavy burdens, following one after another, this trident of knowledge (<s>jñāna-triśūla</s>) has been fashioned by me for cutting asunder those bonds.

children.text: bahubhir api so 'ham eva bhramitas tattvopadeśakaṃmanyaiḥ /
children.translated_text: I too have been led astray by many who consider themselves teachers of truth (<s>tattva</s>),

children.text: tattvam iti varṇayugam api yeṣāṃ rasanā na pasparśa //
children.translated_text: whose tongue has not even touched the two syllables 'tat-tvam' (that thou art / reality).
The supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>), whose heart as guru is impelled by compassion for uplifting those who have taken refuge,

children.text: śrīmān devaḥ śaṃbhur mām iyati niyuktavāṃs tattve //
children.translated_text: the glorious Lord <s>Śambhu</s> has appointed me to this extent in reality (<s>tattva</s>).
Having entered of its own accord, as it were, into the heart of one who discriminates the pure state of each reality (<s>tattva</s>),
the doctrine of the revered <s>Somānanda</s> has been examined and composed by me in this work.

Aho! O Goddesses (<s>Devīs</s>), filled with overflowing bliss sparkling through the movement of the circle of the heart (<s>hṛccakra</s>), bearing upward the sharp trident of knowledge (<s>jñāna-śūla</s>) skilled in cleaving the tips of our bonds —

children.text: cetovākkāyam etad vigatabhavabhayotpatti yuṣmāsu samyak protaṃ yat tena mahyaṃ vrajata kila hṛdi drāk prasādaṃ prasahya //
children.translated_text: this offering of mind, speech, and body, free from the arising of fear of worldly existence, is well strung upon you; therefore, quickly grant me your grace forcefully in my heart!

children.text: vyākhyādikarmaparipāṭipade niyukto yuṣmābhir asmi gurubhāvam anupraviśya /
children.translated_text: I have been appointed by you, O Goddesses, having entered the state of guru, to the sequence of tasks such as commentary;

children.text: vākcittacāpalam idaṃ mama tena devyās taccakracāracaturasthitayaḥ kṣamadhvam //
children.translated_text: therefore, may you who are skillfully established in the movement of that circle (<s>cakra</s>) forgive this fickleness of my speech and mind!

body.text: samāptam idaṃ paratriṃśikātattvavivaraṇam
body.translated_text: Thus is completed this <s>Paratriṃśikā-tattva-vivaraṇa</s> (Elucidation of the Reality of the Supreme Thirty).

body.text:
śatair ekonaviṃśatyā triṃśikeyaṃ vivecitā /
sarveṣu trikaśāstreṣu granthīr nirdalayiṣyati //
body.translated_text: With nineteen hundred [verses], this Triṃśikā has been expounded; it will cut through the knots in all <s>Trika</s> scriptures.

body.text: kṛtir abhinavaguptasya
body.translated_text: This is the composition of <s>Abhinavagupta</s>.
